Love is in the air when the story of The Evil Within begins. Sebastian Castellanos and Ruvik were best friends in middle school, and are now attending Misato West High School together. They are assigned to the same class in their first year, but are given seats on opposite sides of the room! If that wasn't enough, it is announced at the entrance ceremony that the school will be closed in three years. This doesn't bother either of them, as they still plan on having lots of fun together during their high school years.
Sebastian gets jealous of Ruvik making new friends though, so the two decide to deepen their bond. "Let's do something we'd never do with other girls," Ruvik says, and they share a kiss in a vacant classroom after school one day. After that one kiss leads to many kisses, the two begin to realize that the relationship they share has changed completely. But what will happen to their relationship once a disapproving older sister begins to suspect that something is going on between the two?

Overall? A fun game. Admittidly a fairly confusing story for some, but the gameplay (In my opinion at least) more than makes up for it. I grew to like the characters (Especially Leslie and his little hobble) and really got into the game. The boss fights for the most part were challenging enough that it wasn't an easy fight, yet it was still very much enjoyable. The final fight though? Didn't live up to my expectations, truth be told. I died 129 times in my first playthrough, and only one of those times was to the final boss, Amagamation (If I recall correctly). In terms of replayability? Well one of the first things I did after finishing The Executioner was restart the game in New Game+ mode, mainly to work on 100%'ing the achievements but hey, we all have our reasons. The DLCs, for the most part weren't my cup of tea. I didn't get this game for a stealth experience, as in The Assignment and The Consequence, however I really, really did enjoy the slaughterfest that was The Executioner. The story for the DLCs I would say, is better than the main game itself, but that's just a matter of opinion.
For a full playthrough of the main game, and soon to be DLCs and a spoken review, check out my playlist below!

They say that repetive action is a sign of insanity.  This game has lots of that.  Repetitive action or insanity, you say?  Yes!  OK, so, this being a very, very obvious console game, I'll cover the elephants in the room up front.  Silly camera tricks?  Only once or twice...not enough to even notice.  Silly save game tricks?  Oh, yes, yes indeed!  They're all about it.  It really detracts from the functionality, in fact.  Other than that, it plays much like a clunky version of Dead Space.  In fact, while I generally, moderately enjoyed this game, nothing in it is original.  It's as though they took every console trope and nailed them together into a giant bloody ball of game organs.  The characters are neither interesting nor sympathetic.  The plot is tired and predictable, and the game is basically on a themepark rail for much of the time.  And, then, there are some genuinely enjoyable parts, such as when you get to decide what fun toys to use to get past enemies or avoid them altogether.  There are parts of this game where you are required to run and parts where you are required to fight.  It would have been much, much better if you could complete each section by doing either.  That would have provided some depth and originality.  Would have.  The combat system has potential too, in it's kind of slow awkwardness, and this would provide a genuinely special experience, but that totally goes downhill as well.  The mood, graphics, and sound are all technically very good while being ultimately uninspired.  But, in the end, it just lacks the creative genius that would really push it over the edge.  It has some cool sequences, but they feel shallow, and the action detracts from the overall feel of the game.  This is, ultimtely, a neither particularly good nor particularly terrible game.  I'm recommending it, but just barely.  There are definitely parts that will make you feel crazy - that's for sure.

This enduringly entertaining but visually cramped co-op game will be familiar to players of Left 4 Dead 2. Vermintide, however, succeeds in its melee combat system where Valve's zombie shooter fell short. On top of the satisfaction that naturally comes with chopping, burning, slicing and blasting hordes of scurrying, bounding ratmen, this is also one of the more compelling depictions of the stark brutality of the Warhammer universe. Produced by a much smaller studio than Valve, the game's considerable success has led to it being ported to consoles and receiving several (paid) mission expansions. Additionally, the recently tweaked loot mechanics and bounty board - with tasks that reward keys to trade for high-level weapons and cosmetic items - have helped to alleviate the common woe of low-quality rewards.

This game remains somewhat rough and unpolished a year after release, and while the developers currently plan to continue work on it, some basic functionality remains missing. There is an FoV slider - the effectiveness of which remains questionable - but weapon viewmodels are as gigantic as those in Left 4 Dead 2, sometimes even projecting out far enough ahead of you to clip through furniture, which doesn't mix well with the darkness and narrow field of view. If you get a headache from this sort of thing, best take a rain check on Vermintide until the developers get it sorted.

*First off, I'm nominating this game as the best use of a farm animal*  Now for the review:
I REALLY wanted to love this game.  The amazing graphics, the heavy but precise combat system, the strategizing with friends, the satisfying and gory decapitations I grew to love thanks to classic CS, the energetic voice acting, the adrenaline rush of possibly a perfect difficulty, the rich yet gloomy atmosphere, the thought provoking weapon selection, an AI almost without faults (losing tomes..), and prolly some other minor things I can't think of.  All of these amazing features can even redeem the fairly repetitive combat but not the rediculous reward system that has all my friends cringe when I ask if they want to play.
The missions are long and tedious which would be fine if you were rewarded so for going through hell and back, but alas it becomes a grueling and repetitive task in hopes you can actually complete it.   As it stands if you even finish a mission, the game likes to wave the rarer loot in your face like a piece of candy as you roll some dice in hopes to reach it.  This loot is random for all 5 classes so it's even difficult to try and gather 1 of each style of standard white quality weapons to figure out your favorite roles in combat.  I ended up rolling mostly with a particular class just because of what loot was provided to help benefit getting further with my friends.
Overall it's a very fun Warhammer themed Left 4 Dead style game.  I still play it every couple of months it feels like when my friends and I forget the reason we've stopped playing.  But a few missions in we feel good to move on as we quickly realize what we got back into.  Unfortunately this is why I can't recommend this game to the average gamer.  It is simply not enjoyable to repetitively spend lengthy amounts of time for a chance at a random upgrade.  Maybe to the most hardcore player that craves a massive time sink and can tolerate playing with randos online unless he gets a few friends together, otherwise no.
Furthermore with DLC tapping additional life into the game, maybe one day we can see a much more rewarding experience as it has been some really fun Co-op nevertheless.

Early Access Review after many updates:
1:Genre(2/5)
Generally i am not a big fan of turn-based-exploration games, and this one even makes it worse. If you have a large clan, pack , tribe or whatever, you spend most of your turn collecting food. The exploration isn't too exciting either as you come across the same types of landscape all the time.
2:Gameplay(2/5)
As mentioned  in the Genre-Section, this game consists mostly of collecting food. And because you spend most of the time doing that, you may lose track of your animals and what you wanted to do with them.
The most fun part is of course the procreation and trying to create a healthy and good looking pack , but in order to do so, you have to create very many other animals, who then just stand in the way or use up all your foodsupplies. And maybe I'm just unlucky, but i always have the problem that i have 10 females and 1 male in a pack, or the other way around, and you are scared all the time of your last male or female dying.
They have tried to improve the information-section on genes and inheritance, but i think something could be done to make finding good pairings more simple, i.e. being able to filter the family tree.
A point that looks really interesting when reading the game description are the biomes, but there is not a very strong connection yet between biomes and animals and how a different space changes the appearance of the animals.
3:Story(1/5)
Recently they have added a "Storymode" which is a very missleading name, because all it is so far is an inadequate tutorial and a "mission" given at the beginning of the game.
4:Playtime(3/5)
It is possible to play this game for 20+ hours maybe, which is an ok time for the price, but while and after playing it, i would consider it more like a time-wasting activity.
5:Graphics&Sound (3/5)
Nothing special or memorable concerning sound, but the graphics in general are quite nice and fitting for the game, and it is possible to make pretty nice creatures, the world around could use some work on the uniqueness-factor.
Overall: (2,2/5)
I am sorry that I don't know what is missing in the game, but something is missing to make it truly fun.
What I have to add to the review, though is : I really love the detail they put into the DNA and how the different genes are passed on. That is a nice treat for people who like biology and being able to use what they have learned in school.

This game surprised me. Truly.
How many times have you not heard the concept of "Zombies have been done to hell and back. It's boring now, cliche, and generic 'horror' material. A solid go-to concept that game developpers, movie directors, and halloween costume fanatics go to in an effort to get the desired effect of creepy spooky scary, with minimal need for customization and story writing."
Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army 2, pretty much takes every preconception of Zombie themed horror games, and puts a bullet in its head with the carved words "Suck my tallywacker" put in the side.
"I don't care that I'm generic. I don't care that I'm cliche. I don't care that I'm 'just another zombie flick', and I most certainly don't care that my storyline is on-par with World War Z! I'm a zombie game, where you snipe zombies, and magic is the cause. Don't like it? Go F yourself!"
That being said, Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army 2 manages to do something few titles have managed to do before. Take something cliche, and make it fun.
Have you played Sniper Elite of ANY kind before? If yes, then you'll find nothing new here. Gameplay has gotten zero changes from the father-title Sniper Elite V2.
For those who havn't:
The gameplay takes place in a linear third person shooter type style, with predetermined 'jump out and get you' moments where entire flocks of zombies appear from around a corner. There are two moments in the game: There is traveling, where you're moving from point A to point B, with a few handfuls of Zombies to shoot here and there, nothing too stressful. The other is siege, where you hunker down in one spot, and put down trip wire explosives, land mines, dynamite etc., while sitting in your perch and trying to kill every zombie before they overwhelm your position. Between those are safe houses, where you can refill everything, and where you'll get a free checkpoint.
"THIS SOUNDS EXACTLY LIKE LEFT 4 DEAD WTEGELKJBGKLAWBGKI"
Yeah, it does, doesn't it? That's cause it pretty much is L4D, except that it is in 3rd person, and only two kinds of zombies can run.
Slightly outdated, but that's due to its engine being a few years old now, but it is definitely good enough for medium range rigs and up. I can attest to the fact that a computer more than 4 years old will not run this title above 5 FPS unless it was a top end rig in its hayday.
I can best explain this by drawing a paralel to the once popular, now garbage TV show 'Lost'. You all remember how amazingly good that show was, but then the creators just started dragging it out, adding more and more bullcrap to it, until they tried to end it on a good note, and failed MISSERABLY!?!? That's pretty much what the sound is for me in this game. It's the one major draw-back in my book;
The sounds in the start of the game are pretty good. Really spooky scary, demonic whispers from Satan's world where you hear Hitler repeat sentences like "WE ARE ALL LOST!" and women crying for mercy etc. That's all pretty damned cool, and it really did a splendid job at setting the mood....
....
Until you play through like 4+ levels, and realize that the music soundtracks...Ambient sounds...Hitlers little frantic demonic time looped yelling? Is all the same, unchanged. By the 6th level I was literally able to to IMMEDIATELY mimic Hitlers words cause they were on a time loop that I eventually learned by heart cause I started to count the time between them(It's 7 minutes and 30 seconds by the way).
The music though, is good, if a little uncharacteristic, but it's good music to shoot nazi zombie brains to mush with, so I'm not complaining too much in that regard.
Conclusion:
Walk into this game expecting a linear, poorly narrated story that pretty much says 'unholy relic turns dead into zombies and only the relic holder controls them, assuming all parts of the relic are together....Which Hitler didn't quite realize until it was too late.' and you should be fine. I'd say its worth it, and to add a boost to the fun, the game permits many different difficulty varieties...The lowest to get a feel for the genre's controls and getting used to the playthrough etc. all the way up to Sniper Elite difficulty with a multiplier that goes up to as many as 4 times as many zombies as there normally would be(By the way, that means that for every 1 zombie in the normal game setting, there would be 4 extra ones in the highest multiplier)
Naturally, the 1x(Standard) multiplier, plus the regular difficulty settings, are intended for single player playthroughs, whereas the multipliers are for the hardcore games where you cooperate with 3 other players. Yes, there's multiplayer by the way!
I'd say, if you're into Zombie Games, and you have a group of like minded friends who want a shooter where you shoot magical satanic nazi zombies? Then this game is pretty much specifically created to suit your needs. If you're one of those 'ZOMBIE GAMES ARE DUMB, THIS IS DUMB, MAGIC IS DUMB, SATAN IS DUMB, I WANT Call of Duty BACK' people, then I suggest trying Hello Kitty Online instead...Yeah, I went there, deal with it.

I have completed Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, here are some of my thoughts on the game. Let me preface my impressions by stating that my registered play time is in no way indicative of the actual time I’ve spent on the game, there has been a fair amount of idling. I completed the Normal Mode with mostly S rankings and Hard Mode with B and C rankings.
Hotline Miami 2 introduces a larger cast of characters, it is considerably more cut-scene and story heavy than its predecessor. I do, to some extent appreciate that Dennaton have put in some effort to elaborate on the events that occurred in Hotline Miami 1. The extensive story telling somewhat diminishes the mystery that surrounds the first installment, for example, 50 Blessings is revealed as a patriotic movement that was founded as a response to the russian occupation. Beard has his own story arc, that reduces him to just another face in the overall arc rather than the mysterious yet friendly stranger that you kept encountering in the first installment.
Hotline Miami 2 is set out to be a bigger and bolder installment. The game basically retains the mechanics of the first game; building up combos and completing levels as quickly as possible (time is a factor in your final score), while introducing new design choices. Large and open levels make an appearance regularly and the majority of scenes are divided into multiple sub-levels. I feel that the larger levels are at odds with the score attacking nature of the gameplay. I had difficulties determining enemy placement due to the limited view (the Look function rarely helped me) and as a result I died a lot due to being shot by enemies that were off-screen. It is as if the game advocates a careful and methodic play style, while it taunts you for not completing levels in a timely manner with a sufficiently high combo. What makes matters worse are the bugs and inconsistencies in the game. The overall enemy behaviour seems erratic, sometimes they will behave as if they have eyes in their back, other times they completely ignore your presence. Enemies will get stuck in some of the objects in the level and once they are in this state, they can’t be lured out using gunshots. The door slamming mechanic seems utterly unreliable, enemies will clip through doors, causing them to remain standing when they should have been knocked down. Sometimes they will knock themselves out upon entering a room without any player interference. Additionally the behaviour of enemies with pouncing attacks seem to be bugged. Whenever I stood near a door while an enemy was entering the room, they would leap through the door and kill you without having fully entered the room. The gameplay is in a few instances hampered by unresponsiveness, this issue is mostly prominent when playing as Beard. I am specifically referring to when swapping between melee and long-ranged weapons, it either takes ages to change weapons or several button presses. This was not alleviated by rebinding the swap action to another key. Picking up weapons is still as cumbersome as in Hotline Miami 1, combine this with the fact that certain enemies require specific weapons in order to tackle them and you’ve got a recipe for cheap deaths. Again, I would not expect such issues in a game with a score attack aspect to it.
Playing on Hard Mode cheapened my experience even further. Hard Mode alters the game in the following ways, levels are flipped around with some minor changes to the layout, doors are in some instances removed, while windows are added. There's less ammunition in guns, swapping weapons will also remove ammunition and additional enemies are sprinkled on top. Enemies equipped with guns lock on to you instantly making it even more difficult to lure them out of rooms. Combine that with the bugs and other shortcomings mentioned earlier and it is bound to end in what ultimately feels like a frustrating experience.
Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number feels great when it actually adopts the design of the original, some of the last scenes hit the right notes. Speaking of notes, the soundtrack is superb, I did not expect it to exceed its predecessor. The presentation is absolutely stellar, the pixel art effortlessly convey emotion. The visual feedback that is given to you upon successfully stringing together kills after kills got my adrenaline pumping.
Thanks for those of you who took the time to read my impressions, I hope that I didn’t waste your time, I am well aware of the fact that I am echoing a lot of Errant Signal’s criticism.

They say that repetive action is a sign of insanity.  This game has lots of that.  Repetitive action or insanity, you say?  Yes!  OK, so, this being a very, very obvious console game, I'll cover the elephants in the room up front.  Silly camera tricks?  Only once or twice...not enough to even notice.  Silly save game tricks?  Oh, yes, yes indeed!  They're all about it.  It really detracts from the functionality, in fact.  Other than that, it plays much like a clunky version of Dead Space.  In fact, while I generally, moderately enjoyed this game, nothing in it is original.  It's as though they took every console trope and nailed them together into a giant bloody ball of game organs.  The characters are neither interesting nor sympathetic.  The plot is tired and predictable, and the game is basically on a themepark rail for much of the time.  And, then, there are some genuinely enjoyable parts, such as when you get to decide what fun toys to use to get past enemies or avoid them altogether.  There are parts of this game where you are required to run and parts where you are required to fight.  It would have been much, much better if you could complete each section by doing either.  That would have provided some depth and originality.  Would have.  The combat system has potential too, in it's kind of slow awkwardness, and this would provide a genuinely special experience, but that totally goes downhill as well.  The mood, graphics, and sound are all technically very good while being ultimately uninspired.  But, in the end, it just lacks the creative genius that would really push it over the edge.  It has some cool sequences, but they feel shallow, and the action detracts from the overall feel of the game.  This is, ultimtely, a neither particularly good nor particularly terrible game.  I'm recommending it, but just barely.  There are definitely parts that will make you feel crazy - that's for sure.

This game makes me shriek like a girl... oh, wait....

Shortly:
Basically, the game is the type of game that the Resident Evil franchise failed to be; survival-horror 3rd person shooter thats actually scary. The reason why I'm involving RE while saying that is because this game was directed by Shinji Mikami, the person who created the original Resident Evil games.
Mechanically, The Evil Within is very similar to Resident Evil 6. Many of the gameplay elements are the same, such as meleeing and shooting. But TEW goes further than that by introdusing sneaking and few other mechanics, such killing your enemies with objects found from the game world. The game also has character development system, meaning that as you kill enemies or world objects such as barrels, you'll occasionally find skill points (skill goo more likely), and whenever you visit a save room, you can spend those points to enhance a field of expertice of your choosing, enhancing yourself with more health points, stamina or even better weapon handling. But you'll have to choose carefully, because you'll only obtain limited number of those points, so you can be jack-of-all-trades but not master of any.
Like I sayed, the game actually has save rooms, which does what you'd expect it to do; save your progress. But its sad though, because the game also has autosave feature, that makes the save room kinda useless. I'd have preferred the game without the autosave, because with autosaves there's no penalty whenever you die and it kinda dulls the horror feeling for me.
Luckily, this game doesn't have any co-op features like the RE games have. The co-op only ruined the RE games for me, because whenever you made a mistake, your parter was always there to back you up, making the games painfully easy. The Evil Within doesn't have this feature, and I'm happy for it.
As I mentioned, unlike in the RE games, TEW has sneaking option, which allows you to...well, sneak around and insta-kill your enemies with your knife. This is actually nice addition to this type of game, because unlike in RE games, the ammonition you find for your weapons are really scarse to find and you really want to save the ammo for the boss fights, especially if you play on the higher difficulties.
The horror element in this game is real. The monsters are refreshing and the enviorements enhances the fear the enemies gives you (though some of the enviorements are quite dull, especially the day time enviorements).
Graphically the game is decent, the sounds in this game are terrifying and the music fits in place like a dream. The voice acting however could have been a little bit better, but they were doreable.
The story in this game is actually good. Its little confusing during the 1st half of the game, because nothing really makes sense. But as you go on and if you keep reading every note and background stories you can find, you'll shortly connect the pieces and catch on what's happening.
As what comes for the content, it takes roughly about 12-18 hours to complete the game, depending on your own playstyle of course. For me it took about 16-17 hours ( my playtime counter shows only 15.5 hours when I'm writing this, because for some reason Steam didn't record my playtime and achievements at one point when I had internet stability issues ), and I tried to be as much stealthy as possible and I tried to search every nook and cranny for notes and collectables.
Pros:
+ Survival-horror  ( proves that survival-horror genre has not been ruined yet by the Corporate Commander )
+ Story
+ Doesn't let you take a break
+ Gameplay mechanics
+ Money's worth of content
+ No noteable bugs, but...
Cons:
- ...It has performance issues and the framerate drops even with high end PCs
- Autosave  ( I personally think that autosave feature ruins the horror games, because there's no real penalty in dying )
- Letterbox effect, but luckilly you can disable that
- DLCs have story  ( corporate commander strikes again, but these days its kinda standard for games to have DLCs, which is sad )
- While the overall horror is good, its not always horrifying. Especially the day time areas are simply not scary and they remind too much of the RE franchise
Do I recommend?
If you're a friend of Resident Evil games, but are disappointed for how those games lacks the horror, then definitely yes. We definitely need more games like this, and I even think that the Resident Evil franchise could learn a few things from this game.
Verdict: 7 / 10 - Good game (had to drop the rating down from 9/10, because the game is poorly optimized for PC)
( 1 = do-not-bother game
5 = average game
10 = Must own game )

is a pretty simple, but addicting game. You play as a small ship on a flat board that must fend of waves of different geometric enemies. There are about half a dozen or so different shapes, and each shape behaves in a different manner. Some enemies will sit in place on the map, others move about aimlessly, and some chase after you.
Before I talk about the gameplay, I just want to note that this game is nigh unplayable without a controller. When I refer to the controls in this review, it will be in reference to when using an actual controller.
That said, the controls are very simple as well. You use one joystick to move about the map, and the other to shoot in any direction, hence why it’s a twin stick shooter. You can also use one of the shoulder buttons to activate a bomb, which will wipe out all enemies on the map. You begin the game with 3 bombs and 3 lives, though you can acquire more by scoring points, which is done simply by killing enemies.
The aim of the game is simply to rack up as high of a score as you can before you bite the dust for the final time. A game won’t last very long, only a few minutes, but you’ll get enough reply out of it to get at least an hour’s worth of gameplay out of it.
It’s a fun game, but you’re better off just buying
, since it includes the content of this game a lot more. Still, it’s only a few bucks if you’re like me and insist on getting it anyway.

Ah, Niche. This is an odd one - I've got a bit of a love/hate relationship with this game, but ultimately I keep coming back to it. Why? Well, to explain that, I've gotta tell you a little story.
It starts out innocent enough. You've got your little fledgling tribe living happily on a paradise island: plenty of food, minimal predators, temperate climate. You could keep your tribe there forever and never have a problem.
But the young ones start getting restless. They see other islands on the horizon, and are itching to explore them.
So a few of them just set off one day. They end up somewhere new, with new dangers and new challenges. Odds are, they're not prepared for it. Food supplies run low. The predators close in. Some of your tribe die, and the others are weak and desperate.
There's food on this island, but it's hard to get; the plants poison you or injure you, and the prey fights back.
The old pack members make a sacrifice to preserve the young. They take a one-way journey to hunt or gather, and the rest of your pack survives with a few less mouths to feed.
It becomes a tradition. Once they're old and weak, they go off to find food and die in the process.
Then the imperfect and ugly offspring, those not fit to breed, are subjected to the same fate. It's all for the good of the pack, after all.
It's a ritual. It's an honour.
And just like that, your innocent little pack has turned into a clan of ruthless death cultists... and you never even saw it happening until it was too late.
So, yes, the criticisms of this game are valid. If you play it just as a strategy game, after a while it starts to feel directionless, unrewarding and ultimately pointless. There's no solid goal or checklist to tick off. Survival is easy enough for the most part and there's no real motive to explore except for an additional challenge, but that's circular logic. You want to survive, so you move to a harder island? Eh... what?
But the fun starts when - instead of seeing it as a strategy game with you moving a few dumb pawns around to accomplish... well, nothing much - you start seeing it as a story. Because that's the strength of this game, and it's a damn strong one.
Conclusion, then: if you're just in it for the strategy, give this a pass for now. But if you're in it for the animals, or the genetics, or the stories your pack will tell you, then buy this game. I guarantee you won't regret it.

After playing the first Nazi Zombie Army title, I was left dissatisfied with the game and decided to give the second one a chance. Released within the same year as the first one, will this be the game you want to play ?
Story wise this game picks up as soon as the first one ends. We are dropped of by the boat on a dockside and we have a goal, we need to collect three relics which can stop the zombie apocalypse. Just like the first one it's not much of a story, cause apart from the recordings you hear in safe rooms and the pre-mission briefings, there's not much exposition.
Now for record, I'm not a massive fan of Sniper Elite apart from Sniper Elite 2 which I fairly enjoyed.  Gameplay is a carbon copy of the first one and Sniper Elite 2. Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army 2 feels like a mod rather than a full game. Everything from the menu and mission goals are borrowed from the first game. I felt like this was a cheap money grab than a full sequel.
Soundtrack is the game's strongest feature. I love the synth music and it reminded me of the awesome horror movies that came out in the 80's.

The game is even shorter than the first game. It took me 3 hours to finish the entire game and unless you plan on doing a second playthrough, it's not worth getting at full price.
Overall this is a poor sequel and more like a cash grab. My honest suggestion is either get the two games on sale or get  the trilogy which is includes the first two remastered games which I hear are great. Overall Nazi Zombie Army 2 is a bad game and I don't suggest wasting money on it.

4/10 - Wait for a discount or skip

Heroes and Generals is a fairly fun first person shooter with good pacing for a world war 2 themed game. It requires players to move cautiously and isn't prone to a lot of the twitch/sprint gameplay of other more conventional first person shooters. While the game is solid for the most part, I feel that it still has a long way to go before it will truly realize it's potential. For instance, before players can get into the meat of the game, they have to grind through repetetive "staged battles" in order to get up to level 5 which is the requirement to join the grand scale war. This would be fine if it didn't feel so much like a chore than actual game time. Though you can buy your way around this with the purchase of an academy trained soldier, it still sucks for players who aren't interested in making monetary investments into the game just yet. Overall I'd say the game is worth it if your looking for a free to play fps with a fun and interesting mechanic to it, but I wish the game wouldn't hold players back from the real meat of the content for such a long period of time.

This game has a good foundation that could be something great, but is terribly executed.
It is perhaps one of the grindiest games to have ever been created. There's a double-dip grind that players are forced to endure if they want to see ANY semblance of variety or nuance in their gameplay. First, players have to grind experience to unlock ranks which grant access to different roles, weapons, vehicles, and gear. This grind makes a snail's pace look blazing fast by comparison. So, a new player will basically be stuck with the same bottom tier weapons, in the same role, with the same bottom tier gear, for a very, very long time.
On top of that, there is the ribbon system grind that consists of weapon/gear-specific grinding--the more you use a particular weapon, for instance, the more experience you will get for that weapon's respective ribbon. This applies to every weapon, and every vehicle. This is how you unlock mods for that weapon/vehicle. This grind isn't the worst on its own, but it does still contribute to the overall barrier to entry.
Next, there's the credit grind. Your credit earnings scale with your rank; the higher your rank, the more credits you get per match. Everything costs credits--weapons, mods, vehicles, grenades, gear, promotions, new soldiers, etc. And it's all very, very expensive relative to your earnings. What's more, all your gear, including your weapon mods, incurs repair costs for even the smallest of uses, and ammo needs to be replenished constantly. This means your already pathetic credit earnings are going to be even less rewarding the more you actually participate in a given match. A game that penalizes you for playing--novel idea. And there's no meaningful way to earn credit bonuses for playing well--like, if you get a crap-ton of kills and minimal deaths in a match, it doesn't matter. In fact, all that means is you used your weapon a lot, and expended a lot of ammo, so it probably ended up costing you more in the long run.
All of this combined produces a slow, tedious, monotonous, unrewarding, unsatisfying experience to say the very least. Meanwhile, you'll be enduring all of this on the same handful of rather poorly designed maps (they don't even have spawn-camp-protection integrated into the map design, and you will be spawn camped fairly often), with virtually no variety in the gameplay. You'll be put into regularly imbalanced teams where one side has more players than the other, which means the matches tend to be incredibly one-sided, and over befoer you have a chance to do much of anything. You'll be against players that have access to more and better gear options because they've payed for them, and/or have been playing much longer. It's simply not fun 9 matches out of 10, and what fun there is in that 10th match isn't even that great.
In addition the graphical fidelity is poor--the game looks dated, and the aesthetic quality is severely lacking--everything is faded, dull, drab, grey, unimpressive at best and a strain on the eyes at worst.
The sound quality also sucks quite a bit. The only half-decent sound effect in the game is the character's whistle. Guns sound nothing like guns. Explosions sound distorted and muffled. Vehicles sound like lawnmowers inside of tin cans. It's simply all bad.
The game also doesn't handle or feel very good. Jumping feels as though you're jumping on the moon. You can only sprint for about 2 seconds before you inexplicably run out of breath. Getting stuck on hidden collision geometry is common. Vehicle handling is♥♥♥♥♥♥poor. Firing on a moving target is an exercise in frustration because of the way hit detection works. You can literally have someone standing right in front of you, shoot them point blank and inexplicably miss because they were strafing to the side, and the netcode sucks. Also, if you and the enemy shoot each other at the same time, your shot will often never go off or be recognized by the game.
And the list just keeps going, and going.
In summation, overall this game is garbage, and over the months it hasn't shown any signs of improving in any substantial way.

I bought the main game a few months ago, in autumn 2015. Several horror games had been released at that time and having previously finished Alien Isolation, I thought I'd give it a go. At that time, I didn't know anything about the partly negative reviews and simply played the game for the game's sake. Being an experienced gamer and too smug, I picked a hard difficulty and almost wanted to give up because the first level was too hard. As a matter of fact, this game is hard, really hard. If you've played Dark Souls, you're used to dying over and over again, but in the Evil Within, you also don't have the ammunition you need. Add a lot of blood and gore and the basic survival instincts evoked by the creepy music and atmosphere, you get an atmospheric game unlike many others. Hence, if you are looking for the basic horror thrill that'll make you cringe and unable to look at the screen because that mass murderer's waiting for you, you'll be disappointed with this purchase. I cannot state how important that is but this game is classified as psychological horror and will thus also make you experience the feeling of threat, not fear.
You have the option to choose between 3 difficulties, and once you've finished the game, you'll additionally unlock another option. Similar to Resident Evil, ammo drops are rare in the Evil Within and you WILL need to save ammo at certain points. The game has about 14 chapters, which are usually 1-2 hours; beating the entire game took me about 17 hours (with achievements). You also have the option to purchase the DLC (Season Pass advised), which adds another 5-6 hours play time. Several guns are available, as well as advanced weapons, which will ensure your survival at some points. Generally speaking, staying hidden is your best bet at survival, but don't take it for granted. Some enemies will spot you no matter what, and give you a heartattack when they ambush you. Once you hear the famous piece of music Clair De Lune, you'll also know when it's time to save your game and upgrade your skills and weapons with items you'll likely pick up during the main campagne. But be advised that spotting certain items can be a difficult task in itself, since you'll be required to use ammo. Be prepared to compromise, and planning can save your butt ;-)
- In the main game, you play as Sebastian, a police officer who ends up right in the middle of a creepy case. Fighting your way through a hospital, a forest and village, and past hordes of enemies, you soon realize that something is off. The enemies are supernatural zombies, and you are getting chased by an unnatural force. Digging into the background information, you will realize that nothing is as it seems and this world is trying to reject you like an unwanted organ. Somebody has been following you and he is very angry, ready to rip you apart.
- In the DLC, you play as officer Kidman who presents her part of the story, with a different approach to fighting and stealth. Hey, man, you're a lady, you can't shoot that.
Jokes aside, I'm seriously in love with the story. I don't want to spoil too much, but you will get mind♥♥♥♥ed. The story is not linear and is really complex considering the game's overall set up. You will need to pay attention to the details and read as many of the collectibles in the game as possible since they are all part of the main plot. Playing the DLC is essential in my opinion since it explains why the events happened the way they happened. I've read a lot of negative reviews about the story, how it does not make sense, but just like Bioshock Infinite, this game leaves room for interpretation, and you'll need to make up your own mind. Nevertheless, the Evil Within combines survival horror with natural sciences and the human mind. It is an excellent approach to new research and challenges the player with ethical questions. I seriously love the main anatgonist, and he's the best developed character in my opinion, whereas Sebastian is more or less the standard troubled hero on his mission for revenge.
- long main campaign
- predictable character development (main character)
- will seem repetitive after dying again
- upgrading system expensive and will trick you into buying things you don't need
- some enemies are ridiculously OP
- scarce ammo
- no advanced AI (enemies follow a path, or you)
+ game+ mode which allows you to use your upgrades again, on a higher difficulty
+ 1 hit mode which is even more challenging
+ complicated story with a lot of attention to detail
+ best developed antagonist I've seen in a long while
+ blood and gore (and a lot!)
+ achievements are a real challenge (you'll hate yourself!)
+ aiming is hard
+ stripped to basic survival instincts (stealth, low stamina, HP, etc)
+ great graphics + atmopshere (greetings to my fellow games which I cannot play due to my old Nvidia)
+ creepy music and the feeling of threat - ever run for your life? this is what it feels like
+ several types of enemies, new ones in each chapter
If you're into Slenderman style horror and love being unable to look at your screen, this is the wrong game for you. The plot is challenging, the game is frustrating and some enemies are unnaturally strong. However, if you like psychological horror and aren't afraid to look at brains (you'll meet a lot, hello!), this may be the right game for you. Get the DLC on sale and take your time to actually play the game, you'll get rewarded. In for a challenge? In for a chainsaw wielding maniac? In for that sexy antagonist who won't be so sexy anymore once he's undressed? You might as well play this game.
Still my personal favourite game 2015.

Just a brief foreword: this is not a bad game, don't let the red thumb dissuade you from getting this game if it intrigues you.  It's merely a game I don't believe is worth playing, but that doesn't make it bad, that makes it passable and a non-priority. With that out of the way:
The Evil Within is a mish-mash of environments strung together with an empty plot that goes nowhere for half the game. You start out in a hospital, escape it to see the world ending, crash and wind up in Resident Evil 4, wake up and wind up in a castle, fall and get up in a factory, etc etc etc. It's constant changes of environments strung together by a plot that rationalizes it all by saying you are in someone's mind gathering memories from various people due to an experiment.
In the beginning it's played with fairly well, as the changes in environments seem to be fairly sensical and rationally follow through. But around chapter 4 or 5 they threw it all out the window and throw you onto a large cliff with a castle in the distance and your partner who's been missing for ages in the middle of a field. It's pretty sad, since initially it made me question what was ''real'' and what wasn't, but a little before the mid-way point it's painfully obvious that it's all just mental fu*kery, so there goes the intrigue. Not helping the scenario are the characters that don't seem to care that they keep teleporting from environment to environment. First thing they say when they wake up in a completely new area? ''We gotta get outta here''. Realistic. You would THINK maybe they might ASK what the hell is going on or how they wound up where they are; whether they have memories of previous environments or not. Nope. We gotta get outta here.
The environments themselves start out promising and aid the stealth gameplay. Initially you're in a wooded area that is fairly big and truly feels like an area you can get lost in. You sneak by villagers and get an RE4 feeling for the thing, except more stealth involved and large environments to sneak around in. But that's only 20% of the game; the larger environments are eventually thrown out for enclosed buildings, which is to the detriment of the stealth element. Most of the time the enemies see you first, or they're in corridors that you can't sneak by because it's an effin corridor. Or they're in a room with nowhere to hide anyway, so you can crouch and not be seen, but they'll be blocking the way so eff it you pull out your gun and shoot since there's no way to get closer for a stealth kill.
Environments aside, the gunplay is...ehh. By default you can hold a total of 12 handgun bullets, and 8 or so shotgun rounds. That's VERY little, and I assume it was the case to add tension to ammunition management and to shy away from an action-oriented horror game. That's fine in the beginning, since you can realistically stealth through villages and set up silent kills. But later environments are strictly gunplay (or running away) and you'll be backtracking for ammunition you couldn't pick up earlier because you were full. Thankfully you can upgrade your carrying capacity, but it still costs a decent amount to acquire them, but by the time you have such upgrades you'll be around midway done with the game. Around that point the game is 'building tension', which means fewer enemies since it's harder to scare someone with a zombie when 200 of them are constantly on-screen. What that means is fewer enemies and a lot of creaking and background laughter. You'll ocassionally get assaulted by 4 or so zombies (or midbosses), but generally you'll have more ammo midway onwards due to ''tension''.
An issue with a specific weapon is the hanfgun, and it shows a general issue with combat in this title. RE4 had the handguns retain their usefulness by letting you stagger enemies, which would segueway into a cinematic melee attack that lasted 2 seconds and did good damage. This allowed you to conserve ammo; this game's version of the melee attack are matches. If an enemy falls to the floor you can quickly run up to them and light their body aflame for an immediate kill. The problem is that the handgun takes around 4 or 5 shots to stagger enemies and have them fall to their knees. And wasting a match on an enemy that only needs 2 or so more bullets to die is a waste. Headshots with the handgun are also useless, as you need to update it SIGNIFICANTLY to get a 50%+ chance of headshot kills finishing off enemies. In other words, the handgun is useless until you upgrade it significantly. If you enjoyed P.T. you owe it to yourself to play this. Some seriously excellent environmental horror mindf*ckery.

Take P.T., Eraserhead, Picture of Dorian Gray, Jan Svankmajer (google him), and an art history textbook. Put them in a blender with a heavy dose of optical illusions and shadows. Garnish with a paprika of some pretty good jump-scares. That's this game.  A 3 hour victorian themed take on 'what if P.T. were a full game.' I mean that in a good way because this is a very obviously lovingly crafted experience built around gameplay ideas in the infamous P.T./Silent Hills demo.
Pros:
-Amazing visuals, including some really cool optical illusion stuff.
-Gloriously dreadful atmosphere.
-Very nice sound design (play with surround sound headphones if you can - the bass is a big deal at some parts)
-Some genuine jump-scares that got my adrenaline pumping against my will.
-Amazing payoff at the ending with some really cool animation.
-Didn't experience any bugs except an extremely minor one after the ending just before the credit rolls. (A cabinet suddenly teleported closed while I had my head wedged looking in it.)
-The first time I've ever been unnerved by receiving an achievement.  (You will know which one I am talking about when you get it.)
Cons:
-Much of the writing in the backstory items and dialogue is unconvincing and doesn't sound authentically period at all. For a game with so much attention to detail, this stood out as disappointing for me.
-Some puzzles grind the game to a halt for a bit, leaving you doing some boring pixel-hunting for numbers you might have overlooked, and repeating a particular part as you do.
-Some cheap eye-rolling unscary scares.
-Lapses into cliche in its story quite a lot. I also feel like a much meatier story could have elevated this game more.
-Only 3 hours long. It's a good and memorable 3 hours, but for $20 some people may want to wait till a sale. I got it because it has subject matter up my alley (art history nerd) so you may want to get it for the same reasons I did tho.
Overall: 4/5 - I want to see this studio make more games like this (or other genres of fiction than horror for a narrative game if they're keen for it) and get better at making them.

One of my favorite free to play titles!
Do you enjoy class based shooters like Team Fortress 2 or Tribes Ascend?
Do you enjoy MOBAs such as DOTA 2 or Smite etc?
If you you said yes to either or both of those questions you owe it to yourself to give this game a shot.
Right when you start they have an optional tutorial level where you can test out hero abilities, learn about the different AI controlled enemies (called creeps usually, bots in this case), and get a feel for the environmental weapons and events to help ease you into this hybrid style of game. Naturally a veteran of any of the previously mentioned games will want to skip over this, but you can leave the tutorial from the menu anytime so I recommend checking it out at least for the environment attacks.
There is also a co-op horde mode which can be used for increased training before the real deal or as an alternative to regular matchmaking should you find high wait times* or have a more PvE minded team. It lacks the strategy of defending towers or spawning creeps, but is a good way to practice shooting, coordinating team abilities, or having absent minded fun.
*Wait times are currently ridiculous in the 5v5 modes due to low player count
Super Crossfire is the name of the game's main entree. You only have two lanes and one jungle so team fights happen often and are never far away from you. One lane usually has 2 people and the other has 3, causing one of the lanes to be constantly pushed and therefore in need of defending. Alternatively you can have a fifth man roam between the lanes seeking the enemy roamer or hiding for surprise attacks. In the middle of all the fighting and pushing, events are constantly occurring in the jungle like a free money spawning "enemy", a Roshan like boss that gives a buff on defeat, a creep wiping laser and more. This gives the game a perpetual feeling of motion and speed never allowing boredom.
There is another game mode which takes the premise of Super Crossfire and makes it more shooter-esque. Damage is increased, speed is increased, turret shields do NOT come back, health regen changes from DOTA-like to Halo-like, and other changes to creeps and players. This mode is great if you want a faster match or are less fond of the strategy layer.
In Short:
PROS
+ Great Hero Variety
+ Multiple Maps
+ Multiple Modes
+ Map Events
+ Perfect Balance of Action and Strategy
+ Excellent Humor with Top-Notch Voice Acting
+ Amazing Art Style and Graphics
CONS
- Long Matchmaking/No playerbase - game abandoned by devs. (The developers would like to revive it though)
- What's left of the players are the most toxic of the community
- No new content planned (heroes, maps, etc.) again due to abandonment
- Matchmaking isn't separated by skill so new players can get destroyed by long time players
If you can get 4 friends to try it with you a great game is waiting to be discovered even if you stick to the horde mode. If you can find 9 friends you've eliminated virtually all of the cons to this game.

In its current status, it's a nice physics sandbox to enjoy with a friend or two and one of the only physics sandbox games I know of that has simultaneous multiplayer.
If there's anything negative to be said about the game at all, it's the actual physics of the game. They're accurate enough most of the time, but there are several unresolved glitches that will remain unresolved because the tiny-but-vocal fanbase of the game couldn't stand to live without them. If you don't mind playing around a broken physics engine that will literally never be fixed, this is the game for you.
The Steam Workshop is also available if you just want to share creations with others, but being able to play with the same things at the same time or even build things together is a huge bonus for this game.
That all being said, the game is fairly limited in what you can actually do within it. While the "controller" item in-game does provide a degree of fine-tuning, you're not going to find the kind of elaborate creations you would in a game like Besiege. Multiple bearings, i.e. moving parts, on any creation builds up lag very quickly even on good computers and in a world with multiple players and creations it can become very frustrating.

It feels like this game was made specifically for me. I grew up playing Petz (the PC ones, not the crappy 3ds version that came out later) and was part of the vibrant online community for the breeding, showing, and modding scene. I loved a horse racing game I had on the PS2 because of the breeding mechanics. Modern games have largely left breeding that even pretended to resemble to real life genetics behind. So, for years, I've been keeping an eye out for some type of pet/horse/whatever simulator that goes more in depth.
And BOY, does Niche go in-depth! -At least comparatively. There isn't dominant epistasis or redundancy or really any dihybrid gene interactions as far as I can tell, but it does have the basic mendelian genetics of dominance/recessive, incomplete dominance, and codominance thing going on which is more than I could ask for.
The only drawback for me is that I'll have to get used to your favorites dying D:. There isn't really a set goal besides survival and unlocking all the genes. Some type of story mode that forces more objectives on the player might be helpful, but I enjoy the simulation nature as-is. That is not to say this game isn't challenging, but it something like a sim-city game or a civ game.

I reccomend this game, but I bought it on sale so I reccomend it within that context.
This game is a diamond in the rough. I bought this game because I love L4D and I love Warhammer and this game delivers both splendidly. Every character and build has it's uses within the team, there is a variety of playstyles, loot, and upgrades to accomodate every taste, and the voiceover is outstanding; creating dynamic relationships between the characters. I had some friends who had this game so I was able to play with more or less a competent team and that's (obviously) when this game shines. The problem is not many people play, so finding a full team when I'm able to play is harder and harder the farther away from the sale I get.
Which higlights what I percieve to be the biggest flaw in this game; easily fixed design choices. I don't want new levels or modes with the same characters. I want the same levels with new characters, new loot, new trinkets, and new headwear. The devs have allocated post-release resources on expanding things that are less interesting than making a character feel like your own, which is at the heart of the Warhammer experience. The setting is perfect to have races and classes working together that would normally kill eachother on sight. Instead of making vampire-themed levels add a vampire character. Saltzpyre the Witchunter: Bane of Necromancers would have to just deal with it because of the mutual enemy everywhere (which they touch upon with him and the bright wizard). A vampire playstyle/customizable character aesthetic would drawn in more players as a paid DLC, and that's one example of many that could be used from WH's rich lore.
I also think the way loot is dispensed should be tweaked. The crafting system requires you to break down weapons for same rarity-graded chunklets to spend on honing in the perfect weapon, but the game gives you weapons in a trickle that feels stifling. As a player you should be rewarded for losing a 45-minute slug-match that went to♥♥♥♥♥♥with at least a scrap weapon to break down, or a Ranald's Bones with less die. Instead you get an XP conciliatory pat on the back and a nagging feeling you're wasting your time. It feels like the developers didn't want players breaking the game on the second week and went too far in preventing that, so I as a player feel it's more worth my time to try and farm Smuggler's Run on Hard(with bots)/Nightmare(if I happen upon players) over and over for loot in an empty game rather than enjoy the story and atmosphere and ambiently get geared over time.
If you have a crew to roll deep with this game is so much fun, otherwise you might be endlessly frusterated tryng to beat a mission on hard with bots who love dying alone.

In all honesty, if you can get past the bugs, crashes, errors, and terrible actual players then this game is absolutely amazing. All the different missions, the character interactions, the rng, and the loot you can get makes the game worth the trouble of getting it started.

First off I want to point out this game IS free and it IS in beta so many things will be cganged and improved. Now that's said, heres my review:
After playing this game almost non stop for about a week, i have to say its not the worst but its not the best either. It is free which is a plus but it also in some concepts is p2w. THIS GAME IS NOT FRIENDLY TO NOOBS! I cant say that enough. YOU WILL DIE A LOT. This game rewards patience, strategy, and teamwork. If you dont play with at least 2 out of the 3 then you're not going to have a good time. PLAY THE OBJECTIVE.
There are 3 factions; Germany, Soviets, USA. You pick one at the start and you givin a level 0 infrantryman. The starter weapons on all factions are pretty much the same weapon but with a different skin. allthough the m1 grande for the US trumps the other two by a small margin. You will be using these starter weapons for quite a bit if you aren't willing to pay to unlock the others. Which is where p2w comes into play..and where a lot of people seem to be turned away from this game. In order to unlock the next or better weapon you will have to grind for hours before finally making enough to purchase them or you can simply purchase them and unlock them instantly. At the start if you're a decent player you will earn roughly 3k credits a match, if you play the objective. The better weapons cost from 100-300k credits, so that gives you an idea of the grinding aspect. This personally i dont mind because its like getting a big paycheck after a long week of work, you feel like u've earned it. And trust me does it pay off... once you get that better weapon you will see a dramatic increase in your performance. This is where you start to have a ton of fun.
There are two gamemodes Skirmish, which is domination from cod, and assualt, which is a pretty original gamemode where you have to attack or defend 2 or 3 main capture points (CP). There are also 2-3 sub-lines of CP that the attackers need to get through in order to get the main CP. You are forced to play skirmish until you reach level 5 which is a good thing because it lets you get a grip of the game. Skirmish has three maps that are very balanced and fun to play. Assualt has 5 maps that can be hard to understand at first and require much more "patience, strategy, and teamwork" as i stated above. I'd advise not to start playing assualt until you're aquipped with a better weapon. Plus skirmish deals out more credits, faster.
Overall I really enjoy playing the game. Its a new take on fps, as it plays like no other. The game can be pretty frustrating at first especially if you try to force you way through the battlefield to get to an objective. You must be very cautious and aware at all times, taking your time to get to the CP. If you take the time to fully give this game a chance and understand how to win/play i'm sure you wont think the time was wasted and you'll likely have a ton of fun. Allthough the game might not be for everyone but is surely worth the try, as it is f2p.
PS: DON'T JUDGE THE GAME OR POST A REVIEW UNTILL YOU'VE PUT THE HOURS IN!

Remember all the Dating Sims on Newgrounds from back in the day? Turns out they were all missing one critical component: Bejeweled. In HuniePop, simply talking to the girls and showering them with gifts is not enough to win their affection. This 'gameplay first' approach, as the developer calls it, breathes new life into a genre that isn't even really a genre outside of mostly mediocre flash games.
A magical love fairy puts her skills to the test as she tries to turn a lonely loser into a literal sex god - this is more or less the entire plot of the game. There is some 'lore' hidden in various dialogues but the game focuses more on character interaction than story, which works fine. You talk to girls, learn about their lives, present them with gifts and ultimately win her over (or not) by matching orbs of the same color. It may very well sound like a dull experience but many people, me included, were positively surprised by the amount of time that flies by when playing HuniePop. Passive skills, usable items and orbs with varying effects keep the gameplay interesting. While the lack of a story might cause some people to lose interest, I think it's fair to say that this game still has enormous waifu potential - maybe even more so, since the Bejeweled sections can be quite hard at times, so it's all the more rewarding to 'level up' with a girl. Suffice it to say, there should be a Huniefu for everyone in this game. If you've been hitting on a girl for quite some time, she may come home with you but don't lose focus just yet, because the true challenge awaits you in the bedroom - SANIC Bejeweled stands between you and the final (lewd) CG graphic, so hang in there.
Overall this game has everything, simple but effective gameplay, waifus, nice CG graphics and cute voice acting. HuniePop is quite possibly the game many people have been unknowingly waiting for, a Dating Sim that's actually fun to play. The developer is also preparing a Valentine's update for free, so there is at least some additional content coming our way. If you'd like to experience what it's like to win over waifus via puzzle games: definitely give HuniePop a try. Also Aiko a best.

Backslash is a standout competetive local multiplayer release.
The clan system allows you to mix any two classes, or stick with a single class. This gives you a total of 55 different playstyles, and depending on the order you select your clan, 95 different character appearances.
Each class has a passive and 4 skills. Rather than being key-bound skills go into a skill deck and once your mana is full, one randomly becomes available. This means you can choose to select a single class to narrow down your skill deck, but forgo a second passive.
The combat itself is good. Mana generates slowly at first (and the rate seems to be different for different clans) but will generate faster in combat, and passively regenerate faster the longer the match continues. This manages the pace of matches excellently.
The lack of control over which skills you get when also works surprisingly well. One would expect this to reduce your capacity to strategise, but this is not the case. Not only are you forced to adapt to the skill that becomes available, but you are also left with the choice of waiting to trigger it at the perfect time or triggering it at a sub-optimal time and hoping for the best in order to begin the charge up of the next skill.
Balancing is quite good. Due to the single skill at any given time mechanic, syneries between two clans are limited. This means that instead of 55 permeations requiring specific balancing, there is only really 10. As is the case with every game with different classes, the balancing is not perfect, but as of yet I have not encountered any significant balancing issues.
The biggest drawback this game currently has is the two player limit. This is a shame, as it appears perfect for 4 players. Hopefully this is a feature the developers will add in the future.

This game is really fun and unique. Lots of variety with ten different classes (called "clans" in the game) that you can choose two of each fight, giving you eight special abilities (four from each class) that are randomly picked from each time you charge up by beating down your opponent with melee attacks. You can also pick two of the same class if you just want to use abilities from just that class.
The controls are straight forward and intuitive, allowing you to dive right into the game and have fun. You move with the left stick or d-pad, then there is a button each for jump, attack, and using the ability that you "draw" after charging up all the way.
The variety of abilities are what makes this game so fun to play over and over. Even if you pick the same classes over and over, the abilities come out randomly each time, so you always have something new to deal with. The abilities themselves range from offensive, like summoning a sword that you use with your melee button, to attacks like beams that shoot out as soon as you press the ability button. There are also defensive abilities like shields that form around you, or a shield that appears in front of you and stays there until the opponent hits it or it goes away after a while. There are also traps, bombs, and things that orbit you and damage the opponent if they collide with them.
There's a few different modes, including a single player mission mode where you have different scenarios that you must fight through in order to get stars that then unlock more missions. There is also a single player survival mode where you play a series of duels and your life carries over from fight to fight. Then there is a versus mode where you can play against another player or the CPU. It's nice to see a game that takes single player content so seriously, and the AI is pretty challenging.
My only gripes would be the learning curve of getting to know and get good with all the different abilities, but it is an enjoyable process if you have the patience for it. Also, you only start with four of the classes and have to earn the rest, so it might get annoying have to play the same classes over and over as you unlock more.
Overall, this is a great first game from Skeleton Crew Studio that probably won't get near the attention that it deserves. I hope they do well with this game and make more.

This game is a diamond in the rough. I bought this game because I love L4D and I love Warhammer and this game delivers both splendidly. Every character and build has it's uses within the team, there is a variety of playstyles, loot, and upgrades to accomodate every taste, and the voiceover is outstanding; creating dynamic relationships between the characters. I had some friends who had this game so I was able to play with more or less a competent team and that's (obviously) when this game shines. The problem is not many people play, so finding a full team when I'm able to play is harder and harder the farther away from the sale I get.
Which higlights what I percieve to be the biggest flaw in this game; easily fixed design choices. I don't want new levels or modes with the same characters. I want the same levels with new characters, new loot, new trinkets, and new headwear. The devs have allocated post-release resources on expanding things that are less interesting than making a character feel like your own, which is at the heart of the Warhammer experience. The setting is perfect to have races and classes working together that would normally kill eachother on sight. Instead of making vampire-themed levels add a vampire character. Saltzpyre the Witchunter: Bane of Necromancers would have to just deal with it because of the mutual enemy everywhere (which they touch upon with him and the bright wizard). A vampire playstyle/customizable character aesthetic would drawn in more players as a paid DLC, and that's one example of many that could be used from WH's rich lore.
I also think the way loot is dispensed should be tweaked. The crafting system requires you to break down weapons for same rarity-graded chunklets to spend on honing in the perfect weapon, but the game gives you weapons in a trickle that feels stifling. As a player you should be rewarded for losing a 45-minute slug-match that went to♥♥♥♥♥♥with at least a scrap weapon to break down, or a Ranald's Bones with less die. Instead you get an XP conciliatory pat on the back and a nagging feeling you're wasting your time. It feels like the developers didn't want players breaking the game on the second week and went too far in preventing that, so I as a player feel it's more worth my time to try and farm Smuggler's Run on Hard(with bots)/Nightmare(if I happen upon players) over and over for loot in an empty game rather than enjoy the story and atmosphere and ambiently get geared over time.
If you have a crew to roll deep with this game is so much fun, otherwise you might be endlessly frusterated tryng to beat a mission on hard with bots who love dying alone.

In all honesty, if you can get past the bugs, crashes, errors, and terrible actual players then this game is absolutely amazing. All the different missions, the character interactions, the rng, and the loot you can get makes the game worth the trouble of getting it started.

If you’re like me ponder and like to go through a thousand reviews before buying (or not buying) a game, let me give you a short answer: Yes, this game is great fun and worth the money for sure.
Now the points which brought me to this conclusion after roughly 4 hours of gameplay.
+ people love to compare this game to left4dead in a good way and I mostly agree. But actually, I think this game adapts the concept much better than left4dead since using melee weapons work much better than in left4dead and is always a viable option even for the two more range-focused heroes.
+ which brings us to combat. Even though the combat system is simple (quick attack, strong attack and blocking, melee and ranged weapons) is simply a blast to use because it feels just “right”. The weapons feel powerful when literally slicing your attackers apart, smashing their skulls in, shooting holes in their chests or nailing them to the wall with bow and arrow (yep, it’s gory and bloody as heel and benefits the combat greatly). In the few hours I’ve played with all kind of weapons (greatsword, warhammer, rapier, bow, dual pistols and mage staff) and every single one has a distinct feeling to it. If you’ve played chivalry you’ll like this, even if it’s not as heavily implemented here as in that game.
+ about the atmosphere: Of course Warhammer fans like myself love it. But the friend of mine which I play the game likes the atmosphere and game style very much and he is much more interested in the “cleaner” fantasy worlds like lord of the Rings and usually has nothing to do with Warhammer at all.
+ as mentioned above I play this game with a friend (we were looking for a new game we could play together and decided to this game a try). As always playing with people you know is great fun, especially in game that puts a high premium on real cooperative gameplay like this one. Nevertheless, the other player in our team proofed to be good teamplayers as well so it seems that playing with strangers also yields good results and fun game sessions. Straying away too far from the group or speedruning ahead through the level doesn’t get you anywhere. I saw people complaining about this, but honestly, it’s a coop game so of course you have to work together witch other people and stay together.
+ I can’t say anything final about the loot system at this point, but see that this is usually the biggest critic with this game so I will address it. Personally I’m fine with the dicing loot system, but I have to say that I was never one for games chiefly for collecting better loot. I’ll be neutral on this one since it doesn’t bother but I can understand that maybe some people will not be entirely happy with that.
So, overall I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys games which value teamplay, wants to use weapons who feel what they look like, is fond of dark fantasy of any kind or just loves games which a high replay value because this surely feels like has a lot of it.

This Musashi will now review "HuniePop"
*clears throat*
Booting up the game, this Musashi was greeted with pleasant music, and a decent menu. UI itself isn't bad either
Starting the game was also quite pleasant, good visuals, nice voice acting, and, once again, lovely soundtrack.
The gameplay itself, it's kinda like Bejewled. There's a bunch of different tokens, each representing a certain thing. Goal's to match them preferably ones that tailor to the waifu's interest, and avoid the bad one. Simple. That alone was a seller for this Musashi, as I would play Bejewled alot, and get bored and think "Man...Bejewled is a nice passtime and all. Inbetween sessions you can chat it up with the girls to get "Hunie" which will allow you to upgrade yourself, to make certain matches grant more points, etc. You can also buy gifts and foods and such for said girls with "Munie" you get from playing the date sessions.
The selection of girls is pretty nice too. All fully voice acted (configurable if you're the type that wants them to shut up and get on with the.... *ahem*) You might just find a waifu for yourself.
Oh, you can be a girl too. That's an option, don't have to be male if you don't want to. Doesn't change much, just dialogue tweaks.
This Musashi has yet to complete anything, far from it actually. But so far it's been quite good. Haven't noticed  a gamebreaking bug or anything of the sort.
If there's one thing that won't leave my mind, it's the damn soundtrack (It's quite fitting, and very calming, really, really nice)
.......Annd Audrey's text messages. Those things..Those things is gud.
TL;DR
Simple, easy to understand gameplay with a nice reward
Nice selection of girls
Great visuals and soundtrack
Decent UI, nothing too special.
Overall, recommended to people tired of playing Zen or Endless on Bejewled and would like a game with a bit more reward.

I ended up loving The Evil Within way more than I thought I would. It turned out to be one of the coolest games I've ever played.
The visual designs of the environments, the enemies, it's all absolutely incredible and the way you are just thrown around all these different places and situations feels like something you really only could pull off in a video game.
The game keeps a wonderful pace throughout it's lengthy runtime, always mixing up shooting and stealth and never letting you feel overpowered - you will always be on the edge of your seat. It's a very difficult game (and some sections can be pretty frustrating to get through, although I personally enjoy these kinds of challenges) and it thrives on tension - if you're not playing this in a darkened room with headphones, you're doing it wrong. The excellent sound design gives life to the repulsive, insane and wonderfully creative imagery.
The DLC is excellent too and a great companion to the main story - the brilliant and character-driven plot (which admittedly took me a while to really get into in the main game) is made more clear, while new elements are introduced to the gameplay to keep it fresh. There's also plenty of extra challenges by way of MANY achievements and well hidden collectibles if that floats your boat.
All in all, I struggle to understand why this is only rated "Mostly Positive" on Steam. I seriously think it's amazing and extremely engaging.

Nuked Games' Nuked Knight is a difficult platformer not for the sake of challenging gameplay but due to unpredictable/unresponsive controls.
A game that's both colourful and vibrant with its art style will hook players attention at first glance but in the end only those who are patient enough to accept curveballs thrown by the game due to its inconsistent controls will go through it till the end.
+ Easy to understand gameplay; "A" & "D" to move left or right with "Space" for jump
- Controls tend to not respond to when pressing jump the 2nd time when trying to do a double jump; causes a lot of frustration & death as a result
+ The strength of the game; well-made environments painted with bright colours & cutesy art style help channel the frustration away a tad bit
+ Lots of levels and boss fights
+ Refreshing art style that doesn't get old quickly
- Unresponsive inputs is a major killer due to having to restart the whole level due to it no registering at crucial moments
Only recommendable with major caveat to players who are prepared for the game to let you down with its unresponsiveness but will still soldier on to play it.
Definitely not for anyone else who are looking for a good platformer with precision controls and entertaining gameplay mechanics and story.
