The sequel to "Hotline Miami" is just as exciting as a bunch of animal mask wearing gunners could be. Having many similarities with the original game, the second installment of the series offers an array of new experiences while overall maintaining the same style.
The story is based upon the first part. Set in the late 80's of the 20th century, the plot unfolds slowly and very indirectly. Expect a kind of development similar to that of the original, but slightly more branched. This involves the mafia, the army and some crazy folks (classic Hotline Miami). The player can get a grip on the story without really playing or knowing what happened in the first installment.
The gameplay differs not a whole lot from the original "Hotline Miami". The top-down shooter is quite strongly, if not totally, based upon combat. The player needs to break, roll, shoot, slice, smash and tear through the levels. The levels themselves are neatly designed. Their length is just right - not too long and not too short. Having a moderate amount of levels, the game encourages the player to play the levels a few times. Amongst other things, the replayability is pretty great, but gets diminished by the difficulty because it can be quite challenging. Upon meeting an enemy, a hail of bullets goes its merry way to greet the player, killing him/her in one single shot. This high mortality, combined by quick respawns, results in a very fast playstyle, in which a players death is connected to learning the game and its mechanics.
The game is set on the previous games graphics style - a pixelated environment which has a nice bright colour pattern to it. These colours themselves remind the player of the 80's, being quite strong and glaring, but not too disturbing. The soundtrack reinforces the 80's feeling while at the same time appearing pretty modern. The fast gameplay gets supported by the music tracks and they fuel the adrenalin, making the game really enjoyable.
"Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number" is a worthy sequel to "Hotline Miami". Wrong Number adds its own little neat features which slightly differ from the first installment. It is a bit more refined and offers a new and interesting storyline. The atmosphere gets supported by the great soundtrack and the peculiar setting. Overall, the game is great for a few quick, action packed evening sessions. It has a decent length and is definitely worth the raging from all the deaths.

If you take away the Trump soundbites, the Trump likeness, the political likeness of world leaders, and the parody of running a country without triggering World War III, then you have a game that is essentially a commodity trader meets world domination.
This game isn't a tycoon management sim. What you are managing is the "World's Anger" against you as you drill for oil in Alaska, send aid, troops or food drops to countries (including North Korea, China, Russia, and Japan) or decide to build your arsenal as your National Debt creeps upwards into figures I didn't even know existed.
There is nothing real about this game (North Korea is represented on the map essentially where Thailand and Cambodia are...which made it a little confusing during the tutorial...) - Nigel Farage is not, for example, the leader of England, and France, despite everyone's attempts, is still a part of Europe.
There needs to be a sideways-thumb, as I can't genuinely recommend this game for its content nor not recommend this game for gameplay. If you acknowledge that it is an "of-the-moment" type of game, and what you are buying into, then you might find some entertainment here. I went with a thumbs up, only because it isn't broken. This is a functioning game.
If you are looking for a game with depth, dynamics and intricate game-play then this isn't it. The clue should have been in the name. No, this is a game that has been cleverly put together in order for people to let off steam, run with the gags that are marring our social media, and take our minds off what the world could be like this time next year.
The graphics aren't newsworthy. The controls are all keyboard, and it may take a couple trial and error plays to understand what works and how to build up a strategy. If you just want to shoot at foreigners, then you might be better off with something a bit more mind-bending, like CS:GO...
The game isn't politically correct, and it pretty much is what it says it is - the clue is in the name - having been inspired by a Reddit thread. So it isn't for everyone. Right-wing, left-wing, no-wings, this game is shallow, full of stereotypes, with an unpredicatable trading market AI.
Much like the next 4 years is going to be.

Arguably one of the most charming and adorable games I've played in a long time. An endearing Match 3 game that's very anxiety/ASMR friendly and suitable for any age.
Smooth gameplay, well-composed music that's neither distracting nor aggravating, bright and coloring graphics with nice backgrounds and a clean UI, and sound and graphic effects that aren't jarring or flashy.
Nothing that really breaks the Match-3 mold, but the game has so much personality it doesn't need to. Each level has objectives, either tile-collection or "bring the jars to the bottom", with the usual roadblocks of webbed tiles, wood and stone tiles, etc. Powerups are actually useful, are earned through progression, and recharge through matching tiles and making combos. Coins picked up in each level can be spent to upgrade powerups and aren't difficult to obtain. Each level is scored on a 3-star system and can be replayed to pick up missed stars or coins.
100 levels with two difficulties - Casual (with unlimited moves per level) and Challenge (with set moves per level). All Steam achievements but one can be completed on Casual (the last is to finish the game on challenge mode).
As a Match-3 enthusiast, I really enjoyed the thoughtfully-planned levels and the colorful and fun graphics. As an adult I thought the dialogue was a little shallow, but it's still cute and better than most stories I've seen in this sort of game. Munchkins may get frustrated at higher levels with the more challenging roadblocks. Still, I would have no objection to letting my 6 year old niece play - she would probably really like Victoria and all the dialogue about fairies and unicorns, or being scared of spiders.
Scoring can be a little oddball sometimes - 3 stars in-level may equal only 1 on star on map, or 2 in-level is 3 on map. Nothing game-breaking, though for someone as 3-star obsessive as myself it was a bit of an annoyance.
Picked this little gem up at 50% off and would say that's a fair pricepoint for it - I don't think it has enough modes or replayability to justify the regular price. That said, I'm looking forward to the sequel. :)

After my experience with the first game I normally wouldn't have continued on to the second, but I already owned it thanks to a package deal, so I figured: why not? Let's go snipe things.
Of course, this game suffers from all the problems of the first: there's no story (possibly even less of one than before) and the focus is on an arcade experience where it usually makes more sense to use automatic weapons and pistols due to the close quarters than it does to snipe anything (despite the very name of the game).
On top of that, this sequel hardly brings anything new to the table. There's two new enemy types, but that's it. No new guns or explosives. And all the environments are the exact same levels from Sniper Elite 2 - literally cut and pasted - with some lighting changes to dress them up in a poor attempt to make them feel different. But if you've already played that game (like I had) then you already know the layouts of all the levels here, making a quick run through even more tedious.
In short: this is the laziest milking of a franchise I might have ever seen. It can't have taken much time or thought or effort for the developers to grind it out. I can imagine that it might be more fun to play with a full co-op team, but even then I wouldn't want to go through it more than once. There just isn't much here.

Graphics: 8/10 - Nothing to write home about, but still overall good. The atmosphere feels great and really sucks you into the world, but the textures and graphics themselves seem a little rough at times. One moment you'll be amazed as you get high above the city and see fire burning below, next you'll be mixed on some blurriness in a swamp.

Gameplay: 8/10 - This is the best part of the game. Multiple classes to play as, each with thier own design and style. Loot after each mission, to equp and style you're character. The game does take a queue from Left 4 dead in that it's surivive swarms of ratmen (zombies in l4d) by making you're way through a mission. There's some switch ups in missions, some being gather tnt or a last man standing type. It's still strangely fun and addciting, you'll love the loot and it drives you to keep playing atleast 1 more mission.
Overall: 8/10 - The game is being updated pretty regularly and with alot of content already in the game itself. This one is great on the cheap for people looking for good fantasy smashing or a succesor to Left 4 dead. Pick it up.

At first I had fun, but that faded quickly. I haven't played in awhile but here are the basics of the game;
If you like Left 4 Dead, and you like melee combat, you will enjoy the game some. If you love the format of L4D, you will love the game. If you like grinding for gear in a RNG system, where you risk losing even your chance at a reward if you fail then you will probably play the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the game.
Pro's;
*It runs fine in my experience, last I played was on a gtx 680 and a Intel 4670k and I got a good 60fps at high-ultra settings. Good looking too, not super highend, but you can appreciate the details.
*Smooth gameplay - hacking up the rodents of unusual size ('skaven' is heresy) that plague the city is fun. Ranged weapons are great as well, it draws alot of parallels to war of the roses & vikings, so if you've ever played those games then you have sort of an idea of what to expect.
*Challenge - it is ♥♥♥♥ing brutal at higher levels, you will die in a few hits and the game will throw everything it can at you.
If you enjoy a challenge, and you have a group to play with, there is much to enjoy.
Con's;
*The reward system is horrible, horrible, horrible and I think people that defend it are wrong; The only way to earn ANYTHING is to acrue dice by completing levels, at the end of each level depending on the amount (Higher difficulty ---> more, collectable tomes also give dice) and rarity of the dice (difficulty based) determine your CHANCE at rolling a random item for a random class, with 10 possible items on a scale of rarity. Whatever you role, you will get. If you don't finish a match, don't have time, crash, or fail then well sucks for you, wasted time.
*No dedicated servers - host migration, crash, whatever you will struggle somewhat with the servers.
*Frustrating mechanics - The game is unforgiving AND Brutal, it can go out of its way to screw you and failing to obtain rewards while getting your face kicked in gets old quickly.
*Lacks creativity - the DLC may have changed it (with some new stages and a survival mode) but the game could have so much more; Why not a multiplayer suite with the unique 'rodent' classes being available to play versus your standard classes? Why not some tavern games to play while you wait for your friends to join you in the tavern? Why not a open map to explore or something other than more linear waves of enemies.

Have you ever wanted to be a lowly peasant in the Middle Ages? No? Neither have they. Which is why I'm lord of a kingdom that dominates more than half the world.
Mount and Blade: Warband is a medieval role-playing simulation in which you are cast into a war-torn land known as Calradia. And that's it. You decide what happens next. You can join one of the rival kingdoms vying for power, work as a mercenary fighting for gold, or even become king or queen of your own kingdom and join the struggle. Complete wars are fought, won and lost, and each game is different with diplomatic relations constantly being dynamically modified in real time. One minute, peasants have kidnapped a girl to marry their son, the next minute all of Swadia has come down in fury upon the marriage-crazed Nords in vengeance, and the only end to the conflict comes with a peace treaty following a series of vicious skirmishes.
The game is played for the most part on a real time world map where you travel with your party to cities, find and speak with lords, both allied and enemy, play through dynamic quests, and manage your troops, companions and inventory. Cities can be explored, taverns visited to recurit companions and mercenary soldiers, and lords or ladies spoken to in their great halls. This being a roleplaying game, your custom-made character as well as your party can be levelled up, re-equipped and all that jazz via training, shops and combat experience. When a battle occurs and the player joins, the game drops you into a real-time battle as an invudivial person amongst the clashing armies. You can command your forces using various keypresses as well as fight in the battle yourself. Combat itself is fluid and near-flawless - swings are directed by movements of the mouse, which your blocks can be either manually controlled or automatic using the right. Much of the combat is determined by actual skill, though charging into an entire battalion like a fool will always bring certain doom. There isn't a great amount of strategy involved, but it is made up for by the sheer action of a massive battle. The gameplay is addictive, unique, and unlike any other medieval simulation out there. Some quests can be repetitive, but all in all the base experience remains an excellent example of a roleplaying game.
That said, the graphics and sounds are very sub-par. This is NOT something that the game should be judged on, but it should be mentioned that the game does not look great for the year of release. Textures and models are low-quality, though much of this is to optimize the game's already CPU heavy engine. There are parts of the graphics that are nice, however - soldiers get soaked in blood as the battle rages on, and some visual effects and vistas can be rather beautiful at times. The sound is not fantastic either, with some low-quality sound effects breaking up the powerful sounds of horses charging and weapons clanging. There do exsist mods to enhance both of these aspects, which I would recommend to those who cannot live without them. Again, I have to stress that this aspect of the game should not determine wether you purchase it, as the game offers enough game wise that the art aspects don't set it back much - after all, everything that glitters is not gold!
There is a multiplayer part of the game was well, although it is limited to battles only. Servers are always busy although I find them somewhat laggy at times, and players range from the hardcore to...well...trolls. Finding a good server can be difficult, but when you do, your thirty minutes before bed turns into an all night tirade of battle after battle. Player versus player combat is outstanding, with so much intensity and speed that even the best players will always be tested to the best of their ability. Mods like Full Invasion expand on this, adding Player versus All wave-mode style gameplay or defend the VIP-like missions. This game is one of the few that has a nearly even single and multiplayer experience, guarenteeing that fans of both modes will be more than satisfied.
Mount and Blade: Warband, while graphically flawed, is an amazing game and one of my all-time favories. With an enormous modding community and dozens of modifications being produced, there is a near endless replay value to the whole thing. With modules to place the game in real-life Europe, Japan or even Victorian America, or in fantasy universes like A Song of Ice and Fire or (my personal favorite) Tolkien's Middle-earth, there will never be a shortage of options for how to play. Combat is fast and violent but incredibly involved, campaigns can go on for years, and you will never have the same experience twice. Whie not quite to the scale of a game like the Total War series, Mount and Blade brings players a grand campaign intertwined with furious battles and struggles for power unlike larger roleplaying games such as The Elder Scrolls. Fans of roleplaying, strategy, action or even just High Middle Ages society will be extremely pleased by this wonderful and entirely unique game. Medieval life is harsh, complex and dramatic, and Mount and Blade: Warband captures each aspect of it perfectly.

Overall I give this game 4/5 stars. And with the DLC clearing up some plot holes from the core game I bump it up to 5/5. Highly recommend this game to anyone looking for something they can really sink their teeth into.

Star Trek Online may at first seem like your cliche MMORPG. There is the common xp, customization, skill boosting and unlocks of most MMOs, but there is something about Star Trek Online that is truly special. It might be the massive ship battles, overarching story quests, purchasable and customizable ships and an extremely large and epic galaxy to explore and fight for. This game is very cute and entertaining. If you like turn-based strategy games, then this is for you. It reminds me a bit of the board game Small World, as well as the video game Don't Starve (which you can also get on steam).  While the game is fairly easy to learn, it can take a while to really master it.
PROS:
-adorable
-great art
-easy to learn
-sandbox and story mode options
-real genetics!
-great music
-runs well even on weaker computers
CONS:
-can get boring if you aren't a very goal-oriented person. There is only one goal: survive. Once you get the hang of game play, this task is extremely easy. There are achievements and the main "story line" that can be accomplished, but the feeling of having a specific goal to work towards is lacking. Additionally, the story line is simple: you got separated from your tribe and need to go back home. There is no marker on how far along you are towards getting home, and no way to really track your progress. You are either on your home island or not. I would appreciate the game more if there was at least a bar at the top of the screen that showed what percentage of islands you have explored, genes unlocked, and other small goals. A few more larger goals or different story lines would be interesting as well.
-"feminine" game. I wouldn't go so far as to call it girly, but Niche's cuteness is a huge part of the game. Although I'm a girl and happen to love this kind of stuff, some people may be embarrassed to play a "girly" game.
-no multiplayer options, as of yet. It would be nice to play a multiplayer map, where the goal would be to outlast the other player(s). Maybe they could even work together as a tribe.
-It would also be neat if there was a spore-like create-a-creature option, especially since sandbox mode is hardly a "sandbox" version - it is almost the exact same as story mode, but without the goal of getting home.
Conclusion:
Cute, simple, and addicting. Overall I would give the game an 8/10 for the average player, or a 9/10 if you enjoy games like Spore, Small World, and Don't Starve. The use of realistic genetics gives Niche a significant amount of depth to it, although the story is weak and the lack of difficult, obvious goals can make the game boring for those who don't enjoy sandbox style games. Kids could play too, although they will need to be able to read and work out a simple strategy. My guess for a minimum age (based on difficulty of the game rather than content) would be 8. I would highly recommend this game to those who like cute, strategy/puzzle, genetic, or survival games. This game would not be enjoyed much by those who prefer realistic art (vs cartoony), action, or a strong push towards completing goals.

Well, I was honestly surprised. Very positively surprised indeed!
When I first tried this game when it got released, I was bugged by an obscene amount of lag that made the game totally unplayable, but now it's alright.
The core game is quite fun, but in my opinion, Classic mode is where it really shines.
Classic mode is the traditional Ace of Spades Alpha experience: one class, everyone on the same ground with the same weapons and same capabilities, and giant CTF maps where you must out-dig your opponents to catch them pants-down, and bury them in a sea of sand and tears and blood.
That's Ace of Spades!
0/10 would buy, there are no cards of either Aces nor Spades

Here's the thing. If you make a game that is about two things, namely, shooting people in the face and building, you cannot add a mechanic that completly removes one of those things from the equasion.
Ace of Spades had brilliant building and destruction mechanics. But no-one cares, because ther is no point to build anything. One class gets a jet-pack, and can fly over your beautifuly crafted fortress walls. All the primary modes have unique classes that are completly over-the-top and fun to play, but so does Team Fortress. You can blow holes in things, but its a waste of ammo and time when you can just jet over it.
However, ther is ONE MODE that gets it right: Classic CTF. Every player gets the same class, with either a scopeless sniper rifle, a assualt-style SMG, or a ungodly powerful close-quarters shotgun. They also get two grenades, a shovel, and the ability to build. No drill-rocket launchers, no autoturrets, and no jetpacks.
It is the most amazing and unique experience I have ever played in a shooter. There is a kind of authesticity to rushing over an open killing ground and despratly trying to dig a foxhole to escape the next wave of rifle-fire, and assualting into a base by diving into trenches. Or as you sneak around to the fortress thy built around their flag, poke a hole in the wall, toss a grenade in and breaching through the resulting hole. The vanilla rifle is extremly satisfying to use and promotes careful, strtegic positioning, while the shotgun is the most fun shock-and-awe weapon I have ever encountered, able to blow a man-sized hole in a thin wall with a single shot. With a good team, you will build a massive fortress with logical defenses and killzones, all while driving to breach the enemy who does the same.
The problem, is that nobody plays Classic. The mirad of other modes with their fun-and-silly classes distract from the real meat of the game: digging, building and shooting people in the face.
Now it's just shooting people in the face. Like every other FPS out there.

Pick your backstory,grab your gear and go on an adventure in which you will lead a small group of bandits or big armies,choice is all yours.
Join a faction and fight for it,capturing castles and towns.
There are 3 kind of fights: Open field,siege and close quarter.
are the place where the game shines. Both army get spawned on a field(though field maps are quite limited and depend on the zone but so far noticed like 3 kind of battlefields per zone) and charge at each other,unless you order something else to your troops - you can tell them to charge,hold position,stand their ground or move forward/backwards a bit. Sadly you have to be at the point you want to put them so expect quite a lot of running around.
Limit of the map is 150 units total and reinforcments will spawn up to 3 times per fight(once one of the sides lose all their units you either continue the fight with rest of the troops or win/lose) .
is a bit lacking : the attacking army got 1 siege tower/ladder(rarely you may see 2 ladders) to get up the walls and defeat the defenders . So the fight mostly turns into breaking/defending the choke point .
varies quite a lot: bandit camps,capturing castle/town, arenas ,ambushes. Basicly you are spawned with few of your units(5-7, or in ambushes you are alone) and have to clean the area of enemies - there are no reinforcments for you and you dont have access to your horse(only in arenas if it given to you).
Each faction got their own units(starting from farmers up to knights and the like) . Each faction is specialized in different aspects of combat: cavalry,archery, heavy/light infantry,etc . On the other hand you can also hire mercenaries . To upgrade your units they need to gain experience through combat or daily training. Each units got its stats so you have to pick carefuly.
Combat is quite simple(especially if you played Skyrim) - you have mounted and unmounted combat with both of them got their own pros/cons  but both ways the execution is made really well and chance to have issues is quite low(at least from my PoV)
Game got quite big variety of weapons to use : 1h/2h swords, crossbow, bows, javelins, axes, maces, polearms, pikes, clubs, throwing weapons,shields.You can specilize in each of them but can carry up to 4 weapons at a time(bolts and arrows require a slot). Shields got durability and after it deplete they break(for the fight only). During the fights you can pick weapons from the ground in which case you either drop your currently equiped weapon(unless you have a free slot).
While fighting you will gain levels which gives you points towards weapons specialization, different skills(personal(affects only you), party(stacking bonus that affects the party) and leader(takes the highest lvl from the party). In the game you can hire "heroes" that lvl up just like you and you can pick what skills to improve and what equipment to use. You can equip helmet,armor,boots,gloves,horse and 4 weapons. Also you have to feed your army which leads to buying quite a lot of food. After each win you can loot part of the gear dropped by the enemy.
Since the game is a sand box you have to set your own goals but there are quite a lot of things to do . You can get different tasks:collecting taxes for a lord,destroy a bandit's camp,take care of bandits attacking a village,train peasants to defend,collect goods for a town,kill a wanted man or deliver a msg to a lord. If you join a faction you get some war-related quests: scout locations,capture units/lord, defend a location,siege a location,follow the war master, bring cattle to the siege camp. You can join a faction as mercenary(getting paid weekly depending on your army) or as lord(getting your own castle and village to take care of) .
Still there are quite a lot of ways to improve it(aka check the mods) and may get boring quite fast if you are looking for depth.
The game offers quite a lot of hours of enjoyment if you are into big fights(like Total War series but you want to make it a bit more personal) .

ENDLESS REPETITION
Great first moments; you think you're about to play the quintessential Haunted House game...
Then, everything becomes disconnected. Spacial relationships become irrelevent, as you walk repeatedly down similar corridors. The game feels like it's been fleshed out through asset repetition: Walk down the brown hallway -> Brown Door Locked -> Walk back the way you came to enter new but strikingly similar brown hallway.
Some will say this spacial incoherence is fitting given the narrative perspective--the ol' "unreliable narrator"--but to me it bespoke poor level design and an unclear vision for the project as a whole. The fact is that you could play the chapters of this game in any order, because its just a sequence of events with little inevitability linking them together. There is some great art direction and atmosphere in this game, but it feels squandered because... well... I never really cared where I was in the story... I just rushed to get to the next doorway, praying that some new art assets would appear, only to be confronted with the same wood corridors and endless emply cabinets time and time again.

Probably, the most profound and sensitive depiction of the internal struggle of mental patient the video-game world has seen till this day. A person of unknown identity loses control of his memories and sensual abilities and falls into a deep comatose where the memories of his childhood 90s action movies take on a whole new role. The epileptic imagery in the intro might suggest a series of seizures within the temporal lobes of the brain or even the visual cortex over exiting his visual senses making him “see” a combination of memories and hallucinations instead of detecting what surrounds him like with. It is also possible the disturbed visions and colorful memories are the results of the growth of a highly invasive and malignant tumor in the temporal lobes. The case could be similar to Dr. Oliver Sacks’ case of “the passage to India”, where a young girl could vividly see long lost memories of the India of her past after a malignant tumor had grown inside her brain. However the cause of the brain damage to the temporal lobes causing the memories to reemerge are not important, what is to be noted is that these distorted visions of the past brings a certain comfort to the patient. The minds tend to like to compensate for lacks with other things. So the patient while not remembering the exact names of his childhood heroes, his brain renamed them in a way that would sound soothing to him. The struggle lies between recognizing that the visions are mere hallucinations and to face a cold reality of pain or indulge in the fantasy dream world his mind created for him to make him feel happy, like a child again. The visions intermingled with the dreams of a possible comatose has somewhat of a Jungian feel to it. The many characters and objects of his past somehow symbolize many of the figures in his life that he enjoyed the presence of. The characters ad objects are in some way his Jungian dream archetypes. Hailey is the archetype of the child representing his innocence, Thelma his desire to become a hero and achieve glory like his role models, Lance as the father figure he always wished for, Shur foo as the sage etc. Being among his dream archetypes and experiencing a sense a control and belonging pulls him constantly further into his comatose. Eventually, just like Alexander Luria’s “man with a shattered world” , he couldn’t distinguish memories and hallucination and the dreams would repeat themselves over and over again with the same characters his mind created.
The brilliance in this game lies in the fact that it can make us feel the torment of the patient, how such a playful and funny and conforting game could seem more interesting than reality but details such as the Jungian archetypes and the visual and auditif seizures remind us that what can be seen is but a stew illusions. And at that time we can feel the pain the patient feels to be forever stuck in this looping fantasy world and that he will probably never see the “real” world ever again. The pain, the feels.

This is one of my favorite games on Steam! It's very fun, and easygoing but takes strategy and skill at the same time. I love story mode, as it provides an end goal, but it's still an open-world sort of thing, and doesn't make you go anywhere. You can experiment, do challenges, or just try to survive in Sandbox mode. There are so many islands, you can choose your difficulty and your pacing for the most part, although sometimes it surprises you with a challenge. Lastly, the art is amazing! The tribe creatures are so cute, and all the other non-tribe creatures, like the rabbils, bearyenas, crabbits, Apes, etc. are also very well done. The pelt colors and patterns seem to be completely unique for each tribe creature (at least, the tribe creatures with patterns at all look unique), and there are so many genes that it hardly seems possible to get the exact same creature twice. Overall, I would say Stray Fawn Studios did an amazing job all around (still waiting for those wings, though)!

I'm not a fan of where Hotline Miami 2 took the series.  Personally, I felt that its story took all of the mystery and wonderful neon magic that composed the world in the first game and overcomplicated it.  I really, really enjoyed the first game, and I honestly did enjoy this installment until I started to get closer to the ending, when I realized the story was slowly deviating from what the first game set up, and the levels weren't structured as well.
Also, I'm really not a fan of how the story is told
This game does answer some (but not all, unfortunately) of the questions posed in the first game, but they can be hard to wrap your head around without reading a forum or watching a youtube video about the story (it gets kinda Five Night's at Freddy's-level complicated).
I didn't enjoy the way the story concludes, to me it felt like the devs didn't know how to end it.  I also feel like the ending could have worked better had players been more involved in the way it plays out; it felt too random and disconnected and made me feel like everything I'd done up to that point was
Maybe this is the theme the developers were shooting for.  If so, then they achieved it, but I didn't like it.
Gamplay wise, it's an ok sequel to the first game.  It improves in a lot of areas and adds some new techniques that are character-based, making gameplay more interesting.  However I feel as though the level design is not quite as on par as the first game, because more often then not I found myself getting fired at from enemies I couldn't see and killed by enemies I only really had a 50/50 chance of reacting to in time.  There are new enemies that have pretty BS movement speed and melee range, I didn't like that.  The first game was hard but with good reflexes you could manage.  This installment makes everything feel much too random and chance-based.
On the bright side, the soundtrack for this game is fantastic, much like the first game.
Also, my opinions aside, the level editor is a fantastic addition to this game.  It adds a giant replayability factor, which I respect the devs for immensely.
If you're only coming here for the story, you may or may not be disappointed.  However, it's still a good game that's definitely worth playing if you liked the first one.  I didn't enjoy it as much as the first, but you may like it more as many do.
Did you enjoy the first one? Great, get this, it's longer and somewhat more difficult.

I like puzle games quite a bit, but Prismatica just does too many things I didn't really appreciate. I did complete the game in its entirety with all challenge stars, and felt like I was playing a flash game the entire time. That's not inherently a bad thing- there are some very good flash games out there, but this just felt... average when compared to an average pool.
The only gameplay mechanic is rotating a group of 6 hexes around predetermined centerpoints, to recreate the starting colors. Red touch red, Orange touch red and yellow, and so on. Points where all 3 colors connect are gray instead of the expected white, and only show up late. This mechanic works very well and feels almost like unraveling a Rubik's Cube: but ultimately it came down to solving a few hexes on the edge and working to the other side. The final moves were a matter of fiddling around until it worked, which wasn't terribly engaging. I suppose I could have logically worked out a series of moves that would swap two arbitrary tiles, but I never needed to.
There are 48 levels, grouped into 4 groups of 12. At first glance it looks like there are twice as many puzzles as this, with 1 and 1-star: but the starred puzzle areas are exactly the same but with the ability to get the time and move stars (most of which are calibrated WAAYYYY too loosely). Why aren't these always accessible?
4-11 was too large and felt very tedious. I was on autopilot- I guess that's fine for a relaxing puzzle game, but this just felt like a timekiller.
I've played other pure puzzle games for far longer without them getting old- Everyday Genius: SquareLogic is literally just Kenken, but there are some novel additions and most puzzles felt different. HexCells is very similar to Minesweeper, but again, the puzzles felt fairly distinct and there were twists added to keep the interest high. Prismatica starts off average in terms of interest and only decreases from there.
I played the entire game on mute. Couldn't stand the soundbyte that played on beating a level.
Note: this is me not recommending the game. This is not me saying this is a bad game- it's not. But I wouldn't call it good either. It's decidedly average, and that's more than enough for some.

This is a nice, casual game. The game methodology is fairly straightforward. They mix up hexagonal, colored wheels, and then you put them back in order. The hexes are in color (there is a colorblind option as well that includes patterns on the hexes) and the hub of each of the wheels tells you what hex colors go there. There are also mixed colors (yellow and red = orange; blue and yellow = green; red and blue = purple). The mixed colored hexes are, as you’ve probably figured out, for where the wheels overlap. The first two puzzle rounds show you how you will solve the remainder of the puzzles, and then you go through four grades of 12 puzzles.
PRO: Very easy to learn, very relaxing and enjoyable. Good graphic representation.
CON: No additional downloadable puzzles. Once you’ve gone through the 48 puzzles you can go into the options menu reset so that you can run through them again, but there is not a more difficult level to put to the puzzles. I would have loved to see more combinations.
Worth the money? I would say a bit high, but I would like the programmers to give me more content so I would say it is fair enough. Would I pick it up on a Steam sale? In a heartbeat!!

I did a video review if you have ADHD like me.
Great sound design, great atmosphere, an effective mixture of scare tactics to keep you guessing, an interesting artistic motif with tons of great textures and classical art pieces and a lot of creative ways to mess with your mind and make you ask "was that piece of furniture there a second ago?"
That being said, I don't think it warrants anything above 15 dollars considering it's just an eerie walking simulator with a lot of cliche'd twitchy dolls. There's no way to actually die - you can pick up items, walk, and run. The game wants you to believe you're in danger, but you never are. The fear is entirely shallow, which is upsetting considering how great the actual appearance of things is.
Thoughout the game I was constantly trying to mess with the hallucinations to see if the game let me have any player agency, but time and time again it was a scripted death on a linear path. The times that did manage to scare me were when you'd get to a locked door at the end of a hallway, turn around, and there was a loud jumpscare waiting for you. Or when I'd walk into a pretty room, check the fireplace, and when I'd turn around everything in the room would fly towards me and become discheveled on the ground. There's a LOT of turning-around puzzles/spooks but they usually caught me off guard 80% of the time.
Despite playing an early-release review copy, I found zero bugs - save for cabinet and dresser drawers occasionally not recognizing when I tried to grab them.
This is one of those games that I would rate "Neutral" if Steam would allow it, but for now I'll have to give it a reluctant no, solely because, while the game is cool, it obviously took a lot from PT and Amnesia - too much, really - but didn't execute them quite as well as I'd hoped. Combining that with the price tag, I can't justify paying more than 15 dollars for this 4-hour walking experience.

A brilliant little game with many different playstyles and content to explore, Niche has to be one of the most well executed "evolution-esque" survival games out there. The way the game plays out is rather simple; you play as a "tribe" or pack of animals who through breeding can combine their genes with other animals to gain or lose different traits (be that cosmetic or an actual ability). Through selective breeding (or cold hard luck) you can make your species flourish or parish, however, the best part about Niche is that in almost all cases no matter your creature's "stats" (unless they are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥and the creature is a complete genetic deformity) you can still survive very long and have fun in varying different ways depending on the way your creature has evolved (water or land?) and how you yourself can adapt and change your playstyle depending on the environment in game, which I found to be very intuitive. One of the things I really hate about other games is how if you are some how out of the "meta" (a certain path the game wants you to take in your playstyle.) the game punishes you. In Niche, that is just not a thing. Keep in mind, though, that if you do act stupid your species will go extinct, which I think is absolutely perfect because the game doesn't exactly hold your hand but still allows for any amount of freedom you'd like in your decisions and choices.
However, like any other game or gene pool, it's not completely perfect. some of the mechanics in the game felt rather annoying or offputting. Disease has to be one of my main gripes. In-game, if one of the members of your pack gets infected with even the common cold, expect it to spread like wildfire. It seems kind of silly to me how fast disease can spread in this game, especially since it can be so lethal. On top of that there is no real way to quarantine anyone away from your main herd or to banish them without risking other pack member's lives in the process. Currently, the only really effective ways I've found of "quarantining" or culling members who are sickly off of my pack are either commanding them to stand in water untill they die of oxygen starvation or just shoving them some random place wayyyy far off in a forest or jungle untill they die from whatever disease they have. This combined with the fact that animals in this game don't live that long anyway and the fact that diseases slowly take away how long animals can survive really drains from the main gameplay. On top of this, some of the traits animals can have are quite annoying to deal with but absolutely avoidable, so just don't breed with freaks and you should be good.
Overall, I'd give this game a 8/10. There are very few gripes I have with the game and overall it is a very enjoyable experience.

A genetic survival game where you get a certain amount of action points per "animal", per day. Breed male and female and as long as the female is in a nest the next morning she will give birth. Throw in some aggressive creatures roaming about, a few stray animals looking to implant their genes into your pool, the hunt for food, and a bit of island hopping/adventure. That's what you will find in Niche
It seemed like a no brainer for me when I purchased the game. I had a bit of an impression the game was about cross breeding species, manipulating DNA and having your creatures coexist amongst each other. That is not at all what this game is. The game is about a pack of animals that "struggle" to survive in any given habitat where you breed/manipulate the gene pool to where you feel your pack is evolving.
The main issue I had with the game is the 14ish day/turn life cycle. I found it all too common that once you establish an Alpha (your favorite gene combination) and start to breed it the timer is ticking WAY too fast. I wasn't a fan of the randomness or forever losing the option to breed your alpha again after those 14 days. You get a set amount of rounds to enhance your gene pool and during that time the parents of that animal have died off. If all your attempts don't leave you with a sense of progression towards an ideal combination of genes then you lost your opportunity. You will then have to begin an entire new cycle of mediocre breeding cycles in an attempt to get what you want.
The RNG is extremely heavy in this game. In the end I am left with a feeling that there isn't any real goal to obtain or any direction to take outside of just finding a solid food source of bushes that respawn food. Establish a renewable food source and the game leaves you with nothing more than breeding for that optimal pack. It is far too easy to lose genes in this process, so that ruined the game for me. I don't want to breed 4 different +1 armor and +4 claws animals with each other and not obtain a single birth that has +1 armor without remapping half of the other genes, while at the same time creating new borns that are by far inferior to their parents. 2 male, 2 female, about 16 children and not a single child I didn't banish from the pack.
I guess the real issue here is the lack of information or understanding of which genes are dominant and such. It felt awfully random to me and for that reason I am not a fan. For $18.00 idk what I was expecting, but I sure wasn't expecting a game that felt so lacking of content. Maybe I am biased because I see so much potential for this genre. I plan on giving it another run, but the last time I tried I quickly lost interest in trying.

I'm not a fan of where Hotline Miami 2 took the series.  Personally, I felt that its story took all of the mystery and wonderful neon magic that composed the world in the first game and overcomplicated it.  I really, really enjoyed the first game, and I honestly did enjoy this installment until I started to get closer to the ending, when I realized the story was slowly deviating from what the first game set up, and the levels weren't structured as well.
Also, I'm really not a fan of how the story is told
This game does answer some (but not all, unfortunately) of the questions posed in the first game, but they can be hard to wrap your head around without reading a forum or watching a youtube video about the story (it gets kinda Five Night's at Freddy's-level complicated).
I didn't enjoy the way the story concludes, to me it felt like the devs didn't know how to end it.  I also feel like the ending could have worked better had players been more involved in the way it plays out; it felt too random and disconnected and made me feel like everything I'd done up to that point was
Maybe this is the theme the developers were shooting for.  If so, then they achieved it, but I didn't like it.
Gamplay wise, it's an ok sequel to the first game.  It improves in a lot of areas and adds some new techniques that are character-based, making gameplay more interesting.  However I feel as though the level design is not quite as on par as the first game, because more often then not I found myself getting fired at from enemies I couldn't see and killed by enemies I only really had a 50/50 chance of reacting to in time.  There are new enemies that have pretty BS movement speed and melee range, I didn't like that.  The first game was hard but with good reflexes you could manage.  This installment makes everything feel much too random and chance-based.
On the bright side, the soundtrack for this game is fantastic, much like the first game.
Also, my opinions aside, the level editor is a fantastic addition to this game.  It adds a giant replayability factor, which I respect the devs for immensely.
If you're only coming here for the story, you may or may not be disappointed.  However, it's still a good game that's definitely worth playing if you liked the first one.  I didn't enjoy it as much as the first, but you may like it more as many do.

HuniePop is a very fun mix of match-3 puzzle and dating sim.
Similarly to dating sims, you meet girls and go on the dates with them. Unlike the usual dating sims, however, the date spot is chosen randomly, and your success at the date is determined by winning a match-3 puzzle game. Also unlike the usual dating sims, you don’t focus on winning one of the girls, but instead can (and in fact expected to) date all the girls at once, without any negative repercussions.
The puzzle aspect of the game is top-notch. Among other things, you are required to focus on specific pieces depending on which girl you are dating, and there is a huge selection of power-ups (represented by date gifts), and choosing the ones that work well together is very important for late-game puzzles.
Dating sim aspect, however, is kind of lacking. The girls have very distinct personalities and some backstory, but next to none present-time development is happening: as you date the girls you are rewarded with photos and new outfits for them, but your relationship isn’t going anywhere. Meeting new girls and learning more about them is still fun, though.
Final thing worth mentioning: HuniePop was originally an adult game, and while Steam version is censored, I believe it is still NSFW, which may be off-putting for some people. Those who enjoy adult content, though, will be pleased that it is possible to un-censor Steam version of the game (information about that can be found at Steam forum).
I fully recommend this game to everyone who like match-3 puzzles and isn’t put off by adult content. And while HuniePop isn’t 100% typical dating sim, I believe that dating sim fans will thoroughly enjoy it as well.

Ok I've put in over 2 days in this game and all I can say is wow. Just wow this game is well ok I’ll give it its fair share of credit and actually review it. No I’m not trashing the game on what’s bad and not praising it for what’s good. I’m going to tell you the good and the bad of each category. (I’m not a SJW, feminist sympathizer, or neckbeard. I just want others to know what to expect when buying this game.) So I’ll go through it in the standard fashion that I usually work with by going through Story, Graphics and Sounds, Gameplay, Replay Value, and my Closing Thoughts on the game. (Please note that this is my opinion of the game as I’ve played it. Others may have a different experience but to each his own.)
~Story~
Ok first up is story. If your one of those gamers that love dating sim’s and you think “ Hey look this game says it’s got “plenty of plot.”. It must be a great game” or you like VN’s for there story and immersion and you see this game then you should look elsewhere because this game has neither of these. What is there is barely enough to hold any immersion what so ever and there’s no emotional connection to the characters. As the story starts of you’re a hopeless romantic that completely fails at getting any kind of action. Then this fairy-in-disguise tells you she has to go but will see you soon. Then later that night in your apartment she wakes you up and tells you she’s going to teach you how to date the right way. This is where the story starts to draw you in. This however falls flat as the girls you can “date” (I’ll tell you why it’s in quotes in gameplay.) are introduced to you. After all 8 of them have been introduced you go through the phase of “dating” them this is where the story just abruptly stops. There’s no ending to the game at all unfortunately though to some that’s not a bad thing. However it just stopped right as it was building up potential I have no idea as to whether it was taken out or just not able to be put into the game at all. There are 4 other girls that need to be unlocked including the fairy.
~Graphics and Sound~
As far as dating sim’s go the graphics are ok mostly just your average anime theme. The sounds fit the mood of the area you’re in. All the characters are voice acted and the lip sync is spot on. However both the graphics and sound do take quite an astonishing turn and not for the better I’m afraid. When I first started the game I could see both the left side of the character and the outer most side of the huniebee even in windowed form. It wasn’t till I restarted the game that the problem fixed itself. The full screen mode stretches the game and it takes a toll on the graphics to where the characters and backgrounds look wider than they should. The music can become annoying after a few minutes as each track loops constantly making you want to turn it off completely. The same can be said about the voice acting as after an hour of listening to them talk you’ll just want to turn it off. Also there are some odd sexual jokes and ethnical stereotypes mentioned so be aware if your sensitive to that kind of stuff.
~Gameplay~
Now here’s where Huniepop stands out among other dating sim’s there’s 2 types of gameplay a questioner, and a match-3 puzzle. When you select the questioner you get hunie which is used to upgrade traits. When you ask a question you haven’t asked or answer a question she asks correctly you get bonus hunie . This shouldn’t be too hard as each girl will just repeat whatever they asked you; in some cases they will ask you the same question immediately after you asked them. (also some of the gifts are a pretty heavy with misogyny and ethnical stereotypes for example you can give the latina girl a poncho and a sombrero, and the asian girl chopsticks and a samurai helmet so if you’re sensitive to that stuff stay away.) To purchase gifts you need munie (yes like the Kingdom Hearts’s munie) which is earned after you go on a “date”. Each token on the grid represents a trait the higher your level in that trait the more points you’ll earn there are also tokens that have effects on the grid as well. The hearts increase your passion level, the bell’s increase the amount of moves, the tear drops give you sentiment to use you date gifts, and the purple hearts reduce your score. The game is quite simple and easy to learn however the amount of points you need to fill the meter increases with each “date” (this goes for all girls not just one). After 4 successful “dates” you’ll get to take the girl home and play a sex mini game. This part of the game won’t have any purple hearts that decrease your score. However the affection bar will constantly decrease at a very quick pace so you have to combo like crazy. Also the “dates” are just to allow you to get a picture from the girl so it’s not really worth “dating” them after you’ve completed all the hearts and unlocked all their costumes unless you want to have sex with them again. For each girl there are 4 pictures one normal, one slightly smutty, and one with the potential to be masturbatory; add that to getting an after sex shot and you got yourself a nice collection of would be nude’s.
~ Replay Value~
Like with the story there’s very little to nothing worth replaying in the game as when you unlock a picture from a girl you get it unlocked in the gallery in the loading screen. You can play as ether a male or female (I did both) but nothing would really change except a few minor things that you probably wouldn’t notice unless you paid really close attention to them; you can always change your gender in the settings at any time so it’s really no point in picking one over the other.
~ Closing Thoughts~
I thought long and hard on this game and I really can’t say it’s a bad game. However I will say this game is not a dating simulator in fact it’s more of a friend’s-with-benefits simulator. I say that because the game just lacks things that makes a dating sim a dating sim. The story captivates but just disappears after all the girls are introduced leaving a lot of missed opportunities like having Jessie and Tiffany finally put aside their differences and bond with each other again, or helping Audrey with her drug addiction and finding the root of it, or give Aiko some encouragement to actually in joy teaching and get over her gambling addiction , hell even give use the option of helping Kyanna out with her kid would give some connection outside of just “ Hey let’s go on 4 dates and after that we can head back to my place for some midnight loven.”. When I kickstarted this game back in 2014, I was hoping that HuniePop would be the engaging visual novel I always wanted. What I got was... Well, not a visual novel, but it was still REALLY FREAKING GREAT.
HuniePop is more or less Puzzle Quest, but instead of beating monsters up you date all of the women in your town (and more) and eventually try to sleep with everyone.  It's mechanics are surprisingly solid, and even when it gets balls-to-the-wall hard with the last 3 or so girls, it holds up. Some amount of planning and strategy is required in order to complete the later dates.
My main gripe with HuniePop is that the character development is unfortunately sparse and I really wish there was more semblance of a story. I guess maybe HuniePot decided to put more money in the voice actresses, who are fantastic.
If you enjoy match 3-type puzzle games or just want a little more gameplay to accompany your virtual dating adventures, HuniePop is more than deserving of your attention and money. I wholeheartedly recommend this game.

A year on and I still play Vermintide fairly regularly (not often, but I leave it installed because my group still plays it) and a year on, it's still the best Left4Dead successor out there. The aspect of cleaving your way through a horde of man-sized rats while desperately trying to reclaim your fallen teammate and complete an objective provides both a harrowing sense of desperation and accomplishment when you finally complete the level.
Mechanically this has some of the best feeling melee combat is some of the best. The swings have heft to them and the way the rats go flying end over end or get chopped into bits adds a morbid glee to the slaughter. Beyond that, the game is fairly well balanced with regards to the combat versus the horde and with the specials. There are times where things may feel slightly unfair, but more often than not on the regular difficulties you'll be able to look at a situation that went wrong and pinpoint who did what to cause it. On the higher ones the game tends to through a greater challenge at you so that may not ring as true, but there are people out there constantly beating them so it can be done.
There's also a loot system that many people hate and many people love. In essence, you equip whichever character you pick with gear you earn by completing missions. However, the way the gear is earned is a dice roll. The higher number you roll, the better quality gear you get, but due to the roll and the fact that it will draw your gear from a pool randomly, this system can sometimes be infuriating if you're looking to get better gear for your characters. They have, however, added multiple systems over the past year to help give the player MUCH better control over the loot system and help them earn what they want more easily than just relying on a few good dice rolls.
One of the few complaints I can muster about this game is that the developer has constantly meant well in their updates and their plans for the game, but they consistently miss their planned DLC release dates by MONTHS, as well as have offered some underwhelming updates over the past year. But regardless of what the developer has done post-launch with the game and how you view it, the base foundation of the game is incredibly solid and well worth playing.

Mount and Blade Warband is a game released in 2010, which I can safely say can stand on the podium of RPG greats alongside Vampires: The Masqurade- Bloodlines and other such titles. It's a game set in a brutal low-fantasy land, plauged wth violence both formalised and informalised. Slavers roam freely, bandits even more so, and your average farm boy can find greatness with a rusted sword and a lame horse, should he be talented enough to do so.
The game is an RPG through and through. With a text-based , 'choose your own adventure' character backstory, it flings you into the action fighting a band of theives intent on leaving you dead and your money in their hands. This sets the tone. This isn't a comfortable time of prosperity. People are hard. Violence is common. Two men can be butchered in the street, and nobody'll blink.
From there, you're left comfortably to your own devices. Fancy yourself a kingdom? Scrape together an army, take a castle and be preparedt to face the wrath of all the other royals who do not like this impetuous common man (or woman,)   starting themselves a realm.
Maybe you want to become a knight? Well, become well-known enough, pledge yourself to a king, and be prepared to join Calradia's wars, as Nord battles Swadian over castles.
Or maybe you want something a little less honourable? A life of plunder can be yours, raiding merchants and farmers for plentiful loot. It's all possible within this game.
I should mention that there's a distinct difference between the overmap and the main gameplay. Whilst the overmap is a simple thing, with pawns representing everything from a merchant caravan to a lord's army to three bandits with a few rusty knives. Otherwise, the camera takes an over the shoulder view, allowing you to shoot and slash as you please. It's a system that works well.
However, whilst your own story might be fleshed out fairly well... Not much else is. You can marry, but marriage is an annoying and finnicky process unless you want your honour to tank, and gives fairly few benefits. Running a kingdom quickly becomes boring, and you'll be struggling for survival for most of it. Mods help with this, but  'mods' shouldn't be the immediate answer to everything.
Furthermore, it looks very dated. There are games that came out in 2010, such as FABLE III, Fallout: New Vegas, Mass Effect 2 and Call of Duty: Black Ops that still hold up today graphically. (Maybe not so much in the case of FNV, but the point still stands.)  M&B however, looks... Awful, I have to say.
Lastly, the multiplayer was underwhelming. It's simple battle arenas and sieges for the most part, and compaed to the multiplayer-only Napoleonic War DLC, it's not the feature you should be buying for.
Despite thes flaws, it's no reason to deny yourself such a good game. You can pick it up on the occasional sale, but I'd just grab it, and the DLC, at full price. You won't regret it.

Original Review below for Context:
Good All around and a true "Free to Play" MMO game, There are many things to do and content is generally upgraded quartly, but you can always get a heads up by visiting their test server (Tribble Server).
The content (if you play for hours and hours each day) will last you about 1 month as you play the story content to level your character up to 60 (max level), beyond this you start reputation and specilisation systems which all though are a grind (found in many MMO's), do give you access to some of the best gear and "special powers" in the game.
To add to more "free" top-end items you can join a fleet, either start one from scratch with friends and build your Starbase and Fleet Holdings (extra Starbase maps) from the ground up (will take a long time depending on how many active players you have/recruit or how much money you decide spend), or you can join an already Top Tier Fleet and have instant access to some of the best equipment the game has to offer, this includes ships also.
Some of the best ships are only accessible from Lockboxes which are opened by Keys (125 Zen from the Z-store or around 2.3 million Energy Credits "EC's" on the Exchange) or from the Exchange - (Trading Part of the Game) - in which you need energy credits the ingame currency in which to trade with players for those ships/items and also for certain craftable items and rep systems.
As the above statement may make it seem you have to spend money this is a part truth, spending money is a shortcut, if you have the time and patience you can spend the time and effort grinding out another in game currency "Dilithium" which can be earned in a number of ways, not only does this currency buy you some sub-top level ships and used for top level items, it can also be traded in the Dilithium Exchange - this is a player driven market in which Zen is traded for Dilithium and Vice Versa. So in essance....you don't need to spend a penny on this game if you have the time....
The content is replayable up to a point, you WILL get bored eventually but more content comes out all the time which will quench your thirst for Trek.
PvP on the other hand had the potential - but various new contents and implimentations have virtually made it a never ending Power Creep which I Believe will never end - As an advocate of PvP and its community this disapoints me, resulting in my dimihsed hours of late. One day i may return but for now the game has lost my interest even with the new content, Until PvP once again becomes playable that is.
All in all - the graphics are good (except in space pvp where with multiple players using many abilities the games engine is unable to to cope with the amount of particle data being flushed in). Content is good and has replay value for even experienced players.
Hardcore players will get bored quickly as they usually are drawn to PvP. PvE Players will love the content and play for years.
Make no mistake...you will spend money at some point for something cannot resist....
As with any game it could stand to get some improvements - in my opinion it doesnt have enough open world exploration that we all expect from Star Trek..."To boldy go where no man has gone before". There are no new worlds or civilizations to discover except for what the developers release as new conetent, so having an open "universe" to explore with random events rather than scripts would be awesome.
Despite the flaws of PvP there is still and active community - Check out my Youtube Channel and if you play for PvP join the community (OrganizedPvP - in game chat channel) -
is my channel and the official channel of OrganizedPvP.
Hope you find this review useful guys - i wrote as much as i could with out writing a full 10 page review xD.

I was very happy when STO was announced for the first time; imagine that, a game that lets you be a Starfleet Officer, walk freely around onboard a Galaxy-class starship, and have a career. It seemed too good to be true. In the end it was, when the original concept was cancelled and turned into an early version of what STO is now. To be honest, I was too disgruntled to care for a long time. And I didn't.
Then I gave STO a try when it first turned "free-to-play" (F2P), and I didn't like it. I found it cumbersome, the character creation took forever, and generally the story seemed convoluted; I may have been biased a little, too, still.
Then I saw that they now have Tim Russ onboard reprising his role as Tuvok, and I thought I give it another try. And guess what, I actually like it. It's a vast universe, it's focussed on single-player gaming - which I prefer - and a lot of very well known locations and names show up the second you enter the sector map which is kind of a "real-time astrometrics display". I think that idea is very well done, including the controls. There is a bit of a learning curve, granted, and it takes time to get used to all the traits, skills, assignments, inventory etc., but as a Star Trek fan, a lot comes naturally. I don't find the missions repetitive at all, sure the  base idea/scheme is the same, but show me one game where that's not the case. There isn't one.
As a Star Trek fan, and having pretty much played every Trek based game there is, this is one of the better incarnations and currently the only one that depicts the Star Trek universe reasonably accurately. On top of it, the recent revamp of the Earth spacedock is literally breath taking. Plus, some in-game narration by Leonard Nimoy; bonus. It's F2P; give it the benefit of the doubt, and if you don't like it, worst case scenario, you're only losing some time, nothing else; after all, if you never take time, how can you ever have time?
Something else should be noted; depending whether you start playing as a Starfleet Officers, as a Klingon, or Romulan, the game will be a little different. It also seems that the storyline from the latest 2 Star Trek movies was incorporated to a certain extend.

Great graphics, great action, really good explosions always count for something, however the ground fighting could be better, and there should be slightly more variation in the types of missions there are.

If you're into Star Trek you'll see a lot of familiar characters and see where they've tied together the main canon and the new reboot movies. It's free and good for a fair few hours of tooling around, but I tend to uninstall it after finishing the content from each update.

Okay I know what you're thinking "this guy has only played 0.1 hours of the game so he has no idea what he's talking about". Just here me out. This game has issues from the get go. After my first of the game, I had no desire to play further. For starters, the AI is the worst I have ever seen. My goalie started with the puck, turned around and shot it in our own goal. 4 times. same thing from the other team. Their goalie either just handed it to my team or just turned around and shot it in his own goal. On top of that, i had no issues with framerate, but it is slow. The movement speed is simply slow and not engaging. A game about space hockey should be fun, energetic and exciting! However it just doesnt feel that way. In a game centered on sport action, the last thing you want is boredom as the player is running across the field to score a goal. I understand that this is early access, but if you're going to release a game to the public you need to make sure that it works. The bugs in this game can range from annoying to "are you ♥♥♥♥ing serious?". I'm sure these will all be fixed in the future but when you want to get some fans early on, the last thing you want is to drive them away with a game that infuriates them. As many others say, it's a good premise. However as it stands, it's a boring game that needs improvement.
I would reccomend for starters, to make the game faster paced. This way new players can look past some of the bugs and feel the rush of scoring a goal or intercepting a pass. Fast paced action in a game like this is key. Next, fix the bugs. I'm sure that they will, but making a game public access with bugs like this is not smart if you want people to buy your "adopter" packs and such. Nobody wants to put money into a game that has bugs like these.
I want this game to succeed I really do, I wouldn't have written this otherwise (I'm sure my gramatical errors show that I'm in a rush to type this). But it needs improvement. Early Acces is becoming more and more of a grey area as more and more games accept the practice, and if you want to compete, you cannot make a game like this public. It needs time is all, just give it some time.

This is a title where if I could have it ripped off of my account, I would.
I absolutely despise this game.
Ace of Spades: Battle Builder is a first-person shooter game with a mechanic that allows for adapting to constantly changing environments. The entire map can be destroyed and the player can also build upon the map with individual cube blocks and pre-made designs that vary from class to class.
Ignoring that this game is basically a first-person-shooter type game mixed together with minecraft building elements in a fairly poor fashion. It's not too bad, but the design could be improved upon other than seemingly relying on the hype of minecraft ideas and poorly tossing guns and god-awful mechanics into a game and then marketing it.
AoS:BB (originally just Ace of Spades before being bought by Jagex) I find to be a broken, unbalanced mess. I speak for a general public game and not actual private, team-based combat. General public games are a complete disaster. They have absolutely no spawn-protection to speak of, or at least so little of one I couldn't tell there was one even there. Where your team can get camped worse than people staking outside of a videogame store for a console or game release. This is heavily built upon a huge issue of snipers in this game. Snipers can dig themselves deep inside mountains, hide well in the environment, and quickly change locations to be particularly hard to kill. Also an added fact that they can snipe you still outside the max FoV (field of View). So you literally can actually not even be able to see them, unless they have a nice little laser reticle aimed at your head. Which by the way, this games hitbox on each persons head is absolutely ridiculous. I made a video critizing this product and pointing out during my video for my watcher to observe the kill-feed and see that almost every kill in this game tends to be a headshot. Which of course, anyone familiar with the FPS-scene knows that bullets that hit the head generally do critical amounts of damage. Which makes someone who may need a handful of bullets to kill, only need 1 to 4 at most.
The game has four classes, Marksman (Sniper), Commando (Heavy Weapons Guy), Rocketeer, and the Mechanic.
Starting with the Commando, the commando has a minigun, grenades, a rocket launcher, and I believe a pickaxe. The commando isn't really that bad of a choice, though that being said, it's either him or the marksman if you're trying to play seriously. The other two classes in my opinion are a joke.
The Minigun is slow to start and once it gets going it does a slew of damage and it takes out targets fairly quickly and in a reasonable matter. Because the games ever-shifting environment allows you to dodge that damage and figure ways to get out of that mess, it's pretty fair. His grenades are a joke and you'll only be using them to destroy the environment as players can easily avoid the grenades small radius. The rocket launcher is a great weapon but isn't really fair. Since one of the important aspects of this game is to take your enemies by-surprise to take them out since dying is pretty easy. That said, you cannot dodge the Rocket Launcher at point-blank. Therefore you will die and you couldn't do anything to avoid it. Unless your enemy is shooting those things from a distance, then you have an ample amount of time to dodge. Since dodging them is fairly easy and they move at a fair steady pace.
As a note. It's because the battlefield is constantly changing, it's very easy to surprise-attack enemies since there's nooks and crannies everywhere.
The Marksman uses a Sniper Rifle which one hit kills anyone if shot by the head. Which as I said. With the gigantic head hitboxes, is so easy that someone learning how to use the mouse will get rewarding shots like that consistently. The sniper also has the pistol which is generally a very balanced simple weapon only he can use I think, that it takes roughly 4-6 shots to the head with it and your enemy is toast (if they have 75%-100% health). The sniper uses a pickaxe.
The Rocketeer is a joke of a class and is in alpha-stage of it's design for how poorly it operates compared to other classes.
The Rocketeer uses a machinegun that does poor damage and has absolutely ridiculous recoil and is very innaccurate.
His rocketpack has little fuel and takes a considerably long amount of time to refuel. His rocketpack also shaves off roughly 15% of all fuel on-startup each hold. It goes up almost entirely vertically and covers relatively no distance horizontally which is illogical. There's no point to using this function unless you just want to get over a mountain quickly. He also has a gun that shoots blocks out to help make staircases and pathes for teammates. However, it's so badly designed and inaccurate even in close quarters to its target, there's no sense in using it. His only helpful tool is his sentry gun.
Though of course the sentry gun only does damage to those in proximity and doesn't deal punishing damage. So it's easy for others to immediately see it and dodge it while having relatively no hp loss. Also snipers will take them out in 1-2 bullets. And there's usually 3-5 players playing sniper a team generally.
Then we have the Miner, who has a shotgun, a drill, a shovel, and some dynamite.
The shotgun is not very effective at all as it has very high spread and the time between shots is so long that your opponent can quickly kill you while you're loading the next shot. The drill is an incredibly fun tool which digs GIGANTIC holes wherever you shoot it and it blows up at the end of it's course. This tool is insanely fun and incredibly satisfying to use, also particularly helpful too.
His dynamite is boring and it isn't nearly as helpful in destructive damage like the drill. Destroys very little and it's really just a lame equipment slot gimmick.
His shovel digs giant holes at a slower rate than the pickaxe. Also the shovel outdoes anything dynamite can do in just a few relatively moderate-speed swings.
That's all the classes. I forgot to mention that they all have a few more equipment choices outside the preset ones. But they're literally all so awful that the only choices you'll ever take is the other sniper rifle for marksman and the other shotgun for Miner.
The games maps are inspirative and fun and interesting to play on. That is, without the other players blowing them apart. You'll usually have people who's only goal each game is to destroy everything and so boring and dull that the color grey seems like it's as vibrant as the rainbow.
Then there's just simply you not having fun, because you can't do anything or enjoy the map because there's nothing but snipers everywhere causing you to be constantly in scaves and narrow passages and nooks an crannies. Or simply just out getting your head scoped-off on the battfield constantly. And I hate that. I've seen amazingly built maps that do nothing but pique my interest to play on and explore, to be ruined by snipers consistenly killing me and other players decimating the entire map.
Anywho, this review is getting rather lengthy. So lemme just quickly wrap it up with my quick summary of the game modes.
Team Deathmatch: Campers everywhere, complete map destruction, not very fun.
Zombies: Boring. You wander around somewhat aimlessly looking for humans and then you get quickly put out of your misery for a result.
Capture the Flag: Whichever team spawn camps the best to win, wins.
Base Destruction: I find this mode kind of fun, but ultimately no one every really bothers to really protect the main base (or play this gamemode for that matter.), so ultimately it gets destroyed quickly by a miner.
Excavation: Snipers camp the drop-off zone and kill you and have an ally pick up the diamond you were carrying and easily just toss it into the drop-off zone and have an easy point.
This game is terrible. Do not buy this game.

Possible suggestions?
I would LOVE to see some sort of.. threat element added to this game. It could be a sanity meter like Amnesia, a dependancy on light, or maybe the rats can hurt the player, or... I don't know, stepping in paint can coat the player's feet and attract ghosts? (I'm not good at this)
The game is definitely creepy, eerie, a bit spooky.. but to me, it's not scary. adding some sort of threat might help that.
Hm.. now that I'm thinking about paint.. maybe collecting diff colors of paint can ward against different enemy types?
OH or maybe paint can be used to reveal hidden passages or messages.
I'm getting a bit carried away now, hah.
Overall,
It's cute, I like it.
I definitely don't think I wasted my money since it's not yet finished, but right now it's a bit pricy for the amount of content.
I'm definitely looking forward to seeing where this goes!
