Don't let this game's detractors fool you. This is probably one of, if not THE best co-op game ever! It has challenged and since then altered my perception of what constituted the standard of "cooperation" for co-op games.
No doubt there is the perception of lack of content and numerous annoying bugs, however these have been slowly but surely addressed by Fatshark. These aren't game breaking bugs and in fact some add extra challenge to the already inherent difficulty.
A typical player can easily rack up a hundred hours in this game. That is an indication of the content and abundant replayability in Vermintide (that or player fanatics). The game has 2 game modes (aka Story and Survival) in 17+ maps   with 5 classes, each having a multitude of melee & ranged weapons. There are so many possible combination of playthroughs to keep the co-op experience alive and unique.
Due to Vermintide having a heavily player-skill-based melee system coupled with the possibility of ramping up the difficulty all the way to suit the player, it is both easy to learn yet hard to master. Forget about starting in anything less than Normal or Hard, you'll only fool yourself into burning through the content quickly. Ultimately, this game was designed to be played on the NIGHTMARE difficulty.
To me, Vermintide is an unforgettable flurry of intense action, great music, epic moments, interesting backstory and fantastic co-op experience which I'll always cherish.
I've met and made some of my best Steam friends through the gameplay whom I'll trust to guard my back in ANY other co-op game. THAT is how dependent this game is on sticking to each other and working together, which is like probably the 2nd commandment after "right click". I even bought my very first gaming headset for Vermintide just so I could use the mike to better communicate in-game.
Unlike other co-op games, there is completely no room for the elements of self-survival, highest kill-count competition (and the accompanying "money" rewards per "round"), showboating, camping, griefing or other nonsense. Please don't go looking for that kind of experience in this game. Vermintide co-op is all about working together as a team to ensure everyone stays alive to complete the mission.
Maybe you are so used to camping safely in a corner and "stealing" zombie kills from your team mates with your grenade launcher to get highest kill count. Maybe your modus operandi is modeled after some badass "lone-wolf" elite-special-forces-ghost-sniper-warrior capable of taking out half the enemy army himself with little support from anyone. In which case then I challenge you to consider buying this to treat yourself to a real paradigm shift.
The biggest negative is that the vast majority of the early playerbase have probably exhausted the content / gameplay and are feeling "burned out". Therefore in Non-NA regions, there is probably a great shortage of available players.
Overall, Vermintide is well worth the money spent on both the base game and its DLC(s). I mean come on, for that price - what were you expecting? Most AAA games costing thrice the price are exhausted in 30+ hours of gameplay with little multiplayer to offer. Solve the player base issue by buying Vermintide with 3 or more of your closest friends!

As of writing this, I've put around 10 hours into Scrap Mechanic. So far, my experience with the game has been thrilling and entertaining. While there aren't that many different blocks, building materials, etc. in the game currently, and creative mode is the only gameplay offering, there's still a surprising amount of stuff to create and play around with.
I'm sure there are a ton of crazy things other people have been able to construct given what's already available in the game. Maybe you'll find yourself building and decorating your own little home, including, of course, a sliding door and elevator. Or you could try your hand at building a hovercraft. Personally, I've spent a considerable amount of time making wheel-based vehicles; it's been fun modifying and tweaking my creations in an effort to make them more efficient. Like I said, I'm sure you too will find a way to express your creativity -- whether you like finding logical solutions, or simply making something silly.
Scrap Mechanic offers the tools and means to create in an easy to understand way. The interface is clean, and the system of building is, overall, fairly well-done. Although, there are a few minor annoyances here and there, I'm confident they'll be ironed out as development progresses. And, speaking of which, the development process seems to be both steady and involved, with the developers noting several big additions in the works. The ability to save, load & share the things you create being one I'm anticipating most!
If you like building stuff, from structures to vehicles, then I'd recommend Scrap Mechanic, both for what it offers currently and what it has potential for down the road!*
* Since this is an Early Access game, I'll be sure to make an effort to update this review once enough new content has been added to warrant it.

This is the kind of game that keeps me up at night.
Even after I've stopped playing, I think about which combinations of traits would create the ideal hunter, how much it's worth it to introduce sub-optimal genes to increase diversity of immunity genes, whether it's worth it to interbreed risking sickness to preserve certain traits, and much more.
I see some people saying this game isn't hard, but it isn't exactly easy either. If you aren't following a user-created guide after the tutorial, you're still going to have hours of learning ahead of you, and quite some time before you master it.
The rules of this game are all fairly simple and logical; you rarely sit around trying to remember how exactly a system works, because things generally work as you'd expect them to. I think the creators of this game have an incredibly solid base from which to further build this game, which brings up my one complaint.
This game is not done. The game's website acknowledges that "releasing" was just an attempt to raise attention and funds to continue development. The features are all there, the basis for the game is there, it just needs some expansion. It boasts over 100 genes to develop your species, but that really isn't as many as it sounds, especially when you include things like colorings, patterns, immunity genes, et cetera. Adding just a few more possibilities for the more functional features like jaws, horns, paws, bodies, tails, et cetera would go a LONG way in expanding this game.
The islands also need to be expanded, or better yet, reworked. The islands essentially serve as levels, the features of the island shaping the difficulty and ideal traits for that playthrough. Adding new island types would be cool, but this game really begs for sliders. Let us pick the climate, the scarcity of food, how hard it is to gather, how heavy on predators it will be, how strong they will be, what types we want to deal with, how many wild animals there are to recruit, et cetera. This is a pretty core feature of sandbox games, and this game feels incredibly sandboxy, so this part kind of seems like a no-brainer, and a mistake/oversight by the developer. Some further customization options like allowing us to alter the lifespan of our animals, our starting resources and our starting trie would also be nice.
All-in-all, I think this game is great as it is, and it has a pretty straightforward path to improvement.

The easy way out of this review would be to say "Just play it" but I feel like I gotta really dig both my hands into the flesh to talk about why I love this game so much.
I won't lie, I got exposed to this by the TBFP during their 4th Scariness Marathon of last October.  This was one of a few games I genuinely wanted to play.
First off the game is gorgeous.  For a Unity title it blows me away how beautiful it looks.  For one, it's the first time I've found a game with chromatic aberration that doesn't give me a migraine, and it runs surprisingly well on my PC (of course somehow Condemned Criminal Origins gets down to 15 FPS but this game on max runs smooth).  Everything just looks brilliant.
Gameplay is, as much as some might not like me to say, very PT-like.  You go through rooms, doors shut/lock behind you, and you look around the room at stuff and either the door opens or you find a way out.  The game's got a nice way that the doors and some puzzle objects work, a very Frictional-games-ish mechanic.
Now, the atmosphere/story.  I've played games that freak me out but not many have had me as freaked as this game has.  Some might think the whole "haunted house" situation is a bit overdone and there's agreement to be had.  But this game does it so well that it almost feels wrong calling it a trope.  The game describes itself as a "psychedelic horror game" and at first it sounded weird to me but after playing as far as possible at the moment, I see what they mean.  Psychological horror gets under your skin but this game plays tricks on you like no other.  It seems to have lots of fun with disappearing acts, the "now-you-see-me-now-you-don't" shtick, and a lot triggers based on things you're looking at/not looking at.  Either I'm really predictable when I play horror games or the devs behind this one know just what strings to pull and at the perfect moments.  There were one or two times however, where I triggered an event by looking at an item to progress without actually picking up the item (because I didn't know it was an item), which is a bit weird but that's really my only gripe with it all.  The twists and turns offered by the game really pull you under and even the simplest of sounds get to you after a while.  You start to feel like even the brightly lit areas aren't safe.  The story is one of the parts of this game that really caught my eye [SORT OF SPOILERS AHEAD.]
It's always interested me to play a game as a sort of antagonist.  Among the Sleep made quite a stir a year ago with its story about how a toddler perceives an abusive alcoholic parent.  However, this game takes an interesting approach as you play as the drunk, unstable husband (and father) in the family.  Since you play as him, a lot of the game is almost like what you could be forgiven for thinking is the player character having vengeance taken upon him by his family members, a lot of moments sort of put you in their shoes so to speak.  There's a scene (you'll know it when you get to it) that basically has you on the wife's level.  Early in the game everything appears fine but as you progress you see the facade slip away and the whole situation that our painter is in becomes clear and much more apparent as you walk through the impossible space of his house. [END SPOILERS.]
The voice acting is a bit shaky, a lot of times it feels like the game engine's lighting system is nerfed purely to serve the horror aspect, but those are the only other issues I have with the game.  Overall, it's a solid psychological horror story with great feel, atmosphere, tension, and brilliant design.  Definitely one of the best horror games I've played, only it's not finished.  But of the 80% of the game I've seen, it's golden.

The Showdown Effect is a multiplayer only 2.5D shooter. For you who doesn't know 2.5D means that you have 3D character models put in a 2D movement plane. TSE is a fun game, it's competitive multiplayer, with few modes, most popular Deathmatch and Expendables. Deathmatch is self-explanatory , Expendables is a match where there're two teams: one is custom made characters who are defending themselves from the other team who are players who spawn with random weapons.
Gameplay is really slick, you run, slide, wall-jump to get to higher places, you shoot from pistols, SMGs, machine guns, RPGs, slicing with swords. When a round is near the end, big "SHOWDOWN" pops up, and sick guitar riff starts playing, background is starting to explode, that means that it's the end of the match and it's time to see who will be the last man standing: everybody gets full health, no respawn, last man standing gets bonus points. You have in-game store in which you spend money for costumes and weapon skins (only cosmetic changes, there are no buffs in this game) or you can go in "Unlockables" tab and spend points you earn in matches for same things. You also have various characters with various abilities, like temporary shield, poison bomb, rocket boost, etc.
The game is really fun, it has really well done soundtrack, gameplay is interesting, graphics are really nice, and if you have a chance to buy it, I strongly advise you do.

The game is just a mess. I don't usually write reviews but this game really struck me the wrong way just because of how excited I was for it and how disappointed I was once I started playing, so here I am. I like to give games a chance before I make a judgement but this just starts off wrong.
The game is tedious, with the gameplay revolving around moving a small selection of spaces and looking for food, or trying to get nesting material, which is slow. The need for food means you'll probably have the majority of your creatures sitting by a bush, using each of their three turns to collect berries.
Your animals die too fast for you to really get a good grasp of the genes, the functionality of them, or make any attachment. I find in games that getting attached to a character or an aspect of gameplay is the best way to really love something and get involved. The breeding system seems to be nothing more than a gimmick to get you to play the game, while the turn system is horribly, terribly bad and doesn't instill a use of strategy, but rather imposes a limit on playability.
The strategy of the game seems to revolve around sitting characters in front of foods and doing nothing with them except gathering, or occassionally moving a group towards a predator and then picking up the food they drop if they die, and then breeding while working still not moving the creatures you have gathering. You'll also battle grass that regrows in a couple of days and hinders your gameplay, while really not granting any substance to the game as a whole. Disease and illness are another thing you'll probably run into, but it doesn't have enough substance (notice a theme yet?) to make gameplay interesting.
The game is not worth $18, its more worth $10, or even $5, considering the content. There is more variety in some mobile games and I feel like this is the type of game you'd find on the app store for $0.99 rather than $18 on Steam. This is probably a good childs education game, if you have an instuctor going over it with them to teach them how genes work at a purely base level, thats about all its good for and thats even a stretch.
Save your money, the combination of a bad breeding system, a gene system where variety comes from a majority of cosmetic changes, and the shortness of not only each creatures turn, but also shortness of your creatures lives, makes this game a hard pass.
Remember the No Man's Sky release and its lack of content? This is it, all over again.

TL;DR :
A well crafted and intriguing storyline with a huge focus on atmosphere horror game that worth buying ON SALE. Those who have played or experienced P.T and enjoy Silent Hill-esques vibe will definitely be right at home.
Overview :
Layer of Fear is a psychological horror game that focus heavily on atmosphere and a well written story. You are a painter who is definitely losing his♥♥♥♥♥♥as he progress through a labyrinth of insanity to finish his magnum opus. Also eerily good piano soundtrack to keep your pants wet.
Gameplay :
Since the game primarily focus on player experiences, it does an astounding job in creating the atmosphere that truly make your skin crawl. The game also use its music perfectly to immerse the player in the experience. However, you don't do much inside the game except walking, opening and examining item which truth be told, kinda get repetitive and tiresome. Not to mention it is easy to get a headache trying to find things in the dark.
Jumpscares are use decently in the game. It ain't your cheap in-your-face jumpscares but a very well thought one. Although there are a few that you could certainly see miles away, it is mostly a 'welcoming' one that you will enjoy.
There are a few puzzles, nothing mind bending and mainly to trick you into looking at a certain stuff. Replayability is there but not really something you would spend your time with unless you are hunting for achievements.
Overall, it is a walking simulator but a decent one.
Story :
Don't worry there ain't gonna be a spoiler here.
As mention above this is a walking simulator. Except it is a horror game and is rich with subtle story that is conveyed beautifully throughout the exploration. The pacing is okay and it certainly make you craved for more as you uncover the mystery surrounding the protagonist and his family.
Make no mistake though, the story is still a rather cliche one and chances are you will forget it in a day.
Soundtrack :
The dread, melancholic but beautiful song performed by Arkadiusz Reikowski really bring the game atmosphere alive. Every single tense moment in the game were achieved thanks to the song and you certainly would get hooked to it.
Conclusion ;
A boring gameplay, forgettable cliche story with a great soundtrack.

HEX: Origins:
~~~~~~~~~~

What do you call a shape who has six sides? You’re dead right, it’s a hexagon. Now, imagine a multiple number of hexagonal tiles joined together, what would you call that? Wow, you guys are so good! It is indeed a pattern. Let’s make it slightly more difficult. What would you call a pattern of hexagonal tiles which must be filled with coloured hexagons connected together as a shape, while making sure one side of each hexagon touches another hexagon of the same colour? So. . . you’re stuck now, hey! It’s simple. . . it’s Hex Origins, of course!
Hex: Origins is a casual puzzle game which offers over eight hundred levels within four types of modes, as well as a level editor to create your own maps.
As you might already know, I am a big fun of puzzle games, and I must admit that Hex: Origins grabs my attention straight away. As I mentioned above, the game offers four types of gameplay, which are: classic, flow, exploration and treasure hunting.
The first two are very similar and have three levels of difficulty available. However, you must successfully win a certain number of stages to unlock the next difficulty. The main difference between the two modes is that in the flow mode, you have to make sure a flow of the same colour has been established between the emitter and receiver, which are located at each extremity of the pattern. For example, if the emitter and receiver are of the colour blue, you have to make sure a flow of blue hexagon tiles is connected from one to the other first, and secondly, that you manage to cover all remaining tiles to win that stage. The exploration mode is pretty much building a pattern until you use all remaining moves. And the treasure hunting can be unlocked when you find maps during the classic or flow modes.
The gameplay is very simple but extremely addictive. Let’s take the classic mode, for example; a pattern of empty hexagon tiles will be displayed on your screen. At the bottom of the screen, you’ll be presented with five different shapes of hexagons; some will have two, three or even more coloured hexagons. You might have two blue hexagons or one orange and one blue. What you have to do is to use those to fill in the pattern of empty tiles in a specific number of moves to win the stage. As soon as you win the stage, you will receive coins as well as other rewards, such as maps for the treasure quest levels, or power ups.  Power ups are pretty useful when the level of difficulty is rising. One of them is the bomb. By activating it, you’ll be able to clear a certain area which in turn can help you finish a stage.  Delete your previous move, or even recolour a tile, to help you finish the level and score three stars for it. With the coins you earned, you can purchase additional power ups at the store, which can be extremely handy if you have none left.
Graphically, the game runs well, looks ok and the soundtrack is very smooth.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Easy to play and very addictive
-	Over 800 levels
-	Three levels of difficulty
-	Four modes of play plus a level editor
-	Achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	No trading cards at this stage
Hex: Origins is a fun and well-designed casual game, and you’ll always find time to play it!

TL;DR - an action horror game that fails to be both action and horror but somehow kept me playing, 5/10.
It's a shame. This game is one of those that "have potential", however it wastes it all. Let's start with what this game is supposed to be (quote from game's site) "a game embodying the meaning of pure survival horror." or even (Wikipedia) "psychological survival horror" turns out to be a poor action game with lots of gore in it.
The "psychological" part, I think, indicates that nothing makes sense (which is sadly often the case). The story is extremely dumb and unclear throughout the whole game it's actually amazing. There was no point where I finally understood what the hell is actually going on. The way it is presented, the way the characters moves from one location to another, the completely redundant and unrelated notes, journals and audio tapes create one big confusing mess. Characters that are in the game are all stright out of "Most cliche characters in Japanese medias", without even slight changes made. Their lines are written so poorly (or the localization to the western market was so poor) they made me cringe every 10 minutes. They have no depth, no backstory (main character's past is presented with journals we found at specific rooms, but it it absolutely unrelated from the game and also fits to the cliche model of this character), they do not grow, change, show emotion. Nothing.
The other part, "horror", should be replaced with just "gore". There is nothing really scary in this game, only ugly and brutal monsters. The atmosphere is lacking, the main villan looks like he'd be down from 1 hit, multiple events that could be potentially scary are so grotesque they are instead funny. All this increases as the game goes on and it changes from a reather stealthy one to a full-out action game, that's made poorly. It tried to keep it's "survival" part by giving little ammo (Btw I just hate how games call themselves survival just because there's little ammo and there's absolutely no other survival part) which only made it frustrating, when as it goes on the amount of opponents becomes riddiculus.
On the technical side it's no better. Even though some of the locations looked good as long as you didn't come too close, and some models were done very well (safe head!) there was a tone of blurry textures and low poly models. Despite that the games runs terribly. On a 980Ti, with framerate "unlocked" (which also forces vsync on!) I had 30-40 FPS with CONSTANT stuttering. It looked a bit better with a 30 FPS lock, but it still often dropped to 28, causing small stutters. For a game looking like this this is not acceptable. Additionally, turning black bars and grain postprocess by the fault to make it more "cinematic" just shows how ignorant the people behind the PC versions were, or how little money was put into the port. Another, one big technical issue is the camera, constantly jumping, twitching, stuttering, blocking on meshes, getting inside of meshes etc. Also there was a lot of other, smaller bugs, like goats bigger than men, collision-less meshes, LODs cutting off text on signs.. Really sloppy work.
However, despite all of that I kept going, hoping it will all make sense in the end. Even though it didn't, and even despite the absurd final boss fight I didn't really feel like I've wasted that 15h. I had a lot of frustration and even more disappointment which is why I do not recommend this game, but still I also had some fun.

Despite the fact that I'm initially not recommending this game. I must say that this game was perhaps among my favorites to play. To me it felt like an interesting experiment. It felt like a MOBA in terms of mechanic, but it felt like a third person shooter in terms of gameplay and it ultimatelly created quite a unique experience. I moved on to a game like Smite that also prides itself in being a '3rd person MOBA' -- But Smite feels too rooted in it's MOBA mechanics for the 3rd person camera to serve more purpose other than a small and sligtly unique niche. SMNC had a nice balance to it's MOBA mechanics and it's 3rd person gaming elements. The arena and stereotypically commercial commentary was also quite pleasing.
Now for the bad things.. It had it's buggy issues at times and there were many complaints in terms of balance -- but I find a majority of that to be too nit-picky and if you actually participated in the forums; the devs might've listened to you. The problem with this game was opening itself to a new audience. It felt like it didn't attract much of the MOBA crowd, nor the gamers into third person shooting. Hence I felt like it wasn't advertise well and despite some support from a small, but dedicated fanbase.. well.. the game hasn't been updated since the dawn of the planet of the apes. This game has been abandoned. The devs have abandon it and so there's not much purpose to play a dead game.
tl;dr: Fun game with much potential, but was unfortunetly left to crash and burn.

The story is clearly a bit tongue in cheek as you can't take it totally seriously. But that's fine, you don't come to this sort of game for a story. With that being said, one playthrough of this game will take you less then an hour. You certainly won't be battling forever, but you'll get enough enjoyment out of it for your money.

A testament to the ideal that graphics mean absolutely nothing in terms of a game's quality!
(Short Answer)
It's a solid game with brilliant mechanics and wonderful gameplay that completely overshadow its terrible graphics!
(Long Answer)
I'm a strong believer that, while amazing graphics can really help captivate players, they should ALWAYS be an afterthought to a game's mechanics. Mount & Blade: Warband only helps to reinforce my beliefs in such thinking. Graphically I'm sure that a 10 year old could come up with a more visually compelling game, however you'd be hard-pressed to find another game that matches this one in the solidity of its mechanics.
The fighting is complete chaos incarnate as anywhere from a handful to hundreds of soldiers on each side of the battlefield scurry about like chickens with their heads cut off. Yet somehow amidst all of the carnage, there is a beauty and complexity. The melee is simple enough to control, and the ranged weapons offer a fair way of taking out enemies with skilled/lucky shots.
Of course Mount & Blade isn't just about the fighting! There are equal amounts of strategy required for every bit of bloodshed. This aspect is simple enough when you travel alone or in a small contingent, but throw in a few dozens (or even hundreds) of soldiers at your beck and call and things begin to get more complicated. By the time your character leads a small army and a few larger settlements, every single move you make in the world can have serious repercussions. The age old question of, "Should I befriend him and marry his daughter, or murder him and pillage his kingdom?" comes into play more often than you'd think.
On a similar note, the AI show quite a bit of competency. The lower ranking soldiers might as well be armored gorillas, but train a few of them to higher ranks and you now have extremely capable officers in your army. The same can be said for your enemies as well as your subordinates, as enemy commanders are often quite challenging to defeat without the proper preparations. For NPCs, they make the interactions in the game truly political.
It wouldn't be entirely fair if I didn't talk about the graphics for at least a little bit, since there are plenty of you out there that graphics matter the most. The graphics honestly look like something out of the 90's, beloning on the N64 or PS1. Character customization is turned into something of a joke, trying to make the derpiest looking creature possible rather than something that could at least pass for human without a second glance. Despite the simplistic (if not atrocious) appearance of most characters and landscapes, the movement (especially the combat) is suprisingly fluent. You won't really have to worry about messing up in a vital shot of your bow/swing of your sword in combat.

The melee system is extremely satisfying and is the embodiment of "easy learn but difficult to master". Unlike L4D2 when you get hit it's for a good reason and almost always can be avoided.
The loot system can turn some people off but the developers have drastically improved it recently with the Q&C DLC and the improved loot tables.
This honestly is a great game and I can't recommend it enough. Sure there are many glitches and bugs but for majority of the time they do not take away from the amazing experience that is slaying skaven.
If you like Left 4 Dead then you'll definitely like this.

I review indie games over at my site
and this is a copy of the review I wrote for the full version of Battle Forever on 06/24/16.
Battle Forever is an arcade style Beat’em Up game that was developed by Inferno Games and is currently available on Steam. (At the time of this review the game is currently 30% off the regular price of $3.99) I originally reviewed the Tech Demo of this game a few weeks ago so this review is based on the full game. For the record, I played through the story mode to completion with one of the characters in a little over an hour then proceeded to try out the survival mode prior to reviewing this game.
If you have not read my original review of the Tech Demo please check it out here:
-INITIAL THOUGHTS-
So I want to start off by clarifying some things that may not be popular knowledge. For those who don’t know this game was made in 150 days by 1 person with the help of his friend. Now nowhere does it say that on the Steam page does it say that and I think it should considering that would greatly change the opinion of some people who would potentially discredit the game. The only reason I know this information to be true is because I’ve been following the developer diary for this game since February.
-PRESENTATION-
Battle Forever features retro style graphics that take the player back to the classics. The artwork, along with the music really helps the player feel like they are playing an old arcade game. Visually I like the artwork and feel that it starts to get more detailed over the course of the game. I also really liked the UI layout. It is simple and easy to navigate. Other than that I can't really say much on the game's presentation.
-ENGAGEMENT/GAMEPLAY-
I enjoyed playing this game and had a lot of fun with it but sadly the engagement and replayability value for this game is not as high as I had hoped from playing the demo. As expected, Battle Forever’s main source of engagement comes from beating up enemies but unfortunately not much more than that. There are achievements the player can try to accomplish, some of which involve defeating a certain amount of enemies or using a certain move a certain number of times but other than that I felt the engagement was pretty low for me. There didn’t seem to be any reason for me to go back and play through the game again after beating the story mode the first time and I ended up losing interest in survival mode after about 20 or so waves of the set of enemies in the same order.
Gameplay on the other hand was much improved and seemed a lot more balanced from the Tech Demo I originally played. The knockback of the strong attack was significantly decreased to feel more real and make the game more challenging. What I liked most was the evolution of enemies from one stage to the next. Essentially the game simply has two types of enemies (not including bosses), those with long ranged attacks and those with short ranged attacks. However as the player advances through stages the enemies get tougher by increasing the range, damage, health, defense, or even the amount of a unit and by the end the game does get incredibly challenging due to the sheer number of enemies the player has to face.
-OVERALL-
Considering that this game was made by a solo developer in such a short amount of time, I can’t help but like it. On the other hand, I personally feel like the game’s current state is best for a one-shot play though and doesn’t leave too much replayability value in my opinion. However, I would still recommend this game to people who really like Beat’em Up games or retro games in general. If you enjoy potentially hours of using your fists to beat up waves of enemies then I highly recommend this game to you and would greatly recommend check out the survival mode.

As a horror movie fan, I really enjoy Layers of Fear. It does the types of things that current horror movies do to produce scares (misdirection, loud noises, eerie music). Unlike current horror movies, LOF really maintains the fear factor with its players. There were certain times where I really had to take a moment and breath. And other times I was playing through partially squinted eyes.
The game play is slow, but it is made to be. You are exploring the psyche of a drunken painter so of course you would move slow. There are times, however, where it picks up and makes you quickly move to your next checkpoint.
The subtle changes in the environment as the "levels" progress are astounding. Some of the creepiest parts are seeing pictures and furniture changing as you walk past them, only to turn around and see that they have gone back to normal, and turn around AGAIN and see that they have completely distorted.
I highly recommend this game for anyone looking to play a good horror game with great story telling.
BE SURE TO PLAY IT WITH HEADPHONES ON AND THE LIGHTS OFF!!!

Awesome game with awesome developers
That being said, this game isn't going to be for everyone, the learning curve is somewhat steep, with the highest difficulty being near impossible even for experiences players.
The loot system is also very different from other games, and while it did suck back at launch, they have added several (free) DLCs that address this issue, the current loot system is fine. Anyone still complaining about the loot system after the Q&C update either hasn't updated their review or wants their items handed to them on a silver platter with no effort.
As to the DLC. This studio knows how to do DLC right. Not only are their paid DLCs reasonably priced for what you get, they also alternate between free and paid DLC. Even if you don't buy the paid ones, you can still play on those maps by joining a game hosted by someone who did buy the DLC, they don't split the community based on who bought what.
The combat is visceral and fun, pretty much all the weapons are super satisfying to slice or crunch or smash rats with. You can chop off arms and heads and legs, as well as cut rats clean in half.
I think a lot of people didn't know what to expect from this game, hence the negative reviews. This game is heavily dependant on teamwork, if you think you're going to run off on your own and slaughter all the rats single handedly, you will die. This game also does a really good job of poirtraying the Warhammer universe in the End Times, the voice acticing is phenomenal, both the writting and the delivery.
The Characters are awesome too: The Dwarf is always half-drunk and jovial, the witch hunter has a stick up his♥♥♥♥♥ the elf is condescending to everyone, the fire wizard will mumble to herself about giant pyres of burning bodies, and the solider is always trying to boost everyone's morale.
The maps are all varied, there are some where you're killing rat men in the middle of town, some you kill rat men out in the woods, some you kill rat men in caves. The maps are all true to the lore and packed with cool little visual details, all the main missions have 3 tomes and 2 grimoires hidden on them (these increase your chance of getting good dice rolls at the end of the map, with grims giving you a 100% chance dice at the expense of lowering your max health)
This is one of my favorite games, but it's not going to be for everyone. If you want a deep, challenging co-op experience with a high skill ceiling, and don't mind not always getting the exact item you want every time, then this could be your next favorite game.
Oh yea, you also should be okay with killing filthy rat-men. You will kill A LOT of filthy rat men.

It's free, no doubt about it. However, this is one of those games that is a very classic P2P (pay to play). The starting weapons are complete garbage of course, but any above tier weapon requires constant grind. I play two battles, get 17k ingame monies. To get the bolt action Kar98k, you need around 91k. That's over a dozen matches I would need to grind just to get a slightly better rifle. Not to mention that the game constantly taunts you for not subscribing (as any p2p would) by taking away 60% of "would be" xp and offering the ingame currency of "gold" (which you buy with your hard earned irl shekels) for unlocking various tiers of weapons and equipment. It's just not worth the time and energy as you'll be accomplishing very little over a very long period of time (unless you really have nothing else to spend your money on).
Now overall, this game is very ambitious with it's combination of armor battles, minor dogfights, and (sort of) real time strategy. It's very impressive, but it's pretty overwhelming for any newcomers and can be quite confusing to figure out. It would be interesting if the p2p mechanic didn't brutally murder the fun out of it.

Cons: Not a alot of pvp(few maps and no reputation as of yet),  No end game raiding(there are elite stf and hard content, but no large scale raiding), Lock boxes(almost a pro becuase they can be opend by ingame grinding, but if you spend money to open them you will blow throw a weeks check trying to get a ship), Ground combat(I know they are updating it a bit, but its so far where space combat is, still i am hopeful)

Now thats not to say I havent dumped a few thousand dollars, over the life of this game, on this company.   Its really nice and they make so much money now that the updates come every few months.  Also, the content is very well done. Hours and hours of gameplay with no grindy feeling. The company is also pretty generous and lets the players have alot of stuff free that others would charge out the♥♥♥♥♥for.  Its not a big pvp game right now, but give it time and I think that that will change drastically. Possibly later this year. As I said major updates and content releases are every few months. Honestly it doesnt even feel like a free to play except i dont pay a monthly fee.
This company also has a unique way of pulling you back in to play it with updates and events.  I lose intrest from time to time or see another shinny game. Due to it being early access, I have yet to completely finish this game, but I've really enjoyed myself so far (if by "enjoy", you mean being scared out of my mind and unable to play this on my own). The game has a haunting, chilling atmosphere, only strengthened by the weird artwork and the protagonist's paranoid mind. You never know if what you're seeing is really there.
You play the game as a former famous artist, a painter, walking through your large mansion and exploring your surroundings. Several clues along the way tell you what must have happened to put the protagonist in the confused, slightly psychotic state he is in now -- a fire during a grand gallery opening, a drinking problem, grotesque paintings, a missing wife...
This game is all about psychological horror, hallucinations, and perception. While exploring the house, you uncover clues that slowly reveal your/the protagonist's scary past. The game is very apt at playing with your own perception, making the surroundings change with each turn of your head -- these morphing environments combined with the great soundtrack make for a bone-chilling atmosphere.
+ Psychological horror at its finest
+ Great use of moving/changing environments to induce terror
+ Chilling atmosphere thanks to great visuals and ambient sounds
+ Creepy paintings and works of art
- There are some jump scares here and there
- The puzzles are sometimes a little easy to solve
- Creepy wife trope for no good reason is getting a little old
- You
die at some points, but it's not like you absolutely have to hide away from monsters
Overall, it's a great game that really plays with your perception. Doors, windows, hallways, they all change as soon as you walk through or past them, and this is timed really well. Seriously, just when you feel something is off and you turn around -- BAM, it's gone. There are some jump scares, but they're not too cheaply used, and the voice acting is okay.
I'm really curious to see how this one will turn out and what the eventual resolution of the story will be! Hopefully all will be revealed once we've gathered all of the clues...

Ace of Spades is the first person,32 player, Team Fortress 2 and Minecraft inspired love child by Jagex Limited. AoS takes the best innovations from other hit games such as TF2 and Minecraft to make something unique. Aos is a multiplayer only game that takes TF2's class system with a Minecraft's look and creation and destruction. There are 4 main classes each with special abilities and weapons in Aos; The Marksman, Engineer, Commando, and Miner. In this team based shooter it is important to utilize the classes correctly to actually work as a team. There is such a diverse way of the playing the game that there will not be session where you will play the same map the same way. For example you need to capture a flag within a castle. Instead of generically storming the front door, you can fly to the top, break the walls down, dig underneath it, or even build a tower to get inside. The way of taking of objectives are really up to the imagination of the player and his or her team. Also in AoS, boring maps are not a thing. The maps included in AoS is extremely varied, everything from defending a castle from invading ships, Moonbase, to a map with a huge dinosaur in the middle! and the inclusion of the Steam Workshop allows users to create&post  their own maps, so there is basically endless possibilities for maps. The game modes include Capture the Flag, Demolition, Team Deathmatch, King of the hill and much much more. But by far the Zombie mode was my favorite. Out of all the players, 1 starts out infected and goal is to infect other players. Slowly one by one the survivors began to dwindle and the undead began to rise. Panic begins to rise on the survivor team while they frantically try to defend their towers they built. The mode is loads of fun especially when with friends or having a talkative team. Unfortunately that is also the problem with the game. If you are not playing with friends and using strategy the game can become a mess and loose its fun. Also I noticed that finding a nearly full game was difficult. I would click the ranked or player matches and it would load me into a empty lobby. Fortunately they recently added a server browser. Its a same that the game has more empty servers than actual players because the game is actually really fun and worth the money. Plus the soundtrack is pretty good too :) .
Overall
Ace of Spades is a great game that takes the best of games and puts them together. Incredibly fun combat with teamwork and great original game modes as well as a vast supply of unique maps make this game a great experience with friends. Otherwise it kinda falls flat. If you can find a match that is, it is worth a buy, to play for a weekend at least.

I love Deus Ex, and I love Deus Ex: Human Revolution.  Honestly they are both top tier games and while I think the original is better, Human Revolution holds up a little better to the ravages of digital time.   I recently played Mankind Divided and found it to be lacking Deus Ex style almost to the point of not recommending it.   But ultimately I gave it the nod.
I wish I played The Fall before that.  Mankind Divided would look like a masterpiece next to this game.
But this isn't a revised review of Mankind Divided yet, so let's look at this game simply based on the criteria of just a mobile port of Deus Ex.
The first thing that struck me as I started the game is that it attempted the same productions values as the consoles which was impressive... until I saw that they seemed to missed the mark.  The game does try to capture that feel of Deus Ex but when your cutscenes are shortened, low resolution, and the story doesn't live up to the original game,  The facade doesn't last.
What's worse is this could work.  Give a compelling character, and write a short story, maybe a few mop up operations, maybe someone who gets caught up in Sarif industries in the first game, it might actually be interesting as a companion piece.  Instead the game tries very hard not to rely on Human Revolution, and yet tries to be like it.
The story is very weak to say the least.  It's mostly about Neuropozyne shortages and a replacement drug by the name of something I can't really remember how to spell but starts with an R.  The R drug appears to be killing people and they're keeping it quiet.  That's the entire story for the four hours of gameplay.  There's this idea that the main character is on the run from the "Tyrants" a group under one of the bosses of Human Revolution (the game tries to play this as a twist that known enemy of Adam Jensen is a bad guy.  Umm... you guys forgot he was already a villain in another game?)
But the "Tyrants" aren't really well developed, not surprising as again there's about four hours of content here, but that's a common problem.  Adam Jensen isn't the best character, he's a bit bland and just "Head of Security" in Human Revolution.  Yet he has some personality that the player defines.  Ben Saxon (I only found out his last name late in the game, it wasn't a twist, they just never used it except when they referred to someone as Saxon... oddly enough it never felt like they were referring to me when they said it)  is an ex military augmented soldier.
In the world of Deus Ex Mankind Divided that would stand out, in the world of Deus Ex HR that might be interesting.  In the world of the Fall it basically means "he has augmentations like Jensen" and that's it.   He's just a very typical protagonist in a first person shooter, and while he does talk, it doesn't really matter.
In fact much of the dialogue falls into the same area.  Bland and meaningless.  "Go here and do something."  Rarely do people tell you anything other than a simple mission, where as in the original games the dialogue and story is rich, this game just sends you to locations to complete objectives.
Hell the game even starts with a scene where the player head shots three enemies with a cross bow, the second time through it seemed like it was a different gun and that one was tranquilizing the enemies, in the original play through though, you're straight up murdering them.  It doesn't invalidate a no kill walk through but... guys, Deus Ex does certain things.   No kill SHOULD be the thing you heavily hint at to push players towards.
On the other hand it's simple to do.   There's very little challenge in the game, I believe that's moving from a phone to the controller definitely enabled the user to be more skillful, but the game doesn't seem any harder.   It's relatively easy and with no difficulty option there's only one setting for that.
However I will say the game is marvelous at one thing.  Level design.  After playing Prey I really respect Deus Ex's level designs where it always feels like there's more than two ways through any door.   You never feel like you can't win because of a bad build and in fact a no augmentation build can beat this game if you really want to.  That's quite fun.  The game is a little too fast to give away passwords and codes even those you won't need, but overall the level design IS perfect for Deus Ex.
I don't want to bash the graphics but this is the series first chance to see Alex Vega who appears in Deus Ex Mankind Divided.  Well I think it's her, she's white, with a military hair cut, in Mankind Divided she's black with dreads (forgive me if that's incorrect, I literally don't know any hair styles).  Why the change?  Was this game trying to make a link to Mankind Divided?  Ok but it's also got to be a prequel to Human Revolution?   Ok so it came out midway between the games, but why get character's skin color and look wrong?  This is our first chance to meet Alex Vega and yes that is THE Alex in Mankind Divided, so why do it wrong?
The graphics though for a phone would be fine, but for a computer, you shouldn't be expecting anything of quality.  I played this in 4k and it looked... ok it looked weak, I don't think anyone should expect anything better, but dear god the character models looked like something from a Playstation 2 era games, I get it, but couldn't the PC have a little bit better quality content?
But overall as a phone game.... well honestly I wouldn't want to play it for a couple reasons.
First, The main character is uninteresting, and in addition the story is bland as hell.   Deus Ex is intrigue and that's what Mankind really missed out on, but this game just can't even keep up with any of the games.  Even Invisble War the forgotten game is better than this.
Second, the levels are good, but nothing else feels right, it's not really Deus Ex just because of good level design though that helps a lot and I was ready for a shell of the original game.  The level design is fantastic, it's just the reason for me to go through a level isn't the best.
Third and most important, the game is unfinished.  At the end of the game the game asks you if you want to go to another location warning that side quests will be canceled.  I figured it's time for one last scene or level.  I click yes and.... TO BE CONTINUED.  I really hated how Mankind Divided ended, but having a final boss, a mostly concluded story and a bad cliff hanger is better than saying "Should I load the next area" and then instead give me a "TO BE CONTINUED" screen.  Spoiler it wasn't continued.
Deus Ex the Fall currently retails at 1 dollar on Google play, and while I won't recommend it on the phone that's an interesting price, as it puts it up against games like Reigns which I think even that is more expensive.  It started at 7 dollars which is too much but honestly.  It really did try to do a lot on a mobile phone and I do find that impressive, it's just not a mobile phone game falling between a console game and a game you play while you sit on the toilet.  But ok it's a good attempt, even if weak.
However now let's talk about the PC Version.  I paid 2 bucks for this.  I paid 1 dollar for "I can't believe it's not gambling" I also paid 9 bucks I believe for Mankind Divided.  Human Revolution Director's Cut goes for 3 dollars.  The point I'm trying to make is that games are also cheap on Steam, it's low price doesn't make it good, but it puts it in a different price range, and the fact is at under ten dollars, there's a lot of far better games to play.
If you haven't played Human Revolution and even Mankind Divided, go play them, the next steam sale will have them for under 10 bucks.  Well worth the price, and far better than this by a magnitude of hundred times.  They're just fantastic games.  This however is not.  Hard do not recommend, and it really is a cash grab to bring a sub par game over. Do not waste your four hours or money.

B) Play a Match-3 game with the girls to raise their "affection level", get them to 4/5 and they'll send you and Ecchi picture of them, get them to 5/5 and you can access a minigame to f*ck them and win an Hentai picture of them.
This is the game mechanic. The puzzle games are surprisingly fun and addictive and the manga are (not so) surprisingly well drawn and quite pleasurable to look at. Another brilliant game by Shinj Mikami. Psycho Break (the Japanese title of the game) does the genre of survival horror proud. There will be many times in the game where the player will run out of ammo, have no health items, surround by death traps and being chased by huge enemies. This game has elements that work well in horror games. The player will resort to sneaking around and disarm traps for parts to create ammo for the awesome Agony Crossbow. There are also pistols, rifles, shotguns and a magnum,
The enemies that the player will face are gruesome, relentless and ugly. Enemies do not stay dead if you blast a bunch of holes in them. Headshots and burning the bodies are the only way to make sure the enemies stay dead. Boss battles are tense and challenging. Psycho Break has macabre puzzles to solve. One puzzle requires the player to jab needles into precise locations on three different brains.
As for the story, it is best for the player decide.
The game is brilliant, but there are some cons. The game on a first playthrough, the game is long; sadly that is because of the many times the player will die. The game can be completed under five hours; there is an achievement for this as well. The game is unforgiving; especially in the insane Akumu ( Japanese for "nightmare") mode. Akumu mode makes the game extremely unforgiving and one touch from enemies is game over.
The game does turn from survival horror to survival action in later chapters. It is highly similar to Biohazard 4 in this regard.  Psycho Break also has been notably influenced by Silient HIll. The Keeper is far too similar to Pyramid Head; and even the final battle with the Keeper is reminiscent of the final battle with Pyramid Head in Silient Hill 2. Whilst this may not be a bad thing, it would have been nice for the game to have more orginality. Shinji Mikami is the considered to be the father of the survival horror genre.
Overall, Psycho Break is an excellent survival horror game and will leave players frustrated and stressed out if not horrified.

Layers of Fear is the story of a painter who has gone mad, and how you explore his most inner thoughts and discover more about the story as you play. You can get some idea of what's going on from the get go, but the further you progress, the more interesting the story becomes. The game has small clues within each level, but the overall story is presented with key interactions. This is a horror game through and through, although typical jump scares are not what this game leans on. You will see some interesting and bizzare visual affects, and some of them are messed up.
First of all, this game is absolutely beautiful. I mean that in terms to both the graphics, and the art direction. Bloober Team SA knows how to optimize the engine they're using, and use it to full affect. This game runs smooth, and the graphics are top notch. Then there is the art style of this game. As you roam around in the game, it's clear that it takes place in, or inspiration from the Victorian era. There are no computers, no televisions, nothing that we're used to today.
Secondly, the horror involved in this game. It plays more like Outlast than Dead Space. There are jump scares to be found, but a good amount of of the horror comes from the audio. You'll hear creaks and voices whisper in your ear. You'll walk around and hear someone or something behind you, only to find that there is nothing. This alone helps put the player in the painters shoes, and make them think they're hearing things all around thm.
And lastly, the gameplay. It's pretty straight forward, you can walk, run, and click certain items as well as investigate them. That's how the majority of the story unfolds, as I stated above. There is no combat, hiding, or items you can use against anything, you just have to rely on yourself and confront your fears. While that may turn some players away, it is once again another way to put you in the protagonists shoes and understand how he is unable to escape the horrors of his mind.
Overall, I give this game an 8/10. The reason for this is that I personally would have liked to have a little more confrontation with enemies, and I would have like to have been able to inspect more things that are lying around. I love horror games even though I hate horror movies, which I myself find weird. Games like Layer of Fear help push the boundaries of what horror games are capable of. While this definitely isn't the first or last horror game to come out, I hope that other developers will take this game as a lesson as to what games in this genre should try to accomplish.

This game is somewhat in between adventure and survival being neither or both. This is not the place to look for complex puzzles or real dangers and as such it might throw some hardcore adventurers or survivalists off. The main strength of this game is the psychological horror angle that turns weirder and weirder for every door passed. The real fun begins when you have gathered enough information to actually identify  with the poor guy and from there wondering what will happen next and why. A vivid imagination, good headphones and patience enough not to run through the game is the main ingredients to how this game should be played. The game is quite linear being divided into stages preventing you from wandering off and losing the grip on the story, While some might find this irritating it actually balances the game perfectly between a gaming and movie experience. So, what about the cons? The adventure elements are mostly bookshelves and drawers in a neverending sequence and most often without any interesting inside, most puzzles are either way to easy or have the solution clearly explained nearby. The hints to the story could have been fleshed out and visualized much better. A few more objects and a more detailed background would have made this game complete. Anyhow this is minor details that could be kept in mind for later games. Do you like Warhammer fantasy? Or maybe just fantasy in general? Do you like co-op games?
If you answered yes to one or more of these questions, Vermintide just might be for you. The game is a four player co-op game set in the warhammer universe where you and three other players fight against the skaven ratmen.
The gameplay itself is quite similar to Left 4 Dead, maybe Left 4 Dead 2 specifically, but with more of a melee focus. All the different characters also have their own unique items etc. So they all have more of a different and individual feel than the characters from left 4 dead. But the gameplay is quite similar, you play through a level, complete objectives, fight tons of weak mobs and every now and then a special enemy will show up. Combine this with some RPG elements such as items that give you different bonuses and upgrades and you got yourself a pretty solid game.
Personally I have not encountered any bugs within the game so far, but it might be worth mentioning that the amount of players that are online can sometimes be quite low, making it difficult to find any good games to join. This seems to depend on all sorts of things, like what time of the day you are playing etc. But you usually manage to join a lobby without too many problems.

To get better equipment rewards from missions you have to play on harder difficulty settings and your team has to work together. On some maps there are Tomes and Grimoires which help your reward chance if you beat the level while carrying them. Carrying Tomes replaces your character's healing item and Grimoires replaces your character's magic potion item as well as reduces the health of your team by a small percentage. Tomes can be dropped and picked up,
This can cause some... anger issues in some people. If you get angry at your teammates easily then this is probably not the game for you. If you are shy then you can play this game with bots, but the bots will not pick up Grimoires at the time of me writing this review.

Vermintide is a Left 4 Dead clone with a loot system and a very crappy loot system at that.
The game is actually decent however, I only recommend purchasing it if you have 3 other friends who are willing to play with you since the player count is very low. I played through it during the free weekend with my friend and we found it extremely difficult to find players after 4-5 levels (keep in mind this was during a free weekend so think about the regular population).
The combat is mindless but fun, the game is absolutely gorgeous, and the endless amounts of gore and limbs flying everywhere is always nice to see.
The game's biggest issues are the AI director and the loot system. The AI director is as random as the one from Left 4 Dead. One map you may have barely any special rats. Replay the same map and a tank spawns immediately and kills everyone. Attempt to replay it again and 5 armored rats spawn immediately after killing the tank.
The loot system is awful. After completing the game, the end-game revolves around replaying the same maps you just played on higher difficulties to increase the chance that the drop you get at the end of the map is good. Basically, there's 3 hidden tomes and a grimoire on all maps. Their location never changes. You get 1 item drop at the end of each map if you win and collecting these things increases the chance that the item is better. That's all it does.
There is no way to get more item drops. There is no way to control what class the item is for. And if you lose the map, you get nothing (aside from maybe a tiny amount of stuff used for crafting/upgrading).
It is really stupid.
The new free DLC Quests & Contracts supposedly adds additional ways to get loot however, it requires finishing the game and after I finished it and knew that no one that I know would spend $15 on it to play with me, I didn't bother checking it out. If it truly does add additional ways to get loot, then they released it way too late.

This game may not be on par with Human Revolution, but then again, not many games are...
While not perfect, this is still a nice game that deserves to be played. Most of its flaws come from its tablet origins.
If you consider this game as some sort of DLC for Human Revolution, you should enjoy playing it.
Pros:
+ ability to choose play-style : ghost or shooting, it's up to you. Most of the time (except maybe in the tutorial level), there's more than one way to do something (persuasion, pirating, fighting, exploring, breaking walls, ...).
+ interesting story-line, and a bit of background for the villains of Human Revolution (but you MUST have played Human Revolution to fully understand the story).
+ tutorial part (Moscow/Jetliner) is a bit slow, but then the game really shines in all the Panama zones.
+ in Panama: good secondary missions, good level design and nice levels to explore.
+ decent voice acting.
+ very good soundtrack.
Cons:
- tablet-like controls are not optimal for PC. The grenade/item selection menus are great for a touch-screen, but not for a keyboard. No jump button. Some doors and terminals are difficult to use when you're crouched, because you need to be at a certain position to use them.
- graphical glitches happen often during special animations (for example, when knocking out an enemy).
- to be able to move around when pirating a terminal, Vsync needs to be enabled in the settings. Not hard to solve, but you need to be aware of it.
- only one save slot.
- "to be continued" ending (that will never be continued).

This game came in a bundle for some euros when i bought a DLC for Mankind Divided.
I'm a huge fan of the Deus Ex franchise, having played the game since the original came out in early 2000s. I played Deus Ex Human Revolution about 170 hours, completed it 7 times and got all achievements.
The Fall either reframes certain events so that they fit in line with this game's storyline. That makes it interesting to play.
Unfortunately this game just isn't finished and doesn't come close to other Deus Ex games:
-Levels are disappointingly linear, with only the barest attention paid to the world-building and characterization that's so famous in the other Deus Ex games. The zoom-in-while-aiming is very uncommon in shooters and is not easy to use.
-Where in other Deus Ex games you have to explore the world for stuff and upgrades, here you can buy ammo, weapons and upgrades whenever you want.
- You can not jump in the game, what makes it sometimes look a bit stupid.
- There are bugs and mistakes in the game. To name a few:
1) in the Etana hotel I took cover (right mouse button by default) and I fell through the level. Also on other places I sometimes glitched on stranges places. 1 time I was even transported to another room.
2) Enemies can sometimes see you through solid obstacles.
3) You only have 1 saveslot. Hint: In order to create more savegames, go to the appdata map in Windows and copy - paste that map to your desktop. In that way you can create multiple saves.
4) Some achievements are buggy. I managed to get them all, but some I had to do a couple of times. After finishing the game I noticed there is a guide on steam about the achievements. Reading that will save you time to get them.
5) The voice from the woman that explains the (mandatory) tutorial --> The most annoying voice I heard in computer games since playing on a 286 in the late 80's with PC Speaker sound.
6) Graphics are very average.
On the positive note: Nice story, good music (same as in Deus Ex: HR), not too long.
I do not recommend it to people who enjoyed other Deus Ex games. Eidos Montreal should have taken their time to finish this game (make it less buggy) before porting it to PC.

WARNING:  This is an abandoned, unfinished phone port game.  I am definitely NOT recommending it.
OK.  That out of the way, here's the good thing about "Deus Ex: The Fall":  the gameplay and mechanics that exist are very similar to that of the previous (excellent) game (Deus Ex:  Human Revolution - Director's Cut).  Keeping in mind the problems, below, it's actually quite fun to play.
Now, for the bad:
- As noted, above, the game is unfinished and, apparently, abandoned.  It seems it was supposed to be released in episodes.  But, the original was released on 03/18/2014 and there was one patch on 08/01/2014.  After almost 4 years, there's been no continuation (the game ends after about 12 hours of play with a "To be coninued" blurb).  Lengthwise, this is like the "Detroit 1" set of missions from the previous game.
- All the philosophical stuff that defines the Deus Ex series is missing.  I don't know why they bother calling this a Deus Ex game without that.
- If you thought console ports were bad, well, this is a phone port.
- The controls are mostly OK, but there's no Jump command (they've essentially removed the 3rd dimension from this game).  I don't know how they managed it, but simple mouse-clicking is messed up.  It's hard to find the activation box for doors and consoles.  In the menus, if you move the mouse at all between a mouse down and mouse up action, the click doesn't register.  Until I figured that out, the game was nigh on unplayable.  Even after I figured it out, I had perpetual trouble with it (and in some cases didn't get a Save done when I thought I had).
- There's only ONE save slot.
- For something designed for the phone, the character models are actually surprisingly good.  But, for the PC world, they're pretty bad (almost as blocky as those in the original Deus Ex).
- The voice acting is pretty bad.  The voicing of the tutorial segments is awful..
- I don't even know why they bothered with the protagonist's partner.  She's worthless and does absolutely nothing during the game.
So, again, Not Recommended.

I highly reccomend getting this game if you want to get better at talking at girls. WAIT, WAIT, I know that sounds pretty farfetched but I bet you'll understand once I break it down.
1.Steroetypes - If you've had a look at the girls you've probably already given them a stereotype that fits their looks. I know you might not have consciously done it, but subconsciously you probably have. Don't worry if you have however because they fit into their stereotypes fairly well. The blue haired chick is a gamer, the blonde in the leopard print is a porn star and so on. These stereotypes are good when meeting new people because you don't know them yet. Keyword YET, because you need to start getting to know these girls if you want to get an edge in the hard♥♥♥♥♥puzzle sections.
2.Introductions - When you first meet a girl you get the standard three questions to open her up as a possible love option. These introductions are unbelievably easy and they do a good job to trick you into thinking  the 'Talk with her' button is going to be a cakewalk.
3.Talk with her - This button lets you ask the girls questions so that you can earn 'Hunie', which is used to buy upgrades. You get points if you ask her a question you haven't asked her already, you get nothing if you've already asked the question. However sometimes when you press the button the girls will also ask you a question. The question they ask will either be a quizze on what you've already learned about them or a question about you. If you get the right answer you get Hunie, wrong answer, no Hunie. The quizzes are fairly easy since you can check what you've learned about a girl before you talk to her. The Questions about you however, are anything but easy. "Why?" you ask, well let me explain.
4.Seeing the stereotypes - When you start getting asked questions from the girls you'll most likely go back to the stereotypes you have in your head since you don't have much else to go on. The types of questions that can be answered with stereotypes are alrady pretty obvious, but when it comes to the smarter questions, those stereotypes aren't going to cut it. For example, 'the ♥♥♥♥♥' may say "what is your biggest turn off?" and the answer is obvious, "girls who don't let loose".Buut, that was an easy question. You're going to be asked the most outlandish questions, for instance "How do you feel about families?"- the porn star (not exact words in the game, but its fundamentally the same). "Why is this question so random?". You may ask. It's not, if you think it's random then you need to learn about...
5.Seeing past the stereotypes - This is where the dating part of the game shines. This is when the girls ask a seemingly outlandish question and you get it wrong. This is when you realise that you can't base an entire person around a stereotype. This. Is where you learn. To show you what I mean let's go back to that question before, "How do you feel about families?"asked by the porn star. Figuring out the answer would probably go a little something like this.
"Hmm, well she's a flirty porn star. Probably doesn't hang out with family much, let's choose ' I don't really bother with family' and victor- what, how was that wrong!?"
That foolish person (me yesterday) thought that her entire personality was based around a stereotype. That isn't how you should be thinking when talking to girls, whether they be real or imaginary. Once you let go of stereotypes you can then think rationally about a persons thoughts and feelings. Now let's replay that scene with that womens thoughts and feelings in mind.
"How do you feel about families?"
"Damn, that's a tricky one. Does she even have a family? Well... she is a porn star, wait no. let's focus on the facts.
She's 36, really flirty, likes to drink, is a porn star, has a daughter, likes food... wait a minute. Oh.. she has a daughter, she mentioned that once. Hmmm now let's think... well she flirts a lot, so probably no husband. If she's been single and has a daughter she probably raised her by herself. So.... she really must care a lot about her daughter. Yeah. Let's go with that"
[clicks "I think it's important to be close with your family"]
[gets 700 Hunie]
"Sweet"
6.Conclusion - This is an incredible game. Whether your into the difficult puzzles, the Fanservice or the  ingenious questions (my favourite part about the game if you couldn't tell). It doesn't matter. This is a fundamentally perfect game in my opinion, so I'd like to ask a humble favour of you. The Readers of this review.

Mount & Blade: Warband is an amazing Sandbox game set in the Dark Ages. You get to create your own character, with their stats based on a "questionaire". I myself don't know what to call it, but certain things that you pick can make the game (espescially the start) quite easy, but also fatally hard. What I love about the game is the immersion. No big load screens, hunger, soldiers want to get paid, yada yada. You can even see your own feet!
As I mentioned before, this game is a sandbox game, and by that it is one of the best ones out there. You can legit do ANYTHING you'd like to do. Want to enlist in an army? Do that. Raid villages? Do that. Slaughter your enemies and take their castle? Do that. To this day, I still find out what I can do, even though I "beat" the game so many times now.
I also recommend to purchase the add-on "Napoleonic Wars" (or whatever it is called). You'll be able to play in vs. rounds against other players and shoot guns. Seriously - this game + guns = lots of fun. There are also legit teams that do weekly fights and what not.. it's just huge, really. You can make a lot of new friends (that you might need - you'll get addicted to this game) and have literally endless fun.
The modding base is still active, and if you're a fan of GoT, there is a huge overhaul "mod" (if you'd still like to call it that) that does an amazing job to transfer the game settings into the fantasy universe of GoT. It's amazing and I enjoy it so much.
All in all, I can easily say that Mount & Blade: Warband has never let me down. No errors, no shutdowns, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t - nothing. This is a legit great and most of all stable game, and easily one of my most favorits.

My name is SynificHD and I am a YouTuber who uploads many gameplay content, such as this game.
This review will show my thoughts and opinions towards the game, also including a link to the game for you guys to check out and hopefully enjoy; and give you an insight of the game!
The game "The Evil Within" is a third-person survival horror game where you play as a Detective who is to crack the case of the murders of Beacon Mental Hospital, with a mysterious susptect who goes by the name of Ruvik.
You are accompanied by Juli Kidman and Joseph Oda, to help track down Ruvik and stop this madness once and for all.
"The Evil Within" is somewhat my baby, and now having completed the game I can now finally say goodbye as he/she goes off to college and becomes an adult. This game took me almost 3 years to complete which is quite disappointing as you can imagine the game became no longer interesting for me, but sadly this game was quite hard to record as well as enjoy at the same time. The game is quite rich with story but the controls and mechanics are not all there. The game is based on a leveling system that is powered by "Brain goo" as called it, but the problem is that it is somewhat hard to find them and is quite costly for certain upgrades. The problem I encountered the most was the sprint time and how long the animation is for you to "catch your breath", you might as well curl up in a ball and kiss your bum goodbye if you ever find yourself in that situation; go easy on the sprint.
The aiming is also quite terrible as you will most likely miss every shot and run out of bullets, which is also another issue with the game; THERE AINT A LOT OF AMMO IN MOST POINTS OF THE GAME. I could go on and on about how this game can frustrate me but in the end I did enjoy it, and did leave me on a cliff-hanger. If I werent recording this game I would for sure have enjoyed this game far more but I made that choice a long time ago and stuck to it.
I recommend this game to players who enjoy third-person survival horror games, that can handle a bit of gore, and enjoys an atmospheric, rich storyline. But for those who wish to record, maybe reconsider... Unless you buy this on console which may be a lot easier.
Depending on your luck things might work out well for you but for me I went through hell and back recording this game, issues might have occured due to recording other things at once: Facecam, Vocal Audio and the game itself. But I will just warn you now that it may not be the best idea. Although the game was good to record because you could record chapter-by-chapter making things a little easier for knowing where you're at. I give this game a 4/10 from my experience; was not fun recording, certainly not easy.
