When I showed this game to my friend, I only meant to teach him the basics of the puzzles and how to interact with the girls. 7 HOURS later, we haven't moved from the couch and we're trying to explain to my now-returning roommates that yes it's a dating simulator puzzle game, and yes we were leading a Japanese teacher in skimpy shorts back to our bedroom tonight, and yes things would probably get steamy, and no it's not porn, and shut up it's super fun and you don't know me.

HuniePop is a Western Dating Sim, RPG and Puzzle Game. You play a nameless protagonist who has no love life. The Love goddess, being disappointed by the lack of romance in your life, decides to send Kyu, a magic love fairy, to help you out. Kyu profiles eight beautiful, eligible girls in town and after a few helpful tips, starts you on your quest for love... or lust.
The puzzle section (making up the date portions of the game), at its core, is fairly standard Bejeweled fare but with some added complexity. The player has to score enough points to fill an Affection meter within 20 turns, and each girl has favorite and least favorite token types that change how many points each give out, along with Passion tokens that act as a score multiplier, Joy tokens that give extra moves, Sentimentality tokens that allow the use of special items, and Heartbreak tokens that penalize you if you match them. Aside from leveling up a girl's relationship status, clearing a date also gives the player money to purchase gifts for use in the dating sim section, where the player talks to the girls to acquire "Hunie", which is then used to upgrade various traits (such token effectiveness, lessening heartbreak penalties and increasing the score multiplier cap for Passion tokens) for use in the puzzle section. You will want to upgrade your traits as often as you can, so wrack up that Hunie. The puzzle segments get progressively more difficult as the game goes on, so traits are VERY important. Also, if you reach a certain Passion level during the puzzles, you may be sent bonus photos of the girl you dated.
The game plays out very well, having you move from location to location talking to the different girls to learn things about them. At times the girls will quiz you on your knowledge of them, and if you answer correctly you receive bonus Hunie. As you talk to each girl, you will notice a hunger and intoxication meter under their relationship gauge. If you try and talk to them while their hunger meter is empty, they will simply tell you that they are hungry. To continue talking to them you can buy some food in the shop and gift it to them to restore a portion of their meter to continue the conversation. The other option is to leave and come back to the girl later, when her hunger meter will be refilled again. The intoxication meter measures how, well, intoxicated the girl is, and you can buy her drinks to drive this meter up. Doing so gets you bonus Hunie while talking to them, as well as starting you off with a Sentiment level equal to their intoxication level when starting a date puzzle, depending on the girl.
After each successful date (yes, you can and will fail some puzzles), your relationship gauge (measured in hearts) with that girl will go up by one. When you reach 4 or more hearts with a particular girl, and complete a dating puzzle at night, they will offer to go back to your place. This begins a "climax" puzzle, where you have unlimited moves but the objective is to fill the Pleasure meter, which slowly decays over times. Making matches in the puzzle fills the gauge. When you complete the climax puzzle you are rewarded with a raunchy photo of the girl you "conquered", as well as a pair of their panties as a trophy to stash in your inventory. These do nothing but to remind you of which girls you have climaxed.
Oh, did I mention that EVERYTHING is 100% fully voiced acted? Yes, even the climax puzzles. Let that sink in for a second. There is also language and revealing photos. This is certainly NOT a game for children. Please exercise discretion when playing this game with children in the house.
HuniePop is an excellent puzzle game with a dating sim cover. It offers solid mechanics and ever increasing challenge in it's gameplay, in the puzzles and in the "dating". Definitely give it a shot if puzzle games are your thing.

Do you want a multiplayer survival mode with lots of different armies and creatures? There's a mod for that.
Do you want zombies? There's a mod for that.
Do you want improved graphics? There's a mod for that.
Do you want sea battles? There's a mod for that.
Do you wa- you get the point.
Personally I recommend you get the Floris Mod Pack, its the normal singleplayer but with thousands of essential addons.

At first I just played multiplayer against other people. It was fun to go one on one with another player and see who was the best at fighting with a sword - there is quite a big skill gap between the best and the worst. A bow and arrow was also fun to use.
I then started a singleplayer campaign which I found was even better. I started out with a character levelling up his skills to be an all-rounder but I wasn't very successful, and my army stayed small because I kept losing battles.
After having learnt more about the game I made a new character, levelled up certain skills for myself so that I could rely on my companions to offer party skills - a better use of skill points. Different companions like and dislike each other, so I had to find a group of companions which all liked each other if I didn't want them to leave my army. I earnt money by trading which involved learning different locations where I could buy cheap items, and where I could sell them at a big profit. When I came across a tournament in a city I would bet all on myself and earnt some money through winning those. Meanwhile I've been collecting new recruits from different towns and levelling them up, making my army stronger.
As well as this, there are a lot of full game overhaul mods which I've just started trying out. These change the whole map, the factions/characters/warrior types and the weapons, armor and other purchasable items.
There are a lot of things you can do in this game - these are just some of them. Edited for badge

HuniePop is one of those "In Theory it works" style concepts that after a while you realise isn't a great idea. On paper it sounds like it could be fun, puzzle game and dating sim combined. Like peanut butter and chocolate. What's not to love. I can agree, if your intention is to have it in small chunks, just a little here and there, then it's manageable, it's tolerable even. But any more than that and it becomes dull, it drags and you just want it to stop.
The game has a great hook the two genres being combined, and not only that but the dialogue is interesting and witty when you first start as well. But after a while again, it gets boring, you've seen it. The dialogue is the most redeeming factor and that runs thin far too quickly to actually save the game in any way/shape/form. As you progress through the game you end up levelling up, collecting traits that help you, but there's a catch, every successful "date" increases the requirement for the next, not just for that individual girl but overall. Meaning if you want to put the moves on just one girl and make her your Waifu, then sure it'll be an enjoyable experience, but if you want to try and collect them all Pokemon style, then by the end of the game luck is going to be playing a part in just how successful your "accomplishments" are going to be. You can also find yourself skipping days just to get the right girl at the right time, because to "seal the deal" you have to have a date with her at night, and they might be out of town or sleeping if you're unlucky. Combine the dragging gameplay towards the end with the random chance the girl isn't even available and you can end up becoming infuriated rather quickly.
Pros:
- It's an ok pick up put down game. It requires little thought, and some of the characters have redeemable qualities.
- Anything with a match-3 system is going to have addictive aspects to it, because it's simple.
- An English voiced "Visual Novel" is always awesome.
Cons:
- Dialogue gets old too fast
- No matter your traits and "level" RNG can still hold you up and make you feel the grind (giggity).
- The final "sex" game can be infuriating for some players.
- Collecting panties from your "conquests" feels wrong.
Final Thought: If you want a dating sim. There are better games out there. If you want a puzzle game. There are better games out there. If you want Hentai, there's Google.

HuniePop is a very unique game in the dating sim genre, mixing puzzle and memory with elements of a dating sim. Each of the girls shown on the title screen react as you would realistically expect them to. You can ascribe each to a stereotype (and it is mentioned by you resident love expert, too) yet the element of realistic dialogue that comes with their characters help define them from each other.
The puzzle aspect visually resembles Bejeweled and is one of those "Match 3 or More" style games, yet the way the puzzles work add a new layer of depth to the classic idea. Instead of swapping tokens with adjacent tokens you can move any token horizontally or vertically as long as the movement causes 3 token to match up somewhere during the movement.
There are strong elements of fantasy in the game, which adds entertaining content. The game is not vey replayable and is somewhat linear.
I recommend this game to players interested in story and puzzle solving.

Vermintide is a mission-based FPS with a heavy focus on cooperation. There are five characters who have distinct abilities  and weapons and an addictive loot system that leaves me saying "Just one more mission" to get the weapon I wanted until I realize it's 2am.

There's really not much to say about this game, really. Vermintide is basically a Left 4 Dead game set in a warhammer setting. Instead of a survivor you play a hero. You team up with other players or AI to finish a mission fighting through hordes of sentient armed rats and several elite monster harassing you along the way. unlike in Left 4 Dead though, there's loot to be had at the end of each mission. You can use said loot in next mission or use it as an upgrade/crafting material. I think that's about all the difference between the two. If there were more, it's possible that I missed it. Anyway, if you like both Warhammer and L4D, you're going to have a good time with Vermintide.
FPS is not really my forte and I very rarely play it. But in the short time I spent playing this game during the free weekend, I thoroughly enjoy the game. Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide is a good game that look pretty enough (in its own way) and runs quite well on my modest rig.

I'm not typically one to buy horror games. I've owned a few such as Amnesia, Monstrum, Dead Space, and the Evil Within, and I usually can't get very far before I get too spooked. I usually can only play for small amounts of time and have to slowly work through the games, if at all. This game is different. This is the kind of horror game i've been looking for, for awhile. This game feels more like a movie. Horror games usually rely on tons of ridiculous jumpscares, gore, or crazy monsters for fear. This game is a whole other world of fear. I'm not sure I'd say it's scarier, but it's different. This game gives you the constant fear of turning around, fear of opening doors or turning a corner. Anything in this game can and will scare you. It's a weird trip through the mind of a mentally ill alcoholic artist dealing with an immense amount of grief, just trying to survive in his own home. It's a really unique experience as you slowly uncover what happened in his life and follow his slow descent into madness. This game scared the living♥♥♥♥♥♥out of me, but it never scared me away. I kept wanting to get further and push through the nightmares to see what I find on the other side of the door. It does have a lot of jump scares, but they're used well. They're not cheaply thrown in all over the place, and they're often hard to predict.
I think of this game as if you were paying for a really immersive interactive movie. It's $13, or cheaper on sale, for about 1.5 hours (game isn't fully complete, will likely be 2+ hours), but the time spent playing it is a very fun and unique experience.

There are some puzzle elements added as well, and the ending of the game is very well done. I can't help myself from reccomending this game more so since the release.
I've played through this game 3 times and have watched others play it a couple of times as well and I'm still not done with it. I'll be replaying it again to see what else I can discover and see where new decisions may lead me in this personal hell that is Layers of Fear.

HuniePop is one of those "In Theory it works" style concepts that after a while you realise isn't a great idea. On paper it sounds like it could be fun, puzzle game and dating sim combined. Like peanut butter and chocolate. What's not to love. I can agree, if your intention is to have it in small chunks, just a little here and there, then it's manageable, it's tolerable even. But any more than that and it becomes dull, it drags and you just want it to stop.
The game has a great hook the two genres being combined, and not only that but the dialogue is interesting and witty when you first start as well. But after a while again, it gets boring, you've seen it. The dialogue is the most redeeming factor and that runs thin far too quickly to actually save the game in any way/shape/form. As you progress through the game you end up levelling up, collecting traits that help you, but there's a catch, every successful "date" increases the requirement for the next, not just for that individual girl but overall. Meaning if you want to put the moves on just one girl and make her your Waifu, then sure it'll be an enjoyable experience, but if you want to try and collect them all Pokemon style, then by the end of the game luck is going to be playing a part in just how successful your "accomplishments" are going to be. You can also find yourself skipping days just to get the right girl at the right time, because to "seal the deal" you have to have a date with her at night, and they might be out of town or sleeping if you're unlucky. Combine the dragging gameplay towards the end with the random chance the girl isn't even available and you can end up becoming infuriated rather quickly.
Pros:
- It's an ok pick up put down game. It requires little thought, and some of the characters have redeemable qualities.
- Anything with a match-3 system is going to have addictive aspects to it, because it's simple.
- An English voiced "Visual Novel" is always awesome.
Cons:
- Dialogue gets old too fast
- No matter your traits and "level" RNG can still hold you up and make you feel the grind (giggity).
- The final "sex" game can be infuriating for some players.
- Collecting panties from your "conquests" feels wrong.
Final Thought: If you want a dating sim. There are better games out there. If you want a puzzle game. There are better games out there. If you want Hentai, there's Google.

HuniePop is a very unique game in the dating sim genre, mixing puzzle and memory with elements of a dating sim. Each of the girls shown on the title screen react as you would realistically expect them to. You can ascribe each to a stereotype (and it is mentioned by you resident love expert, too) yet the element of realistic dialogue that comes with their characters help define them from each other.
The puzzle aspect visually resembles Bejeweled and is one of those "Match 3 or More" style games, yet the way the puzzles work add a new layer of depth to the classic idea. Instead of swapping tokens with adjacent tokens you can move any token horizontally or vertically as long as the movement causes 3 token to match up somewhere during the movement.
There are strong elements of fantasy in the game, which adds entertaining content. The game is not vey replayable and is somewhat linear.
I recommend this game to players interested in story and puzzle solving.

For years, DX: The Fall has sat on my Steam library solely because I bought it in a bundle for the Deus Ex games, and it has been one of the few times where I would rather pay the difference rather than have it on my account. Perhaps to some critics this is the equivalent of a bl0wjob to review because the game is so awful it’s almost comically bad; however, The Fall is a far more disgusting prospect that gained critical acclaim by its iOS critics. The problem with The Fall is not being one of worst DX games, perhaps worse than Project Snowblind; it’s a synthesized, failed project from SquareEnix to shamelessly piece-meal games, add microtransactions, and enforce sequel-baits rather than finish a storyline with resolution that plagued Mankind Divided and the future of DX.
Before the release of Bulletstorm, Epic Games released a free parody of modern COD/BF games that made fun of everything from the storylines and heroism of the campaign to the absurd multiplayer progression models that sells these games to wide audiences. It was a marketing stunt that was successful in critiquing modern FPSs in order to sell its game on its “old-school” FPS vibe, and people enjoyed the lampooning of the highest selling game at the time.
DX: The Fall on PC feels like the same self-aware spoof of a bad DX game. Instead of being a free spoof with a marketing purpose, the game is an incomplete episodic experiment of how to streamline the DX formula on an iOS device tech-demo. The tech-issues alone with the absurd “recoil” that warps the screen as if on a trampoline, limp firing system, AI behavior and simplified complexity all adds a so-bad-it’s-good quality that would be entertaining if it wasn’t being serious. Even if the game was remade into the Human Revolution engine and the gameplay expanded upon, the game would still be a disgrace because of the many shortcomings made in its design, level-structure and overall incompleteness.
Levels are divided up by loading-screen with two or three entrances that are smaller than the original DX and barely larger than Invisible War; security itself is a farce of a threat that can be quelled with a Rambo style of playing; ammo is littered all over the place with a limited supply of weapons; non-lethal options are simplified dialogue sequences and melee attacks. Everything about the gameplay complexity of Human Revolution is reduced to an almost satirical level of ineptness and simplicity.
Perhaps the one positive quality about The Fall is it was the scapegoat for how bad Mankind Divided could have been as the future episodic content of TF may had acclimated players to accept the microtransactions to overcome any challenge or to reward impatient players. It’s a shame that one game had be scraped in order to save the future of a series because there are some ideas worth salvaging as well as a different character for the modern DX games.
The storyline of Ben Saxon, the augmented soldier of The Fall, is a nice contrast to Adam Jensen much like how Daud was a foil for Corvo in Dishonored. In the setting of The Fall, it takes place during a Neuropozyne shortage and monopoly during the timeline of the Australian Civil War mentioned in past games. Unlike Jensen, Saxon is someone who relies on Neuropozyne to keep his augments, which could have added a greater sense of risk-reward to the game having to choose moral dilemmas for selfless acts of preservation and power as well as being a part of dividing lines in a civil war orchestrated by corporate interest that are tearing a country apart from the seems of its innovation. The potential to make a truly noir/war storyline in contrast to the espionage storyline of Jensen is something that truly saddens me that we’ll never know the full details outside of one novelization written between the two official games, Human Revolution and Mankind Divided.
This was perhaps the basis for Mankind Divided that also dabbled in the moral dilemmas and rising civil war scenario due to augmented people in Prague, which goes to show that had The Fall been successful the storyline and characters could have been worth praising in the franchise, yet its success would have made Mankind Divided into a far greater catastrophe than what it became. Why either game had to suffer is perhaps the more pertinent question to ask SquareEnix, but given the situation that came as a result this is one positive I believe I can live with if The Fall’s failure will teach this publisher a lesson as how not to handle a beloved series.

I got this game a two or three weeks ago and have enjoyed it immensely (currently about 50 hours on record).  It is a great co-op game that relies on people's cooperation and skill (thankfully everyone but the newest player realizes people need to stick together).  I originally thought it was Left 4 Dead (L4D) with swords, but it has a bit more depth than L4D with unlockable weapons, difficulties, stat boosts, cosmetics, and levels (which also vary in length).  All of this makes each character have a different playstyle, which keeps the game refreshing and allows for a lot of variation in playstyle (as opposed to only going for min/max'ing).
I really enjoy playing this game and nothing really beats knocking the stuffing out of rats.  It is really rewarding to see improvement in your play and be able to take on more challenges and harder difficulties.  The only downside that I have seen from others is that the game can get boring if you are trying to grind for a certain weapon, but that is only if you treat it like a grind.  Thankfully I never have run into this issue.

I really, really like Scrap Mechanic. It's a fun game that's got lots of stuff to do. You can easily waste a Sunday afternoon making inventions in Scrap Mechanic. There's loads of blocks to choose from and stuff to build with, and your creations can range from simple cars and tools to big, complex machines. Especially after the recent welding update, the possibilities have become endless, all in a really good physics environment that makes you consider concepts in your virtual inventions that you do when you work on real robots, like weight, balance, engine power, et cetera. Great for tech geeks!
However, there still are a few problems. The UI needs improving, and the mouse movement is weirdly sluggish and hard to control. It's probably easier with a controller but with a keyboard and mouse the controls can get a bit clunky. Not to mention sometimes the GUI breaks and the walls of text provided to identify different blocks become impossible to read. Also, your computer may have problems starting the game. I've always ran it well but for some reason my brother's computer, which is a copy of mine only with an i5 instead of an i7 inside, cannot get past the boot screen without the game crashing, and we haven't found an explanation. Plus, being an early access game means there's still a ton of bugs to work out, but since the team is regularly working on this game new fixes come out all the time.
Aside from the above issues the game is incredible fun and if you like robotics you will become hooked. It's beautiful and runs great. However, watch out for game-breaking bugs and your PC might like to crash it on startup even if you meet the recommended system requirements. Fairly robust and enjoyable game with endless creative possibilities, just watch out for issues because sometimes getting it to work correctly is like playing computer roulette.

For those of us who remember Creatures or parts pf Spore, Niche will feel familiar in some aspects. I know that there isn't a huge playerbase for a type of game like this, a strategy/genetics/survival hybrid, but it's a very underserved market and this game goes to great lengths to fill a lot of those missing pieces. If you came for anything other than breeding cute animals and watching them all die out because you fail as their God, then you are more than welcome to find another game to play.
Niche could use a few more perks and maybe a introductory tutorial on how the genetics work, but if you remember Creatures, that didn't come with a tutorial either and you probably figured it out over time. This game encourages you in much the same way. 'Here's the tools, here's the bare minimum to get by, make your own fun'. In the entirely good way. I'd like to see this title continue to grow even after full release, as the current project is very enjoyable and perfect for that niche audience of animal/monster breeders.

I've put an alright amount of hours into this, and I think it's about time to say what I think about this game.
Niche is for exactly the kind of playerbase it says - a niche market. Most people probably will find this game boring or repetitive, and at times, it is. It's a game I like to play when my friends are telling stories or I'm listening to a podcast. It doesn't take much concentration, but still just enough overall to keep me playing.
I have still yet to beat story mode, as the game can be surprisingly difficult at times. Mostly it's slowly moving your way through an area and just collecting food or trying to survive, but every now and then there is that panic and rush for more food or a suffient mate to carry on your tribe's legacy. This game is right about making it hard to survive very long, because it's a genetics game. Lots of things don't work. I LIKE that about the game. It makes it feel very important to pay attention to little things in your tribe's gene pool, and you have to consider what needs to change to improve survival. But usually, things aren't that easy. You'll come across a lot of weird future mates in the wild, and have no choice but to try your luck with them. Usually, it ends up in more oddities that need to be fixed in future generations. And don't even get me started on Rogue Males. Please, guys. Leave my females alone. We don't have enough food for more babies that will end up being made Omegas.
When I first saw this game my instant thought was "huh, so this is a furry game, right?" and yeah. I kinda is. If that is something you refuse to deal with, then I guess this game isn't for you. The way the animals look all together is just very, uh, furry-ish? But I've come to think it very charming, and start to understand why some people who play the game like to add their own lore / story to their tribes.
On the topic of adding your own lore, sometimes I wonder if that's how the game is meant to be played. The gameplay is repetitive and kind of dull after a few hours, which makes sense being a genetics game where your goal is to simply survive, but it gets a little stale. I think people add stuff to their playthroughs to spice it up, and that's cool! I'm not so good at assigning random lore to my tribes, personally. Because that one Rogue Male will come up and breed with all of my females, and I'll be at kind of a loss for how I can make that a cool part of my story.
This game is, hmm, it's hard to say if I actually recommend it. Since it gets stale and the entire game is VERY much for a niche market (which consists of furries, people who played spore as kids, or a combination of both). For people who are PART of that market, go buck-wild, my friends. It leaves some stuff to be desired, but it's a solid enough game in itself for me to not regret getting it. But I know A LOT of my friends would really not find any fun in the game, and that's important to keep in mind before making the purchase.
All in all, it's good enough to keep my attention. I'm looking forward to possble future updates that will spice up the gameplay a bit more. The art and music is fine the way it is, so gameplay is all I'm looking forward to being improved, even if just a little. I think the game would benefit from random events, even if its extreme stuff like "oh hey look at that, a meteor. Have fun trying to survive that!". I think the game would be a lot more appealing with that kind of thing added! I personally enjoy the game, so I recommend it, but maybe look into it before you make the purchase.

HuniePop is a 'dating' sim game wherein your objective is to date every good-looking woman you meet, and eventually bed them. 'Dating' is in air quotes because the dates themselves are... uneventful. Each date consists of playing the "Match 3 or more" bejeweled-esque puzzle. You must fill your score bar to succeed at the date, which will increase your girl's Heart Meter by 1. Failing a date yeilds no increase, but you still recieve Munie, the game currency, regardless of success or failure - but you do get more for success. This is the core mechanic of the game, and it works well. The challenge is neither too great or too small. I say the date is uneventful because whatever you are doing on the date is essentially left to your imagination. The girl does react to your puzzle combos, but thats all. The dates are indistinct from one another. Yes, you change location, the girl changes outfits, but they are void of anything else.
Munie, as you might expect, buys gifts for your girls. Your second resource - Hunie - is spent to increase your attributes; that is, how well your combos work in the puzzle game. The mechanics are simple to learn, and don't take too long to master. The more you fill a girl's Heart Meter, the more pics you earn from her. Once you fill a girl's Heart Meter to 4 or 5, you can bed them and earn their final picture, and her panties as an in game item (use still undetermined)
The girls themselves are well designed. They all have backstories, different personalities, and different tastes. It's nice to see this much effort put into making the girls feel unique and alive. Theres 'something for everyone' so to speak. Personally I don't see how anyone would date Audrey Belrose, shes way too ♥♥♥♥♥y.
With the praising asideI felt that the game suffered from a lack of gameplay variety. Playing the same puzzle game over and over gets stale by the time you unlock the last girl (yes, there are hidden characters, another plus). I would have liked to see more options in dating - like choosing a date location. Each girl has a favorite hangout, but you can never put that information to use. The ability to ask questions directly would be nice too, having to keep pressing 'Talk to' until you finally get every possible question asked is tedious. There could be more variations on the puzzle game itself - maybe the girl is having a bad day, and broken hearts do more damage; or maybe the girl is feeling oddly romantic, and romance token combos give more points.
Overall, this game is good. Not amazing, just good. I understand the price point is low, and trust me, you will get more than $10 of fun from this game; but it still feels lacking. I would have gladly paid $20 or $30 for more features.

So if you haven't played this wonderful title yet, why not ? It's fantastic. Really, It is. And it is certainly not getting the credit that it deserves. When I see those older games of a similar ilk, grabbing the limelight and attention; Games like Left 4 Dead and Killing floor and all that. It can be quite safe to assume that there is really no justice in the world. Anyone who's into these types of co-op wave / level survival games, who hasn't snapped this up yet. Be aware... You are seriously missing out !
No, there are no zombies to brutally blow to pieces, just rats. Legions upon legions of giant, man-sized rats. Which you will mostly have to hack your way through with an assortment of melee weapons. I could imagine that the thought of mainly hand weapon combat could be a turn off. Especially if you weren't over enamoured with this sort of feature in the likes of L4D or in other FPS fantasy titles, such as the terrible combat mechanics in your average Elder Scrolls game. Must admit, the thought did put myself off for a good long while. But having taken the chance to try the game out, I found that the combat in Vermintide, although still sort of basic, was incredibly fluid and an awful lot of fun. The action is tense and the gameplay itself is very solid. More so than I would have given credit for just by watching a few vids on Youtube ! Every slice of weapon, or bash with a hammer or shield, lands with a satisfying squelch or crunch. The physics of your blows are a wonder to see, as you carve your way through the hordes of enemies that will throw themselves at you and your fellow players.
The animations are great, the levels are beautifully designed and the overall graphics are wonderful. The environments of each level are great to wander through and explore. And explore them you must if you want to get the secret special items that are hidden away on most of the levels. Although not really essential to collect. They do help with the bonus game "Ranalds Bones", which is played at the end of every round. This is a basic RNG game played with a number of dice that determines your reward after getting through a level. The more secret items that you collect the more dice you have to play with, thus giving you a higher chance of a better reward. These rewards usually come in the form of a weapon, either melee or ballistic. Or you can get a trinket, which can be equipped to give your character a certain skill or bonus. Or you could just simply walk away with a hat. That is purely cosmetic and does not provide any bonuses at all.
This randomised loot system has been accused of providing quite a crippling grind to the whole game (depending upon how you look at it). In some ways this could be Vermintides greatest failing. But in other ways it is also the games greatest success in providing longevity. Giving life where the likes of L4D and KF have gone well past their welcome. Though it doesn't help matters when the die rolls in Ranalds Bones tend to be excrutiatingly poor. It can be assumed that the RNG system has deliberately been set to have the lowest possible results. Which can be more than a little frustrating and is definitely somewhat unfair. Making it feel like the dice are weighted. However the game does provide you with more than a few ways to gain higher graded gear. With more options that have been added over time. So it's not all bad.
All extra equipment that you win will help immensly when you want to access higher difficulties. The higher the difficulty you play also increases your chance of a better reward. And that seems to be how the games progression (and that of your character), is measured.
There is a levelling up system for you as the player. But so far I haven't been able to determine whether this has any direct affect on your game, or whether it is just pointless meaningless numbers. So far I have found no evidence that higher levelled players would fair any better than lower levelled ones. If they were given the same gear. It all seems to be down to the quality of your loadout and of course, your skill.
Although sort of basic and arcadey even. There is a certain depth in Vermintide that I can't quite put my finger on. But whatever it is, it keeps bringing me back for more. It is a really fun and fluid experience, The plot is pretty basic but it does provide a bit of story with each level, with some sort of objective to achieve. And the interactions between the characters as they go through these levels are wonderful. With some real snappy one liners uttered to each other throughout. And although this game is touted as a Co-Op experience. It is more than possible to play through most levels solo, though don't be expecting an Offline mode as such. As it does not exist. You will always be online whether you choose to play with others or not. And some of the levels on certain difficulties are just downright impossble to get through alone, due to the inept abilities of your teammates AI. Unlike L4D, AI controlled characters have deliberately been made to be completely incapable of handling certain situations. But as long as you are prepared for these events and have equipped you and your team with the right gear. You can get through most situations and most of the levels. However, all that could more than likely change with future updates. As Bot behaviour has been tweaked and improved more than a few times since the game exited Early Access.
That said, I wouldn't want to have you thinking that solo is a necessary, essential option or anything. As Vermintide does happen to have one of the most friendliest communities around. Of course you'll still find the occasional obnoxious imbecile. That is unrealistic to not be expected. But on the whole, it is a rare gem of a collective, where the veterans and the new comers can get along and enjoy the game together.
However there are certain advantages to running solo. Like you can always play your preferred character ( A minimal concern, seeing as you can just be the Host to do this). And you can take your time with the levels, as typically in Co-Op it can all seem like a chaotic mad dash to be the first to get to the good stuff (A typical curse of Co-Op based games. A trait that I have never truely got along with, finding it more than a little annoying). A solo run gives you plenty of room to explore the levels properly and learn where it's secrets are hidden. Which isn't a difficult task, just in a Co-Op match when you've got the more experienced players running all over the place, grabbing stuff willy-nilly. I feel that I didn't really start to experience the levels properly until I had the gear to be able to run solo and actually root around in them. And despite the faults of your AI buddies, you can always rely on them to watch your back (Something which personally drives me up the wall in all Co-Op situations, when your fellow team mates, brainlessly rush past you to get to the bad guys first leaving your rear flank totally exposed). Your AI buiddies won't shoot you in the back either. Which can be a proper pain as higher difficulties (Nightmare and Cataclysm mode), come with friendly fire damage. Unlike L4D, crouching isn't really that much of a help, as the Skaven are usually only about as tall as you when you duck down. So you will find that you are always shooting downward, when they get within a certain distance.
So that's Vermintide. A game that has borrowed it's assets from a few past classics and in some ways has surpassed those that it has moulded itself from. A wonderful hack n slash that hasn't exactly garnered the attention from gamers that it so rightly deserves. But if I was having to choose a personal GOTY for 2016. Then this would certainly be it, without a doubt.

I'm shocked at how great the game is, compared to when I played and reviewed it a year ago ( Dec 2015 for 2 hours ).
Although the game borrows the specials from Left 4 Dead ( Tank, Boomer/ Spitter, Hunter, Smoker ) playing the game for a few hours and calling it a "Left 4 Dead" reskin, sells the game short. For hardcore gamers, the game is easy on "Hard" difficulty and really comes into its own on "Nightmare" and "Cataclysm" difficulty.
The Soldier and Dwarf are the tank classes. The Elf and Mage are the ranged classes, with the Witch Hunter being a hybrid class.
The fire mage has an interesting mechanic where she builds up heat, every time she casts a spell. When she goes over a threshold, she takes damage. If you cast a spell after maxing out the heat damage, you can explode and die, which is funny. You can vent out the heat at any time.
There is so much equipment in the game: 1 handed swords and maces; rapiers; 2 handed longswords; great axes; greatswords; hammers; shield+axe/ mace/ hammer. Each weapon can drastically change the way that a specific character plays, to the point that even if you originally did not like a specific character, you might really enjoy them when you use the shiny new weapon.
The Witch Hunter uses a fencing sword, which was pretty amusing.
I have finished every map currently in the game, on both Nightmare and Cataclysm difficulty. There are only a handful of Cataclysm games being played in the world at any given time, so you will need a reliable internet connection, that can connect to most of the globe ( the netcode is very solid and I did not have lag problems connecting from North America-East Coast, all the way to Russia, Japan or Australia ). On Cataclysm difficulty, taking two hits will take half of your life points and with the new changes to the loot tables, most of the higher tier loot can be obtained on Nightmare.
I love the loot system. It rewards you based on how well you can play as a team. You have the option of carrying a cursed grimoire, which gives a guarentee of better loot but at the cost of the entire team receiving a reduction in their maximum health, for the duration of the mission. In dire circumstances, you can throw the book away, permanently destroying it, to receive your health back. It sets up an interesting risk / reward mechanic.
The voice acting is like something from the movie, "The Lord of the Rings."
If you are a hardcore gamer, two of my favourite maps in the game are in the Drachenfels DLC ( "Castle Drachenfels" and "The Dungeons" ). "The Dungeons" is considered the hardest map in the game and most players don't have the stomach for it. Casual gamers might not see the value in the Drachenfels DLC but at the same time, the DLC gains you access to a "triple cross bow" and a "glaive". The Triple cross bow is fun to use and the glaive is the most overpowered weapon in the game because you can one-shot enemies on Cataclysm, where every other weapon requires 2 or more strikes, so it's a crutch weapon that turns Cataclysm into DisneyLand yet if you are trying to solo Cataclysm with AI bots ( who are dumb as f* ) it can make the mission bearable.
The Schluesselschloss DLC turns Vermintide into a wave clearing game, similar to Killing Floor 1, except that you basically stand on an elevated platform, on one map. I only played the game mode a couple of times and considered it a boring waste of money, since you can get a better experience in the main game. Some people like the high rewards that you receive for surviving the waves.
Tips for new players:
- When reviving someone, you can block attacks by holding down the right mouse button while holding down the "E" key.
- The spacebar is the jump/ dash key and you can dash backwards by holding down S + tapping the space bar.

Deus Ex: The Fall is not an abhorently terrible game as the ratings might suggest, but it is a bad and unecessary port of a fairly decent mobile game (I did play the iOS version of this game first and is also why I was intrigued to play it again), which is why I am not reccomending it.
Deus Ex: The Fall on Steam is wholly unecessary.  It is a very basic port of, what was built and intened to be a functional (and somewhat impressive iOS game for it's time), and on those mobile platforms, I believe it sucesseded.  The problem here is that there were no moves made by Square Enix to formalize this into a console experience, and so it fails as one.
-- The graphical and audio fidelity is akin to what the PS2 and the original Xbox can push out
-- The enemy AI is insultingly dumb, practically non-existant, resulting in very little challenge for the player whatsoever
-- The world design is pathetically straightforward providing a very linear, fairly bland, and repetitive experience.
-- The menu system is adequate at best.  The store is uni-directional, meaning you can't sell anything, which is terribly
inconvienient.  Item, ability, and weapon "hot-keying" is cumbersome and if it weren't for your active abilities it would be altogether useless. The absurdity of being unable to map your own controls is an archaic flaw.
-- The hacking mini-game is the absolute best part of this game!  I would actually go and perform hacks, even when unecessary, just because it was so fun.
-- The achievements are actually quite reasonable all things considered.  If you're a completionist (like myself) the achievements almst make it worth it.
-- There is a story here, and I have read the supplementary material that relates to this game making it more worthwhile, but it's nothing ground-breaking and unless you are a fan of the series entirely forgetable.
--The dialgue sounds very canned and cliche, I ended up just skipping over most of it to be honest.  You are given the opprotunity to choose dialogue a few times, but it is almost inconsequential and easily navigatable.
I only relied solely on "stealth"  in my one playthrough and I don't see how or why you would want to play this game any other way.  Even when I played it on iOS I was hesitant to play more aggresively because I doubted the gameplay design, balancing and mechanics to perform well enough.  This skepticism remaned unchanged and I really don't think this game should be played any other way just based on my two experiences with it.
There is a game here, but it is so so very bare-bones.  I got everything I could possibly want out of this game on my first 10 hour playthrough with no intention of going back to play NG+ (yes, they actually offer that).  If an unchallenging, uninsipring, not-unique 10 hour experience is what you're looking for this is your game right here, but for everyone else, if you really want those easy achievements, wait to get the discounted Deus: Ex bundle like myself.

I'm going to start this review by stating that I absolutely LOVE this game, and any like it.  Twin-stick, frantic, progressive, high-score-chasing shooters are remarkably addictive to me.  I have 100's of hours logged between console versions of Geometry Wars, the pc clone Grid Wars 2, and the "Pew Pew" games for iOS/Android, and while I'm far from a high score chart topper, I feel I have enough time in them to offer an opinion.
I was THRILLED to see this come across on Steam, as Steam has become my gaming "platform" of choice in recent times...but sorely disappointed, once I logged into the game.  Yes, the core game is here.  Yes, it's amazingly fun and addictive and has that undeniable, "Just one more game" syndrome to it.  Yes, it's visually stunning and crazy hectic and a great showcase for wow-ing your friends as you dodge things they can't even see and somehow come out the other side still shooting.  Yes.  All of that.
BUT.  This game was a rush-job port for an easy cash in.  For starters, there aren't any achievements in the game, at all.  None.  Furthermore, yes, there's a leaderboard....but it's LOCAL ONLY.  This completely eliminates all of the high score chasing mania that made the originals so incredibly long-lived.  And, on top of all of this, not a single glimmer of any of the extended game modes is anywhere to be found.
So, yes, I'll still turn to this game in those moments where I want to kill time without thinking about it, or worrying about save points...and I'll still recommend it to anyone who does have it...but the sad truth here is that this could have been much, much better.

The controls were just far to bizarre for me, my underwhelming ultra-special move didn't even work for a full bout (I pressed Space a lot and not once did it trigger), and I can never tell when my AI team mate is going to pass to me (I haven't tried live players yet- I don't feel like the controls are natural enough to even consider it). Plus, I can never seem to catch the puck. Banging the left mouse button to steal and then having to _hold_ that same button to keep the puck (and then _release_ the button to shoot) is immensely counter-intuitive.
The whole time I felt like I was fighitng the controls. The WASD thing just seems like a terrible design choice- something more akin to a space simulator movement system seems like a better fit- where you have a "thrust" button, with directionality based on the mouse facing. I can see what they are trying to do, akin to an old double-joystick shooter, but it just doesn't feel "right". I would much rather see it "catch" the puck without much input, and reserve holding down the button to "power up", then release to shoot if they are going to do it that way (something like the old NHL hockey games from my youth). At least then you'd have a little variability on how you were shooting, rather than every shot going at the same speed (unless you manage to hit it with your special move, that is).
"Events" are massively annoying with how counter-intuitive the controls already are- they need to be something that can be turned off, especially when first learning the game.
And the game seems to memory leak something fierce- after two or three bouts everything lags and I have to shut it down and reload. The graphics settings don't seem to work right- the game looked fine until I went to look at the resolution options, and then, not changing resolution at all, it suddenly went all stretched out like the aspect ratio is wrong. I didn't select anything, I just opened up the drop-down and left it right where it was. And full screen versus windowed mode should stick between sessions. Also, it seems that some of the time when you check "full screen" it actually remains in windowed mode and vice-versa.
All in all a really rocky start for what sounds like a fairly interesting concept. But I can't stomach the controls or the other issues after playing for nearly an hour. Uninstalled. Not recommended.

I went into this game blind, having only seen a few screenshots. It blew me away. I was expecting some low quality SPORE ripoff, and what I found was an incredibly deep hex grid survival RPG hybrid. My goal going in was to create some kind of cute fox creature and scavenge corpses to survive. I had no idea that I would be evolving my cute little foxes into gill-necked sharkfoxes with raccoon hands for opening shellfish on the ocean floor, with hooked tails suited to catching fish and webbed feet for faster swimming. Likewise, I had no idea that an hour later I would be scrambling to splice in fennec fox style giant ears to survive a savannah archipelago that was being rapidly consumed by cleansing fire. I played this game until my computer melted, and was hyped the whole time. My 20 day lifespan foxes struggled constantly on the razor's edge of the knife which is extinction, and I learned how to handle new threats just to allow defenses against old threats to be lost to the generations. It was amazing.
My only complaint: The tutorial is mostly nonexistent, making your first playthrough basically a forfeit dash towards extinction. I was about 4 hours in before I started to understand the mutation/heredity system, which wasn't explained at all. It shows you how to move, pick berries, and befriend another fox, and then you're on your own. Good luck. You'll need it, and probably die anyway, and it will be totally worth the experience.

This is a saired review with Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army 1 as both games are practicly identical even to the achievements one can get playing them.
Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army 2 is quite a unique zombie game when compaired to the rest zombie games that we 've been hammered with the last few years. It takes the unique sniper gameplay established by the game Sniper Elite V2 and implements zombies into it. Quite simple really but at the same time glorious. Theres really no counterpart for landing the perfet headshot on a zombie and then watching the bullet slowly turn the zombies bowls inside out. It never gets old. In addition to shooting zombies with your sniper rifle you can use both an SMG of your choise and a trusty old pistol , and trust me you ll be using those a lot more than you 'd think, which is something I really enjoyed seeing as how both the SMG and the pistol where left practily completely unused when I played the Sniper EIlite V2 game. The zombies are also masterfully done with each enemy type having plenty of unique animations that make them seem remarkably realistic and terrifying. These are the strong points of the game, as unfortuneatly it does come with some weak points.
First of all the entirety of the maps available to play on are recycled material from the game Sniper Elite V2 that just have had a paint job of blood and satanic symbols done to them and then mixed to make new maps. For someone thats played the game Sniper Elite V2 this is quite disapointing as you are not greeted with anything fresh as far as sceenery is conserned. The game itself is also quite small containing only 5 levels, each lasting about 30 mins on the highest difficulty. However it should be noted the gameplay does give the game some replayability. The story is also quite monotonus and dull and moreover most chapters goals are "Survive the siege of zombies" or "Clear out the Zombies" something that adds to the general apathy you ll develop for the games story. By far the weakest point of this game and one that really saddens me is the fact its almost completely dead. Out of 2 days of playing during christmas and while the game was on sale I barely got into 10 lobbys ,and in most the same people kept coming up. For a game thats based around team work this is a big minus. Most of the achievements available while quite simple required a 4-player team, and so it was a real struggle getting them all. And it is realy a shame that this game has been abandoned to such a degree because its a really solid, good game.
To conclude , Sniper Elite Zombie Army 2 is a unique, fun and an overal great game. It does have its drawbacks and it is for the most part dead, but if you manage to gather some friends, or build a group using the steam forums its a must buy for any zombie fun out there.

Make America Great Again: The Trump Presidency is not a bad game, it's not a great game either. You control Trump who's in a helicopter and go around the world making deals and fighting ISIS. The controls are a bit clunky. Or rather, moving around from one end of the map to the other feels a bit labored. The countries aren't always easy to find. I didn't know that Europe, France, & England were 3 separate things you could click on at first.
Making deals is a bit arduous, esp since most of the countries with good buy/sell prices are the smallest, meaning you can only sell 5 units at a time. You can threaten or bomb countries to get them to lower their prices, which was fun. I threatened India and failed; so I bombed the shiite out of them and took their goods for next to nothing. AMERICA
As far as combat goes, this game has it. It's a bullethell-lite style of play. I did fell like the hit box on Trump's chopper was a bit too big. But, if you take the time to get your upgrades before you go to battle there's really not much of a challenge there.
Overall this isn't a bad game and I would recommend it to all my friends, no matter who they voted for. It's a serious satire that doesn't bring in any of the hate mongering we were told to believe during the campaign.

Proclaimer: This game is designed foremost for a co-op experience. I would not recommend it to be bought if you do not have a gaming group to go with it. But I highly recommend it if you can amass 3-4 friends together, and this is why..
So, ever wondered how Left 4 Dead would work if it was more melee based? Welcome to Vermintide, more or less. Off the bat, you will notice that it is a shameless copy of L4D, but that is not a bad thing in the slightest. Set in the dark fantasy of Warhammer's End Times, you and up to three friends are pitted together against an unending horde of Skaven, the rat-like humanoid beasts of the Warhammer world. The special enemy rats are mostly copied from L4D as well; You have the Packmaster (Copied from L4D's The Smoker) which will grab a player; You have the Gutter Runner (Hunter) which will jump on a player and claw at them; and so on.
The combat itself is simply satisfying. Rats will be flung to the walls when struck by that two-handed hammer and skip around burning after being blazed up by the mage's fireballs. The sounds, visual and general feel are top-notch. The classes play well together and there are plenty of co-op tactics to discover. Try sticking the dwarf with their shield first to a doorway while an imperial swings their two-handed great sword from behind the cover! Difficulty also scales well; there are a total of 5 different difficulty levels and Hard - the third difficulty level - does mean hard.
Light ARPG elements are mixed in; you can grind for some new gear and unlock features of your weapons. But they are not the focus of the gameplay, though I would not mind more gear and character customization options.

For me, a viable game has to be able to be as good solo as it is multiplayer to some extent. I don't really like playing with randoms and when my friends are not on, I would like to play games solo without losing much. The bots in this game are nice in theory but even in easy games they will bug out and lose the game for you. Playing solo feels like a crap shoot, you might get a game where bots don't fall off every ledge and actually help you beat the match. Other times one will drop and the other two will back track into madness to try and rescue said bot and then all go down. They are also not very good with defending objectives or prioritizing special enemies.
I get some games are more MP orientated, but this is just frustrating to say the least. When I DO decide to play with randoms, the community seems pretty elitist and I will get kicked out of hard and nightmare games because of, I can only assume, my player level being lower than they like. I will also host my own games and let people join . Quite a few times someone will join, sprint through sections taking the bots with them and when I get hit by a special, they leave the game and I'm dead. Way to mess up my solo run. Contracts added some replayability to the game but all the good stuff is on harder difficulties where, again, its hard to accomplish when bots don't work the best and other players won't let you play because you aren't high enough level.
Overall, it can be a fun game with friends and I want to get into it, but the community and bots make it hard for me to play at all if I don't have 3 friends on with me.

This was a fun little diversion.  I've seen it on sell for as little as $2, and for that kind of price I think it's worth it.  As others have mentioned, this definitely feels like a mobile port.  In places the graphics looked super blocky to me (even reminded me of the original Deus Ex a bit, and not in a good way, ha).  I played with the steam controller, and that worked out well. I had to go into the options and turn on the controller, but after that the controller worked perfectly.
Obviously this game doesn't hold a candle to the experience of one of the full fledge Deus Ex games.  It is quite shallow and very short.  Think of it as a mini, bite-sized adventure.  But I enjoyed the little story and I thought the music was fantastic.  The voice acting was pretty meh, but I didn't find it distracting after the first few minutes (once again, it definitely reminded me of older games in that regard).
I played the entire game peacefully and stealthily, and I had a lot of fun trying to clear all of the bad guys in a section without getting caught.  I also knew the game was short, but was still surprised when the credits rolled.  You could probably speed run the game in 4 hours or something, but I spent a bit more time finding all the goodies I could and buying augmentations.
As I said, for a couple of bucks, I think it is worth it.  I enjoyed spending a bit of time in the Deus Ex universe, and I don't regret picking it up and playing through it.

A wise man once said "to make a great video game you have to capture a moment in time, whether it's 5 minutes, or an hour. After you have that moment you have to expand upon it until it's something that people not only love, but will cherish for years".
I know that it's entirely pre-emptive to say that A:CE will be around for years to come; but I hope it does, I really do. The controls are smooth, the matches are fast-paced and involving, and the art is amazing. The developers have done an excellent job of making everyone on the team feel important also.
Slower PC ? Don't have the fine-tuned twitch reflexes of someone who's been playing NHL games for a decade ? Doesn't matter. You can be a lumbering goalie and STILL play an exceedingly rewarding (and more importantly; necessary) role for your team. A:CE strays from other MOBA games in that "tanking" or "support" is FUN! You might not be as fast as a forward, but there's nothing like freezing the enemy team solid on your side of the court, passing a rink-long pass, and watching your forward breeze by the goalie. It's teamwork personified; and it's FUN.
Give this game a try guys. I never-ever write reviews, but I just had brag on this diamond-in-a-very-rough stone that are other MOBA-type games.

Super Monday Night Combat is a 3rd person MOBA game that the developers stopped caring about, and everyone else also stopped caring about.
I had the game way, way back, and I liked it a lot. It was comedic, interesting (I had no idea what a MOBA was at the time) and just fun.
Then it died. Nobody plays anymore, hitting about 150 at peak play times. Try dividing those into 3 different game modes. The classes (Or "Pros", as they're called in-game) are varied to a degree, enough to make them different, while fitting into the same basic archetypes. They were pretty interesting as characters aswell, such as a Superhero, a stereotypical gamer, a gorilla in a tux, Leonardo Da Vinci's clone, things of that sort. They used to switch every week, letting you play as 9 of the 18 or so classes, and you were able to buy the ones you liked enough to keep playing as with real money. The current pros haven't changed in at least 6 months because Uber doesn't care about the game anymore.
There's customization abound, with each Pro having a good 9 or so weapons, and enough costumes to keep you looking different from the rest, if you're willing to spend the large amounts of money to buy them. This game was very, very Pay to Win, no weaponry aside from the standards could be used for free, but you could enjoy yourself none-the-less when you were losing.
The camera was a little wonky and the gunplay wasn't the best, but it was a good game when it came out.
As said, I really, really liked my time with the game. So why am I giving it a Not Reccomend? Because nobody cares anymore, that's why. How do you play a multi-player only game with no community? How do you try every Pro when the Developers don't think about switching them anymore? How do you enjoy an unplayable game?
You simply don't.

Part of me thinks the devs making this game had the following epiphany:
Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is a top-down shooter/beat 'em up. It has also been called a top-down ♥♥♥♥ 'em up. For obvious reasons. You play the game through the eyes of various character in a non-chronological fashion. You know, kind of like the more renowned Quentin Tarantino films. Just like said films, the plot isn't actually all that revolutionary, but by changing the presentation, it requires the player to actually stay alert and put some thought into it all. That's where the similarities end though. Where Tarantino's works are more often than not well-paced dialogue films interspliced with brief, memorable action beats; Hotline Miami 2 is a depressing, acid-fueled, blood-drenched, bad trip of a pixelated nightmare.
That's a compliment, by the way.
How does it hold up when compared to the first one? Hard to say. I really like the original because it was bold, new, fresh - yet it also had a very palpable retro feel. On one hand, Hotline Miami 2 is like your typical sequel: more of the same, but bigger and better. However, there are a few little differences which you wouldn't notice at first glance that really change up the pace. For example, the first game had a fairly arcade-like feel: plowing your way through the stages, each stage taking up only a couple of minutes.
Part 2, not so much. The locales are larger and a lot more varied, requiring a slightly more tactical approach. Where part 1 was mostly hallways and small rooms, part 2 doesn't shy away from big, open spaces - also known as 'a killing zone' when dealing with gunfire. If you didn't have agoraphobia before, don't worry, this game has got you covered. So, that's different, but is it better? A matter of personal preference, really... I think, in the end, I got more out of part 2 than I did out of part 1 - mainly because of the story - but the original is still my go-to game for a short session.
The soundtrack is still spot on. To be honest, the music really isn't my genre, but it just fits so. Damn. Well.
To cap it all off, this game has one of the best climaxes in any game I've ever played. Not that it's original or mind-blowing, but it just fits the overall atmosphere and is executed masterfully. I'm not going to spoil anything, but the synesthesia of audio and visuals is perfect, solid proof that you don't need tons of money and a 3D engine with PBR materials to create true immersion. It is also the reason I give this game the "Whoooaaaaaaa, Dude!' award (Steam Autumn Sale 2016).

I don't really like playing with randoms and when my friends are not on, I would like to play games solo without losing much. The bots in this game are nice in theory but even in easy games they will bug out and lose the game for you. Playing solo feels like a crap shoot, you might get a game where bots don't fall off every ledge and actually help you beat the match. Other times one will drop and the other two will back track into madness to try and rescue said bot and then all go down. They are also not very good with defending objectives or prioritizing special enemies.
I get some games are more MP orientated, but this is just frustrating to say the least. When I DO decide to play with randoms, the community seems pretty elitist and I will get kicked out of hard and nightmare games because of, I can only assume, my player level being lower than they like. I will also host my own games and let people join . Contracts added some replayability to the game but all the good stuff is on harder difficulties where, again, its hard to accomplish when bots don't work the best and other players won't let you play because you aren't high enough level.

I want to love this game, i really do, but no matter how i try to look at this game, it's lacking.
First of all, i went and dropped the game for a while since i was getting bored of the grinding system and lack of players back then in SEA servers, and that was on it's first build.
I came back after seeing that the loot system was fixed, giving you better rewards if you play on higher difficulty (which was almost a year after the game was released btw), and i find that it's still the same old game.
The problem with Co-Op games like this one, L4D, Payday 2, or those sorts, is that you're much better off playing with other players. Now here is where this game main problem lies: playerbase.
I'm located in SEA, and playerbase is a recurring problem throughout of my games, but this game took it to another level. Finding games is hard, and since back then there's no lobby search, you're really lucky to get a lobby. Now with the lobby search is a thing, there's not a lot of people playing as well, and those who plays are either grouped up in a lobby, password protect the lobby, or quits after someone joins.
Alright then, playing alone it is then!
Nope. The bots isn't quite smart, and playing with bots is an absolute chore, since they let themselves get surrounded, get ambushed, does not avoid the big guy, and the worst of it all, their stats is the same as a human player. In Payday 2, while they can't do anything good except revive you, at the very least they can be a bullet sponge. In this game, bots can't do anything effectively except revive you, and they get downed as quick as yourself.
And there's no mods that can fix this.
So if the core gameplay is lacking, what else it is to say?
It also doesn't help that the equipment plays an important part as well. If you don't have high rarity weapon, you can't do much on higher difficulty, but if you play lower difficulty, you can't get high rarity weapon. Sure one of the update now gives you more control over the RNG, but it's still a major grind to get what you need, and since grinding requires you to play a game, and there's little to no playerbase at times, how can you grind properly?
TL;DR Buy this on sale and if you have regular friends playing it. If not, don't bother

At the start of the game, you are nothing more than a humble traveller arriving in the great land of Calradia, whether your reasons be for invoking vengeance on a foe or for a simple lust for glory and power. You start off with little, but if you chose the correct story you can start off with very good stats, which is fantastic. You usually start off with a crossbow, the clothes on your back, and  sword, and having a shield included is not uncommon either. The start of the game is you arriving in a city of your selection, whether via caravan or ship. You're ambushed by a bandit, and once you defeat/are defeated a merchant unique to the city comes up to you.
The interactions are always the same, no matter what merchant. Blah blah blah, brother has been kidnapped, get 5 troops, etc. Then, after that, there is no story but what you make. Rivaling kingdoms will invade each other, whether it be because they're getting too big for their shoes, to regain lost land, or in hopes of becoming more powerful. Each nation has it's own speciality, such as the Rhodok's being effecient in defending castles or the Khergit's horsemen causing fear and dismay across the open battlefield.
Generally, the first people that are out are the Khergit's due to their complete and utter failure at defending castles. The Sarranid are also subject to fall, but if you join them and have a strong enough force you can very easily make them a force to be reckoned with. It is simply wonderful to see the AI having cracks at each other, whether you've gained enough reknown to be known across the land or not.
Whether it gets easier or harder later on is difficult to say. It is definetly very hard in the early game, since you don't have much money to support your party, and if you lose a tournament that had all your funds in it boom, you're gone. However, you don't have to worry about the responsibility of defending a castle, which can be a great pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ especially if you do my playing style which is amassing a large army of cavalry and tearing up the battlefields.
Later in the game, it is much more common for you to be gaining money, but as I said you have to worry about making a great garrison to defend any castles given to you by your selected king, and then wages are also incredibly high due to the size your party should be at at this point.
The game is very fun, though does have flaws;
Pro's:
With five rival kingdoms that battle each other differently every time you play, the replayability value for this game is virtually infinite.
A sort of create your own story game, where you take up arms to a kingdom and eventually become a great king, ruling with either an iron fist or a kind heart.
An interesting character creation screen, starting with you deciding your father's line of work and ending off with what city you ventured off to.
You get all dem ho's.
Five unique kingdoms that have their own strengths and weaknesses.
TOURNAMENTS!
You're allowed to purchase productive enterprises that can either get you a lot of money or a small amount of money.
A market system, where some things will be sold for more in certain areas while it'd be much cheaper in others. Once you figure it out and buy productive enterprises, you're set for life.
Con's:
Graphics are somewhat poor, but the game does a good job of making it work, and if it's still an issue I believe there's a few mods that can solve the problem.
I've encountered a few bugs here and there, but only one of them was really game breaking.
Steals your soul.

A good side-story to Deus Ex: Human Revolution, unfortunately this game only contains Part 1, the planned Part 2 never get released. Graphics quality is not that good, but since this game originally released for smartphone, I'm not complaining. I think the developer did a good porting job. Gameplay is really fun and similar to DX:HR, but more simplified, think of it as DX:HR Mini. I got this game really cheap from Steam Summer Sale 2017 Deus Ex Bundle and for me it's definitely worth it. I just hope one day we will get Part 2 and the rest of the story.

Honestly, this game isn't nearly as bad as people make it out to be. Sure, the tutorial is kinda 'casual' and an experienced Deus Ex player might be angry about that. But after that, I find that it gets much better and more open.
The graphics are what they are, but let's be frank here: the graphics of the original Deus Ex weren't beautiful either, even by 2000's standards. The initially reported mouse acceleration problems were fixed as far as I can tell, because I had no problems with it whatsoever. The game is a bit buggy at times, when achievements don't unlock immediately or when you clip out of the level, but if you quick save often (which you should anyway), this becomes less of a big deal. Also, clicks sometimes don't register right away or sometimes you want to pick something up but end up talking to a person nearby because the item highlighting doesn't work properly. Things like that, nothing game breaking, and with a bit of patience it's all doable.
Yeah, you can buy gear anytime in the pause menu, which is kinda hard to explain within the game world. That's the only real problem I would say the gameplay has, because it makes the game very easy and trivial at times because you can just buy more ammo or whatever else you need in the middle of a difficult situation.
It's a mobile port, alright. It's a fairly straight port and doesn't use the same engine as Human Revolution. But Deus Ex games were never about the graphics alone, and as far as I'm concerned the gameplay is mostly intact here. Sure, it has its compromises here and there, which makes it a bit of a lesser experience than DX:HR. But nonetheless, I had fun with it and would recommend it if you know what you're getting with this game. It's not THAT terrible as many people say, but it's not the exact same experience as DX:HR. I like it for what it is.

This is ether going to be one of the better, or worse MMO's you will sit down and play to be utterly blunt about this.
The main factor into this is the space combat, that set's it apart from any other MMO to date. Your ship has crew who's activtly 'reparing' it , you have to adjust your power setting to effect your weapons damage output/shield strength/engions for movement/auxellery for skills, and then control your shield FACING strength as well to detur attacks and oh so damaging torpetos. All the while your ship has both a fore and aft for weapons to be attached, a deflector dish, shield, engions, and generater for power, and a number of slots based around tactical/science/engerneering focus. That's quite a lot of stuff to be taken into account of, and goes far beyond the bare bone 'armor/rings/weapon' many other MMO's fall into doing, inclduing when placement, distance momentum and other factors all begin effecting space combat by quite a bit as well.
...But then you get to the ground combat and it all becomes the same ol 'tab selection' MMO you've played a billion times over in anything else. While they have tried to make it more 'dynamic' with crouching/aiming, and even a 'shooter mode', the entire combat is just far too basic to put any effort into it beyond 'stack best gear/sets, auto attack anything nearby till dead'. Thankfully, the space combat tends to be the most done and played overall, sadly there are still a lot of 'ground only' ordeals you will WANT to do for goodies.
Witch we come towards the second desion breaker. This is one of the few F2P games where you are able to 'buy' the Cash Shop Currenty...without spending real life cash to earn it. In essance, there is a materal, dilitinum, that is collectable from missions, and as a 'refinement' cap of 8000 a day. So even if you collected 10K in a day, you only get 8K of that usable one day, and then the other 2K the next. This stuff can ether be used for specal 'reputation rewards' such as specal weapons/equipment sets for both space and ground, used to gather fleet based gear ( the best gear in the game ), or can be sold off on a market to buy Zen ( the cash shop cash ) from others who have put it up. Admittly, this means buying the Zen slows down your ablity to buy the equipment sets and the like, but this also means you can acually get anything in the cash shop store...as long as you put enough time into the nessary farming and selling to earn it all.
The game past that is what one expects from a F2P experance, some of the 'best ships' are on sell via the cash shop, account boosters gallore more less inventory enlargements, useless pets and ship bridges to be spiffy with, along with some of the most insane prices fror some of the better stuff ( most of the ship 'packs' cost $50 for 3 ships, and you will want all three of them. ). While I might play this a ton, I can't say it doesn't have a lot of flaws towards it, so I couldn't recommend it towards anyone, but I can at least do my best to be informative about it.
