Niche looked like it was going to be a really fun game right up until I hit the tutorial and it became obvious how poorly designed the interface is.
One step of the tutorial tells you to click the family tree button "in the lower left", but there are a lot of buttons in the lower left and most of them aren't labeled.  None of the stats are explained in the tutorial, nor is the mutation mechanic, the action count, or many of the other important features.
It gets even worse once you leave the tutorial and puts you on an "easy" island.  I don't dislike hard games, I love a challenge.  But there's a difference between something being hard because it requires skill and something being hard because you can't win if the game decides to throw the wrong thing at you.  Here's the setup for this problem:  All of your animals have a limited lifespan and can take a maximum of three actions per day, two or even one if they're not fully grown.  Those actions include moving, collecting food, cutting grass, attacking things, mating, everything.  Each of your animals also require one unit of food every day which must be located and collected.  Movement actions are limited to one space at a time if there's tall grass in the way and almost every space starts off with tall grass.  That, in and of itself, was frustrating enough.  All three actions in a day would be spent cutting grass and moving to find food while the food meter slowly goes to zero.  And then just when you think you've got all your space cleared up for easy movement and your food sources located and you might actually be able to start playing the game, the grass starts growing back.  It doesn't even grow back in the order you removed it, it's as though every space has a percent chance of just spawning new grass every day.  If you do manage to secure enough food sources to keep your animals fed, some bigger creature shows up and starts systematically killing them off.  In my first game some huge black thing showed up and started attacking my animals one at a time and it took three days of all three animals attacking it with every action to kill it and by that time it had killed two of them and the last one was starving.  This is the easy island right out of the tutorial and it didn't get any better in subsequent games.
So no, I don't recommend anyone buy this game.  If it was in early access I could cut it some slack for not having its systems sorted out yet, but this is a full release which means someone had to look at this and say "Yup, that's what I want my game to be".  That's upsetting because this game looks like it has so much promise.  Revamp the tutorial and rethink the core systems and I would give it another chance, but the way it is I can't bring myself to start up another new file.

This game exists somewhere between the Red Orchestra and Battlefield games so if you're familiar with them and enjoy those games this will probably feel pretty good. The controls are fairly straightforward for vehicles and infantry movement alike and while there are not many maps available yet, they vary greatly in size which allows a good change of pace when transitioning from one game to another. If you like shooting and enjoy the sights and sounds of WW2 battle, it's entertaining enough. This is unfortunately where the praise ends.
Before even starting into the gameplay I have to express just how much I dislike the UI. The menu screens cannot be moved or minimized at all, anywhere. So, for example, if i'm in a squad with my friends and i want to change weapons, I have to leave (or completely disband if i'm the leader) the squad, change my gear, and then reform the squad. The equipment also has this strange habbit of only showing the stats of weapons you DON'T own, so it is impossible to compare your equipment with things you're interested in buying easily. You also cannot look at what weapons/tanks/planes/etc will be available to you if/when you switch roles AT ALL. I had to look up the paratrooper weapons on a wiki just to know what they are! The menu is extremely crude, although at least everything is functional.
As for gameplay, I had the opportunity to play with a friend who was a higher rank so I was able to play in matches against/with people of higher rank, allowing me to see what fights look like when tanks and planes get involved. While encountering a tank as infantry is just as terrible and scary as it was in Red Orchestra (you will die, it's a tank), the weapons are completely outside my expectations in the worst way. In spite of realistic elements such as tanks being immune to rifle fire, sniper rifles killing you in one hit, etc, there are a tremendous amount of weapons in this game that do not perform even remotely like they would in real life. My main complaint is that the garand and other semi-auto rifles (starting weapons) have had their damage values nerfed tremendously but still have the recoil and performance of a full size rifle (high kick and poor CQC performance). This trend disappears with machineguns and higher priced weapons, which have near-zero recoil or inexplicably amazing DPS.
This transitions to my final complaint, sniper rifles. Overall they are not THAT great and I can name many games which have bigger problems with them than H+G, but with the recent opportunity for players to pay real money to instantly have a soldier promoted to recon and given a scoped rifle, most maps i've played on have revolved around dozens of people camping and using 1-hit kill weapons to pick off the attacking team. This is terrible because most maps are very big and have many large open fields with zero cover and most houses allow infantry to climb onto the roofs. Combine this with the fact that the game sometimes doesn't play gunshot audio or shot a tracer when you're being shot at, and you're left with dozens of mysterious deaths just trying to get out of spawn or approach an objective.
Will I keep playing? For now, yes, because I understand the game is still in progress and these changes are fixable, just let this be a warning that the game is far from done.

It's the early 1900s, and "the Master Painter" has returned to his seemingly abandoned home to finish painting his magnum opus. Take control of the masterpainter, and follow him on his journey as he furiously masterpaints all over his house. Watch as he masterpaints and coats the walls in his creative juices. Assemble sentimental objects to help aid in the masterpainter's masterpainting. Collect old notes from his wife about how his chronic masterpainting has ruined their marriage. Bear witness to the adverse effects that a masterpainting addiction has on your mental health. Can you help cure the masterpainter of his masterpainting addiction, or will he shoot his biggest, most creative load of all time?
Layers of Fear tells a cliche story, but it tells it very well. To its credit, it doesn't seem to be trying to reinvent the wheel when it comes to story telling. What it does do, and it does this very well, is create an amazingly terrifying atmosphere that is guaranteed to unnerve even the most seasoned horror game fans.
The setting is nothing new, but the concept is: It's your stereotypical haunted house simulator with a literally artistic twist. The rooms you progress through are randomly generated. This helps keep the game fresh if you're one of those completionist types who needs to replay games to find all the collectibles. Beyond that it's mostly just a gimmick, but a welcome one at that. The house is beautifully crafted and the atmosphere is very thick. The sound design is extremely well done, and It's easy to get lost (figuratively and literally) in the world of the Master Painter.
Speaking of the Master Painter, the guy is a total scumbag. What we learn of him doesn't
a pretty picture. He's an abusive, neglectful alcoholic who, as metioned earlier, does nothing but masterpaint all day. It's impossible to identify with him in any way, unless the player has an affinity for art. The voice acting feels off... that's not to say it's bad, it's just that it doesn't seem to fit the character that the developers are presenting to us. All in all, the protagonist is interesting, but he's mostly just a flanderized "tortured artist" type of guy.
I would definitely recommend this game to horror fans. It's a must play. I'm hesitant to recommend it to adventure enthusiasts, as the story is shaping up to be very cliche and predictable, but you should give it a try if you're at all interested. It's definitely something people should experience.
Now if you'll all excuse me, I'm going to go browse ArtHub and masterpaint.

Just to start off with, if you're not a die hard Sci-Fi fan or Trekkie, Chances are you won't get very much out of this game.
The Good:
Story - The entire game is more or less one big love letter to the pre-Abrams Star Trek universe, filled with locations, ships, references, and even a few characters straight out of the TV series and movies (Some of which are even voiced by the original actors!). From helping Dr. McCoy fight an interdimensional menace to exploring Deep Space 9, anyone familiar with the series will feel right at home, if not get a little too excited at the notion of commanding your own Galaxy Class starship.
Space Combat and Exploration - Speaking of starships, space combat and exploration is pretty much the bread and butter of the game, and what many will, no doubt, enjoy the most. The combat is a bit slower paced than what some might expect however, as you'll be spending most of your time draining the shields of enemy ships before pounding their hull with torpedoes, rinse, repeat, until your opponent explodes. This isn't a bad thing, and it certainly makes for some very memorable sequences. There's also a lot of exploration, which will make up the bulk of your time between skirmishes with Klingons/Romulans/Borg/The Demon Spawn of Q (How is that even possible?!). This primarily involves you flying planet to planet, carrying out a series of randomized - though ultimately very similar - tasks.
The Bad:
Land Combat and Exploration - This will make many want to rip their hair out in frustration, and rightfully so. The ground combat is about as dull and rage inducing as it sounds. From objectives not being clearly marked, wandering around a planet's surface for 5 and a half hours trying to figure out where that last tree you have to scan is, to some VERY lopsided boss fights that you will win just by the very SKIN if your teeth. This is worsened by the fact that certain ground missions are bugged, and if you don't do things in a CERTAIN order - the game will NOT recognize that you finished the mission, and will make you start the whole thing over - from the VERY beginning.
The 'Meh':
If anyone was hopping into this game hoping to hear the sweet sounds of Jerry Goldsmith's iconic scoring for the Star Trek franchise, prepare to be disappointed. The game's music primarily consists of a decently orchestrated soundtrack made up of synthetic instruments. Considering this was originally published by the now dead Atari, who by the time this was being made they were practically broke, it's excusable, and composer Kevin Manthei does an admiral job of capturing the essence of the series in his music. This will be hit or miss for some.

First off, and this is probably the biggest thing people will complain about: the game, as of this writing, pretty much lacks a story. The only narrative here is that you meet a Love Fairy, and she decides to help you get better at hooking up with pretty girls through match-3 puzzle mechanics. As my friend described it: "It's basically a really well-polished Newgrounds dating sim." Though I agree with him wholeheartedly, the lack of a story did not bother me at all. I didn't buy the game looking for a nice story or well-developed character arcs...
I bought the game for its unique and solid gameplay: the strategy for the match-3 puzzles is deep and complex enough to keep the post-game from getting old or stale. It never feels grindy to keep playing, and I actually want to try to unlock all the outfits, hairs, and trivia. I will, however, say that once you've maxed out your stats and get enough of the Date Gift items, the gameplay will start to become easier even as the Affection quotas climb higher and higher. But up until that point, the difficulty curve is just enough to keep the puzzles challenging without becoming frustrating.
The voice-acting is great as well. Each of the girls sound distinct enough to be distinguishable, and the voices fit each girl's character very well. The girls themselves aren't the most fleshed-out characters. But do not let that dissuade you either, because they most definitely are not one-dimensional. Each girl has nuances that you can pick up through their questions for you. The correct answer isn't always what you would expect for that girl. There are also many subtle details within the girls' background information that gives them a little more life and depth. The reason why Jessie likes the winter time and Christmas decorations is a one such example, whereupon putting it together, I couldn't help but say, "Aww, that's sweet."
That said, while I appreciated that the girls were very diverse both personality-wise and ethnically, the focus on two of the girls' ethnicities seemed... incomplete, for lack of better term. It felt like part-way through the game's development, they made a decision to drop the ethnicity focus for every girl, but just left Kyanna's and Aiko's ethnic stuff there cause it was already done. This is really a minor nitpick, I know, but the game would have felt more polished if they had either gone through with the ethnicity thing, or scrap it entirely when they chose to take it out.
A minor problem I had with the game is that, while very functional, the user interface is a little obtuse and lacking. For example, closing the game window is the only way to exit the game; there's no way to quit the game if you're in full-screen. Another minor issue I had with the interface is that the Profile screen took too many clicks to navigate. I thought it a bit tedious to have to click back to view another girl's profile and found myself wishing there were some tabs to click through or even just arrows to cycle through them.
Besides those minor nitpicks, the game plays wonderfully, and the characters - while a bit underdeveloped - are interesting.

To start off, I personally think it's wonderful that it mixes videogame genres. It has action, horror, survival and even a little stealth. I personally don't think its really scary at all. If you want a scary game, get Outlast, Amnesia or PT (scary as hell but it's not available anymore I think). The game isn't the scariest, but it's definetely more interesting and bizarre than the games previously mentioned.
I usually don't like survival games with incredibly limited ammo and supplies but this game gets it right in my opinion. Each and every shot is incredibly precious and I was just always scraping by but was never out of ammo completely. It hits a sweet spot. The survival aspects weren't what kept me playing though; it was the atmosphere and combat.
Each weapon has this meatiness to it. They really pack a punch and it's so fun to kill monsters with them. There are also parts where you can booby trap an area and slowly kill a group of enemies. It's rewarding when you manage to succeed. The graphics are very detailed and immersive and the monsters spooky and deformed. It's a fantiastic mixture. That being said, the game is on the difficult side. It's definetly a japanese type of game. It strangely reminds me of Bloodborne but not nearly as difficult. Its still pretty challenging though but equally rewarding when you overcome the challenge.
Overall, I find this game to be special and it will stick with me for a long time to come.

This game has a simple premise: you simply move your ship around, and shoot at the baddies, quite similar to that old game Asteroids. Geometry Wars starts off easy, but once you hit around 10000 points, it really starts picking up and getting harder. There are two weapon upgrades you get, that alternate every 10000 points. A rapid fire machine gun thing, and wide shot. You also have a bomb that can kill all enemies on the screen at once. Yes, you will need to use it. There are many varieties of enemies, from the type that simply float around, to big long snakes that you have to hit in the head to kill, to those green squares that continually try to ram you and are smart enough to dodge your fire. It is a beautiful game: all retro graphics, with very nice anti-aliasing and wonderful multi-color explosions. I strongly recommend purchasing this game if you love a fast paced arcade-style game, with wonderful visuals, and brilliant 'just one more try' game play. LordWildMan score: 5/5

Niche is very relaxing in it's own way while retaining a bit of challenge to it- it all depends on how you play, really. Your pack could stick to an easy life on one island, building different families and not having to worry a day about food.. or they could venture out into more unforgiving lands like the tundra or savannah, where hazards and predators are far more eager to make short your Nichelings' lives. The only way to guarantee that they will survive is through evolution. Play with different genes and try to optimize them for survival by giving them horns, tusks, fangs, claws, and and even armored hides!
I've had this through at least half of it's beta (albeit I hadn't had a lot of time to play a whole lot), and it was certainly a treat to watch this game evolve and grow as the creatures within do.

I love games like this but they need to do something about that tutorial. It gives you the barest sense of what to do and then throws you to the wolves. As yet, I have absolutely no idea what I'm supposed to be doing aside from getting food and making babbies.
That said, it's a damn fun game and I can definitely see the complexity and depth so, despite the complete lack of explanation, I'm going to keep digging into it.

First off congratualtions to the team on the official launch!
Secondly:
TLDR: A breeding game with a twist. This game is amazing. If your into survival games, if you like turn based games, if you love animals and like a challenge (especially when it comes to breeding a creature you like) this is the game for you.
I've only ot 12 hours on this account but I originally logged about 40 hours on my sisters before buying it myself. I think I started playing back on 0.3.0 and the game has come on leaps and bounds since then. I originally saw this game and knew I would love it just because of the art. Its such a cute game with amazing artwork that has inspired allot of beautiful fan art in return. I've also always loved games that involve breeding animals, it fascinates me and this game takes it that one step further by making genes that your survival depends on.
Cons:
-If you don't like micro mangment your not going to like this game. You have to micro manage every move and action your creature makes. You have to choose specific genes you want to try and breed into your tribe for EVERY creature.
Pros (AKA why I love the game)
-If you like micro managment see above, I like micro managment, at the very least it dosnt bother me!
-With a diverse gene pool of colours, patterns, claws, eyes, horns and special ancient genes (plus many more) you end up with a diverse and intresting tribe of creatures. Its can be a fun challenge to try and breed a creature that can not only survive and thrive, but look exactly how you want.
-Challenging terrain makes for intresting game play as your forced to adapt to your enviroment. From growing gills to deal with water and posion fangs to help you harvest poisnous berries your forced to hunt for the perfect mate to join your tribe.
-The danger doesn't just lie in what is under your feet but what lurks around you. Rouge males with negative genes stalk you through the grass waiting for a lone female to stray from the tribe, leeches lurk at the water's edge waiting to grab onto a passing baby (or even worse a bird swooping down and grabbing your baby!) and the big bearyenas roam around. These threats force you to keep on your toes and depending on what genes you have in your tribe you can try to fight or run. A fun update before launch added the possibility of bearyena hybrids that can introduce important genes into your tribe and I hope to see more hybrids introduced in the future!
To sum it up it's a cute entertaining game. If your unsure watch some of the many youtube videos that are already out about previous releases. Its a challenge to survive which is a good thing.

Emily Meyer is investigating homicides and finds herself in a story of revenges. However, she experiences herself an out of the world moment and helped by a medium throughout this...
Ghost Files: The Face of Guilt is telling the story of an homicide detective and ghosts. The plot is interesting but expect some twisting points. Anyway, what's interesting is the several out of the world moments, where Emily can find clues for her cases. But as high my expectations were, I was disappointed by the character herself. I don't mind middle-aged people, I'm slowly arriving to that point (though I would say that I'm still young, being 34 and half at the moment of this review). But I didn't really connect with her.
The gameplay is the standard one: use items, combine them, find them, solve puzzles and clear hidden objects scenes. However, now, if you want a above average game, you need to have a little twist. Here, it's the use of forensic tools for analysing fingerprints or blood which is really nice in the real world while it's the alchemy of elements that makes the ghost world interesting.
The graphics are also nice when you're in the other world: it's really dark and even a little tortured. Compared to that, the real world seems dull and sometimes, you're not even feeling that you're in contemporary setting. But well, aside from that, the rest is nice. The soundtrack is also enjoyable.
I've put so much expectation in this game that I was more disappointed in it because of the lack of the connection with the main character. It's really the only downside of the game. Yet, I'm still recommending it because I still found fun for the majority of it.

Sucks to say, but this has to be one of the worst AM games to date. The hidden object puzzles are pixel hunting, sometimes they are unresponsive. The story is a weird mash of themes, and the puzzles leave a lot to be desired. You can tell they try tried, but they really missed the mark on this one.

This engine has obvious limitations. All the puzzles in this game I have already played in other publications by Artifex Mundi, so they felt highly repetitive - even more so since they were also repetitive in itself, which could potentially make it just as boring for people who have not played other AM games. There isn't even a reward (achievement) for playing this title at highest difficulty or for doing the mini game instead of the HO puzzles.
Also, The HO scenes didn't vary on my second playthrough, the objects needed are always the same, which only increased my boredom. The achievements were mediocre, too, the game overall posed no challenge whatsoever.
The story seemed somewhat fresh at first, which got me prematurely excited, only to quickly realize that the mystery's solution was 100% stereotypical, hence obvious and predictable and void of fun. The bonus chapter was a bad joke; you don't even get to fuel the Elemental Forge with runes here, it was just a quick "clicking-through" experience with a non-existent story.
Some of the voice acting (except for the main character) was quite bad and partially annoying.
While the game is technically flawless and sports beautiful, athmospheric art, I overall cannot recommend it.

Ghost Files promises some realistic police drama in the form of a hidden object game, but it just cannot follow up its own premise. At least it is teeming with half-decent hidden object scenes.
The first half hour of Ghost Files: The Face of Guilt shows such a great promise. It starts up as a realistic police procedural drama, where we have to use our forensic skills and some standard modern hidden object game mechanics to capture a serial killer.
This premise lasts about thirty minutes before the forensic equipment decides to sit out most of the game as unused clutter in the inventory, and the realism exits stage left the moment we end up in a ghost realm to look for magical runes.
To the game’s credit, at least it manages to retain an above-average quality. The plot never stops and the detective work brings plenty of surprises, even if the final twist is quite dumb and comes from nowhere.
Gameplay is similarly above average, thanks to the dozens of decent hidden object scenes and some of the nicer puzzles. You probably will not remember Ghost Files for long, but it provides as much entertainment as most other HOGs can for a similar price.

Before buying this game, you must understand what this game is and what it is not.
Funfair Ride Simulator III was originally a app for Android and iOS smartphones where the user is able to control several different funfair rides by using slider controls, lighting controls, funfair jingles and camera positions. Through the different camera positions is also a on-ride cam where it looks like you are in the ride just as you would in real life. The game has a built-in customer system, where customers respond to the way you control the ride.
The game was originally released on iOS and Android with two rides and seperate dlc packs. Some people believe there is a difference between the price of the DLC packs. This is a misconception however. On ios and android, you pay 1,99 per ride that you would want to unlock. FRS 3 for mac/pc is a updated graphical version of this android and ios app and therefore explains why the graphics are not set to the same standards as their latest release, Virtual Rides III. If you wish for realism, buy Virtual Rides III. If you want a quick, easy and fun funfair experience, buy FRS III.
With the mac/pc version you get 3 rides instead of 2 to make up for the ride packs created. All rides are placed together in ride packs of three. While on ios you pay 2 euro/dollar per ride, you pay 6 euro per 3 rides on the mac/pc version. The price is exactly the same. The DLC idea was built within the time that this was still a ios and android app, what some users disagreed with. However, I believe that the majority of them never played FRS 3 on their smartphones.
Now on to the game, i enjoy the mac/pc better then the version on my smartphone due to the larger screen and the accessibility this game has. I recommend this to all funfair enthusiasts. Just please keep in mind that Virtual Rides III has more customization, more rides in the base game, and a more authentic funfair experience.

Well. Where to begin?
Ah yes.
Jesus Christ.
How this game isn't branded as 'Sniper Elite: 5000 for the Achievement' is beyond me. You want zombies? This game gives you zombies:
of zombies. And I'm not talking Left 4 Dead's hordes that cack-handedly slap you in the face in the hopes of making you feel bad, every single one of the shambling fascists is more than capable of dishing out a bucketload of damage before you're able to shoot or kick them away. And yes, this version of Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army comes with the ability to
. Thank God! A marked improvement over those awkward 'Oh God, it's right in front of me and slapping me with a torch, blindly noscope, blindly noscope!' moments from the previous instalments. I say instalment
, since if an enemy was right in front of you in SE:V2, it turned into a frantic mess of you flipping your SMG out and randomly spraying.
Oh! That brings me to my next topic: The new weapons. Well, I say 'new' quite losely, since they were in the previous instalment of 'Hitler Forgot To Say The Lord's Prayer Before Playing With an Ouiji Board', but c'mon. What you're given is the set of DLC rifles from V2, including the good old fashioned Lee Enfield and M1 Carbine (My personal favourite), and a few other new toys including the MP44 and Webley revolver. I'm not saying they're bad weapons; By all means, use whatever you like since one rifle headshot puts down any regular shuffler with absolute ease.
But just know this: You miss a headshot, and that guy's probably gonna get right back up and smack you in the face with whatever is in his hand.
Among the hordes of normal mindless grunts, you do have a few guys to keep you on your toes.
There's undead Snipers in gasmasks, capable of leaping from perch to perch through a sheer disregard of the laws of physics.
There's Fire Gods, which are 8 foot tall burning men that supercharge other zombies if you don't stop them, and those zombies run at you like they're on fire (They really are. What a nice bloke, setting his mates on fire.)
There's everybody's favourite exploding runners, who run at you whilst screaming demonic noises that are actually marginally disturbing.
And then, of course, there's your old pal: The giant, trench-coated MG42 operator that takes a good few headshots to take down.
They never said this would be easy to play. One wrong move, you're surrounded. One missed shot, he's already back on his feet. One wasted grenade, you've only removed 2 out of the 16 that are shambling at you. But with steady nerves, you can get through it.
Of course, your nerves are unlikely to be steady when you discover the darker secrets of the game. Hitler is long gone from the Fuhrerbunker, so that's just one less problem. You wouldn't really have had time to kill him, anyway: You'll probably be discovering disturbing easter eggs, keeping an eye out behind you, and all while everything is probably plotting how to rip you to shreds. Mannequins can move themselves. Lights can change in an instant. Things can wake up without warning. And Sieges can happen at any time.
Yet, through all this, it's probably one of the best looking zombie games I've played for a while. Sure, the amount of mist and whatnot can play havoc with lesser PCs, so make sure you can run Sniper Elite V2 on at least medium before you give this one a go. Yes, there are probably more frightening zombie games. Yes, there might be games with a better co-op experience (EVERYBODY is going to be stealing grenades from each other in this one, so just get there first). And yes, there are DEFINITELY better zombie games available.
But for £10.00, this is probably one of the best available for a tenner and does come with an air of fear you just don't see in games anymore.
And what was that you just saw shifting down that hall?
Better save that grenade, it's probably just another shuffler.

Update - 11-7-2016
I left a brief review last night, because I felt it was imperative to get my review/upvote in the system.
As far as I can see, people are giving a good game a needlessly hard time.  Studios like Fatshark make PC gaming great and deserve support from those who enjoy their work.
Indie dev's who get it right are the only things sparing gamers from the tender mercies of mega publishers.
I am not hardcore, but avid.
So off the soapbox, on to my actual thoughts about the game.
My PC is a windows 7x64.  Dual core intel @ 3.0 ghz.  8 gigs system ram, sata HD, Nvidia gtx 1060, slightly overclocked.
I am sometimes damned by my core count with games released after 2015.
Even though this game recommends a CPU that out specs mine as a minimum, it performs well (60fps, smooth) on nearly the highest settings on my machine.
This is because fatshark has done an excellent job optimizing AND delineating relevant settings on the graphics tab.  It has a small prompt on each attribute slider, telling users whether a setting affects CPU or GPU.  Very useful to me, as I have a fantastic GPU and a dated CPU.
(Guys.. vram is a must for pretty textures, I upgraded my card to a 6gig unit for less than $300, plug and play)
So even with my pitiful dual core, this game smoked...  I have read comments about performance issues and have trouble understanding why they have happened.  I'd guess in most of these cases, the developers are not to blame...  as games get more demanding, computer will become obsolete...  this is an unfortunate reality of our market.   If we want better than what consoles get, it has to happen.  Developers can only optimize so much...
Gameplay:
As I previously stated, the play feel is much like left for dead.   Co-op is fun, and playing with bots is fine as well, should you choose.  I like the idea of a loot system, though I haven't gotten far into it.  L4D had random weapon drops,  I will have to decide over time which I prefer...  as an RPG fan, I usually go in for loot and inventories.
It is easily a plus to play the story missions with all BOTs on your team, this can be a plus because of the great voice acting the characters have.  Their dialogue adds superbly to the narrative.
Setting:
Much to love here.  I hate that bloodborne never came to PC.  Medieval culture and fantasy is a very dramatic setting in my mind...  the fact that Vermintide is set in th warhammer universe makes it even better.   I am a real time gamer who envies the Dawn of War crowd all their content, and I love every chance I get to explore the 40k mythos in a game I can actually play with any proficiency. To start off, I personally think it's wonderful that it mixes videogame genres. It has action, horror, survival and even a little stealth. I personally don't think its really scary at all. If you want a scary game, get Outlast, Amnesia or PT (scary as hell but it's not available anymore I think). The game isn't the scariest, but it's definetely more interesting and bizarre than the games previously mentioned.
I usually don't like survival games with incredibly limited ammo and supplies but this game gets it right in my opinion. Each and every shot is incredibly precious and I was just always scraping by but was never out of ammo completely. It hits a sweet spot. The survival aspects weren't what kept me playing though; it was the atmosphere and combat.
Each weapon has this meatiness to it. They really pack a punch and it's so fun to kill monsters with them. There are also parts where you can booby trap an area and slowly kill a group of enemies. It's rewarding when you manage to succeed. The graphics are very detailed and immersive and the monsters spooky and deformed. It's a fantiastic mixture. That being said, the game is on the difficult side. It's definetly a japanese type of game. It strangely reminds me of Bloodborne but not nearly as difficult. Its still pretty challenging though but equally rewarding when you overcome the challenge.
Overall, I find this game to be special and it will stick with me for a long time to come.

Having read the hype on this game and reading the many positive reviews it seemed ideal for my choice of gameplay. I am a huge fan of the Silent Hill games, less so of the Resident Evil series but I do enjoy them.
I am on 100MBit broadband and it still took a few hours to download the 60GB (including DLC) so I figured this must be a graphical feast.  I fired it up and it defaulted to 1920x1080, which was promising given what I had read in the reviews, then I headed into the Survivor level gameplay.  Initially the video clips seemed well done but then I realised they were no better than most of the PS3 ones I've seen. No matter, the gameplay must be great from what I read. I managed to skip the video that explains what happens to you and woke up in the first part of the story.  I went down a slide a few minutes later and then spent about an hour trying to get through the next couple of rooms.  Poor camera angles and FoV made it very difficult to move safely and the enemy ignored the distractions.  I think I must have died an average of 10 times a minute for the majority of the hour.
Finally I gave up and asked for a refund.  As a seasoned gamer, I don't claim to be a gaming ninja, I should be able to get past the first and second scene of a game without this much difficulty and frustration.  I have never struggled so much with a game as this one and I didn't find it particularly scary either.

A truly brilliant and gruesome survival horror masterpiece. Definitely one of the most terrifying games I've ever played, and I think it easily eclipses the best of the Resident Evil series. The craftsmanship on display here is second to none. It is exceedingly beautiful decay, oxymoronic as that sounds. Fantastic character design, environments, textures, effects, everything. Framerate gets a bit choppy when specs are set to max and motion blur and tons of action are going on. The game is also HARD, fair warning. Definitely manageable, though I do have to say the encounters with the black haired demo psycho ♥♥♥♥♥ almost made me throw in the towel. So yes, there are some unfairly difficult segments. I do think it's worth sticking it through to the end just to see how twisted Shinji Mikami's brain can be. Storyline is pretty good though incredibly convoluted. Apparently the DLC helps explain a lot of the backstory, so I ended up purchasing it but haven't played that yet. The main character is also not very likeable, with stiff dialogue and unbelievable reactions. "What the hell is going on here?" Really dude? That's all you can say after going deeper and deeper into this nightmare? Yeah, a bit too nonchalant when his whole world is caving in around him.
8.5/10 - major downsides being the at times completely unfair difficulty and the fact that the main game does not flesh out the storyline enough. Otherwise, a seriously enjoyable frightfest.

The Showdown Effect wasn't actually that bad. It had some potential, but it fell short due to its absolutely terrible use of peer-to-peer matchmaking.
I live in South Africa, and we don't have the greatest connectivity, but I can play just about any multiplayer game with a latency of around 200. The Showdown Effect is not one of those games. Because of the use of peer-to-peer matchmaking, a player has to connect to one central player's computer and, well, it doesn't quite work. 50% of the time the "host" (central computer that all players in the same game connect to) has an awful connection, 20% of the time the connection just drops due to the host quitting his match, and the rare occasions when it does work, you will probably be in a server with rocket-launching tryhards that spoil all your fun, and diminish your chances of having a good game.
This takes me directly into my second point; I can hold my own when it comes to shooters, but not when the game I'm playing is horrendously balanced - on both sides of the spectrum! Good luck playing with a rifle, because it does fưck all damage and it has a reload period of about half the length of a match. However, equip a rocket launcher to your character and just about every player who can't dodge to the degree of a ninja will be your cannon-fodder.
It doesn't stop there, though. One of the easily-unlockable characters has INVISIBILITY. Yep, you read that right. You will not be able to see your enemy for a few moments, and in that time he can swiftly dispatch you to your grave. I guess the dev team for The Showdown Effect weren't too bothered with a very, very important aspect of competition - equality.
There are a handful of positives to this game though, such as the neat animations and the interesting levels with referenced events going on in the background. The cons heavily outweigh the pros, though - and for that I'd have to not recommend this game.
For the achievement hunters out there, expect to take around 3-5 hours to get all of them, but be warned that you need the Deluxe Edition content to get 2 of the achievements, as one of the requirements is to play as 2 characters that aren't acquireable in the base game.
In conclusion, I don't think The Showdown Effect is worth your money nor time, and so it is thrown straight into the bargain bin.

text: I got this game for free and thought it might be cool since it was developed by the Magicka team, so I booted it up. I went to search for a game and there was exactly one other person playing online. I haven't touched it since.

Multiplayer only games certainly have their place, but as far as I'm concerned that is in the realm of free-2-play games and should not extend to other pricing models. The reasoning for this is that as soon as the playerbase falls off, you're left with essentially a useless product, which often has a self cannibalizing effect as people are unwilling to buy your game for fear there will be no one online to play with. The Showdown Effect is one such game, something that may have been fun at one point, but is now more akin to a virtual ghost town.
I spent upwards of an hour waiting in the "Ranked" lobby and never once could find even three other players to start a match with. "Custom" games fare little better, with not even a hundred simultaneous players when I check two different times during the day.
I'm not mad that I have a dud in my library, but I am disappointed that I didn't get a chance to play what appears a fun and somewhat original game. The one custom match I made it into was surprisingly entertaining, with a great sense of movement, and clever use of line-of-sight to determine in what enemies were visible. It wasn't the most balanced multiplayer experience, but I would have definitely liked to play more of it.
But alas it isn't to be, which leaves me with this review. Unless you have a group of 3-7 friends who you know for a fact will be playing with you, there is no way I can recommend The Showdown Effect. Regardless of its actual quality as a game, one that must be sustained entirely by its community is worthless when said community has all but completely died. Strange as it sounds I hope that Paradox decides to switch this over to F2P as they have with some of their other titles, and in turn that more players will begin populating the servers making it playable once again. Until then, I would feel cheated knowing that others bought this without having said my bit, and I hope you will take a moment to consider this before pulling the trigger.

A HOG where you can interact with the real world and the Limbo(Between Life and Death).
Gameplay
Ghost Files: The Face of Guilt uses the traditional gameplay from HOG where you need to get objects and do actions to advance,plus the gameplay changes when you go to the limbo,making you use the element forge to get out from it. The game also features some lab tasks like analysis of some evidences like fingerprints.
As a bonus,in this game you need to find 3 kinds of objects hidden in all the scenes.
It also features a bonus chapter after the main game.
Graphics
The Graphics are very beautiful,with detailed places and cutscenes.
Sounds
The Musics get you in the feel,but the main feature here is the voice acting that is very good and combines with the characters very well.
Final Note: 9.5/10
Ghost Files: The Face of Guilt is an great HOG game,The mini-games and puzzles are very balanced,but not hard. The only downside in my point of view is that the game is a pretty short, even with the bonus chapter,but it doesn't affect the experience you'll have.

You get to play as Emily - a detective/cop/officer that doesn't beleive in "spiritual mumbo-jumbo." Of course, this changes because...near-death and otherwordly experiences? EH. Honestly, this game wasn't very
. Not that I really expected it to be, although, it is called "Ghost Files."
I truly wanted to enjoy this game. I wanted it to be one of my new favorites. However, you don't use your super handy-dandy forensic lab like I had hoped. And, even after the "otherworld" places that you go through, the main character doesn't really address any of it. In my opinion, the psychic is a random character that they threw in so they could say they had one. Overall, the plot was just about what you'd expect from an average HOG.
The hidden object scenes were decent. There was a mixture of word, shadow, and picture lists (I don't know technical HOG terms even though I've played way too many). The puzzles were basic, literally the same puzzles that you can come across in every HOG. Not bad, but nothing too challenging. Also, the music was weirdly intense for some situations. It put me on edge, but nothing came of it.
When loading out of hidden object scenes and cutscenes, it always froze for a few seconds before it loaded me back into the game. It froze long enough to make me wonder if it was an issue. I'm not sure if it was on my end or if it was just how the game did its thing. Thankfully, it never crashed. There were no serious bugs that kept me from getting achievements or finishing the game.
I didn't dislike this game, but like I said, it's not a brand spankin' new favorite of mine. I purchased it when it was on sale, and if you're interested, I'd gently encourage you do the same.

I have mixed feelings about this game and I wish there was an option neutral instead of recommend and not recommend. The official introduction emphasizes police techniques that will help you conduct your investigation but what the fail to tell you is that you will use it only once. Once for fingerprints, once for blood sample, once for ballistics. What is the point then? Without those “police techniques”, the game would not differ.
The plot is simple and predictable, if you’re hoping for unexpected twists and depth, don’t.
Puzzles and HO scenes are quite simple and not challenging. Easy way to score the “perfect game” if that’s what you’re into.
Map, navigation, etc., are all standard and similar to other AM games.
I have finished the main game and the bonus chapter under 4 hours, it felt much longer though and not for a good reason. Gameplay is extended by meaningless actions, not very important for the plot, i.e. replacing the ink in the pen to sign insignificant document, which requires four steps action (seriously, why would you do that?).
The game is average. You can play it for badges and achievements but buy it on sale only.

Here are some technical fixes to really improve the gaming experience too (Side note, I really like the letterboxing but it can be disabled in MANY ways not mentioned here. The easiest being in the game menus...):
***How to remove the 30fps cap***
-Select the game from Steam library, right click on it and select properties.
-Add "+com_allowconsole 1" (without quotes) to Launch Options from General tab.
-Run the game and open the console with "insert" key.
-"r_swapinterval 0" (without quotes) for fully unlock the fps.
-"r_swapinterval -1" (without quotes) for 60fps cap.
-"r_swapinterval -2" (without quotes) for 30fps cap, this is the default value.

Free weekend player here.
I'll start with the fact, that i have never played any Warhammer game BUT i did play L4D2 and KF which i both own and like a lot.
I think that this game is for sure a solid title if you can learn to live with it's flaws.
I'll try to point out what i like about it and what i don't.
- there is very little to none introduction to the game menu (actually the Inn that You land in) and You have to discover how it works for Yourself
- the gameplay is based on same "story mode/coop" mechanics (group interactions, special enemies, etc.) with little changes made in almost every aspect of the game, so if You're more experianced You'll know the drill, and if You're a new player - You won't be spending hours to learn how to play
- it has much better feeling of melee combat and the atmosphere is in general different (more like medival battle)
- ranged weapons are in overall polished and interesting (diversity in specs, alternative fire modes) but run only one type of ammo
- character coversations are also on very high level (You can always say when there's i.e. dwarf or elf in the team, not to mention they can and WILL act hilarious from time to time)
- there are some preety small, but yet attractive built in systems that have influence on gameplay (small eq on each hero, niche crafting in the inn and some rng loot at the end of each successfull mission)
-sadly it's more buggy than L4D2 (during the free weekend i managed to stuck in walls, crates or under the surface of water.... i also seen teammates/enemies flying so high, that You could only see a tiny red spot in the sky...)
- special rats dont care if You're behind a shield or that you jump to the side... they just do "what they are meant to do"... even if its absurd... so You can shoot'em from a long range... or cry for help :)
- the biggest special kind of rat (tank equivalent) is freakin' unstopable... the tank from L4D took breaks to throw something so You could take a breath while hiding behind something... or You could just play with him hide and seek between various map objects.... but this THING is just rushing towards You and Your only hope is that the team manages to kill it before it breaks through your block for the 10th time... dont bother running away... it's faster :P
- lobby matchmaking is good - it will search for closest servers, with the mission You have chosen to play and with a free hero slot that You have picked in the first place - If it doesn't find a perfect match, it will propose You to play a diferent hero or host a game on desired map
In overall im positive about the game.
I love the atmosphere, the theme, the fast and chaotic hammer swinging :P , and even the pesky vermins :P
Sad part is im still not convinced enough to become a fan of it.
Constant glitches here and there, lack of balance (or maybe there is a need of more enemy interactions? so it's rather lack of content?) and preety high game price discourage me from buying it...
My advice is - make the title richer - or even cheaper than it is now.
Personally I will wait for higher discount.

I love niche, and I have had it for a while, so I thought I might write a review.
Niche is full of content, (with even more coming!), and you can mish-mash stuff however you want. There are two modes: sandbox and story. In story mode, you start with Adam losing his family and go on the quest to find them with his new mate, eve, whose descendants search for the fabled adam's island where Adam's family resides. You can go full or do-or-die in sandbox, facing harsh climates and deadly predators completely unprepared, or you can travel around the peaceful islands, experimenting with the random genes you received and telling story's.
I have found that most (correct me if I am wrong)of the negative reviews on niche are made by people who have p,Syed under an hour, and they complain about the fact that the game seems "boring", "confusing", "repetitive", and that's true, at the start, but as you advance to new islands and survive, your tribe's story's become more complex and interesting. The only way for it to be boring is if a) you spend only 30 mins on it like most of the negative reviewers did and then just drop it, or you have no creativity at all.
Niche allows you to build your own culture and traditions. You shape the feel of your world, choose the colors and landscapes.
The unlocking system for niche genes is quite clever, based on real genetics but a little more loosey goosey so you don't have to wait billions of generations like in real life. You can completely change the genetic make up of a tribe in 3 generations!
Although the island unlocking system in Storymode is a bit tedious, you can just switch to a Sandbox game and BOOM you are on the island you wanted to be on.
Niche is an overall great game!
My only critique: (take note these are minor things, not that important. I like to nit-pick :P)
is that there should be a creature creator that lets you see what combinations would look like and what they would do.
is that there should be more uses for digger paw
Is that fully-hybridized nichelings should have better movement, although it is true that it would be a little op. But still, I would like the movement to be at least 2, maybe even 3, but not one!
(This is only if you want more than 5 games or you want to play older versions but still have room to make new games on the other versions)Is that there should be a way to get the save file of a game without having to dig through your folders (and the folder it's in does not appear on some platforms) like maybe a small button on the screen next to your worlds that will open up the folder automatically.

Let me start by saying I own the original majesty and expansion on disk and have played it for years.  So I will be comparing it  to M 1.
The two games are very similar.  Almost identical on the surface.   However, M1 is very hard to play on modern machines.
1. The early game is a bit of a struggle financially as your income is severly limited until you are able to get trading posts up and running without losing them.  In M1 you could place a trading post anywhere on the map outside a limited radius from your marketplace.  In M2 you are restricted to only a few preset locations for trading posts, but the upgrade for them is a weak turret able to defend from weaker foes.  Your progress in the game is entirely limited and artificially paced by your gold income, so it can be a little frustrating in the early game.
2. Guilds are limited now to 3 heroes while in M1 you had up to 4. The way M2 is set up, the number of heroes you have doesnt have much impact on your income like it did in M1.
3. Your marketplace has a set income per level and you can only have 1 marketplace, period. M1 allowed you to build many marketplaces and use the marketday feature to get more money to help you in the early game.  M2 controls the pace of your economic development rather harshly IMO.  It makes one of the campaign scenarios almost impossible that depends entirely on saving up a set amount of gold in a rather short time.  Gold that you need to defend your settlement from the constant onslaught of dragons and elementals from day one.  I tried that scenario a number of times now and still havent managed to save up the required gold(35,000) in the time limit. Im constantly having to hire or ressurect new heroes and upgrading everything so they can survive against dragons and elementals.  I think its possible to win, but I havent done so yet.  So anyway... the economy design in M2 is rather weak IMO.
4. They have combined the graveyard with the mausoleum from M1.  Making a graveyard that now produces enemy skeletons on your settlement and you can also pay to resurrect your heros from it.  You do not have to buy a graveyard, it just appears at a random location by your settlement once you have had a hero die.  It takes up alot more space than the M1 graveyard though and that can cause problems when trying to organize your settlement.
5. Guard towers are nearly invincible in M2 compared to M1.  However, when you upgrade your tower, your tower guard doesnt get stronger, which was a little disappointing to me.  A tower is cheap and can handle all but the strongest creatures, but also a large number of medium sized creatures can overwhelm a tower without hero help.  The point is, they are strong and I surround my castle with them right away at the start of a game.  I think they are a little too strong, and the guards a little too weak.
6. The Inn.  M1 inn were a good source of steady income.  They produced gold regularly just like the peasant huts but a little more and heroes loved to hang out at the inns which also generated more gold when they did.  The Inn in M2 are pretty useless.  They dont generate gold and you can use them to create hero parties up to 4 members after upgrading it.  I think they do get some gold from heroes that visit the inn, but it seems that heroes prefer to run home instead of to the closest Inn.  To me the hero groups seem rather pointless, plus it costs you 500 gold just to form the group.  Overall the Inn isnt worth the investment.
7. Temples.  Temples have almost become a moot point in M2.  You cant build one until you have upgraded lvl 3 castle and guilds, AND they cost a fortune to build, AND you can only build them on preset spots on the map whihc often are far from your settlement, AND you cna only hire 2 temple heroes or for an exorbant price you can convert an existing hero to a temple hero.  By the time you are able to get a temple, your heroes are already powerful, have everything, and most of the map will be cleared out.  There literally no reason to get a temple except that its something to spend your late game gold on.  In M1 you only needed a lvl 2 castle to build most temples and then you could hire all the cool temple heroes and get the spells relatively early in the game and enjoy them.  M2 has botched up temples IMO.
8. Heroes Inventory space.  Too small.  They get 2 slots for a weapon and armor, and 4 slots for everything else.  Well guess what....   **** the magic bazaar and the 7 different potions available. Maybe its more than 7.  Im not sure since I havent finished the campaign and there are blank slots in the stores.  I will build a magic bazaar because it generates automatic income, but I do not research any potions.  Your heroes have limited inventory space and they need that space for the 2 magical protections at the market, a weapon and armor, healing and mana potions.  There is no room for anything from the magic bazaar.  They ****** up with that.  I dont recall how much inv space heroes had in M1, but I dont recall there being any issue.
9. The Hall of Heroes.  Its a nice touch for the campaign, to be able to select a hero that you can hire again in the next scenario.  However...  by the time you can afford to build it and hire those old heroes, your new heroes will have caught up to them in levels and power so its rather pointless.  Better to just build another guild. Plus, what use is it in a multiplayer game?  Or even a custom game(if there is custom games... I havent checked)As far as I can tell... none.
10. Scouting missions.  I dont recall from M1, but in M2 it seems only a ranger or elf.. and maybe a rogue will take an exploration mission.  I played one scenario and didnt have any of those 3 guilds and I would place exploration flags out, and not a single hero would do them, no matter how much money I put on them.  That annoyed me.
11. The heroes are generally strong at low lvls compared to M1.  In M1 you would have heroes dying all the time at low levels with no equipment.  It made sense.  But was easy enough to just hire a replacement.  In M2 the heroes at low lvl are pretty strong.  Unless of course the incoming foes were high lvl.  They just run away.  Depending on the difficulty, they almost never die.  Warriors get tons of health, and clerics heal themselves... alot.  Plus, each guild can research special attacks, so not only are they tougher, but they hit really hard late game, even without upgraded weapons and armor.  Wait til you hire dwarves.  They are REALLY powerful. A lvl 1 dwarf is the equal of a lvl 10 warrior, at least.
12. Something else about the dwarves.  They use hammers.  Or battleaxes.  I cant tell.  But there are no axes or hammers for sale in the blacksmith.  Only blades.  The dwarf can buy the blades and it counts as an upgrade for their hammers, or whatever.  A design flaw?  A cut corner?  Whatever it is, its sloppy and it breaks the immersion factor.
13. The game runs really well, even on high settings with all the bells and whistles.  But, its still just as cartoony as M1.
Summary.  It seems they tried to cut a few corners here and there, maybe even tried to innovate a little bit from M1, but overall I think they screwed up what they tried to change from M1.  From the restricted economy, which is no fun, to the limited hero inventory and the preset building locations which limits the building freedom you had with M1, and the pointless endgame buildings.
There are no custom games in this.  M1 had complete customization, this does not.  Overall its not a terrible game, but it has more than enough shortcomings that I cannot recommend it.

Majesty 2 Collection is a real time strategy fantasy kingdom simulator, much like it's predecessor, Majesty. However Majesty 2 was developed by a new developer: 1C:Ino-Co. I don't have any other comments on the developer, I just wanted to highlight that this game has a different developer.
Majesty 1 was developed by Paradox Interactive and released in 2000, Majesty 2 was developed by 1C:InoCo and released in Apr 19, 2011.
*impersonates the Majesty Crier*
"Welcome Majesty, it's been some time since we've last met, probably about 10 years. Many things have changed, some changes are good, some changes are bad, but change they have."
Text doesn't really sell the impersionation, but one of the staples of the Majesty series was definitely the voice antics of George Ledoux, who voiced the Royal Advisor, Venn Fairweather.
As the story goes, the realm has had years and years of peace, and suddenly something stirs up your old enemies again and you need to return to the battlefield to protect your people.
Seeing as this is the Majesty 2 COLLECTION, you're also picking up some DLC with the core game; Majesty 2 (The core game), Kingmaker expansion , Battles of Ardania expansion , Monster Kingdom expansion. Naturally each expansion has it's own twist on the Majesty 2 Narrative. My personal favorite was the Monster Kingdom expansion because you find yourself making an alliance with your previous enemies. For once, *I* was the one summoning hordes of rats and goblins! Payback is sweat.
Not to re-invent the wheel, but if you want a better break down for the majesty game-play mechanics I highly suggest checking out my Majesty 1 review, I'll add a link at the end of this review. The quick explanation for anyone who hasn't played Majesty before: You set various flags with bounties which your hero's will either: Attack, explore, or defend. Depending on the flag you set.
You also control the buildings you can construct, and can cast several spells, but only if you have the gold to lay the foundation for a building, or cast a spell. So there's a type of fantasy economy going on in the game. You build a marketplace which sells potions, Hero "mynameismud" walks into the marketplace you made, buys some potions, your tax collector walks by, picks up the taxes, returns to your castle, BAM now those coins are in youre treasury which you can use to upgrade your marketplace.
There are different objectives and goals depending on the mission you're playing, as you progress you unlock more difficult missions which will have special conditions, sometimes you can only use a certain type of unit, other times you cannot construct something, other times you need to explore to discover the neccessary item/unit/guild/building.
The gameplay at surface level doesn't seem to have changed very much from the days of Majesty 1... but the game definitely feels different. Somehow the only way I can describe the game is "....more difficult". which doesn't seem like a very fair criticism. Majesty 2 feels more fast paced, and less forgiving if you mess up. It also feels like you need to do what I loving call "over building" more then I did in Majesty 1.
So basically my strategy has always been "Build as much as you can as early as possible, build enough hero's to keep your servants safe while they construct your money making buildings, then proceed to build the lowest costing guilds moving forward. So if I have 5 ranger guilds, I'll build some rogue guilds, and then warrior, then come back to ranger guilds when the price is lower then the other guilds.
You never really felt like you had very much control in Majesty 1, so the fact that I feel like I don't have much control in Majesty 2 doesn't really phase me, but something just doesn't feel quite balanced in Majesty 2. It doesn't take away of my enjoyment for the game, but some people will definitely be put off by it.
In conclusion... I'm biased for this game. I strongly suggest taking my opinion with a grain of salt when considering if you should play this game or not. I adored Majesty Gold Edition, even replaying the game I started playing and beating hard missions because I just adored the gameplay and had a knack for playing it.
Majesty 2 is quite different though, the spirit of the game is kept pretty well, but the changes will rattle most avid Ardania fans. I can't recommend Majesty 2 to everyone like I can for Majesty 1
But for those of you who might have an idea what you're getting into, this game could have been WAY worse, trust me, I played Lords of the Realm III recently.
Anyway, thank you for taking the time to read my review for the Majesty 2 Collection. I hope to take this game on as a video review sometime, but until that time. My name is Atratzu, and I approve this review.

Star Trek Online is a DEFINITE must have for Star Trek fans. There are a few things to consider though. If you want to pilot the "Enterprise" like many do, you will want to be an engineer class to fly it. That's ok to be an engineer, just keep in mind that it is a tanking class and the "Galaxy Class Cruiser" is an engineering class ship. So with that being said, here is some info on the rest:
There are three classes: Tactical (DPS), Engineer (Tank), Science (Healing and Support). Each class can branch out and take talents from all the different class trees. That being said it is better, in my opinion, to stick with what you picked in the beginning because your character is molded for it. I do like that the game is designed to let you decide, it just feels like I have to "choose" to be bottlenecked into the appropriate class talents.
The current level cap is 50 which is the "Vice Admiral" rank. That's cool and all...I just want more.
The UI is simple and easy to use. Very easy and customizable chat system.
Overall learning curve can be a little steep. There is a lot to learn and a lot that the game has to offer, so to me, that's ok.
Graphics are just ok. The galactic scenery is nice, but only if your card can take playing at max. The problem is that playing on max gives way to some framerate issues. During large encounters is where a lot of the problems come for a good deal of the player base that I have played with. I am going off of the masses of people that say something in chat during these encounters. So to those of you reading this and feel like commenting something like "I have a *fill in the blank* video card and it works fine for me". Please keep your "cool hipster" comments to yourself and go have some more coffee. You won't be blown away by the graphics, but it still gets the job done. Look at screenshots or watch a video. Never trust anyone's words when it comes to describing a visual based opinion. There are a multitude of outlets for you to pursue the evaluation of graphics.
Sound: Superb. It definitely sucks you into a Star Trek universe. The opening of the game when you log in just makes you want to raise your arms in epic-ness. During large encounters, however, the sound glitches out a bit. You'll hear a photon torpedo go out every now and then, but it is so damn impressive how big the fights are that I really don't care. It almost adds to how crazy everything gets.
Gameplay: This game is divided into two main parts; Ground and Space. Space is where a majority of the game comes from. You spend a lot of time in your ship. There is no first person view, and you can't pilot your ship from the bridge. You can visit the bridge and can even customize it to look like old versions of the Enterprise, or make it look like a futuristic Romulan Warbird bridge. All of these things cost real money but are a lot of fun. The ground gameplay is a little wonky and clunky. It still functions, but is far from being a main focus. It's fun to explore the procedurally generated worlds that are in the different quadrants of space, but to actually fight is...meh. If you are a traditional MMO raider looking to transfer into the sci-fi genre, leave now. This is, as stated in the beginning of this review, a game for Star Trek fans. Since I love seeing new worlds and love to explore in games, the ground game is passable for me. I just love to be a part of it.
Fleet (Guild): Really awesome idea. Basically you take nothing and build something extrordinary. You and your fleet donate your time and resources to create a "Starbase" where you and your fleet mates can go and hang out. But that's not all! You can get gear and equipment from fleet vendors using "Fleet Credits" that you earn by helping the fleet! Each time you upgrade your starbase, you get new things you can access such as fleet daily quests and new vendors.
With all that being said, this is a Free-to-Play game. It converted me to set up a subscription quickly because of how much fun I was having. I played up until ten for free and ran into my first "Free Account" problem. I had just recieved a new officer for my bridge which was exciting because they give your ship new abilities. I just got a shiny new ship and was ready to add the new officer...but wait...I can't add him! What's wrong?! Oh! Free players don't get another slot for their officers...Well screw that! I want the new abilities! So I subscribed to $14.99 USD a month. Again, I only recommend this for the fans of the series. I am planning on becoming a lifetime member. That's one payment of $299.99 USD and that's it. No more paying in unless you want stuff from the C-Store which is real money used for premium items like the "Next Generation Bridge" etc.
Final Scores:
If you are a Star Trek fan- 9.5 / 10 (Would be perfect if I could pilot from my bridge)
If you are a general MMO player- 6 / 10 (Graphics, sound glitches, and clunky ground play overshadow everything if you are
not psyched about the story and/or immersed by the universe.)

STO is a very well executed space MMORPG. The story is relatively engaging for an MMO, and the graphics are nice. If you are even a little bit of a trekkie, there is a great deal of fun to be had here.
That said, like most MMOs, it gets samey rather fast. It takes longer than most, which is something I really have to give the developers a great deal of kudos for, but eventually, you're going to feel like you're doing the same thing over and over again. Something that helps combat this is that it has the concept of user-created missions. You can actually get on a special account type and create missions for others to play. These range from the awesome to the "meh", and is another unique feature to STO.
The fact that this is free to play, and the paid addons are reasonable, makes it definitely one of the better MMO's out there. If you liked Earth and Beyond back in the day, you'll probably like this. Recommended!

I really wanted to like this game, because the concept behind it was so appealing to me. However, after playing it I cannot recommend it. The main problem is that you need to have a large tribe to maintain genetic diversity, but managing a large tribe quickly becomes a boring chorelike slog.
Almost as important is that managing your creatures genes is the central mechanic of the game, but the genetic records of your tribe are on a seperate screen from where you order them to mate. This means that you constantly have to dig through the records, and then hunt down the approprate creature, to have them mate. A feature that put a genetic overaly over the main game screen could have made breeding a lot less of a hassle.
In addition many of the islands are covered in tall grass which obscures you from prey and predators alike. The only problem is that it also obscures static features like berry bushes and nests, it would have been nice if the devs added a feature to mark these so you could remember where they are.
Finally there is no option to automate your creatures even if they are doing repetative tasks like gathering from the same berry bush.
I love games like this, and they are doing a great job at making it more and more interesting. :)

The only issue that I have is that the DLC isn't available because of the broken content but I'm still happy with all the missions that I get in this collection for only $5 so I'm not complaining too much. Ok not entirely sure how to review this. On the one hand it is challenging and can be fun but on the other it can be unbelieveably frustrating with some level design that is so shockingly bad some of the levels are literally impossible unless you retry them 20+ times. The thing is most levels are tough but ultimately fair, if you play them correctly you win. However there are 2 levels very early on where you can literally lose before you have the chance to do anything. I'm not exagerrating with that, your builders can all be killed before you even construct your first building and you have no chance the rebuild. The dragon mission is like that too, sometimes the dragon comes and does nothing, other times it will come and kill all your builders AND destroy the buildings before you have built them. This is extremely stupid level design as you lose before you start. On top of that there is the extremely annoying bug that can cause the game to crash WHICH CORRUPTS THE SAVE! Yep, that one time you do survive and get a save, the game loses it. I cannot begin to describe how insanely idiotic and frustrating that is.
You then have cases of heroes being stupid, a hero that is a high level will happily walk past a bunch of enemies tearing your base to pieces despite being more than capable of killing the lot with minimal effort. The paying money to influence hero actions is a good system but let down by the atrocious AI and the fact you can't refund a flag you placed if you change your mind, once the flag is placed the money is stuck to it permenantly rather than losing it upon the completion of the task.
All this is a shame because the fundamental idea behind the game is interesting and it would be nice to see it remade. Having said that I cannot recommend this game just because the rat king and dragon missions (which you can't skip) are so SO♥♥♥♥♥♥poor and frustrating that you will be lucky to see the rest of the game without giving up and uninstalling. If those 2 missions were fixed to actually be fair then I'd recommend this as a fun game, all the other missions are acceptable.
TL;DR 2 very poorly designed levels (ie impossible 90% of the time) and stupid AI ruin an otherwise interesting and challenging game. Avoid unless you have the patience of a saint.

I did not have much expectations for this game when getting into it. Star Trek games really arn't that great. there are very few that do decent. This one i believe isn't a decent one. With the F2P model you can spend a mass load of cash just to get one currency. There are three currencies in this game. I see no point in 3 currencies, 2 would of been fine if the currencies were e-cash and In-game.
Graphics- Graphically this game is.. decent to say the most. With max graphics it really did not look all that graphically intense. Though, this game made my computer's fan run non-stop so it used a decent amount of my computer's capacity. Now my computer isn't a gaming computer; but, it can run things like Tera, Cube World, and Space Engineers; all of which are graphically intense even at low graphic settings. STO even on high graphics, has major issues. For example: the windows on the ships are noticably textured on a layer above the ship and dont look like windows/lights. The space scenery on max graphics does not look at all like max graphics should be. The UI for the NPCs is not good. The NPC UI feels like im using an ATM with the ability to scroll.
Combat- Now i have not played alot of this game clearly, but of what I have played, the combat is super slow. Clicking an enemy does not auto shoot, you have to manualy click each seperate weapon, or kind of weapon. The combat bored the living crap out of me, it got to a point where i just said "ugh.. more enemies. Welp Im just going to sit here in one spot and let them circle me while i spam click my shields and weapons until maybe 5 minutes later i get one of the enemies shields down so i can hurt them a little before their shields come back up." Missing in this game is horrid, how someone can miss a giant ship with a lazer in space is beyond me, You cant even control where the lazers fire other than what enemy. Ground combat, is majorly horrid. Your character movement and combat is so.. slippery/clunky. You use a "skill" to fire your gun at the enemy. Combat consists of smashing either your mouse or your hot key to kill the enemy, no need for any skill at all, you could just stand infront of them taking their shots while you both shoot at eachother.
Movement- controlling your ship does not feel like you are controlling a space ship one bit. There is only Yaw and Pitch and a graphical "roll". If you are looking for a decent space game, this is not it unless you can deal with the faults of this game.
If you don't want your time wasted, avoid the hassle of creating an account and dealing with their half broken account login system. (You make an alias/account name, then verify, then it doesnt even work with your alias. The login only works with email, but only works not even half the times i tried, and I made sure there were no typos what soever from what i made both the pass and email.) Then don't bother unless you have a Star Trek fan friend that 'Really' wants you to play with them.
On a more brighter note. If you dont have a great computer in this day and age this game might be an ok game to play in small spurts if your just in it for the Star Trek theme. Otherwise, it's not that great of a game, like most Star Trek games are sadly. Though, I don't follow the Star Trek theme or the movies and show. I tried to be as... fair as I could from a gamer's standpoint about the graphics and gameplay.
