Deus Ex: The Fall is a direct port from mobile devices. As such, it suffers from a few common issues; non-rebindable keys, relatively poor graphics and sometimes clunky controls. However, it is not a terrible game.
The Fall was clearly made to milk the franchise. There isn't much love or inspiration to be felt in its level design, weapons or story.
The levels are linear, but the developers clearly tried to copy the standard Deus Ex multiple-paths approach. It's clearly inferior to HR's (and the original's) excellently designed areas. Its hub, Panama, also doesn't feel very new or interesting, but it offers some variety in missions which I actually found fun.
The visuals are dated, which comes as no surprise given it's a mobile port, but they aren't horribly ugly and have that Human Revolution look. The soundtrack was ripped from HR in an attempt to bring back the atmosphere of the former (it does, to some degree, succeed in that).
The block-based Deus Ex inventory system was scrapped in favor of an unlimited all-in-one inventory-store, which works well considered this is a relatively entry to the series. Enemy AI is, at most, downright handicapped, so stealth is easier than it should be.
However, I was able to look past all this and found a fun little Deus Ex fix. Why am I giving it a thumbs down, then? See, I expected the game to be short, five or six hours, ten at most. I got my 6 hours out of it, but I also expected an ending to the story, however uninteresting it may be. It ends with a cliffhanger. A ♥♥♥♥ing "To be continued..." that cuts you off without anything remotely similar to a conclusion. One moment, you're sitting tight, expecting an epic final mission, or at least a boss fight and explanations for some loose plotpoints, and the next you realize you get none of it and are basically screwed. And since this game was generally unfavorably received, it isn't likely Ben Saxon's story will continue, at least in its current form.
So there you go, Deus Ex: The Fall isn't as bad as some might make you believe. It doesn't live up to the high standards of Deus Ex, but is fun in its own right. Without Deus Ex slapped on it, and maybe if it was originally on PC, it would score a solid 7.5/10. It isn't, however, finished, so keep that in mind if you ever want to buy it.

I am re-reviewing the game from Early Access now that it has been released officially as version 1.0.
The start up UI has been completely reworked and looks much nicer and easier to navigate around. Pressing 'Play' the UI now presents you with two different game modes which are 'Story' and 'Sandbox'.
'Story' mode is like a beginners tutorial. It tells a little story about the first two Niche creatures on the island while teaching you to work the game.Much of the in-game UI has changed since Early Access and the tutorial now goes over where most things are located and what things are.
I made mention of a few things missing in my last review which are still missing in this version of the official release of the tutorial.
- no explanation of gene menu
- no explanation of mutation menu or using it
- it points out nest and food, but somehow forgets and important point of pointing out population?
additionally i feel like it should have mentioned RANK (alpha, beta, omega) as it plays an important role. it doesn't mention this even briefly.
'Sandbox' mode is what you would expect it to be. It is what most people who have played the game before, or have done the tutorial already, would play. It now allows for MANY different starting settings compared to what was just a one size approach in Early Access. For example if you chose 'Easy Islands' and 'Tiny Green' it would give you smaller size islands that are grassy at the start of your game. There are Easy/Medium/Hard/Killer settings for different island difficulties as well as different biome types.
Fortunately now that niche has reached a more 'stable' state information about what the tutorial leaves out can be found if there are questions about it. Which was one the major issues in the past.
Overall I would definitely recommend the game now that it has officially released. It was fun playing it in Early Access and I am looking forward to playing more of it now that it has released.

Right. Since I've managed to finally 100% this game, might as well throw in my two cents. Here we go.
I've played this game a lot. Before I got it on Steam, I played the version from Good Old Games. Finished it, like, thrice on normal, once on hard. The first time I was disappointed, the second time I was even more disappointed, but somehow the third time was the charm. Why? Let me get to that shortly.
Many people keep saying that HM2:WN plays completely differently to the original. And this is true. Huge locations, more windows, gunner enemies able to snipe you from the other side of the map *coughcoughdeadaheadcough*, which might prove frustrating, especially to the players who remember HM1 - to the point it almost seems unfair. Hoping to have any kind of fun with this game, one has to keep that in mind.
But, compared to HM1, the combat and the movement are a lot more responsive and smooth. This makes the game a bit easier to control, which is nice.
I don't exactly like what was done with the masks, but I can't say I despise it completely - since there is a proper storyline now, consisting of several branches woven together, with several different characters at different points in time, each one has their own set of abilities, few of them selectable before the scenes. This adds quite a lot to the game's variety, and considering how some of HM1's masks were easily favored over the others (basically, you'd play either Rasmus for secret ending or Carl/Zack for high score, or Rick, because "good shot" was just too damn good to pass), only now you really have an actual choice on how to tackle a level. The downside is you can't pick your favourite mask on every level in the game - and several characters don't even have any customization at all.
I mentioned the story. It is pretty good - I used to be mad at the ending, and once you get there you will realize why, but after a second thought it is actually a strong, sensible conclusion. There might even be some feels on your way there, especially considered what happens to the only likeable protagonist in the series.
The game is pretty short, but this is an issue that is easy to overlook - since we've got a level editor now, and Steam Workshop has several creative folks who make stuff that is actually good, in theory you've got an unlimted supply of fresh, playable and fun maps. Some of them are better than the original ones, which solves the issue with shotgun snipers and windows of death everywhere.
What can I say? I was thinking I'd give this a negative review, but the phonecall... I mean, the level editor really made me change my mind.

Join a demented artists descent into madness from haunting memories of the past. Layers of Fear takes a similar approach to games such as Penumbra and Amnesia: The Dark Descent as it uses a couple of similar mechanics. The player gets to roam around the artists mansion and uncover small detail on his life before you - the artist begins to reflect on a project that will warp the home into what lurks inside this unhinged man. The game uses excellent timing and scripting that will alter the perception of the artist.
While Layers of Fear has a few things that need to improve as the time I am writing this the studio has done a tremendous job of building up a character and his house with pride only to see the dark depth that lies behind that canvas.
My only gripe and a message to the developer is to add more roaming and utility to the space that is available make the home more than hallway haunted house. The gameplay should give more options for failure and more puzzles to confuse the player and not go through step by step key by door unlock. With that being said Layers of Fear is a psychological horror that paints a beautifully deranged future for the true horror genre. I hope to see more like this from this studio.
NOTE: Do realize this game is in Early Access and is not a finished product. At this time the game will give you around 2.5 hours of gameplay or so and I would expect with the detail given so far that the game will have around 6-7 hours of gameplay time in all with the finished product.

I gave The Evil Within some very harsh criticism when it first came out. The game was buggy, infuriating, and made no sense. With the annoucement of The Evil Within 2, I decided to give the original another go to see if anything had changed. I have to say, I really enjoyed myself the second time through.
Not to say The Evil Within is without it's problems. Even after all the patches and the ability to unlock the game at 60fps, there are still performance issues and a lot of stuttering. The game is also very difficult as well, even in New Game+, mostly due to the gameplay being very trial and error and being very stingy with ammunition and health pick ups. I understand it's survival horror, but they took it way too far.
The story is excellent, although sometimes it stumbles over itself and the narrative can get a little disjointed. The DLC missions help to explain a lot of the holes left by the main story and reveal a little more character background that makes the main characters seem a lot less one-dimensional and stale. Voice acting is okay, but most of the characters sound very stiff and just not that into their roles.
What The Evil Within does that many games can't is create atmosphere. Every moment of the game creates an intensity that is unmatched. Shinji Mikami did an excellent job in helping you become absorbed in your surroundings and fearing what is behind every corner. You can become so lost in the tension that you forget about the games other shortcomings.
On the second run around, The Evil Within is a solid and engrossing psychological horror experience with a few speedbumps. If the devs can make the second game smoother with a more stable storyline, stronger characters, and slightly more forgiving gameplay, The Evil Within 2 could have the potential to be one of the best survival horror experiences ever.

Don't waste your money and more importantly, your time on this game.
The game starts off with a strong first chapter, bringing memories of classic horror games like Clock Tower and Haunting Ground. Where all you can do to survive is stealthy move around and use your wits.  But after chapter one, the chapter I'm assuming was used to sell this game to investors, the game becomes pure crap.
Instead of creating a fresh game, Mikami is satisfied with repacking Resident Evil 4 in a half♥♥♥♥♥way and delivering a product that can be summed up as garbage. Seriously, it's all here:
*The Gigante type fight
*Enemies wielding guns and wearing armor late game
*Enemies doing the open and close shutter trick segment
*Chainsaw guy chasing you
*Enemy with claws stalking you, only to become quicker with damage taken
..and more.
The saddest part being that they had creative segments and enemies in the game but instead of focusing and building around those, they tried to do mix and match fragments of different genres. Resulting in a game that has no idea what type of horror game it wants to be when it's not being a pure action game with horrible controls.
Then there's the control system. It constantly feels unresponsive and awkward. Making the many action sequences the game throws you in feel like a chore to get through. Many times you'll be fighting hordes of enemies RE4 style but in TEW, you'll struggle just to get your cross hairs to line up and if they do, don't be surprised if you still miss. I honestly can't tell if this was an intentional design choice, to have a control system geared for non-combat scenarios but force the player into multiple combat situations or if this came about from using a game engine meant for FPS, but Tango messed up with this combination.
To top it off, the story. TEW tries to catch your attention by giving you the story in piece meal without context. Trying to get the effect of having you engaged in putting the puzzle together, a staple in horror games. But TEW goes too far in the no context direction and combined with the other shortcomings the game has, you jsut stop caring about the story very early on. To the credit of the writer, once you complete the game(and DLC), the story makes a deal of sense and it's passable.
Overall, this was just a poor effort and game by Mikami and Tango. The parts they did do right were not build upon and the remaining sections feel just thrown in or a repacking of RE4. To the point that you being to feel like you paid money to play a very bad version of RE4 in many sections.

I note that this review is was an assignment for my College English class. So prepare for the equivalent of 3 and half pages. TLDR: skip everything to last paragraph.
Warhammer: The End Times - Vermintide, is a first person shooter type video game developed and published by indie-game company Fatshark; released on October 23 of 2015 for $30.00. I bought the game on a whim after seeing that it had been received by the gaming community in a sense of “you’ll either love it or hate it”. I have recommended this game to almost every friend that I game with that has a beefy (as built specifically for gaming) enough computer to run it.
First things first I would directly compare Vermintide to Left 4 Dead 2 (or just the Left 4 Dead series in general really). Vermintide takes inspiration directly from Left 4 Dead in many aspects; level design, camera work, special enemy types and plot. The plot (which there is little to none of in both games) in which Vermintide subs out Left 4 Dead’s zombie overrun modern cities, for a victorian era city that is infested with man-sized ratmen called the skaven. Skaven are actually a refreshing sight from the hundreds of zombie games being released in the recent years. Both Vermintide and Left 4 Dead have a similar idea with the 4-player co-operative system being that you are 4 people in the wrong place at the wrong time trying to escape a city overrun by a numberless foe. While in writing this may sound like a terribly horrifying thing, one can rest assured that it is not as scary as it sounds.
While Vermintide and Left 4 Dead have their many similarities they are also totally different games in many ways, with Left 4 Dead being the simpler of the two. We will start with the obvious one that I assume makes or breaks the game for most people; Vermintide is significantly harder, complex, and more so unforgiving than Left 4 Dead. It is safe to say that if you’re the kind of person who is impatient and likely plays only on the normal difficulty in Left 4 Dead you will strongly dislike Vermintide. In this game you can easily spend countless hours dying over and over on the same mission with the same people with no check points. That’s right; Vermintide has no implemented checkpoint system. If you fail at any point of the mission, regardless of if you were right at the end of it, you must take it from the top of the mission. My friends and I have spent hours on the harder difficulties of this game just repeating the same mission over again due to us dying in various places of the mission. These missions can take anywhere from 5 to 50 minutes each with varying difficulty depending on the set difficulty and objective of the mission.
The difficulty settings in the game are a simple set up with five difficulties. The easiest difficulty being Easy, which progresses to Normal, then to Hard, Nightmare, and Cataclysm. Each of these difficulties has different loot that is rewarded so that your hard work is not in vain (which we will get into later).
This brings me to the missions of the game and objectives. Each mission consists of at least one  “Go here, do this” objective (which tend to be the shortest missions if that’s all it says). While seven of the thirteen available missions (nine of sixteen if you include the add ons) include bonus objectives to the “Go here, do this” which consists of items called Tomes; which take up a player’s healing item slot, and Grimoires; which subtracts from the player’s base health which means that in less hits the player will die. This makes the game more challenging and fun and frustrating all at once. (This being something we can safely refer back to the bit of there being no checkpoint system).

The player does not just make the game harder on themselves for no reason of course, as there is a loot/treasure reward system in Vermintide. The system works in a roll of seven dice; base dice have a 2/6 chance of giving you loot/treasure, dice that you acquire from tomes have a 4/6 chance for loot/treasure, and dice that you acquire from grimoires have a 6/6 to give you loot/treasure. (I add there are also dice to be found called “Cursed Loot Die” which are randomly spawned from opening chests that have a 3/6 chance for a good roll, these are just beyond your control). So if you make things harder on yourself by acquiring this bonus objective items you can acquire more loot to aid you and make your life easier in the long run.
Loot would be the generalised term we use in this case for weapons, trinkets, and helmets. There is a whole slew of weapons from handguns to rapier swords to wizard staffs that we cannot possibly cover all of them so you will have to discover those on your own. This same thing applies for trinkets which supply different bonuses such as a chance not to consume a potion when you drink it. While helmets are all strictly cosmetic items that have no effect on your actual gameplay. There are 5 different qualities of weapons and trinkets that effect the items power, as mentioned when we spoke of difficulties. The order of weapon/trinket quality from best to worst is as listed: White, Green, Blue, Orange, Red. White quality items being as though you are wielding a sharpened piece of paper, and red quality items being as though you are slaying rat men with Thor’s Hammer. These item qualities are not directly associated with each difficulty as you can roll a blue on easy; they simply make the game easier for the player that has time to put into the game.
What everything boils down to, is if you liked Left 4 Dead on the harder difficulties and would not mind having some compensation for your toil and hard work, I recommend buying this game right now. However, if you are someone who always played Left 4 Dead on the lower difficulties but like the thought of a Victorian/Medieval era Left 4 Dead, then buy it while it’s on sale. On the flip side, if you have never played a game before, or are a casual gamer; do NOT buy this game. Vermintide is definitely a game for someone who is more on the seasoned gamer who is not faint of heart.

First I want to say is that I played this game for 439 hours. I have a few characters which are high in rank. The concept about the fact that people say this game is pay to win is true but also false at the same time.
The graphics just look amazing while you watch the pictures and the videos. The moment you find yourself on a map, the game doesn't even come close to what you saw on the Store page (but this is the case with a lot of games). That said the game has some sort of arcade feeling.
The moment you reach level 3 thats the moment you will unlock all of the maps. You will find yourself around tanks, planes, paratroopers, snipers, all sorts of different classes. At first you are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥but you just need to adapt and know what to do. The lack of communication makes things a lot harder though you can always aim at enemies to mark them. After a battle ends you get your rewards but also a bill to repair your gear. Since the last update all the prices went up and so did the repair cost of the weapons. The good thing now is that you can pay for everything in credits. They have implemented a lot of ribbons to discourage pay to win. In the previous updates you just could buy some gold and unlock every weapon, modifications, etc. Now its way harder to do that because you have a ribbon to unlock the weapon and a specialization ribbon, in time you will unlock modifications and different ammo for your weapons to use ingame.
The game uses a "Veteran Membership" so you earn your 100% experience, a bit more credits, etc. In the previous build you had to pay this with gold but now you can with credits as well. So the previous builds were pay to win for sure but since the last update it's moving away from that.
The grinding is harder than in the previous build and what I also saw was that they didn't raise the credits you earn in the different ranks. Because depending on your rank you will earn more credits. Also the balancing of the factions is non existing. Optimization isn't there as well. The game uses a lot of CPU power and also graphics power.
The game needs a lot of work and Reto doesn't seem to work a lot on the game. The servers are also a huge problem. They lack the amount of servers to maintain a steady population of players. Their maintenance for the servers takes always 2 to 4 hours and even longer.
It's a fun FPS for a couple of hours but nothing more. If you play and grind your way up in the higher ranks then it becomes quite fun because then you can start buying assault teams and join the war aspect of the game. If you don't like heavy grinding, a lot of good players, arcade looking games or historical inaccuracy then you won't enjoy the game. If you want a better WWII feeling then Red Orchestra or Rising Storm will do the trick.
This game could become better than Red Orchestra or Rising Storm if Reto (dev. team) would get of their lazy asses and start implementing a lot of new stuff that makes it more realistic, work on the optimization and server problems and start to listen to its community because we give the devs a lot of ideas for the game yet a few have been implemented so far.
This game gets a 7/10 for me personally but overall to the people I would give it 4/10 maybe 5/10 depends on how you experience the game. You won't lose anything by trying out the game, after all its "Free to play".

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong number is a sequel that also serves as a prequel and a “sidequel” to Hotline Miami. In it, you play a myriad of characters from all sides of the previously established ’50 Blessings’ story, all the way to the completion of the series.
Gameplay in HM2 features much wider and open areas and as a result you will be getting shot at from off screen very frequently. Frequent use of the shift key is practically mandatory in order to reduce the chance of walking into your own personal shooting gallery. There are also two new enemy types: “thugs” and “dodgers”. Thugs cannot be killed with traditional melee weapons (sans special abilities) and will bleed out when shot with small arms, dying a few seconds later but staying alive long enough to kill you if you’re in range. Dodgers on the other hand will dodge all projectiles and must be killed with a melee weapon or thrown weapon. The addition of these two enemy types, combined with the larger levels makes for a more tactical experience and you will find yourself pausing to evaluate the situation more frequently than you did in HM1.
The music and visuals in HM2 are almost good enough of a reason to play this game. If you enjoy any kind of future-synth or outrun aesthetic, you will love this game as it is full of tracks by Perturbator, Carpenter Brut, Magic Sword, and many more. The graphics themselves are oozing with 80’s style neons and the occasional VHS effect serving as an interstitial between timelines.
Before playing HM2, I had heard some complaints about the open area maps and off-screen enemies shooting the player.  Thanks to the eventually added level editor, everyone will now be able to make and play the more claustrophobic style of level design seen in HM1. It pretty much completes the game by giving the player the option to make up whatever level or campaign they want.
I have to say I was pretty impressed with Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number and definitely recommend it, even to people who have no experience with the genre. It’s one of those games that is just instantly appealing once you dig into it, wanton violence and all.

HuniePop is pretty much your regular light dating sim. You ask girls generic questions, they in return quiz you to find out if you've paid any attention at all and in the end, if done correctly, you've humped every girl in town. For some reason though it feels more fun than dating sims usually. I'm still trying to determine if it actually is more fun or am I just being fooled to think so.
If you've played any dating sim before, especially any western-made, you've seen most of this game already. First you're introduced with your mission to get down with every girl you meet. Sometimes it's because you're trying to win a bet, sometimes you're doing it just for the hell of it, sometimes you're getting revenge, and so on, and so on. This time the reason is a magic fairy who comes to your aid because you're a pathetic mess and need to get some poon-tang ASAP. Then you run rampant around the town meeting girls and memorizing trivia you learn from them. Wooing the girls can be made easier by handing them various obtainable gifts.
What's different in this game is dating. Instead of putting anything you've learned in actual use, you're playing a round of Bejeweled... Candy Crush... You know, that puzzle game where there's a board full of bricks of different colors and you're supposed to swap bricks to create lines of three or more of same color. You need to get certain amount of points and you have 20 turns to do so. If you succeed, date is successful and your prey likes you a little bit more. However, every time you win a date game, next date becomes more difficult with higher target score. You can improve your in-game skills to get point multipliers, but at some point you're likely to find yourself in a situation where every move has to be magnificent. There's no time limit though, and sooner or later you're gonna understand why.
Once you've managed to bend your target under your will, it's time to move to your bedroom. Again you're facing your nemesis, the bling-bling puzzle game, but this time it's slightly different. You have unlimited moves, but your score keeps running down to zero. In order to reach your target you need to score faster than your points decrease. During this your conquest stands next to you in her underwear moaning. It's rather peculiar portrayal of intercourse, I must say. It makes you feel like you're rolling all over the place like a tornado, trying to twist and tweak everything you can, as fast as you can. If you can conjure a hysteric state of mind at will, it will be extremely helpful.
The game is put together very well. Graphics are pretty, background music can run hours without becoming annoying and voice acting is a lot better than you would expect, although sometimes it's difficult to believe that every girl has their own voice actress. Girls have extremely different, yet quite stereotypical personalities. Dialogue varies from hilarious to awkward to annoying, so a lot, but thanks to voice acting you don't want to skip any of it (unless you really hate the girl in question).
There are some minor nuisances. Once you've done the deed with a girl, there isn't any reason to interact with her again. There are some minor details like costumes and hairstyles you can always try to unlock but nothing that affects gameplay and nothing that matters at all in any way if you're not gonna see that girl anymore, and again, why would you? Item inventory has less space than there are items to obtain. For some reason this becomes quite annoying, especially because there is absolutely no reason to limit the size of inventory. Also, there are Steam cards but no achievements. Personally I would've picked achievements over trading cards, but that's just me.
I still don't know for sure whether HuniePop really is fun or just masked as fun. I'm playing it hours at a time, but I'm not exactly sure why. It doesn't really bring anything new to the table. It doesn't offer anything I haven't yet seen. If you're familiar with dating sims this one is going to feel familiar right off the bat. I recommend this game, but ONLY if you like the genre or want to find out what dating sims are. Even though it's very generic, it's still very well made and an excellent example of a dating sim. If you've tried dating sims before and haven't liked them, this one is not gonna change that opinion.

An excellent game that combines various genres (puzzle, RPG, dating sim) very well. Very addicting.
The first thing you should be aware of is that, between CGs explicitly depicting the female anatomy and the pursuit and outcome of having sex, the game's content is elevated from softcore titillation that Steam has typically released up to this point (i.e. Sakura Spirit) to hardcore hentai. Fair warning that that's what you're getting into; at its core, you're playing for sexy porn pictures, and you're buying a hentai game. It's good porn if you're factoring that in.
The game is VERY fun though. It incorporates a simple match 3 game that you've seen countless times, and adds enough rules and stipulations to distinguish it from other games. At later points in the game, you'll have to play carefully to make the right plays, deliver the right gifts at the right times to reach the end of a date successfully with limited moves available to you. There's enough strategy to engage you meaningfully. And, let's face it, exploding coloured tiles has always been supremely satisfying. And then the game changes when you successfully bring a woman to your room, and the game changes in such a simple and yet genius way, removing the time limit and turning the game into a race to pop matches as quickly as possible.
The main progression comes from learning more about the girls, increasing your skills, and expanding your options for game-changing items in dates. It feels meaningful and coincides well with the gradual increase in difficulty as the game goes. Gameplay is the best part about the game, really.
Surrounding the gameplay, it's just a very professionally done package. Full voice acting is solid for the most part, the OST makes for delightful BGM when doing puzzles, art in general is very crisp and clear, the character sprites have solid variety in how their expressions change and in changes of clothing; lip sync is an incredibly nice touch.
The writing in the game is smart, witty, and plays primarily to the expectations of a western audience and to the mentalities of a "player" picking up women. It's exceptionally tongue-in-cheek; the dating sim is, by nature, a genre of manipulation and telling the girls what they want to hear, and HuniePop replicates that without falling prey to traditional Japanese writing tropes. There isn't much of a narrative and the characters aren't exactly deep, but the writing is spot on for interactions between any number of them.
It's an exceptionally well-done game. You won't be disappointed.

Ah, Ace of Spades, where to start. This game used to be the♥♥♥♥♥♥ I played it before it came to Steam, and it was a simple, yet addicting mix if Team Fortress and Minecraft, and had touches of Battlefield and Roblox. So when it came to Steam, I was understandibly excited. They had greatly improved the gameplay, and had added a plethera of maps, gamemodes, weapons, and 4 classes. The gameplay was tight, the graphics greatly improved, and each class was pretty balanced (Except for the Sniper).
And then came the updates. First they added a new DLC, which was 1930's Chicago themed, (No idea why they chose that theme), and for me and many other people, the game would crash instantly when you played it for the next few months. That was the begiining of the end. People could only play the DLC maps if you owned the DLC, and the gamemodes were exclusive to those 2 maps. (People can probably agree with me that City of Chicago would  have been an awesome Zombie map.
Then they changed the skin of the commando to look more "Rambo-y", which looked awful, then they nerfed the Rocketeer class, and turned it into the "Engineer". I actually stopped playing then, 'cause everything that was fun about the Rocketeer (verstile, hit-and-run tactics, great in zombies), and nerfed it. Instead, the Enginner had very low health, a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ jetpack that ran out of fuel almost instantly, weaker weapons, and weaker items. About half the community, said "♥♥♥♥ this" and walked away. This just left the new players, and the whiny 12 year olds who spammed sniper. This completly ruined the game. Then as if they hadn't done enough damage, they removed the ability to browse servers, and added a lazer module to the Sniper, so whenever you zoomed in, your position would be revealed to everyone on the map. Then they just went ahead and added the Chicago DLC to the game, so people had essentaily wasted 5 dollars on buying it before-hand. The final straw was when they added the "Battle Builder" element. Sounds pretty fun right? No. No it wasn't. The game would lag when ever you tried to put down a larger model, and often the maps were so big that the game would crash. Also nobody played the user-made content. People can't even host their own games.
Right now I can unfortunetly not reccomend Ace of Spades to you.  If Jagex (who has a long history of runing games) decides to patch the game, and remove all of these mistakes, then play it again. But right now, the game is broken, the achivements are unattainable, the community is awful, and filled with griefers and hackers, and the gameplay has been completely ruined. So, with great sadness, I say that this game is unplayable currently, and I would not advise buying it.

Oh wow. This. Is. Scary.
It truly is, and I thoroughly enjoying my time in game. This is beautifully executed, and relies much less on jumpscares than many other games. There are some, and they are pretty decent, but what takes the cake is the feeling of insanity holding your character firmly in its grip.
the house is like some kind of hell, confusing, scary, full of secrets and hidden things. Sometimes it's like some kind of bad trip. Walk into a room. Nothing in there. Turn around, the door is gone.
There are some insanely (literally) cool ideas here... some scenes for example related to a still-life of fruit, or a piano in a basement. You will see, if you keep going.
Also, the game is quite unpredictable. Sometimes you are absolutely positive there'll be some kind of a cliché jumpscare hitting you.And it doesn't. But then, when you don't expect it, something totally crazy will happen.
Also, slowly but surely, through newspapers, monologues, things you find, you get an idea that there is a totally HORRIBLE backstory to the character, his family and his house. Wait until you start unlocking the secrets related to your current painting.
Even though there is no direct reference, I find myself thinking of Lovecraft-style horror, not only because of the old school vibe of the house, but because the game sometimes only HINTS at terrible things, instead of showing them to the tiniest detail. The atmosphere creeps you out, makes you imagine what is behind all this, even though you haven't even seen a lot yet.
The game is not at all open world in any sense of the world. It's very much on rails, dictating where you go, and there isn't a ton of interaction with items, no inventory etc. (mostly, you pick up keys or items for your painting)
It's weird, it's mysterious, it's nutty, sometimes yucky, it's scary, shocking, yet very beautiful.
Big gratz to the developers who really came up with some killer ideas, and created a VERY scary, immersive and atmospheric game. Up for a scare? Something that's not about cheap jumpscares and more about getting an idea of how someone goes insane, with all the weirdness and unpredictable, irrational stuff involved? Get. This. Game.
If you play it with headphones (recommended by the devs) and lights off...don't say I didn't warn you.

Plain and simple this is Left 4 Dead with swords does that mean this is a bad game? Not at all players will find plenty of replay ability in the form of a gear system. If you’re into Left 4 Dead you can buy this game knowing you will have the same amount of fun or more if you prefer swords to guns.
Graphics – The game sports a dark and desolate atmosphere just like Left 4 Dead. If you have a beast of a PC you can make the game look beyond epic as it has plenty of video features. You can still run this game on a decent rig if you’re playing on lower settings just beware some frame lag when dealing with huge hoards.
Gameplay – Ok so I know I’ve said it a lot but this is Left 4 Dead … with swords. You can find enjoyment in the fact that this game has different playable characters that use different weapons and play differently from each other and an RNG loot system. At the end of every stage you will need to roll dice which can be improved by playing on harder difficulties or finding special items throughout the stage to collect your loot be it weapons or trinkets with all kinds of stats and skills. Each stage is a large map where the party must navigate to the end objective while fending off HUGE hoards of rat monsters. Though some stages will be more like medium fields where the party must gather items to a single point than escape while still being ravaged by big rat monsters.
Story – The game has pretty minor Warhammer story fallowing the rise of rat people who want to kill and eat everyone but I’d say more than Left 4 Dead with the party starting at a fortified pub and deciding on a mission to help prevent the rats from snuffing out the last holdouts of humans. These range from get food, get guns, break important rat things, and find wizards who can help you. This allows the game to have a form of story in the idea that your party is holding out in the city while each mission is an objective needed toward the singular goal of survival.
Recommendation – Overall Vermintide is a great buy for a group of friends looking for something fun to lose hundreds of hours to, finding lots of gear and killing hoards of rat creatures together.  If you had this on your radar and you have at least one friend this is worth adding to your library.

**BIG IMPORTANT NOTE** (Please don't mind the  small amount of time spent playing, I played the version I got from the Huniepop site, but I got a Steam Key anyway. In total, I'd say I spent 8 hours playing through the puzzles.)
Gameplay: 8/10, Solid Snake
Puzzle games aren’t my thing (I’m only playing Bejeweled Blitz to get 250/250 for 500k and above), but Huniepop’s twist on the Match-3 puzzle genre is spectacular. I found myself actually thinking about what moves to make since you only get 20 moves to hit the amount of points required. Trait and stat allocation was really addictive to me; do I bang out a ton of Hunie (currency) for better point return on Romance orbs, or increase the chances of Power orbs dropping after a 3-match?
Hint: Audrey is the best for getting drunk and farming Hunie off of.
Artwork: 6/10, Just Managed To Avoid Drowning
In-game artwork could use some improvement. The CGs are pretty damn good for an indie game, but some are a little lackluster. Especially the ones post-bonus round. They're 8/10 at best, so there’ll be only a handful of folks playing to get off to the CGs (and how you wank off while trying to make the gem matches is beyond me)
Writing: 7/10, Pretty Good
Huniepop does a good job at making the characters distinct from each other. Each character feels like they have their own voice (literally, with voice acting). From the questions and information you get from talking to them, you learn who they are, what they do, and in some cases like Audrey, a glimpse into how they view the world.
Dialogue is great, and is very entertaining. Especially Audrey Belrose, queen of mega♥♥♥♥♥es. The dialogue choices are amusing, as well.
However, you don’t get much else in terms of characterization, and you don’t go so deep into the character’s personalities and stories, which is a shame. In fact, there is no real plot other than “get with all these girls, you horny boy/girl.” The characters just SCREAM to be put into a visual novel! C’mon Huniepot, give us some more!
MORE “♥♥♥♥♥ FACE, ♥♥♥♥♥ FEELINGS” DIALOGUE, PLEASE.
Audio: 9/10, Boss
Best part hands down. English Voice Acting alone puts Huniepop above and beyond other similar titles. They really got some talent for the voices (especially Audrey). The tracks are great for the date locations; personal favorite is the Ice Rink’s theme.
Overall: 7/10. Pretty Good
Marred by a concept that didn’t go far enough, Huniepop’s mixup Match-3 gameplay actually brings suspense and excitement in the otherwise slow puzzle genre (the /v/ stream was a good example of that). There were interesting characters that feel more like great concepts that were only taken half-flight and never got that far off the ground. The artwork is inconsistent in quality; you’ll love some and then wonder why some characters get a single nipple in the post-sex CG.
So…here’s for a sequel? I want more ♥♥♥♥♥ FACE ♥♥♥♥♥ FEELINGS.
How to Improve: More story, more fleshing out of the characters could have made this title even better. I feel that the voice acting may have limited and slowed the amount of actual dialogue in the game (dev probably spent all his money on Kickstarter paying the voice actresses).
I would throw more money at the devs if they could include a full story/routes for the girls. There is so much potentil for character development!
And more CGs!
tl;dr Came for the ♥♥♥♥♥ FACE, ♥♥♥♥♥ FEELINGS, stayed for the most nerve-racking games of Bejeweled-with-a-twist because there wasn't anywhere near enough of the 9/10 dialogue to sate my hunger. Needs more dialogue, but the puzzle gameplay can get really intense.

There are quite a few free flash games online that all do the same thing, so what sets this apart that you would want to spend money on it?  Well, I'll go over pros and cons:
PROS:
1)  Voice-acted - turns out this is actually a much different experience in a dating sim, which kinda makes sense
2)  Puzzle aspect has a lot going on and actually becomes fun (minus the spin they put on it at the end when you get the girl)
3)  Unique way to get money and "hunie", your EXP points
4)  Wide variety of the girls and their personalities, each of them feels unique and well fleshed out - the voice acting helps with this a lot
5)  You can be male or female - while this isn't a big deal, it really only changes the pronouns they use, it's a nice option to not assume the sex of the player
CONS:
1) RPG elements are about as shallow as you would expect for level-ups that would affect a puzzle game
2) End puzzle sucks, it just does, there's no strategy and it's hard as heck
3) While there is a tutorial in the form of an invisible fairy, she doesn't cover EVERYTHING, which leaves you wondering what the heck some things do.  Since there is no wiki for this game yet, I had to just keep playing until I figured it out.
So my final verdict would be, it did keep me up until 3am when I played it, it's addicting and well made.  If you like this type of game and looking for one with polish, this is a good buy.  If you are looking for a game that will just throw a bunch of naked anime-style girls at you, sorry, this isn't it.

TY is back! While keeping a very tongue in cheek nature, it's everything you might love about Australia. From crazy slang to key-taring Blue Tongue Lizards, Robot-Sharks and everything in between. It's not the 3d platformer you might recall but that doesn't stop it from being an absolute blast. Consider the transition Rayman made from 3d -> 2d, presentation and gameplay is close.
Screen resolution scales up to 4k+ while the hand drawn graphics stay crisp. Both kb+mouse & gamepad controls were responsive and all keys remappable. Entire game is spread across several acts containing larger levels with multiple segments, complete each and continue onward or leave and spend gems. Gems can used to obtain new boomerangs or different costumes & characters. One playthrough won't be enough, levels contain many hidden areas to discover and the game provided alternate modes of play such as time-attack.
Biggest downfall is the difficulty, little on the easier side and maybe aimed more at the younger generation. With it's uniquely Australian visuals and sound, decent amount of content and great price point, TY 4 gets an easy recommendation and a big thumbs up.

The Evil Within is the resident evil 4 of today. There, i said it. But that's really what it is, after Capcom started making the RE series more and more action focused it really lost what it was all about. Gladly Shinji Mikami and the buds at Tango Gameworks are here to save the day.
So yeah, if you've ever played RE4 you know what to expect. Horrific looking monsters, spine tingling near death experiences combined with QTE's, weapon upgrades, difficult aiming of guns with satisfying gore efects. It's all here. But i'd actually go even beyond that and say that TEW has a stronger sense of dread than RE4 ever did. The atmosphere is absolutely stunning, great lighting effects, music and sfx all come together to make for an experience with a lot of memorable moments.
What really impressed me with the game was how unified the arstyle is although the locales and characters vary drastically depending on the level. It all feels like it's supposed to be there, even when you jump from a medieval village to a destroyed modern day city. TEW also isn't an easy game, which makes it stand out from the rest of the garbage they come up with these days. It really does feel like a title from 2005, and while some people might find that a bad thing, i actually welcome it with open arms. Games back then just had that little something they're missing these days.
So overall, if you're not afraid of gore or a story that REQUIRES you to think (A lot, actually.) then this is a no brainer. Go and get The Evil Within, you won't regret it.

Do not buy this, do not play this. It's a PC port of a game made for Android / iOS which sounds like a pretty bad idea in itself. So expect graphics and AI designed to run on a smartphone, not to mention absolutely HUGE UI made for touch, pretty straightforward objectives and short gameplay (afterall, the game must fit on a smartphone). Do not worry about gapes in storyline as it takes place before Human Revolution events an is rather disconnected from it. It also leaves an open ending with "to be continued" pomise, which I don't believe. If you're coming from HR and expect a sequel, this is not it. Mankind Divided is.

Boy oh boy, am I glad that Steam allows players to "not recommend" games, because this atrocity does not deserve the Deus Ex moniker. It doesn't even deserve to be a PC or home-console game.
To quote Adam Jensen, "I never asked for this".
On the surface, the game looks promising. You play as Ben Saxon, a mercenary once affiliated with the Tyrants (the guys who attack Sarif Industries in Human Revolution), who defected from the Tyrants and is now pursuing his own investigation into the global conspiracy. Ben Saxon is basically a reskinned Adam Jensen - the HUD and augmentations from Human Revolution are all intact.
Sounds like it could be fun, right? Well, maybe, if the game were developed as proper Human Revolution DLC using that game's engine. Except it's not. It's a port of a mobile game. You think console ports are bad? I'd take a console port over a mobile port any day of the week.
The technical flaws due to "mobile-itis" are apparent from the very beginning. The controls are god awful, and at the time of release, could not be remapped. Movement feels stiff and it's easy to tell that the mouse is just simulating a finger drawing across a touch screen. Worse still, some compromises that were made for touch screens also crept into the PC port. For example, on the mobile version, to fire your weapon you need to hold down a button, which brings up the weapon sight. You aim the weapon and release the button to fire. On the PC, you hold down the left mouse, aim, and release the left mouse to fire. Yeah, what the F-word?! I don't know if this was patched as of 2015, but it sure wasn't working too well last year when I played this game.
The graphics may have won praise when viewed on a small phone or tablet screen. On a PC monitor, they're inexcusably bad. The models are low res, animations are choppy, and corpses just disappear into thin air due to game engine constraints. Even the Xbox 360 can do better than this, and that's a 10 year old console.
Now all this could be forgiven if the gameplay were even half as amazing as Deus EX HR or the Missing Link DLC. Well, obviously it's not! Enemy AI is beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Human Revolution's AI was often the butt of jokes, but those guys are Einsteins compared to the stooges you face in The Fall. I couldn't believe it when I was able to walk up to enemies HEAD ON and do stealth takedowns without raising alarms. They must be blind, deaf, and dead. It's almost like the devs turned on cheat codes for everyone.
Part of the fun of Human Revolution was carefully rationing resources when upgrading augmentations and weapons. It was also necessary to visit specific locations to get upgrades, and this encouraged exploration (which opened side quests). In The Fall, you can simply buy augs and weapon upgrades and even ammo on-the-fly, and somehow it magically appears in your inventory. Finding money is also stupidly easy. That kills incentive for exploration, and it's far too easy to become The Terminator in a short time, which removes any challenge in the game (not helped by the dumb-as-dirt AI).
To add insult to injury, the game's SHORT. I finished it in five hours. It ends with a message telling me to wait for the next episode, just like a typical mobile game. So far, there has been no mention of that second episode.
This game should be ignored by everyone. Don't even pirate it. Send a message to Square Enix that we will not tolerate this sort of blasphemy.

Nice comes across as a rather cute game until you actually spend some time play it. If you have played the original Kickstarter demo, a lot of features were added, but somehow the game feels pretty much the same.
Played the Kickstarter Demo, and also most recently at Quo Vadis 2017, and on the day of this review, and it doesn't make a polished or even sophisticated impression. After so much time and money invested, especially the UX could be a lot better. Even with a person explaining the newest additions to the game to me, I felt myself lost in the game. The menus are highly static, and the camera controls are so basic, it's not enjoyable to navigate the game.
Artistically, the game has a long way to go - the creatures are not animated in any real sense, and face the player as billboards (I don't quite understand this design decision). They have some faint breathing animation, but other than that all they do is follow the mouse cursor with their heads, which are on a ball joint (not actual IK targets or anything). You can actually turn their heads 360° and more by circling them with the mouse.
Copious amounts of grass can often make the gameplay very obscure, because it occludes UI and other important elements on the screen.
When you drop a creature into the water, the game makes no effort to explain what happened. They'll drown in a real awkward position way below the map, even though you could just move them out of the water again.
The game mechanics are interesting enough, but obscured by a very unwieldy UI. Especially combat is plain awful and could use several iterations of revision. :) There are some moments when the game is really interesting, usually when you need to bootstrap your tribe after a mishap.
I chose to not recommend this game because it's simply not moving anywhere fast, and is technically and design-wise still lacking in a lot of places. Gameplay is generally bland and repetitive, and UX is poor. The graphics are subpar and animations basically nonexistent.
I'll update this review for the release version which is slated for August. I wish the developers good fortune with this game, but I honestly feel we gamers and backers need to provide a modicum of perspective here.

HuniePop on first glance is yet another dating sim, with manga styled characters and alot of cuteness. But it's also a Bejewelled style puzzle game that's surpringly addictive. At parts.
HuniePop is what I'd call a mixed bag, for a few reasons. The first one is the diversity of the character types likely means some you'll like more than others, and given the aforementioned "just another dating sim" elements. You probably won't care to bother with the characters you dislike.
But let's talk about the good points.
There are eight girls in total, as I've mentioned with vasty different personalities. With an additional one unlocking "earlier" on. And apparently another one as an unlockable. Having fully maxed 3 girls I can assume the final character is endgame stuff.
The dating sim elements themselves are kinda... bland. Most of the text from a character will be them answering the questions you ask them in order to get to know more about then. There's not really any scenes of flashed out dialogue aside from the initial meet. Which leads to the characters quickly becoming boring. Simply put, it's hard to properly converse with them beyond the questions you ask. The characters even began to feel slightly 2D, as in personality wise. I'm really not an expert on dating sims at all though.
So I can only give how I thought they seemed. To talk to them you have to feed them food to increase their bar, which seemed a bit silly, but it works somewhat. There's also a way to get them drunk, but I tried it on a girl and maxed out her drunk meter and it didn't seem to do anything.
The puzzle element is basically a Bejeweled style mini game, and is actually quite fun, the puzzles becoming harder and harder. The only problem with this is you need to complete them to progress. Which may annoy some people. The best thing I can say is to focus on your favourite girls first, so their puzzles are easier.
Once you hit 4 or 5 stars of affection you can then ask the girl on a date at night, and if you beat it you'll take her home. Complete a different variation on the puzzle with focus on speed rather than strategy and then the obvious "climax". If you have the patch installed it does make the game literally hentai. Without the patch though it's suggestive.
So in summary, I still recommend this game since I did have fun with it for a bit, and I'm not done with it yet in terms of girls I like.

HuniePop is pretty much as advertised, a sleazy dating sim using Match-3 mechanics. If you don't like the idea of a game like this, it probably won't convince you otherwise. But if you are open minded, it's a good game, if a bit too much on mark at times.
As far as the dating game aspect goes, it's not terribly deep but has pretty good characterization. For the most part, the women seem like individuals, not objects. Nikki in particular is probably exactly the sort of woman that almost every gamer guy would like to find. The writing is good (and funny, at last if you aren't uptight), and in many cases, the voice acting is surprisingly well done.
It would perhaps have been nicer if the goal wasn't to sleep with all the girls, but have a possiblity of an ending with just one (and going beyond just the one final screenshot of them)
As for the Match-3 mechanics, it's half-good. The dating portion uses something of a puzzle mechanic to it, certain girls like certain color/shape jewels, so you have to concentrate on getting those (and maxing out your traits to empahsis those, at least later in the game).
That goes out the window for the sex match-3 game. That's more like the various "Blitz" games, you simply have to match jewels as fast as possible without pausing or thinking.  I guess some might find it fun, but it's mostly just a chore, and at higher levels, an exhausting chore. And in many cases, the reward isn't worth it. Some "ending" scenes are pretty good, others are not.
All in all though, you get more than your money's worth. If only dating was this easy in real life...

HuniePop on first glance is yet another dating sim, with manga styled characters and alot of cuteness. But it's also a Bejewelled style puzzle game that's surpringly addictive. At parts.
HuniePop is what I'd call a mixed bag, for a few reasons. The first one is the diversity of the character types likely means some you'll like more than others, and given the aforementioned "just another dating sim" elements. You probably won't care to bother with the characters you dislike.
But let's talk about the good points.
There are eight girls in total, as I've mentioned with vasty different personalities. With an additional one unlocking "earlier" on. And apparently another one as an unlockable. Having fully maxed 3 girls I can assume the final character is endgame stuff.
The dating sim elements themselves are kinda... bland. Most of the text from a character will be them answering the questions you ask them in order to get to know more about then. There's not really any scenes of flashed out dialogue aside from the initial meet. Which leads to the characters quickly becoming boring. Simply put, it's hard to properly converse with them beyond the questions you ask. The characters even began to feel slightly 2D, as in personality wise. I'm really not an expert on dating sims at all though.
So I can only give how I thought they seemed. To talk to them you have to feed them food to increase their bar, which seemed a bit silly, but it works somewhat. There's also a way to get them drunk, but I tried it on a girl and maxed out her drunk meter and it didn't seem to do anything.
The puzzle element is basically a Bejeweled style mini game, and is actually quite fun, the puzzles becoming harder and harder. The only problem with this is you need to complete them to progress. Which may annoy some people. The best thing I can say is to focus on your favourite girls first, so their puzzles are easier.
Once you hit 4 or 5 stars of affection you can then ask the girl on a date at night, and if you beat it you'll take her home. Complete a different variation on the puzzle with focus on speed rather than strategy and then the obvious "climax". If you have the patch installed it does make the game literally hentai. Without the patch though it's suggestive.
So in summary, I still recommend this game since I did have fun with it for a bit, and I'm not done with it yet in terms of girls I like.

HuniePop is pretty much as advertised, a sleazy dating sim using Match-3 mechanics. If you don't like the idea of a game like this, it probably won't convince you otherwise. But if you are open minded, it's a good game, if a bit too much on mark at times.
As far as the dating game aspect goes, it's not terribly deep but has pretty good characterization. For the most part, the women seem like individuals, not objects. Nikki in particular is probably exactly the sort of woman that almost every gamer guy would like to find. The writing is good (and funny, at last if you aren't uptight), and in many cases, the voice acting is surprisingly well done.
It would perhaps have been nicer if the goal wasn't to sleep with all the girls, but have a possiblity of an ending with just one (and going beyond just the one final screenshot of them)
As for the Match-3 mechanics, it's half-good. The dating portion uses something of a puzzle mechanic to it, certain girls like certain color/shape jewels, so you have to concentrate on getting those (and maxing out your traits to empahsis those, at least later in the game).
That goes out the window for the sex match-3 game. That's more like the various "Blitz" games, you simply have to match jewels as fast as possible without pausing or thinking.  I guess some might find it fun, but it's mostly just a chore, and at higher levels, an exhausting chore. And in many cases, the reward isn't worth it. Some "ending" scenes are pretty good, others are not.
All in all though, you get more than your money's worth. If only dating was this easy in real life...

+ Interesting variant of match-three games.
+ Each character has a different set of favored and unfavored colors of affection tokens (gems).
+ You are provided with a limited inventory in which they can store various reuseable date-gifts (buffs/powers) to use during a date.
+ It's interesting to try and figure out what the optimal kit setup is for particular girls, based on what gifts you've already unlocked.
+ You don't typically have to 'grind' to win. However, as each successful date increases the difficulty of the next one (for all girls), there will occasionally be periods where some stat raising will be needed after you realize that a date can't be won. (Even failed dates give you benefits though)
+ Menus are for the most part easy to navigate, aschetically pleasing, and color-coded for convenience.
- Exceptions are the nearly identical "Girls" and "Girl Finder" menus, one of which is like your stalker encyclopedia while the other advances the day and teleports you elsewhere.
- The sex mini-game is completely dreadful since it relies on you just finding matches continuously while the climax meter drops at constant rate. Where as in the normal dating games you had various powers, gems did different things, and 4+ gem matches were worth more, the mini-game just gives all matches a fixed value. This makes for a very tedious and board-layout (not skill) based obstacle.
+ Conversations, gift/food-giving (consumeables), and intoxication meters are initially an interesting management simulation given that each day there are a finite set of girls you can see in a day, monies available, and gifts to purchase/give. (Ignoring how strange or offensive those particular mechanics are theme-wise.)
- Then you realize time goes on forever and the resource management aspect no longer matter.
+Upon further reflection, there's a ridiculously high chance that this entire game (writing, voice acting, and mechanics combined) is a parody of (eroge) dating sims; when considered at such, it is absolutely brilliant for all of the negative reasons listed above.
+The relationships are unsatisying 'cause you're only available goal (to ♥♥♥♥ as many girls as possible) is so superficial.
+The hentai presented is only erotic when the girl is alone. When having sex it's a completely frustrating variant of match3 followed by an image of her by herself then a ***shot in the same pose.
+All of the mechanics are soo thematically wrong and the dialogue is either so bizarre or boring that it's either completely ingenious as a self-aware parody or should be considered completely ironic that something "so bad" could finally be made.
+ You're actually given the perfect stalking device that keeps track of Facebook-like info (likes/dislikes/triva) AND physical locations!
Where it gets it so so right: I initally find it difficult to flip my review though, because it still left me feeling unsatisfied; however, that may be the point of a game which satirizes Fedoras and vapid dating sims where your only goal is to get laid.

The gameplay is suprisingly fun and interesting, but it's the parody element of it that is really why I would recommend the purchase. If you're wanting to play something seriously (IE want to play a a game with depth and satisfcation), you don't want this. (Unless you really want another match-3 game) This is effectively playing an episode of South Park where the focus is dating sims/being a 'Fedora', but instead of Stan and/or Kyle,
have to be the voice of reason to figure out how 'wrong' and unfulfilling the underlying perspective is. I recommend watching
if you want to get a good feel for the game. (The only downside is that you don't hear the character voices, but consider that a bonus surprise for if you do actually play it yourself.)
If you're more interested in any of the non-parody pieces above... I'd recommend the following instead:
* RPG match-three: Puzzle Quest
* Well written dating sim with some (optional) porn: Katawa Shoujo
* Well written VN with puzzles: 999 (DS)
* Parody dating sim whose twist is that it actually has a lot of depth: Hatoful Boyfriend
* Social sim with awesome RPG gameplay: Persona 4 (PS2)

I'm glad that I picked this game up on a Steam sale once, because it is not even vaguely worth full price and the cost of DLC.    Let's go point-by-point:
Plot:
Something about some kind of psychology experiments on mental patients, who are now some kind of monsters.  Mental hospitals with immoral experiments conducted on patients have been a horror plot device for as long as horror has been a genre, so this is totally unoriginal.  You will have an impossible time connecting with the characters, who are pretty much carved out of wood and very hard to get into.  We've got our emotionless hard-boiled badass cop, his comparatively weak and uninteresting straight-arrow sidekick, their hot chick (who runs around in heels, by the way, which seems impractical) damsel in distress, the mental patient with weird insights (again, trope city), and our scary antagonist who seems to be motivated by... well, nothing but being evil really.  As another reviewer mentioned, you will get something approaching character development for about fifteen seconds when the protagonist talks about his drinking problem and his personal life, but then it's gone and you're back to shooting people.  Why are you shooting people?  Why have you ended up where you are?  You'll eventually get your backstory but it's apparently at the end of the game.  I can't even play to the end, it's such an uninspiring story.  I just wiki'd it and saved myself a few hours.
Graphics:
Not too bad, honestly, once you set the frame rate right and get rid of the black bars.  Not setting the world on fire, but not bad.
Audio:
Stock audio clips galore!  I kept expecting to hear a Wilhelm somewhere.  The music isn't particularly good for instilling dread and it's not very good at keeping with a theme, which brings us to...
Design:
I didn't look up anything about the making of this game before buying it.  You'll recognize immediately upon starting to play that this is a Japanese-made game, which means cultural presentation is going to be clumsy as far as how characters interact and their displays of emotion, as well as certain style/theme choices.  Some people enjoy that, I'm not a huge fan.  The overall 'mood' for the game is a complete mishmash.  It's kinda like the TV show Archer where you're not supposed to have any clue what year it is.  Why is there a 1940s mental hospital in the middle of what appears to be a modern city?  Why is the apparently modern city right next to country bumpkin ruralsville?  The clothing for the protagonist and the other male cop looks like it's pulled from some 1980s detective show, while the damsel is wearing heels for no reason except I guess she's supposed to be sexy and worthy of saving.  Some of the monsters are more original-looking than others but none really stand out stylistically in the same way that, say, necromorphs in Dead Space did.  You've got your people in the village with scary farm implements (trope), you've got your mutant dog thing with an extra mouth, you've got your weird thing with some human characteristics but too many limbs (trope), you've got your chainsaw dude (trope), you've got your butcher guy (trope).  Basically, the memorable villains were all recycled.
Speaking of recycled things, one of the main guys apparently was a big influence on RE4.  RE4 was a pretty solid game, nothing against it (it's a third of the price, go buy it instead!), but this game borrows too liberally from it.  We get it, cults are scary and insane rural village people with farm implements intended for murder are scary.  I mean even the Spanish influence was similar, given that most of the characters have Spanish last names.  You've already done it, go do something else!
As for scariness, I'll admit I'm a wuss, but even the horror elements aren't that scary.  Torture porn and boatloads of gore have been done and aren't that scary, and it feels like the game's go-to element for scaring you is putting more blood and guts on the screen.  The crouching figure in the corner that turns around and they're scary and the game screams at you?  It's been done to death, and this game loves to pull that on you.
Gameplay:
Here's the ultimate indictment of the game.  It just isn't that much fun.  Gunplay is clumsy at best, camera angles aren't great, the mechanics like shocking yourself with green goo to upgrade yourself and your weapons feel stupid, and it feels like it wanted to be a shooter but just couldn't bring itself to be a decent shooter.  You've got your same basic set of weapons (revolver because nobody knows what year it is, pump shotgun, sniper rifle, and crossbow with KRAZY ELEMENTAL BOLTZ) that are in a ton of games, but none really stand out.  Bosses can pretty much all one-hit-kill you, too, which sucks.
Conclusion:
4/10 on a good day.  You're playing a middling horror movie that lasts too long.  Treat it like a bad horror movie and watch it on YouTube.  Use the money you save to go buy some tasty food to eat while you watch.  Much more enjoyable.

Hotline Miami 2 is probably one of the worst designed games I've ever played. If you want an incredibly unfair game that punishes you for not predicting an enemy from across the room (which you can't even see), then get it. If you like well designed games that rewards you diligently for learning from your mistakes and stuff, then skip this game and play the first Hotline Miami or Super Meatboy or something.
There is nothing rewarding or worthwhile about playing this game. Every level is a waste of time. There are enemies that can see you and shoot you from across the room when you can't even see them. I've played and beaten a couple of "hard" games like Casltevania 1, 3, and 4, Megaman 1-6, Ninja Gaiden, Super Meatboy, etc. so I'm no stranger to difficult games. But you have to understand that there's a difference between a game being "hard" and a game being "unfair". Hotline Miami 2 basically boils down to the game punishing you for not having every single aspect of the level memorized. Add in a completely lazy soundtrack (minus a few tracks from Carpenter Brut and Mega Drive) filled with annoyingly awful songs (Ms. Minnie, She Swallowed Burning Coals) and this game is not even worth a penny of your time. Even the good tracks like Roller Mobster get annoying because of the crappy level design that basically forces you to replay the levels over and over again until you memorize every single enemy placement and timing.
There's also the fact that this game is a lot more linear in design as far as how you can approach the levels. In the first game, you could start off with a gun but end the level with a brick. You were given a lot more choices on how to complete a level - you could have gone in guns blazing or fists only. You could have done a stealth run and only used melee weapons, etc.
Hotline Miami 2? Nah they force you to choose a gun in a few levels and you can't even drop it. The Hawaii levels are especially annoying with this and it really ruins the pacing of the game. Horrible game design choice.
I really hope that if there's an HM3 that they go back to how the first one was designed. But for now, please, do yourself a favor and skip this game completely. It's seriously not worth your time or money.

Become Sebastian Castellanos, police detective. He needs to unravel the elaborate mind-bending mystery of a small village because...uh...all part of the job.
Gameplay:
The beginning of the game was, I suspect, heavily influenced by Resident Evil 4. The experiences are cut and paste. Things get shaken up later on, though. Minus points for originality, I'm satisfied with the gameplay. I am beginning to wonder if we're trying too hard to depict horrible parodies of human life. After a certain point, it becomes ridiculous.
Story:
At first, this story made me downright angry. Early game, there are many moments that it fails to capitalize on, narratively speaking. Early on, the story fails to provide stable footing. We aren't able to orient ourselves until much later in the game. Characters make strange decisions for seemingly no reason. Many of them respond to the hideous events in strange ways. Expect liberal amounts of deus ex machina to move the plot along.
That said, the antagonist's story does get more interesting. Once you begin to understand which events are "real" and which are not, you can begin putting pieces together, and understanding the logistics of what's happening. Unfortunately, many questions will remain unanswered.
Characters:
The protagonist alternates between silence, and cursing. You'll seldom hear more from him than, &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥"
Oh, is that giant, nightmarish monstrosity in your way, Sebastian?
Don't mind Seb. Abominations of humanity irk him.
He seems more annoyed by his enemies than genuinely threatened. This is one reason the game isn't scary; the character isn't even scared. To be fair, none of the characters are interesting early-game. Two characters are not necessary. The villain grew on me. The attempt at pseudo-psychology felt a little lazy, but eventually I was so eager to understand what was happening, I quit worrying about it. The ending, though, was not exactly mind-blowing. I got the gist of what happened.
Given the fun gameplay, I recommend it. However, horror fans who've played the Resident Evils, The Silent Hills, and Amnesia (And seen any number of horror films) will be neither surprised nor frightened by anything here. One or two enemy types are  interesting, but by and large they're nothing new. On a good note, many enemies do require some sort of strategy to deal with; they don't go down easily. Boss fights in particular are fun, though will involve just a bit of trial and error. There is definitely some fun to be had here, even with the bland story, and of course, players new to the horror genre will most suitably be made to vomit and/or have nightmares.
Recommended, with caveats.

A developer whose track record consists of billiards and mini golf games, then churning out a "survival" FPS zombie shooter? That already sounds like the death knell for this game out of the gate. Regardless, I went into it with an open mindset, as I have certainly been surprised in the past by the likes of Contagion.
I was sorely disappointed about 10 minutes in. While the overall polish looks decent for a first entry into the FPS genre, everything went downhill from there. There are probably about 4 different zombie models and 3 maps, alongside 2 "different" game modes. And I can't help but assume that a lot of these assets were purchased off the Unity store (or at least could have been) as they are so woefully uninspired.
Uninspired is probably the word you'll be thinking most during any period of time you play this game. The gunplay isn't abysmal but there's no real weight to anything you do. The zombies listlessly attack from seemingly 2-3 feet away. The environments have a good look to them but still feel like a UDK template. And the lack of any real challenge or increase in tension just turn this into a shooter template Unity could include with their engine as a jumping-off point.
If you're looking for a game in this same vein that would actually be fun, Killing Floor has been free in the past and does this type of game unspeakably better. Don't waste $15 on this. The only way they could redeem this would be to MAYBE add in co-op and reduce the price to less than $5. As for now there's no reason to purchase this game.

700 day veteran here and it was once great, but apparently now Perfect Worlds vision of this game is to add a reputation tab upon reputation tab and charging out the rear end for pretty ships.
Basically the reputation system is a resource sink system where you level to unlock gear purchases, upgrade your abilities, and thats about it. There is also a fleet reputation system where it's basically the same thing, except you can eventually buy Fleet Ships, which costs you Ship modules for the ones with increased statistics.
The reputation could be a good thing, that is if you didn't just have a very short list of missions to choose from that earn you the marks to progress through your reputation tier.
For example, one tier is the Omega tier, which basically the only way to progress is by doing Borg missions. You have the Romulan tier, for Romulan marks etc. etc. My thing about the whole system, is there should be one mark currency no matter what you do. That way if you have to grind at least let it be a mission(s) you enjoy doing. Also, the reputation is not account bound, so if you like switching between characters, it's just more work for you. They changed it recently to where if you max a rep tab on a character, you can purchase a token for twice the experience to one of your alts. By the time you reach max rep on one character, even spending half the time on another is just too much.
I speak a great deal about this system because once you reach your level cap, this is all you can expect to be doing for the forseeable future.
The fleet reputation I can sum up nicely. If you're in a huge fleet, fun. If not, soul crushing and forget it.
The journey to the level cap is fun, space battles very fun. Ground combat underwhelming and tiresome.

Overture is a fast-paced roguelike game where you wander through each level until you find a mini-boss, kill it, descend down the stairs, fight a boss, defeat it and move on to the next level. The game focuses a lot on action rather than complex character building - item stats are shown right on screen so you can pick the one you want quickly and move on. As you play, you'll unlock new classes and you can use your accumulated money to power up each class. Upgrades become more expensive the more you upgrade a class, but there is no limit to upgrades so as long as you accumulate money, you can keep on upgrading your favorite class until you're powerful enough to beat the game.
The two main issues that hinder the game are:
1. Confusion - there are times where there is just so much happening on the screen at the same time that you won't know what's going on or where is your character, which might lead to troublesome situations and even character death.
2. Fluctuating difficulty - the game is very easy at times, then suffer from sudden difficulty spikes. You could be having a perfect streak just demolishing all enemies quickly and then, suddenly, you find yourself completely surrounded by enemies, projectiles flying all over the place, you get lost among the confusion and then bam, your character's dead. And since it's a roguelike... It means starting all over.
Apart from these, it's still really fun to play, even if there's the occasional frustration.
One thing I have to mention - AMAZING soundtrack. I would 100% recommend purchasing the OST as well!
