HuniePop is pretty much as advertised, a sleazy dating sim using Match-3 mechanics. If you don't like the idea of a game like this, it probably won't convince you otherwise. But if you are open minded, it's a good game, if a bit too much on mark at times.
As far as the dating game aspect goes, it's not terribly deep but has pretty good characterization. For the most part, the women seem like individuals, not objects. Nikki in particular is probably exactly the sort of woman that almost every gamer guy would like to find. The writing is good (and funny, at last if you aren't uptight), and in many cases, the voice acting is surprisingly well done.
It would perhaps have been nicer if the goal wasn't to sleep with all the girls, but have a possiblity of an ending with just one (and going beyond just the one final screenshot of them)
As for the Match-3 mechanics, it's half-good. The dating portion uses something of a puzzle mechanic to it, certain girls like certain color/shape jewels, so you have to concentrate on getting those (and maxing out your traits to empahsis those, at least later in the game).
That goes out the window for the sex match-3 game. That's more like the various "Blitz" games, you simply have to match jewels as fast as possible without pausing or thinking.  I guess some might find it fun, but it's mostly just a chore, and at higher levels, an exhausting chore. And in many cases, the reward isn't worth it. Some "ending" scenes are pretty good, others are not.
All in all though, you get more than your money's worth. If only dating was this easy in real life...

Edit: Revised for better structure. Edit (part 2): Adding Parody Category that made me flip my recommendation.
Review based on various reasons to buy this game:
+ The dialogue present here was the strongest seller for me:
+ Game has completely ridiculous gift purchases (for the girls) available, for example a hispanic girl loves to get Marracas, a poncho, and etc...
*Where it fails: Most dialogue and content actually comes off as meh and forgettable! (Aside from the tutorial character, who's like an older Tiny Tina addicted to porn that has much more interesting dialogue moments)
+ All girls' lines are fully voice acted.
+ The girls look cliche, but are more often than not well drawn (Except for the red head...)
+ The girls move, blink, and are lip-synched to their dialogue.
- A lot of what they say and expect you to say is stereotypical and the winning answer is always chosen to please the girl you're pursing rather than any depth on your part.
- After you learn a girl's trivia information (like her interests, history, and height) most conversations will just be proving that you can recall those facts to her.
+/- The goal is not to pursue one at a time, but ALL girls.
- The dating portion is purely you just playing match-three games, with no real intimacy/interaction gained in the relationship other than getting laid after 5 wins.
*Where it fails: Relationships in this game are not only completely shallow, but are also kind of disturbing. Once you've had sex with a girl character, the only real reason to talk to them again is either for a quickie (another run at the sex mini-game) or (more likely) milking them for money and stat points.

+ With the applied "patch", there *are* uncensored pornographic images...
- However there are far more of these (with better quality) available via Google.
+ Several of the masturbation images are actually pretty erotic.
+ While the anticipation (IE build-up) is well done...
- The payoff is quite a let-down.

*Where it fails:
The 'payoff" consists:
A) Sex as simulated via an obnoxious mini-game with repetitive moaning sound clips.
B) A few images of semi-nude women after sex and ***shot. (Not sure why someone would have to put effort into *receiving* oral btw)

+ Interesting variant of match-three games.
+ Each character has a different set of favored and unfavored colors of affection tokens (gems).
+ You are provided with a limited inventory in which they can store various reuseable date-gifts (buffs/powers) to use during a date.
+ It's interesting to try and figure out what the optimal kit setup is for particular girls, based on what gifts you've already unlocked.
+ You don't typically have to 'grind' to win. However, as each successful date increases the difficulty of the next one (for all girls), there will occasionally be periods where some stat raising will be needed after you realize that a date can't be won. (Even failed dates give you benefits though)
+ Menus are for the most part easy to navigate, aschetically pleasing, and color-coded for convenience.
- Exceptions are the nearly identical "Girls" and "Girl Finder" menus, one of which is like your stalker encyclopedia while the other advances the day and teleports you elsewhere.
- The sex mini-game is completely dreadful since it relies on you just finding matches continuously while the climax meter drops at constant rate. Where as in the normal dating games you had various powers, gems did different things, and 4+ gem matches were worth more, the mini-game just gives all matches a fixed value. This makes for a very tedious and board-layout (not skill) based obstacle.
+ Conversations, gift/food-giving (consumeables), and intoxication meters are initially an interesting management simulation given that each day there are a finite set of girls you can see in a day, monies available, and gifts to purchase/give. (Ignoring how strange or offensive those particular mechanics are theme-wise.)
- Then you realize time goes on forever and the resource management aspect no longer matter.
+Upon further reflection, there's a ridiculously high chance that this entire game (writing, voice acting, and mechanics combined) is a parody of (eroge) dating sims; when considered at such, it is absolutely brilliant for all of the negative reasons listed above.
+The relationships are unsatisying 'cause you're only available goal (to ♥♥♥♥ as many girls as possible) is so superficial.
+The hentai presented is only erotic when the girl is alone. When having sex it's a completely frustrating variant of match3 followed by an image of her by herself then a ***shot in the same pose.
+All of the mechanics are soo thematically wrong and the dialogue is either so bizarre or boring that it's either completely ingenious as a self-aware parody or should be considered completely ironic that something "so bad" could finally be made.
+ You're actually given the perfect stalking device that keeps track of Facebook-like info (likes/dislikes/triva) AND physical locations!
Where it gets it so so right: I initally find it difficult to flip my review though, because it still left me feeling unsatisfied; however, that may be the point of a game which satirizes Fedoras and vapid dating sims where your only goal is to get laid.

The gameplay is suprisingly fun and interesting, but it's the parody element of it that is really why I would recommend the purchase. If you're wanting to play something seriously (IE want to play a a game with depth and satisfcation), you don't want this. (Unless you really want another match-3 game) This is effectively playing an episode of South Park where the focus is dating sims/being a 'Fedora', but instead of Stan and/or Kyle,
have to be the voice of reason to figure out how 'wrong' and unfulfilling the underlying perspective is. I recommend watching
if you want to get a good feel for the game. (The only downside is that you don't hear the character voices, but consider that a bonus surprise for if you do actually play it yourself.)
If you're more interested in any of the non-parody pieces above... I'd recommend the following instead:
* RPG match-three: Puzzle Quest
* Well written dating sim with some (optional) porn: Katawa Shoujo
* Well written VN with puzzles: 999 (DS)
* Parody dating sim whose twist is that it actually has a lot of depth: Hatoful Boyfriend
* Social sim with awesome RPG gameplay: Persona 4 (PS2)
* Can stright up Google H-games online too.

Super MNC has a lot going for.
On the basic level, Super MNC is an experiment in blending games like DOTA(2) and League of Legends together with face paced third person shooters. This generated some interesting and arguably fun concepts.
Sadly it falls short from a small playerbase and a general lack of improvements over the previous game, Monday Night Combat. Super MNC also suffers from a very steep learning curve, which drives many new players into total fustration.
However, Super MNC still carries the charm that MNC had. The humour, the immersion and the atmosphere are all present. If there is one good thing to say about Super MNC is that the atmosphere of the game is one of the best. The environment is really vibrant, the maps generally have great aesthetics, and the game has great music and sound assets. It would dishonest if I said that I did not enjoy this game.
But sadly, it falls short.

If a World War II game actually makes you feel like youre actually in a War, then the Developers did a great Job. This is what happend to me. Considering the fact that you have to capture flags isn't realistic at all. But this isn't about realism.
Those type of moments where the enemy comes into a house with 3 or 4 people and youre the last survivor who must defend it are just great and satisfying. Im going to split this into two parts: Pros and Cons. I will also talk about the different aspects about Heroes and generals: Audio/Atmosphere, Gameplay and Graphics.
There's not really much to say. The graphics are just average. Nothing special but it fits to the game. They could improve a bit but honestly im already fine with the graphics. The weapon and car graphics are the best graphics in the game so far. The soldiers all look the same. There's no variety between Soldier A and Soldier B except for the tankcrew or the paratroopers for example but all of them have the same faces. Its not clone wars.
The Gunshots are really great! I mean they are just perfect compared to other games like CS:GO. On the other hand the distant Gunfire shots are horrible at Mid-Range. If someone shots a rifle 40 meters away from you, you will hear it. In this game, you wont. At least its not so easy. I cant really say much about the Tanks because i played this game for 9 hours. So bare in mind that this is an early review.
If no one is shooting or driving you can hear absolutely nothing. There is no wind or Animal sounds. Just nothing.
In the games menu where you can customize your soldiers you will hear the games Soundtrack over and over again, which can be annoying.
Like i said Above the fights are just intense and satisfying. The game itself is very easy for me because i already have a KD of 1.85 after 9 hours of playing. If you are new to the game the objectives are pretty easy: Capture the flag. Just like in WW2.
There are microstransaction in Heroes & Generals but it doesnt affect the gameplay. At least not for low-level battles. The matchmaker is pretty good in this game but sometimes you have to wait 90 seconds till the battle starts.
Let's get to the "Campaign map". Yes the campaign map you got me. Heroes & Generals is also a strategy game.
The map itself is europe with every single city on it. But i completely ignored it at the start because for low levels like me this map is totally useless because you have to be a Corporal to fight on it. Anyways Generals or Lieutenants can start battle on it and YOU as a soldier can fight on these battles! Want to fight on the battle of Berlin? You can do it, if youre level 5.
+ Very good Battles itself
+ Immersive
+ One of the best Gunshots sounds ever
+ Capture the flag: Just like in WW2
+ Very easy to learn.
+ Customizable Soldiers/Weapons/Appearance
+ RTS Elements
- No Atmosphere if nobody is shooting
- Battle may turn into Grenade Spam
- Only a few Maps
- Distant Gunfire is Awful
- No Variety between Soldiers
- The Map design is really wierd sometimes
My personal Verdict:
It's a great game and theres literally no reason to not download it because its free!

Dead Purge: Outbreak es un juego de disparos en primera persona donde nos enfrentamos a oleadas de zombies, así de simple. Es algo parecido a Killing Floor o similar a Left 4 Dead, pero sin esos pequeños elementos narrativos o pequeñas tramas que les hacen un poco más dinámicos, este FPS se limita a ponernos en la acción de una vez, imaginen el multijugador cooperativo de Call of Duty Modern Warfare 3, en el que podemos intentar sobrevivir en los mapas mientras vienen olas de enemigos a asesinarnos.
Lo mejor de Dead Purge: Outbreak es su apartado gráfico, estéticamente de gran calidad, pero eso es poco si nos ponemos a mirar las siempre quejosas necesidades de los jugadores de hoy en día. Mi queja de este FPS es el precio, sus $15 no lo valen, si tuviese un precio de unos $5/$8 sería pasable. 
En general las mecánicas de su jugabilidad son buenas, la sensación al disparar se siente muy buena comparada a otros juegos que hemos probado, el movimiento del personaje se siente un tanto lento pero ciertamente es real si lo ponemos al lado del caminar de un ser humano. Dentro de la muchas quejas que leemos en Steam, está que a veces el personaje se verá atascado en algunos elementos u objetos de los distintos mapas, sobre todo en las puertas, inclusive, una pequeña mata en el suelo, será motivo suficiente para que nuestro mata-zombies tenga problemas para circular.
Dentro de las partidas, los zombies te siguen donde quiera que estés, eso es bueno, estos enemigos sedientos de sangre tienen un desplazamiento muy letárgico, llegando a ser presa fácil de cualquier principiante en un FPS; este pequeño detalle hace que el juego se torne aburrido para aquellos que buscan acción o algo más movido. Tras finalizar cada oleada, un drone aparece del cielo a modo de tienda en la que podemos hacer refill para nuestro equipamiento, o comprar nuevas armas que nos den alguna ventaja para el comienzo de las nuevas oleadas, en las que se supone los enemigos son más fuertes. Al igual que el precio del juego, los precios de las armas en el drone son sumamente altos.
Otro dato que puede agregarse a las cosas a mejorar, es la estabilidad técnica del juego, el acabado final pareciera no venir bien pulido, y a pesar de que cumplimos con los requisitos recomendados, el juego no anda a unos 60 FPS constantes con los ajustes gráficos al máximo (suele rondar los 45-50). El juego tarda bastante en cargar.
En pocas palabras, Dead Purge: Outbreak no es un mal juego, simplemente le falta el elemento especial: MULTIJUGADOR. Sería el complemento perfecto para un título que tiene visuales tan bonitas y una jugabilidad tan agradable. Al contrario de los comentarios negativos en la tienda de Steam sobre Dead Purge: Outbreak, podemos decir que es un título decente, no es malo, no, simplemente le hace falta el multijugador en linea para que sea un juego pasable.
¿Que si lo recomendamos? Si, en oferta a $7, si.

NIche is a wonderful casual game for those of us who just want to see what each day will bring. Each adult creature (I call them Nichi ) have 3 gems representing the amount of moves they can make each turn. Spend them wisely. Grow your population, your food supply and create the most interesting (and sometimes hilarious) creatures you'll ever see. As you struggle to adapt and conquer life's struggles face off against vicious predators, gather food via berries, nuts, or bunnies. That's it, only you can make the limitations on your tribe. Think that's too easy?
Go to the Jungle. There you face creatures that can brush off your attacks and highlight your weaknesses. Food is abundant, but will you eat it or will it you?
Not a jungle person? Go to the mountain! Dive in the hotsprings, fend off the balance bear. Use pack tactics to corner your bunnies and feast. Unlock new precious genetics and revive a species encased in ice.
Even the ocean is yours to conquer if you so wish. But I warn you hunt in packs. The fish are incredibly fast and hard to catch, plus you don't want to be alone when the leeches come for you.
As this is early access there still isn't particular perks or a unique experience for players looking to live in the savannah biome, but the creators work tirelessly to evolve the game right along side your creatures. I can't wait for the finished project.

스나이퍼 엘리트2의 맵을 다시 재탕한 재창작물. 전작인 나치 좀비1과 마찬가지로 4인 코옵이 주된 컨텐츠이며, 전작의 장점과 단점을 그대로 가져왔다. 그도 그럴 것이, 전작도 스엘2에서 맵을 재탕해서 만들어진 작품인 만큼 엔진이며 여러가지 요소를 그대로 가져와서 만든 작품이기 때문이다.
쓸데 없이 높은 사양과 그에 걸맞지 않는 그래픽이 최고 단점이다.
특히, 나좀1편도 무리없이 돌아가는 컴퓨터에서 나좀2가 버벅인다. 역시 아수라 엔진은 개적화의 대명사인 듯 하다.
게임 자체는 1편에서 이어지는 스토리를 다루고 있다. 1편에서도 대놓고 후속작 암시를 했는데, 이번 2편에서는 스토리가 전체적으로 마무리 되는 느낌이다. 그러나 해보면 알겠지만, 엔딩을 봐도 ♥♥♥을 덜 닦은 느낌이 드는데 어찌보면 스토리가 마무리되었다고 볼 수 있지만, '그'가 여전히 어찌되었는지 알 수 없기에 3편이 나올 가능성도 있다. 2014년에 스엘3이 나오는데 스엘3 엔진으로 나좀3이 나오는 것은 아닐까?
위에서 요구하는 사양에 비해서 그래픽은 좋지 않다고 이야기했는데, 사양을 떠나서 그냥 그래픽만 보면 괜찮고 좋은 수준이다. 아마도, 사양이 높아진건 안 그래도 좋지 않은 아수라 엔진을 가지고 1편에 비해서 특수 효과를 더 많이, 액체를 더 많이 표현하다 보니 좀 더 시스템에 부하를 주는 것 같다.
그만큼, 특수 효과(번개, 피로 물든 강 등)는 만족스러운편.
특수효과와 좀비의 종류가 약간 더 추가된 대신 상대적으로 각 챕터별 체감상 길이와 플탐이 전작에 비해 줄었다. 전작의 경우 한 템포마다 그 길이가 길어서 가끔은 ♥♥♥줄타는 맛도 있었지만, 이번 작은 그 길이가 짧아진 편. 스피디 해져서 빠른 진행이 가능하다.
코옵 위주기 때문에 솔플을 하지 않는 이상 X레이 킬캠은 거의 나오지 않는다. 전작의 장점도 그대로 가져왔기 때문에 코옵으로 사람들과 같이 할 경우에는 꽤 즐거울 것이다.
정리하자면, 나좀1편과 별반 다르지 않다는 것이다.

HuniePop... where should I begin? For starters, its a straight up Bejeweled game with lovely girls, voice actings, and lewd pictures with a very little plot to start from.
As you make a new game, your first assignment is to find a girl and date her, and eventually "Sleep" with her and thats pretty much it.  As you talk to a girl, you gain "Hunie" for upgrading your personality, ranging from Talent to Luck. I guess thats where the games "RPG Elements" starts and finishes. As far as I know, you can ask a girl on a date imidiatly. When you "Go on a date" you have to complete this Bejeweled Minigame with only twenty turns, and restoring some turns by matching up some bells. After four or so dates, and during the night, you can sleep with one of the girls after completing a date minigame. Guess what minigame this is? The same one as the dating minigame, except that you no longer have turns, but instead, your love meature depletes quickly. This is the meat of the game, and to be frank, I am dissapointed.
The most part of this game I enjoyed was the girls themselves. They are all interesting and have a very good personality. They also benefit from a really good voice actor, who was really really good. You can unlock clothing for each girl after an successful date, if they where wearing something different during the date. Each girl has a really good idle animation, which I enjoyed.
What I dont like about this game is this, your main objective is to sleep with girls and nothing else. The main plot is just that, sleeping with girls. The girls is interesting at first, learning their personality and their likes and dislikes, but eventually they become boring. They'll ask you questions you answered million times before, and it just gets boring after a while. The game gets harder after each date, even on easy they are harder. This really discouraged me from continuing, I only played until I slept with the two girls I was interested the most.
I really wanted to have a very good Western VN, I wanted to have a really really good plot that I'd remember years in the future. Thats what I expected, and its wasnt something I got. What I got was a puzzle game with anime girls and sexy images. Actually, I got the adult versions. Basicly, I got nudity and a better sex noises, but that doesnt count it. Seriously, the gallery in the game just looks straight from a VN, something I wanted. I really hope HuniePop will become a VN in the future, as I really wanted to know and learn each girl, and have a route for each girl.
If you want to read a very good Western VN, play Katawa Shoujo. It may not take place in the States, but it was made in the States.

I only lasted around 40 mins or so playing this free mmo game.
It's clearly inspired from the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games.
When starting the game you will be prompted to choose a name for yourself, then choose two factions, Locals and Aliens. The locals are those that survived since the start of the zone's outbreak, while the aliens is a given name to those that come from outside the zone. It's stated each faction has several classes, though you don't actually get to pick them at the start. I presume that's later on.
The character creation isn't too bad, it has 25 head options, the rest are starting clothing, boots and pants, which are either 8 options to 5 options with boots and pants.
Overall the graphics aren't amazing, it feels like a game from 2006 or even before.
As said, the surroundings and theme feel alot like a stalker game. You'll have to be highly interested in stalker games aswell as being okay with playing a low graphiced game to enjoy this. It's not horrendious mind you. But it's no way near perfect.
Apparently the game started as russian only, but english has been added to the quests and dialog with npc's. There are just quite a few english typo's, aswell as a few laughable sentences that is no doubt poorly translated by someone who was a russian. For any grammar nazi, it is cringe-worthy, but hey, even Overkill made a few typo's in their payday 2 game.
The guns look slightly better than the character textures and you can switch between first and third person.
The enemies are quite various, but also rather low textured. Interestingly though, there are anomalies in the game, another element famous from the stalker series.
Once you leave the starting zone, you have a choice to go into a safe zone (a large town) but warned that if you leave it, you will be out in open pvp atmosphere. You also have a second choice, to go to the same town, but it is just pvp instantly, so there won't be a safe zone.
The game also has a store to buy ingame currency for real money, but the buyable stuff that requires this currency don't look impressive, more like retextured items that other vendors already sell ingame.
I only managed to play around 40 mins again, so I haven't covered all of the game, no doubt by far. But I wasn't impressed when I arrived to the town, and quickly decided to save my time on other games. Again, this free game is worth a try if you enjoy stalker/wasteland games, if not, you'll only be in it for a few minutes before deciding to uninstall like so many others.

I had heard many terrible things about the game, so my expectations were quite low. Therefore I was pleasantly surprised by this game. I'll start with the flaws and work toward the good:
Cons unique to this DX iteration:
- It's fairly short
- Weak characterization
- Weak story
- The "purchase any item, any time" mechanic seemed OP
- Weird unresolved cliffhanger ending
Con shared with DXHR:
- You have multiple ways to accomplish a subobjective (hacking, conversation, combat, pathfinding), but because XP is awarded for each of these activities, I always tried to do them all instead of picking a particular playstyle and following through (i.e. sneak past the guard using the secret vent, get the XP, then double back and take him combat takedown XP). The game rewards these seemingly ridiculous redundancies; it breaks immersion, but... need XP for supersnazzy aug abilities. (Another example: I snagged the keypad passcode from an email [awesome detective work!] but will still take the 2 minutes to hack the keypad anyway because it gives me XP. Perverse!)
BUT... if you enjoyed DXHR, you'll probably enjoy this. Some of the elements are simplified a bit, but you'd be surprised how much is still there and the similar to DXHR. Prior to starting into this game, I had a hankering for some DX and was contemplating yet another playthrough. Instead I played this and the itch was scratched (with new-to-me content to boot).
Minor pros as compared to DXHR:
- There aren't any space limitations in your inventory, which wasn't game breaking, and actually just turned out to be conventient.
- The textures and graphics were originally designed for mobile. They look just fine, plus everything loads really fast and runs smooth
- Move silently is a passive aug instead of an active one. To me, this is a good streamlining decision.
I'll put it this way. I was WAY happier with The Fall than with The Missing Link.
Final thought: This game did not introduce any new gameplay elements as compared to DXHR, so if you skip it, you aren't really missing much.

Cons

- Endgame items (ships/upgrades/customization) costs either weeks of time or money

HuniePop... where should I begin? For starters, its a straight up Bejeweled game with lovely girls, voice actings, and lewd pictures with a very little plot to start from.
As you make a new game, your first assignment is to find a girl and date her, and eventually "Sleep" with her and thats pretty much it.  As you talk to a girl, you gain "Hunie" for upgrading your personality, ranging from Talent to Luck. I guess thats where the games "RPG Elements" starts and finishes. As far as I know, you can ask a girl on a date imidiatly. When you "Go on a date" you have to complete this Bejeweled Minigame with only twenty turns, and restoring some turns by matching up some bells. After four or so dates, and during the night, you can sleep with one of the girls after completing a date minigame. Guess what minigame this is? The same one as the dating minigame, except that you no longer have turns, but instead, your love meature depletes quickly. This is the meat of the game, and to be frank, I am dissapointed.
The most part of this game I enjoyed was the girls themselves. They are all interesting and have a very good personality. They also benefit from a really good voice actor, who was really really good. You can unlock clothing for each girl after an successful date, if they where wearing something different during the date. Each girl has a really good idle animation, which I enjoyed.
What I dont like about this game is this, your main objective is to sleep with girls and nothing else. The main plot is just that, sleeping with girls. The girls is interesting at first, learning their personality and their likes and dislikes, but eventually they become boring. They'll ask you questions you answered million times before, and it just gets boring after a while. The game gets harder after each date, even on easy they are harder. This really discouraged me from continuing, I only played until I slept with the two girls I was interested the most.
I really wanted to have a very good Western VN, I wanted to have a really really good plot that I'd remember years in the future. Thats what I expected, and its wasnt something I got. What I got was a puzzle game with anime girls and sexy images. Actually, I got the adult versions. Basicly, I got nudity and a better sex noises, but that doesnt count it. Seriously, the gallery in the game just looks straight from a VN, something I wanted. I really hope HuniePop will become a VN in the future, as I really wanted to know and learn each girl, and have a route for each girl.
If you want to read a very good Western VN, play Katawa Shoujo. It may not take place in the States, but it was made in the States.

I hesitated purchasing a beta version of a game, but it was well worth it! I had been watching a youtuber play Niche before I made the purchase and it absolutely helped me make up my mind. I play Niche every day and the updates are actually fun to look forward to - if there are bugs in the game, they are reported and every new update is a new chance to learn and explore an entirely new aspect of genetics.
As a fair warning this is not a game that has a "winning" aspect. A successful pack of animals can be maintained for long periods of time (both in game time, and real time). However there is the chance that the pack can go extinct. I actually found this to be a great aspect of the game, the threat of extinction adds realism to the game.
Overall, I love this game. I play it everyday practically and am always very glad to receive the monthly updates! I cannot wait to see what this game creates next. I highly recommend purchasing now on the ground floor, in order to be a part of the building and the growth of the game. It is a highly recommended purchase!

This game has brilliant ideas and is fun to play with a whole new perspective on battlefield combat. Instaed of controlling the whole army, you control you and the army from your commands. This game may be full of new and original ideas but they haven't been fully developed into the game for example on the map, the water flows the wrong way and looks really bad. The whole map doesn't look realistic enough compared to games released now such as fifa and black ops and elder scrolls online which is disappointing. The polotics aren't nearly as good as you'd want them to be as there is practicaly no diplomacy at all. The main problem with single player games is it is almost impossible to lose as king because if you send an emissary to become their vassal to a kingdom that is just about to reck you then they will always accept and give you 30 days to see their leader but if you don't see their leader then they declare war on you again thus meaning you have 30 days of peacetime infinately. Luckily there are some mods freely downloadable from the steam store that makes the game more bareable but in the end you either find it too easy or too hard depending on the difficulty setting. If you change the difficutly setting constantly then it ruins the game because you always win because you wouldn't set it so that you lose. The mod 'diplomacy' fixes a few of the diplomacy problems between other kingdoms but it is still poor. 'Persistent World' mod is the mod that makes so many people actualy play this game because you are online with other people and can talk with them and basically do what ever you  want in an open world. The original version (called native) has on open world that you can explore with your character on the battlefield but when you have to move around using the map when your not fighting, you can't see any graphics but the map for ages. Persistent world mod lets you join servers that let you do whatever you like  unless an admin of the server spots you in which case they will either ban you or kill you. Persisternt world is good but gets frustrating having said that it is the best feature on the game. Overall, if you want a game to waste time on then you should consider this if you are prepared to play on persistent world otherwise you should look elseware.

The Fall tells the story of Ben, a mercenary, who works with Namir's team then gets betrayed. Essentially, the story is his struggle against his former team members while at the same time he tries to uncover why there is a shortage of the so-called Neuropozyne which is a must medicine for all augmented people.
Now, what should be noted about the game is that while it looks similar to Human Revolution it is a toned-down version of it. This was initially released for iOS mobile systems but later on was ported to the PC. Unfortunately, many limitations remained on the PC version so much so that this is amongst the worst PC ports.
The upside:
- an interesting story that serves as a sort of prequel to Human Revolution; while it is not as complex or interesting as the "main" game it is nice to see Ben's story through and meeting some familiar faces during the missions
- considering it was initially made for the iOS the game looks quite well - naturally, textures are of lower resolution and characters / objects consist of fewer polygons but the creators did their best to make a game that reminds us of Human Revolution
- the story wraps up around 5 hours which is not bad for a game originally intended for mobile phone users; many achievements and a new game plus mode make sure we have a long-lasting experience
The downside:
- Putting aside the toned-down graphics the game has some awful limitations: jumping and picking up objects is simply not possible this time. While the former I did not particularly mind the latter would have been good for distracting enemies. Also, the inventory we have now represents the shop itself: all items show up in our inventory, we just need to buy the missing ones - provided we have enough cash. They could have just put a vendor guy somewhere in the slum to make it a little harder to purchase stuff.
- Pressing buttons does not always work. It's best to click twice when picking options during dialogues as the game finds it really hard to register our selections in menus. During gameplay this is not an issue. Oh yeah and the menu options are simply HUGE - they could have just created a different main menu with smaller font size.
- While the 5-hour long story I appreciated I did not understand the "to be continued" message at the end. The "Pacifist" achievement that refers to the story calls it "Part 1" which makes me assume originally there were plans to release further episodes. I guess the game did not do well financially.
Deus Ex The Fall is an interesting game whose shortcomings mainly stem from the fact that it is a port. While I do appreciate what N-Fusion has done with a little more effort the result could have been closer to offering a real PC experience.
Do I recommend this game? Well, if you are not a die hard Deus Ex fan I do not. But if you are and you do not mind spending 2 euros when the game is discounted you may find this game an entertaining one. After Human Revolution and before Mankind Divided I enjoyed the ride - I just wish it'd been better.

Bottom line up front:  One of the best co-op games I've ever played, Vermintide takes the Left 4 Dead formula and improves it in every way.  Buy this one!
Obviously, I've played a LOT of Vermintide.  I've played extensively on solo, with on-line pickup groups, with family, and with friends across the country.  I've played all the maps with all the characters, and beaten all the maps on the hardest settings, but still have no problem going back through for a lark on easier difficulties.
Essentially, this is an episodic game set in the Warhammer universe, which is a high fantasy setting with steampunk elements and includes familiar fare such as woodland elves, gold-loving dwarves, magic users, and monsters.
The overall plot involves a band of four adventurers travelling through various locations in a city overrun by Skaven (Ratmen). It plays from first person, and emphasizes close combat for most of the characters. As you beat maps, you unlock more of them, and eventually you reach a conclusion and a victory (of sorts).  The "last stand" mode lets you just fight rats eternally with no plot elements to get in the way.
For those familiar, the game takes tremendous inspiration from Left 4 Dead.  Some elements are nearly identical:  The opening camera swoop on every level, the character banter on elevators, the need to stick together, the various "specials" among the enemy (to include a leaping assassin and a tank), the periodic hordes if you wait too long, the limited weapon switches, the two types of health recharge, the "fight off the horde while something happens" set pieces, and the overall post-apocalyptic "empty city" feel to the levels.
Key differences make this game great (and better than the L4D series):
1)
Items show up as rewards for completing a level, with a dice roll determining the final reward.  These dice can be "weighted" by player choices during the level:  If you pick up a "grimoire," then for that level, you have substantially less health AND lose an inventory slot, but a much better chance at the best items.  Essentially, you're choosing to make the game more difficult so that you can benefit at the end...IF you are able to win with the self-imposed restrictions.  The items can be cosmetic, but the vast majority are weapons and trinkets.
2)
The aforementioned items are how you improve your character, and they persist between games.  Like with most of these sorts of games, you'll end up with a lot of items you don't need, but in the "hub" area you can use the shrine and forge to improve or combine your weapons to make them better, or to reroll their bonus traits.
3)
There are five characters:  wizard, elf, soldier, dwarf, and witch hunter.  Each has distinctly different playstyles, but the true innovation is in the wizard class.  She is finicky to play at first, as her spells (essentially ranged attacks) are unlimited except by "overheating," which means that you can sacrifice health in order to cast more fireballs in the thick of battle.  The elf switches readily between ranged and melee, the dwarf and soldier excel going toe to toe (either with big heavy hitting weapons or with defensive shields), and the witch hunter is something of a mix.  They are well balanced, as evidenced by the fact that player preferences don't lean particularly heavily toward one class.
4)
The beauty of a well-coordinated team is better shown in Vermintide than in almost any other game I've played.  The hardest difficulty, Cataclysm, is essentially impossible solo or with an uncoordinated group, but with a tight group, you will cover for each other, help each other, and constantly encourage each other.  Although there is friendly fire on the hardest settings, the damage is meager and doesn't incite the same rage/revenge that I saw in other games like this.  The best trinkets give permanent passive boosts which help the entire party (item duplication, heal sharing, etc.) further encouraging group dynamics.
Other things you'll like about the game:  the graphics are very immersive, and feature occasional sweeping views, well-detailed models and rooms, and a variety of locations and challenge types.  The plot pushes you forward enough to give a steady sense of purpose; the voice acting is excellent with so many spoken lines that I'm still hearing new ones even hundreds of hours into the game; you can pick the gear for your bots (you always have a party of four no matter how many humans are playing); the bot AI is strong enough that they can effectively support you on all but Cataclysm difficulties; the enemy rats are nasty, primitive enemies with just enough tactics to keep you agile.
There are a few negatives:  The best (red) items are so hard to get that despite playing as much as I have I only have one, and it isn't that great :)  Gear is mostly random, so you can easily play through an hour-long nailbiter session on Cataclysm difficulty and end up with a junk item.  Your characters level with experience, but the rewards are essentially nil...level seems mostly to serve as an indicator of player time investment.  You can't direct bots at all, which can be frustrating at times, and there are some occasional disconnect bugs I've encountered, particularly when playing with folks from other countries.
But these are the quibbles of someone who has played for so many hours that I can see the seams in the game a little more easily than someone trying it out for the first time.
Overall, this is a great buy, and one of my all-time favorites.  Go for it!

Nine years after the release of Resident Evil 4 - the last Resident Evil game which Shinji Mikami, the creative mind behind the early games in the series, directed - The Evil Within was released. The game is in many ways a rehash of RE4, and in some ways brings a new approach to the survival horror genre. While true survival sequences are few - though they're definitely present - TEW felt much more tense to me than RE4, by far its closest comparison, did - probably mostly because of the more significant scarcity of ammo. There's no truly new territory compared to the RE series here, other than the setting, but the characters are a bit more interesting - particularly the villain.
I recommend the game for anyone who likes the idea of an action-horror game with a bit of suspense. If you played and enjoyed RE4, this one's worth picking up, since it feels more like a spiritual successor to RE4 than any of the subsequent games in the RE series.

I was recently given a copy of Dead Purge: Outbreak by Microlith Games (I keep typing Monolith), it's a pretty solid game, the movement of the screen is a little weird, but easy to get used to, Dead Purge: Outbreak is very similar to Contagion, except prettier and runs really well.
Overall the game is pretty fun to play and is fairly easy, though the game is missing a few features that would make this better.
The biggest difference between Contagion and Dead Purge: Outbreak is that the weapons and ammo that you loot are dropped from the Zombies, this is a problem because it removes the fun out of exploring the map, on top of this, if there is a weapon on the floor and you can't see it, once you pick it up, you lose your other weapon.
Dead Purge: Outbreak really could do with a placement style looting sytem, rather than the Zombie based system, this would promote exploring the map more.
The gunplay isn't the best, but not the worst either, the slow motion stuff lasts too long and in my opinion, makes it harder to aim, plus, there is no obvious drawback to hip firing and aiming down the sight.
Yes it's obvious that the dev has used Unity Assets, but that's not a problem, this is an indie game, not all of them have dedicated graphic artists.
I only played Survive, that was the mode I was most interested in, but I will update the review to reflect the other game mode (if I remember).
The reason I recommend Dead Purge: Outbreak is because it's actually quite fun despite it's quirks, it's not a buggy mess and it runs very well.
On my PC, I found no FPS drops, no locking up of the game and on Ultra, the game is very pretty, so I have no arguments there.
The "Research" system is very basic, which isn't a bad thing, it gives you what you need, no junk.
The biggest issue is the movement, the running is too fast, the sway is insane and the gunplay isn't that well polished, a headshot should kill right?.
Overall, I do recommend this game to pass the time when you're bored and maybe to play with friends if the dev decides to add multiplayer support, but if you're looking for a full gameplay experience, I'd say it's best to avoid the game, as it won't offer you that experience in it's current state.

I loved Hotline Miami so much that I bought it on my PS4 just to play it again. But Hotline Miami 2 was a huge disapointment.
First of all, the level design is awful. It would be excusable in most games, but this is Hotline Miami. You only get one chance. Remember how in the original Hotline Miami you could only get hit once before dying, but the stages were well-designed and short, so they didn't make you angry when you played them? Well, Hotline Miami 2 did the exact opposite of that. There are a lot of windows, so enemies can see you almost anywhere. On top of that, you can get killed by enemies with guns that you can't even see, and it feels unfair that you can't see the enemy, but they can see you. Also, the levels are too open. Most of the time, you will get through levels by going through a door and luring enemies to you so you can kill them without dying.
Second, the mask system was screwed. Remember how in the original game, after unlocking a mask, you could use it whenever you wanted? Well, now you can only use them on certain levels. Sometimes, during soldier missions where you are controlling a soldier during the Vietnam war. That might sound pretty cool, and it would have been, if you could actually pick up weapons. You get to choose your gun before fighting, but you have to choose wisely because if you run out of ammo, that is the only gun you can use. If you run out, better hope there is spare ammo nearby, because all you have after that is a knife.
Third, the story is dumbed down. Instead of mysterious phone calls and the three internal voices, everything is told to you directly. Maybe this is just me, but it doesn't feel quite right in a Hotline Miami game.
Overall, the only things you could enjoy in this game are the story and the level editor, but the cutscenes for the story could be found with a simple google search, so if you want to use the level editor, then thats the only thing this game has over the original, and the only reason I keep coming back to it. If you don't want to use the level editor, then get the original Hotline miami if you already haven't.

Before I bought this game, I thought about what I expected from it. My expectations were:
- Entertaining for 10 minutes, until the novelty wears off
- Rote, grinding gameplay
- Low replay value
- Average game overall
This game more or less met my expectations.
The core gameplay is centred around two main goals, paying off the national debt and defeating the Islamic State.
To pay off the national debt, you fly around a world map buying and selling oil, supplies, and food to make a profit and pay off the national debt, with a few trivial mechanics such as the ability to invade countries and drill in Alaska for oil, but the restriction on doing these things is the threat of angering other countries and setting off WW3, which is the only losing scenario. The trade is repetitive and gets rote very fast, and it takes a lot of it to pay off the national debt. This took up the majority of my time in-game, I must have spent about 90% of it trading and using the related mechanics. To defeat the Islamic State, the other goal of the game, you have to play an arcade game in which Trump fights ISIS soldiers, which is funny the first time, and annoying the second time. You don't know how long the levels are or how much is left, it's difficult to aim, and it's really only fun the first time you play it.
The novelty of the game wore off very fast. There aren't many Trump sound bites, and while they're funny the first few times, they get annoying after a while, along with the soundtrack, and after about half an hour I muted the game and switched on spotify.  Having pepe as the newsfrog was funny at first, but like pretty much everything else in the game, it lost its comedic value rapidly.
After completing the game the first time, I started a new one, but couldn't be bothered to finish it. There's little replay value here, it's just the same grind all over again. You probably won't be inclined to replay it unless you're an achievement hunter.
Overall this game is average, but I still recommend it. It's better than a lot of indie games I've played, and it's great for a quick laugh, even if it's lacking in a bit of substance beyond that. It doesn't overcharge (at the time of writing) for a game you'll probably only play through once or twice at most.

Remember that one game with Bush fighting Al-Quaeda? How about the flash game with Bush and Gore boxing?
If you can somehow dig that out of your memory, then this game will bring all those good times running right over you in all  their topical glory!
MAGA: The Trump Presidency is essentially a flash game that you pay for, but is it really worth a few dollars?
Kind of.
To be honest, the interface is a little difficult to get a hold of for the first few minutes and you might find yourself clicking on the wrong country every now and then, but it's by no means the worst thing I've ever encountered. Aside from that, there's a very (very) simplified form of resource management that boils down to trying not to blow the US to smithereens - with a few truly Newgrounds-style flash mini-games in-between. The mini-games are simple side-scrolling shooters and platformers, so don't be surprised at the lack of originality; though, for a quickly made, topical game, it's not surprising in the first place.
The real attraction here for me, though, were the sound bytes from Trump's speeches peppered into the gameplay. Whether you like him or not, it's at least amusing to hear him spout his more famous sayings while blasting away ISIS operatives or building the wall on the Southern border.
Personally, I thought it was a fun little romp for a few bucks.
Have fun!

Nearly every of the playable classes and sub-classes are ranged in some manner with their attacks give or take a few with stranger means of fighting close-range or with unusual other skills. It reminds me of the older installments in the Gauntlet game series.
It features hectic level design of spread out areas with enemies all over as well as treasure chests, cursed tombstones that can trigger a mass summoning of enemies, mini-bosses and imprisoned NPCs you can free and have follow you along to fight beside you throughout the madness of it all. With every run you accumulate gold which you can use to either unlock new characters and classes or simply upgrade and power-up ones you have giving them a permenant boost to their starting stats making enemies take less shots to fell. As you play you'll find and be able to equip various randomly dropped and found pieces of equipment to boost your character's stats as well. Although the gear itself only lasts that run. Once you die it's back to square one.
The pixel art design by Oryx is quite popular among a lot of Indie Roguelike and Roguelite titles from what I have seen and I simply adore the style of them used in this magnificent indie title. The music is a fast-paced, blood-pumping chiptune style that fits the game's style and matches up nicely, complimenting the game's visual aesthetics as well, blending it all into one fast-paced, retro, rogue-lite shootemup that will make lesser men rage and those with the reflexes to survive want to jump out of their seats.
My only complaints with this game is that it's resolution and window-size is a rather awkward wide-screen that leaves you vulnerable to enemies above and below you with the HUDs taking up most of the upper portion of the screen. This seems like something hopefully they would fix in a future update to make the overall view of the area in-game larger and more accessible.
Aside that my only other problem was moreso my own fault, despite this game's simple, pixel-art style it can be quite punishing on those with cheap Intel Graphics Cards or GPU's with it's heavy use of particle effects. I noticed heavy frame rate drops and lag sometimes even in levels where there was rain or heavy enemy fire on-screen. (mine are intergrated with my laptop so I'm stuck with them.)
I highly recommend this game if you're looking for something to scratch that Rogue-lite Shooter Itch that you've had after growing tired of any of the other lovely games of this style. With it's fair price it's a game you can't afford to pass up. One of the few times I've ever backed a game on Kickstarter.
I hope to see more games like this and SanctuaryRPG: Black Edition that have this much replay value and fun put into them in the near future.

I had read a bunch of god-awful reviews about this game before finally finding the courage to dish a few Euros out for it. Perhaps the fact that I was expecting an unplayable mess let me enjoy it more than I should have. Or maybe my tolerance for crap has increased manifold since I last had it checked. Either way, The Fall felt like a stripped down, flatter version of Human Revolution - and having said that, it didn't feel unplayable at all.
What the rest of the review talks about:
+ visually faithful to the previous games
+ good potential for exploration
+ a short story in the Deus Ex universe
+/- easier and (more) relaxing to play as sleuth
+/- few familiar characters
- poor UI adaptation and game mechanics
- some obvious glitches
- no real boss fights
Admitting that I am a huge fan of Deus Ex, I enjoyed doing all the stuff I did in the main game: hacking, sleuthing, taking down anything that moves on the map in the most Ghandi-esque manner possible. The main quest is supported by five side-quests, the map is structured in three large areas with several buildings accessible in each and the environments are all very familiar if you've played Human Revolution. It is absolutely a retread of the original and took me about six hours to complete, while eliminating all AI enemies.
So I can understand why someone who doesn't have the patience to go through this level of time-wrapping and wishes for something new and original in the Deus Ex universe will be disappointed. Although conceived like the Missing Link, this port is inferior in its execution and obvious bugs arise that smack of superficiality from the developers. Most if not all the ones I encountered were just glitches though and did not pose any software farts. Storywise, only a few familiar characters appear with minimal roles and there are no real boss fights to talk about. What compounds the bad word of mouth for any new player will be the irritating tutorial which introduces you to the world and the slightly altered game mechanics and controls, which are simplified compared to the original. Oh, and the messy interface too.
But these seemed mostly trivial obstacles to me, none of which were deal-breakers. The game, while quick and dirty in a sense, allowed me to roam across the map and do things at my own pace, with few restrictions controlling story elements. I feel I paid a fair (discounted) price for a minor entry in the Deus Ex universe and was able to enjoy the hours spent playing it. So I would go out on a limb and recommend it to fans of the series who have a sense of lenience and patience about themselves.

Heavily inspired by The picture of Dorian Grey authored by Oscar Wilde.
As the description says, you take the role of an artist who is travelling through his house on a mission to finish his masterpiece, as you progress through the game, its begins to become darker & much more twisted, revealing bits and pieces of the storyline to you over time.
Pros
- Extremely immersive in terms of visual & audial prowess, the creators of this game dedicated alot of time towards ensuring it caem out looking & sounding gorgeous, not only that, but the amount of detail that has been put into the artwork and architecture really portrays some amazing talent within the fields.
- Immaculateley timed. The creators of this game have tried and tested every scare tactic. Theres is a perfect mix between jump scares & drawn out horror. Play this game at night alone and you will s**t yourself.
- Extremely well done storyline. The game offers you insights towards what has occured yet it manages to hold off the suspense by adding twists that you would never expect, ensuring that you will not be able to fully guess the plot until the very end of the game.
Cons
- There are a few graphical bugs, though not that many. Antialiasing is a problem at the moment as you will tend to notice most objects surrounding your character are jagged at the edges.
Altogether this game is a must have, the concept is fantastically original. It is definetley worth the 13 USD if you are a fan of survival horror, for it is a game that you shall never forget.

In December, I purchased Niche after watching several youtubers play it themselves, and I can say that I have yet to regret doing so. Niche, a Genetics Survival Game is wholy unique in its gameplay, with new features added every month. In no way, shape, or form are you meant to grow bored with the absolute variety of genetics to pick over and mutate: Genes for underwater survival, genes for the cold, snowy climates, genes meant for stealth and warding off predator, genes meant for the fastest of creatures, and genes you avoid at all costs yet still manage to keep them in your pack anyway. This game can be hours of fun and sometimes it can be minutes of frustration, but this is all due to the game's random generation and luck aspect. When you have a child, you have no idea which genes they will inherit from their parents, and there is only so much you can put in the mutation menu before you just have to cross your fingers and pray.
It is very easy to grow attached to a certain creature in your group, even when they may not have the best genetics. When food is short you struggle on who to keep and who to banish, who collects food in the face of a carnivore attack and who risks their lives. It's not very simple to make a perfect tribe, and more than once I have been forced to sacrifice a baby to a bird or move a dying elder into the waiting jaws of a carnivore, just because they were sick and I lacked strong creatures who could protect them. Several times I have grown teary eyed when my favorite creature dies or I am forced to leave behind reliable creatures because they aren't prime genetic material.
Overall, this game is made to challenge you with its multiple avenues of genetic exploration and completely random world generation and infuriating obstacles. Some may view it as a casual time waster, and some may view it as a chance to weave a story. I will be honest when I have viewed it as one or the other on several different occasions. The fact of the matter is that, if you let it, this game will worm its way into your heart, make a nest, and have a ton of nichelings.
As a player, I have invested over 60 hours into this game, and every time there is a new update I willingly make myself comfortable and invest another good chunk of time in a single sitting. Whenever I am bored, I can easily open up this game and either start where I left off or begin a completely new save.  Thank you guys for making a game I can casually enjoy yet invest myself so deeply that I cannot untangle myself from the web of genetics. I cannot wait for the final version!

I have logged over 300 hours into this F2P MMO, but I cannot say it is a particularly good game.
It features the same old hotkey-based ground combat that pretends to be a third-person shooter; do not let this fool you. Aiming is not required, and ground combat can be accomplished more efficiently through traditional target/hotkey combat.
Space combat is much better; the target/hotkey system feels more appropriate for this type of combat, which leaves you in a vast, open area. Distance is often your last defense, as line-of-sight mechanics are few and far between.
My problem with this game lies in the questing and content. Quests, or 'episodes', are quite long and can sometimes be enjoyable, but once you hit max level, which you will before you finish half of all the episodes, there is hardly any reason to complete them.
Not to mention, there are player-created episodes that, on average, are MUCH better than the ones provided by the developers. Unfortunately, the rewards for player created levels was greatly diminished. STO feels like a grind, even at max-level; repeating the same matchmaking instances over and over gets tedious... fast.
Also, the game does not feel properly balanced for PvP whatsoever; at the least, a better matchmaking system is required. Overall, the game is carried by its license. As far as F2P MMO's go, it has a very fair monetization system, although I will say that buying ships can get very pricey and there are plenty of bundles for over $100 USD. Not to mention, there is the lifetime subscription for 200~ dollars or so. I very highly suggest against this, and spending money in the game in general. At max level, costume sets can be earned, and being in a Fleet can earn you ships. Buying ships is not necessary, but still available at decent prices.
If you enjoy Star Trek enough to buff-out the great huge flaws of this game then I would suggest it. Otherwise, there are better F2P options out there, such as Tera Online and PlanetSide2. It is definitely carried by its license but any Star Trek fan would enjoy this for at least a few weeks. Again not a terrible game by any means, but it is very much carried by its license. The developers update the game quite frequently. You can expect two big patches a year, I'd estimate.
It's worth it to spend some money in-game (which I did not do), but if you decide not to, it's still a fun game. I'd reccomend playing as a Ferengi, since there's no legitimate reason not to.
It's a lot of fun if you like Star Trek. If you are not a fan of Star Trek you will not like it.

The developer of this game approached me via email to ask if I, a "content creator", would be interested in it. I figured, eh, it doesn't look awful, maybe it'll be a decent half hour of whatever. I admit my eye isn't especially well trained to spot Unity Asset Store flips, but this game does make it pretty insanely obvious - most of the stuff in this game comes from within the first page of search results for very basic terms, and there are really, really clear signs (like screens that outright say "OFFICE PACK" on them) that this isn't really the creator's own work.
Even beyond the asset flips, I wasn't thrilled with how guns work, the economy isn't very well balanced, grenades are too dangerous to use in 90% of situations, it's too easy to get stuck on things, and there's only really two kinds of zombies (walking and crawling). It comes off as a frankly amateurish rip-off of Killing Floor 2 - I'm pretty sure the shop interface is meant to be a complete mirror of KF2's, in fact.
On the technical end of things, I found that the game would slow down a lot for no reason (an underperforming machine will actually bog down the game speed, not just the frame rate), the ACTUAL slow-motion effect takes entirely too long (fortunately you can force it to end by reloading), there's a Melee Attack key but it only works on a small handful of the guns, controls cannot be rebound, menus indicate support for gamepads but my gamepad was doing absolutely nothing...there are things in place here that make me wonder if the devs did anything more than rudimentary testing on it.
I haven't paid for it, but in my opinion, neither should anybody else. If what you're after is a by-the-numbers zombie shootin' game, there's so many better ones out there for your $15.

Sometimes, when I'm on Steam, I'm not really even sure what the Hell I'm looking for. I know what I like in games, and I just sort of flit around trying to find something that appeals to me. Well, Mount & Blade: Warband has just about everything that appeals to me in a game; strategy, combat, customization, as well as some RPG elements.
To me, MnB is the child of an RTS and an open-world RPG. While the RPG elements and story are not at the forefront of the game, it doesn't matter in the least. It has an empire-building feel along with fantastic battles. The combat, while at first felt clunky, now feels pretty damn good. Check out my list of bullet points below:
(TL;DR - This game is a fantastic mix of strategy and actual combat. There are endless optioins when it comes to customization of your army's units. Do yourself a favor and buy this right now.)
Combat
-Pros-

-If  you like to get into the thick of combat you have your choice of melee weapons both 1handed and 2 handed; swords, axes, polearms, and the like.
-There are also some ranged choices if you prefer to slay your foes from afar; bows, crossbows, throwing axes and javelins.
-The combat engine is pretty great, once you get used to it. You can block and attack directionally, from both sides, above-head swings and thrusts with a myriad of weapons. These attacks come in very handy depending on the weapon, as all melee weapons have a 'reach' statistic, which allows you to plan battles accordingly.
-You can gear yourself up to be a heavily armored mounted knight, with a lance, sword and shield or rather you can be a quick and nimble ranger, bombarding your foes with a rain of arrows.
-Cons-
-There is a slight learning curve to the combat, however, the developers have AUTOMATIC settings on directional blocking which can help a rookie immensly. Also, there are difficutly sliders for the AI, both in combat and in the world that can help you get started.
-Occassionally you can get stuck, typically while defending a castle where the AI on both sides just sort of slams into each other in some sort of chaotic slug fest, which can, at times, leave you on the edge of a battle, looking for a way to satiate your bloodlust.
Unit Customization
-Pros-
-You can level and outfit your character however you want. You can go full blown combat and become a Master at Arms, or you can dedicate yourself to more financial pursuits and focus on leadership and trade skills. It's completely up to you.
-Units in the game can come from a few different nations, each nation has perks that are beneficial to each unit type. A quick example is that the Nord Huscarl (an upgraded Nord footman) is by far one of the best melee infantry units in the game. Meanwhile, the Swadians have the best cavalry with the Swadian Knight. So train your troops accordingly to maximize their potential.
-Heroes can be acquired to your party throughout various towns and cities on the world map. How you outfit them, and level them, is up to you.
-Cons-
-Sometimes outfitting a hero NPC can be cumbersome, forcing you to switch between various menus to make sure that you're equipping them properly. Not a huge hinderance though.
Strategy / Empire Building
-Pros-
-There are so many ways to strengthen your standing in this world it's unreal. You can align yourself with the various nations or strike it out solo and conquer the whole damn map.
-Actual battles can play out VERY differently based on your individual playstyle. You can organize a healthy mix of units, cavalry, infanty and archers and strategically attack your foes, or just charge right in, completely up to you.
-All of the major cities and castle in the game can be captured by laying seige to them. You can align yourself with a nation and join their war parties to do this, or raise an army of your own and claim everything the sun reaches. Just be sure to train your units accordingly before attempting a seige.
Overall
-Pros-
-Great combat.
-Excellent customization
-Wonderful use of strategy in and out of battle.
-Endless replayability. Seriously. You could play this game 100 times and have a different experience each time.
-Cons-
-Slight learning curve, not too bad.
-Dialogue is pretty ridiculous sometimes.
Long story short, it's an excellent game.

I recommended this game when I was 1.5h into it, and that did not change after beating all the levels, working to improve my times in the first stage, and trying the procedural generator.
It's a good precision platformer.
---
Mad Dojo has short fast difficult levels and tight controls. It's not as tight as Super Meat Boy or iZBOT (which are masterpieces in this regard), but still feels responsive and rewarding, especially after you learned how the obstacles and death traps work and start speedrunning.
You can run, jump, double jump, and throw shurikens. You can throw shurikens while running or in mid air. Shurikens have 3 uses - they cut bamboo sticks to make them shorter (so it's easier to traverse), they block incoming shots to protect you, and they push the water dynamite barrels farther from you so you're less likely to be hit by the explosion. I would like to be able to throw at a faster rate - currently, it's like you can throw 1 shuriken/second and sometimes that feels slow.
Often the ninja starts running without any input from the controller - that is a big source of cheap deaths, given we are always surrounded by death traps and there is little time to react when it happens. The same can also occur while in mid air. The issue is much less noticeable during speedruns, such that in the last 3h it happened just a few of times. This would be my #1 priority to fix.
I find it too difficult to consistently grab&hold the top of the bamboo sticks/platforms. It could be that I didn't learn to trick or didn't get the timing right yet, but this mechanic may need some tweaking as well.
---
Mad Dojo has 2 game modes, the main stages and procedurally generated levels.
The main stages: there are currently 2 worlds, with 15 levels each. The first levels in each stage are rather easy, then they progressively add new (or more difficult variants of) obstacles and death traps. Some of the levels are similar to each other and can feel a bit repetitive the first time around, thus new stages would/will be welcome, but while speedrunning you will have to think about the fastest route and change the strategy based on the placement of the traps and platforms. I'm bad at speedrunning, but managed to finish most levels in the first stage in 15s or less, a couple in under 20s, and a couple below 30s. I didn't try speedrunning the levels in the second stage, but they felt larger/longer.
Procedurally generated levels: It generates simple beatable levels of varying difficulty and length - some I could complete in under 20s, some it took me 1m30s. Currently, it the procedural levels only use obstacles and death traps from the first stage. After some time, you'll be able to predict what kind of obstacle will come next and be familiar enough to know by heart how to traverse it, but predictability is inherent to procedural generators. It would be nice to be able control the size of the levels and difficulty of the course. Also, whenever we die a new level is generated, but sometimes I wish I could go through the same course until I beat it.
---
When we finish a level, the level cleared screen is shown. Here, there are only 2 options - start the next level or return to the level selection. An option to restart the current level would be welcome.
While playing a level, we can restart by opening the pause menu and choosing the corresponding option. That's very fast to do (less than 1s), but I'd like to be able to bind restart to a key/button so I can completely avoid the menu.
---
The song fits the visuals and overall feel of the game, which is good, but after a while it got too repetitive and I turned it off. I disliked the sound effects. This is very low priority, though, as it's the gameplay that makes or breaks this type of game.

Mad Dojo is a very nice indie game : nice graphics and effects, nice music, smooth controls... Well everything you need to enjoy the game. The only part is that the game is quite short but hopefully several levels are quite challenging, especially in the first world.

You are a wannabe ninja and you are trained by your sensei with a very tough training including various obstacles and deadly traps. Each day you will train harder and harder to be the ninja you always wanted to be.

The game offers great pixel art graphics with several nice effects : a trail following your ninja, some nice sunrays and some nice backgrounds.

Sounds are nice and you will hear a distinct music in each world. And of course the music is quite nice.

It's mostly reach the end of the level without dying. Your current time is shown at the top of the screen so the aim is to get to the exit as fast as possible if you want to get in the top of the leaderboards.
The game contains 2 worlds with each 15 levels. Each world has their distinct hazards and traps.
The only annoying thing is that the first world has mostly deadly traps which is less the case of the second world. So your energy bar (health bar) will only help you during the second world.
Hopefully you are well prepared : you can double jump, wall slide and even use kunai/shuriken to help you to reach the exit. The game will also show you your last deaths on the level.
Even if you beat the game you can still enjoy it and play some randomly generated levels which can be much harder than the campaign.

Most of them are easy to obtain. Only one or two levels may be tedious to finish as well as beating a procedural level.

is a platformer in which you play a ninja who can run, jump, and throw shuriken while dodging obstacles in his way. Mad Dojo is a fun take on the hardcore platforming genre a-la Super Meat Boy.
While I wouldn't necessarily call Mad Dojo as hard as SMB, you will have your reflexes put to the test by 30 different levels, and countless combinations of separate, procedurally-generated levels. Your deaths are recorded, which helps make stalagtite-evading much easier in the cave levels, although after a few of them, you realize how obvious the placement of them is, so evading will come naturally.
The difficulty curve is like a roller coaster, I found level 15 to be more difficult than 16-30, and levels throughout 16-30 gave me different scattered challenges, with some significantly easier than others. While it had my mojo for expecting what would come next off, it didn't detract from how much I enjoyed this game.
Overall, Mad Dojo is a nice, albeit short, platformer that is a great option for anyone on the 100% completionist trail. I encountered no broken achievements, and completed this game in what I felt was a quick time (about an hour of actual gameplay) for a full completion of a good quality game.

After you start collecting loot you can break down the ones you don't like at the forge or fuse a bunch of low level stuff together for better iteams. You can also enchant or pray for better stats. These concepts will give you a reason for replayablity.

Browsing through my library, I see a lot of older multiplayer games on their last legs. Updates have long since stopped coming, the player base is dwindling, and low moddability ends up being the final death knell for the game.
PVKII is the opposite, and that's why I nominated it for the "Labor of Love" award.
Some modders seem to be driven by an otherworldly energy to create and maintain their works. They don't update often, but they update long after AAA titles from the same year of release have shut down their servers. For example, both BIoshock 2 and PVKII came out in the same year (2010). Bioshock 2's multiplayer is dead, but PVKII has a new playable character coming up.
While the player base is trickling down, I never have an issue finding people when I start up PVKII. Sure, a few of the players will have high ping, but that's no problem because they're usually pretty friendly. The fact that it's free also means anyone can play - bring some friends along and learn together!

Developed by Black Shell Media, Overture is a roguelike game inspired in the oldie 8-bit AAA RPG games that demands a lot of skill of the player due to its intense difficulty but rewarded with lots of action mainly killing crowded hordes of zombies, skeletons, fire summoners, dragons, big minibosses, as well to collect everything that will help you in your intense journey, added with the auto generated dungeon system that allows the stage exploration in order to get gear improvements and hard boss battles that guarantees that gaming sessions won’t be repetitive.

Overture offers to the player an 8-bit console look like game, with amazing soundtrack that matches perfectly to the game. Controls are based in WASD configuration to move your character and the mouse helps you to aim – represented with a sword – in order to aim where the shoot goes. When you put the cursor in the same way your character walks, your character goes really fast. Also, stop shooting will help to walk a little faster. Combine them to rush: It is a key to survive when you are surrounded and you need to escape as soon as possible. As some roguelike games, you have only one life to face all the hordes of enemies that will be pursuing you until they see you dead. With 24 characters divided into four classes – 4 by default and 20 unlockable via game money - the game counts with variety in terms of character skills and firepower.
Also, the game counts with a simple RPG system where you level up, you can pick up items with specific properties that help you to find more HP, MP, EXP and other special attacks that are not present by default. It you see that the game is so hard, you can upgrade your characters via game money to increase firepower stats to rise the opportunities to continue alive and kill faster the hordes.
Like other games of the same genre, it has a menu – press C key - to see the properties of your character, equipment with their description and a save feature that disappears once you die. So save when necessary.
Although the game has only 10 stages with their bosses, it has a high replay value due to its randomly generated dungeons – even bosses are not the same, except the final one -. You will feel that exploring blindspots and chests you need to find throughout all the stage will reward you with interesting items that will help a lot.
However, be very, very aware. Overture is not a walk in the park. The game is really hard and will slap you in the face when you don’t expect it. The death sequence is really bloody and will help you to figure out how many foes you left before dying. Shooting to the horde and escape from them is not an easy task, but expect to step unintentionally to traps set in all the stage that will release more hordes. Add also the minibosses that will attack you at long distances. Once you beat all of them, you will be satisfied, but expect a hellish challenge in stage 2 and so on. The rewards at the end of the stage are really, really helpful and motivates you to endure in the game.
Pro tip: If you are annoyed of the visual garbage that all kills generate in the stage, press alt + enter to change to window mode. If you want again fullscreen, press them. That will clean everything and will help you to see better the stage.

•	The game generates the scenarios allowing replay value.
•	Amazing 8-bit soundtrack.
•	20 characters to unlock via game money and explore their specific skills in the battlefield.
•	Fast paced gameplay.
•	Responsive controls and intuitive menu.
•	Possibility to upgrade characters via game money.
•	Save feature in middle game.
•	RPG-Like system.
•	Loots and items, LOTS OF THEM.

•	Incredible high difficulty for novice players.
•	Hordes are a big challenge to kill and they attack you from all angles.
•	When you die, the save disappears.
•	Visual garbage – in tons – when you kill a horde or stage items.

Overture is a really enjoyable and entertaining game, even if it is too difficult at the beginning. Black Shell Media has done an incredible work using 8-bit-like graphics and music to surround the player in an immersive rush-to-kill game. This game is a big reference of some NES games, and reminds us that simple graphics and outdated music don’t mean that the game would be easy. Overture will punish you intensely: will kick your butt, will punch your nose and will make you bleed profusely when you’re with your guard down, with no breaks and no pauses. Indeed, you will feel that you can finish the game and you will try it again, and again, and again.
