When playing this one must acknowledge the fact that this is a mobile port. Of course the graphics, level design, AI, crowd dynamics, mission variety, combat mechanics, etc. are all subpar compared to Human Evolution, but if you are a fan of the Deus Ex lore and storytelling, The Fall should provide some, albeit short, entertainment. Hell if this game is named The Fall Episode 1 then people will realize why it's so short. It's essentially just one level of a large game.
I personally would like to see how the story goes. This has the potential to become an interesting sidestory in the Deus Ex universe.

Despite it's flaws I found it a good game and recommend it if you understand going in that it's not a complete game and may never be(I would have been quite angry if I had bought it at it's asking price but it's an excellent game at the two dollar mark).
The game seems to be the first third of the game as it takes place entirely in one location(aside from a training mission).  I expected two more Panama length segments of the game(as I did not know it was episodic).
The level design is good(albeit limited) as is the story(thus far - the surprise to be continued ending sucked).
The graphics are by no means awesome but also not akin to 90s graphics as some people have been saying.  While the models are low polygon(by todays standards) the textures are far superior to those of the 90s.  There are occasional rendering glitches which last less than a second which mostly happen when you're performing takedowns.
The animations are limited.  There seems to be only one animation available for special moves(such as takedowns) which becomes repetitive quickly(they also don't take place where you initiate them but move them into a larger nearby area, then move you back to where you were).  The speech animations seem to be the only thing that could have been ported from the original Deus Ex.
The voice acting is ok aside from the tutorial lady.
There is no physics that I noticed at all aside from gravity.  There are no movable items so you can't even stack crates nostalgically.  That brings me to my next point: you can't jump.  I missed jumping greatly as it could have allowed more complex level design.
Overall the controls are mostly usable but suffer from their tablet roots.  The dialogue controls are bad.  The interface controls fail to register the first click frequently.  There also seems to be a dead zone where you can't activate items in the world(I can hack something 3 feet away, 1 foot away, but not 2 feet away for some reason).
There is only one save slot(both manual and quick saves use the same file which is overwritten on every map change (which is often).
Vaulting over barriers was hit or miss(mostly miss) as it seems you need to be in just the right spot for it to work.
The hacking mini game was the same as in DX:HR(which I quite enjoyed) although it seemed to suffer from interface issues.

If you go in knowing that it's a port of an iOS game, it's really not that bad.
Pros:
- You can now buy any item at any point in the game
- It's pretty short (just over 4 hours)
- It's relatively cheap (but buy it on sale anyway)
- Hacking has stayed the same
- New Game+ if you want to max out your augs
- The entire game takes place in only one city, so you can clear out buildings early in the game and just waltz through them later when you actually need to get somewhere
- Traditional lethal/non-lethal options are kept
Not Quite Pros But Not Quite Cons:
- No more body hiding required, as bodies disappear after a few seconds. Good for being stealthy, bad for knowing if you killed somebody or knocked them out.
- No stealth-based achievement. You can still get Smooth Operator after missions, but there's no equivalent of The Foxiest of the Hounds
- No boss battles
- No mention of the Illuminati
- Significantly fewer takedown animations
Cons:
- The map is too small. Instead of the outside of Panama City being one giant map, it was divided into four or five smaller maps, so travelling places meant you were looking at at least two loading screens between the time you left and the time you got there.
- It's a port of a mobile game. The graphics and interfaces reflect this. You get used to it, but it was still lazy.
- You can't sell items, and now I have 20 mines and a hundred beers that I can't use.
- My pistol is apparently stronger than my assault rifle.
- The cover mechanic is wonky. The game couldn't decide if you just need to click the right mouse button or actually hold it to get into cover, and when you moved the mouse to look behind you, you would move out of cover.
When it comes to bugs and glitches, I'm either incredibly lucky or they were all fixed, because I played through twice and I never encountered any.
In summary, 3/5, not deserving of all the hate it gets, but doesn't live up to Human Revolution. If it wasn't a Deus Ex game, I think more people would have liked it.

You can have a lot of fun playing this game.  You select your own crew and get better ships and upgrades to your ships.  Outer space is open world and you can go to any planet at any time.  Not all planets are exploreable.  Many planets have missions.  All the usually MMO stuff PvP,PvE, and etc.  The game has a basic crafting system that allows you to upgrade a standard device (weapon,armor, or etc) from common to uncommon to rare and finally very rare.  Upgrades are pretty linear for example each new level engine is +5 on the speed.  You start with 50 engine speed and you can get as high as 115-120 in increments of 5 per level.  You can create or join a fleet so you can eventually get ultra rare mark 12 gear.  It is better to join an existing fleet as upgrading your starbase, mine, and etc take a long time unless you have dozens in your fleet.
There are a number of good missions that are really fun.  If you have a good video card you can set the graphics high enough to look really good.  Just like any other MMO there are missions you have to repeat over and over to build up your relationship with other species and gain access to special gear and other stuff unique to their species.  I have played over 1200 hours but now I just check in once a week for new content.  While you are off on main mission you send your duty officers off on missions by themselves to level each skill including science,trade,engineering and etc.  Make sure you start stock piling dilthium early as you will need a lot of it and buying cost really money.

I bought the game very much blind on a whim after getting a big card game fix from Yugioh and wanting more. I saw Neptune from Hyperdimension NepNep and saw a card game and clicked "add to cart". When I started playing it the first thing I noticed was the speed it threw achievements at me, within 10-15 minutes I had around 25% of the games achievements, these quickly dried up.
Let me be very clear from the get go, this has a LOT of fan service, including
a mode in which you power up your girls by rubbing their lady garden, honking their hooters and pinching at their bottoms. It's all very surreal and comes out of absolutely no where. I wish I'd researched it more before I bought it as it is totally not my kind of thing, but each to their own I guess!
The actual gameplay other than that is solid, 3 lanes to put your cards into which are only battle cards. These cards move forward one space at the end of their turn and attack. There's some cards which can do magic to stop this happening, there are some cards that don't move, some can move opponents backwards. There's a lot of strategy to the movement to be fair. Then there is 3 different kinds of card, attack, buff and healer. These have "types" kind of like Pokemon, if you put two types together you can fusion them like Yugioh. It's all actually very entertaining and strategic stuff!
The voice acting is good, the music is not distracting and the in game menu sounds are also good(not annoying).
The graphics are stellar to be fair, your waifu's will look hawt, your cat eared girls will look like lady cats. The cards actually looks pretty good too. The nudity is there without being full frontal.
Overall, I wish there was less fanservice as they actually have made a very enjoyable game, I wish the story was less stereotypical anime story of nonsense but with girls. The plot seems to revolve around girls being touched, talking about touching, being ashamed of boobs and fighting each other. I'd recommend it for the gameplay, I'd say its your GOTY if you like card games, plants Vs zombies, lane attack games and most importantly if you like anime grills.

is a simple retro platformer where you roll around trying to get to the end goal while collecting stars. If you think that sounds an awful lot like Sonic the Hedgehog you’d be right. This game is clearly inspired by old school Sonic games, from the level designs and graphics to the way bosses are destroyed. This a fun game in its own right and also pretty darn cute as well. There is however no story to be told.
You roll around, that’s about it. While you roll you have to collect stars and avoid dangerous death spikes, lasers and the like. There are also enemies along the way but you can easily jump on their heads and dispatch of them, the thing I had the biggest issue is was jumping onto small platforms and making sure I didn’t roll off since it is a ball and balls tend to roll. Your ball does not have any special powers or abilities which is a shame. A little something to spice things up every now and again would be fun. My favorite part of the gameplay was the puzzle aspect thrown in. Door in the way? You have to hit the switch or put something on top of it to get through.
I used a game controller to play the game and the responses were good. The only issue I had was that I could not find a button on my controller that would pause the game, I still had to use my keyboard for that. The retro feel of the game is really compliment by being able to use the controller. I also just figured out after over two hours of play that you can change the color of the ball so I made mine pink.
For me the graphics reminded me too much of Sonic the Hedgehog, like the first level looks strikingly similar to Green Hill Zone. However, the graphics aren’t so much of a direct copy and more of homage, that being said I do think the graphics could have been polished a bit more. The graphics are more akin to a Playstation One game than what I would expect in 2016. While graphics aren’t everything and this game is fun either way, they could have invested a little more into it. The audio is fine, though, the levels have catchy tunes and I had no issue there at all.
+ The game is very cheap.
+ Offers a good amount of gameplay for the price, game has six levels with three areas each plus a boss battle each time.
+ Overall presentation looks good.
+ It has trading cards.
- Only one play mode, no time trials or hidden areas that I could find.
- While the graphics weren’t bad they could have been better, the menu interfaces were also simplistic.
I do recommend this game to players who enjoy platformers, the game has a nice price tag and is well made. It’s fun, colorful and has great controls. This game also has achievements which are relatively easy to collect which is another draw. Buy it, play it and enjoy it you won’t regret it.

As games go, Deus Ex: The Fall isn't the worst. But it definitelly has problems.

However, if you're going to get this game, please play at least one other Deus Ex game before playing The Fall.

Deus Ex: The Fall; let me first point out that I went into The Fall expecting it to be the absolutely worst game I have played, this was due to the media completely disregarding it straight away. I also want to point out that this is the first Deus Ex game I have played.
So lets get into it;
The gameplay in The Fall is your pretty standard first person shooter/stealthy type game. Sadly though they are not done brilliantly. The gun play is bad to say the least, you can shoot a guy in the head at point blank range with a shot gun five or six times and he still won't die, you can also be crouching right in front of an enemy and he won't notice you, like literally, you can be under his nose and he won't bat an eye lid.
The graphics are OK, that's all. It is in no way a pretty looking game, it looks as if it is straight off the PlayStation 1 (no disrespect to the games on that platform, it just looks very dated). It tries to make it self look better than it is by using plenty of lens flare though.
The voice acting is really bad, the main character, Ben Saxton, is British, and boy do they put that point across, it is the most generic British accent you will ever hear and at points made me cringe; games that have been out for ten years or so have better voice acting in than The Fall...
Level design is a very narrow sighted open world type setting, you can roam around the city, exploring, having meaningless conversations with civilians, and finding items. You will also run into a couple of side quests, five or six to be exact. Granted that's nothing really to brag about when you compare it to other games which have side quests, but this is certainly not a completely linear game and leaves room for the player to choose what to do and when.
With the gameplay elements not being exactly up to scratch, this can fluctuate the difficulty levels at time. I didn't feel as if it was a good enough stealth system for me to use the stealth approach, so I just went with the all guns-blazing tactic. I hardly ran into any difficult parts throughout my play-through. The most difficult aspect I encountered was the hacking system on doors and computers. You can either find out the password/pass-code by exploring the world for clues, or hack the system. The hacking system at times was infuriating and I had to resort to looking up codes on the wiki, or looking up the location of the clue.
I finished Deus Ex: The Fall in just about four and a half hours, this was including doing the majority of the side quests and doing a fair amount of exploring for extra items and codes. If you want a Pound (£) to hour ratio, it's not bad on that front, the game does end on a cliff-hanger and I would of liked to have seen just a little bit more of what happens, looking at the chronology of Dues Ex, this is one of the first games in the story, and Human Revolution will reveal all I suppose.
There is a mire of technical issues with this game too; firstly the controls, you are not able to rebind any of the keys - this to me is an absolute must in ANY PC game. If I have a whole keyboard in front of me, let me use it damn it! Also, when navigating through the menus, your mouse clicks are sometimes not registered until you click four or five times, this made purchasing extra painkillers (the game's version of a health pack) and ammo become something of a chore. This problem also makes it into the actual game play too, as you can be standing behind an enemy, hit your stealthy take down key, but have to press it a number of times before the game recognizes it.  These little things made me annoyed, and they could of been fixed very easily if it was QA'ed properly.
The final verdict, do I recommend Deus Ex: The Fall? This is when I wish Steam would have a "maybe" option available; because I had to admit, I did have some fun while playing, I finished the game after all so it wasn't so bad I couldn't bring my self from seeing the ending. But it is a bad game, it doesn't do much right, the poor voice acting, the buggy interface and broken game play elements would of grown tiresome if the game's length was any longer than it already is. So as I have to give a straight yes or no answer, I will sadly have to go with a "Do Not Recommend" for Dues Ex: The Fall. Fans of the Deus Ex series will probably want to play it purely for the lore and story aspect, but nothing more.

This game, unlike most horror games I've played recently, does not realy on jump scares alone. The terror stems from the events and happenings of a man and his family who are experiencing situations that can happen in life, which makes it feel VERY real and unsettling. The psychology behind the events and the impact it has on our painter and his wife and child (children?) has conjured up a very dark and unseen evil... The unseen, for me, is quite possibly the most scary part about this game.
I am excited to experience the rest of the game. I would highly recommend this game to any horror enthusiast and anyone who appreciates art and story telling. This is a MUST HAVE! It's one thing to watch someone play this game, but to experience it yourself... is ALWAYS the better experience.

"Ace of Spades" is a song by English rock band Motörhead, released in 1980 as a single and the title track to the album Ace of Spades. The song spent 12 weeks in the United Kingdom Singles Chart, peaking at No. 15.Initially issued as a 7" vinyl single on 27 October 1980 as a preview to the album Ace of Spades and autumn tour, Bronze Records also released a 12" vinyl pressing in special Christmas picture sleeves, limited to 50,000 copies. The picture of the band in Santa outfits used on the cover was taken at the Aylesbury Fair, while the band were on tour.Bronze also issued German and Spanish 7" vinyl versions which had a different sleeves, as well as a Japanese release, with a colour picture insert with song lyrics in English and Japanese. One sided test pressings (not mis-presses, but used in the trade) escaped the pressing plant and are on the market.The song opens with an overdriven bass solo played by Lemmy. For the lyrics, he said he "used gambling metaphors, mostly cards and dice – when it comes to that sort of thing, I'm more into the one-arm bandits actually, but you can't really sing about spinning fruit, and the wheels coming down".On 6 September 1980 Lemmy was interviewed by Graham Neale on BBC Radio 1's Rock On Saturday show, "Bomber", "Ace of Spades" and "Love Me Like a Reptile" were played. The following month, on 6 and 20 October, the band played the song on BBC TV show Top of the Pops.In the studio version, the last lines of the bridge are "I don't want to live forever/And don't forget the Joker". In the live versions and the Rock Band 2 remake, the last lines are "I don't want to live forever/But, apparently I am""Ace of Spades (live)" is a 1988 7-inch vinyl release of the song by Motörhead. The single has no picture sleeve; it was issued (and withdrawn) in a plain white paper cover. All three songs on the single appeared on the band's No Sleep at All live album, which was recorded at the Giants of Rock Festival in Hämeenlinna, Finland on 2 July 1988.The band had wanted "Traitor" as the A-side, but "Ace of Spades" was chosen instead, when the band noticed the change, they refused to allow the single to be distributed to the shops. So despite the popularity the song had achieved, this single was not as successful as the original version, which reached No. 15 in the UK Singles Chart in 1980, as it became only available at gigs and through the Motörheadbangers fan club.The song became a staple of the band's live set, with Lemmy acknowledging that despite becoming "sick" of performing it, they "can't ditch Ace of Spades, it wouldn't be right. If I go to see Little Richard, I expect to hear Good Golly Miss Molly, or I'd be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off".[9] Live versions have appeared on the albums No Sleep 'til Hammersmith (1981), Nö Sleep at All (1988), Everything Louder than Everyone Else (1999), Live at Brixton Academy (2003) and Better Motörhead than Dead: Live at Hammersmith (2007).It was the first song that Phil Campbell and Würzel played with the band – on the Bambi episode of The Young Ones. The lineup is particularly rare until 1987: Lemmy, Campbell, Würzel and Taylor. Taylor had already left the band by the time the filming started, but kept to his promise of making the performance.In September 1993, WGAF Records re-released the original 1980s track on CD-single, cassette single, 12" vinyl picture sleeve and picture disc versions, the song was coupled with "Louie Louie", "Dirty Love", and "Ace of Spades (The CCN Remix)", and although the band were not too pleased with the CCN Remix version, this single peaked at No. 23 in the UK charts. First cards can have skills and for use those skills you need mana, and as you know summon cards need mana too.. so you have to do a little of math for win. Games makes reward for summon 3 cards of same color, actually bonus are so great that i suggest make 2 color decks.. example (red, blue), or yellow blue deck (the one i use for main card+nepunia) the bonus are like this.. second summon of same color is +1 on mana, and 3 time is +3 mana, 1tk,1hp for all cards.

If there were a "meh" review this would be the time to use it. Let me break it down:
*Play this game if...*
If you’re looking for fanservice you’ve come to the right place. This game is ripe with anime girls in provocative positions. As you progress you get to "interact" with your team via minigame, with a reward of an article of clothing removed. The girls never get completely nude but nothing is left to the imagination believe me.  As for main gameplay, it’s a fairly simple game. The later levels can be a challenge but generally anyone with any strategy game experience should breeze through this one.
*Don’t play this game if...*
If you want an engaging story with vivid characters then definitely steer clear. This game wasn’t designed to… well... be a game. Its fanservice that you can interact with. The “world” is akin to the Mario World dots and lines over map with no deviation for exploration. The gameplay is basic, and while I did loose from time to time I would not consider it challenging. For anyone whose played card games like Magic or Yu-Gi-Oh then the pain of never getting a decent card in your hand might bring about some flashbacks. Also as many of the other reviews have stated, there is no multiplayer so unless you like playing with yourself…. Oh sorry… BY yourself, then probably not a game you would enjoy.
*Bottom line…*
I had fun while playing, which is what I want when I play a game, so that’s why it gets the recommend. The cards artwork is pretty and you can tell the artists generally gave each character their all. The music gets a little repetitive but that’s nothing sliding some volume controls down and running something in the background won’t fix. I didn’t consider this a complete waste of time and would like to see something similar again in the future, though with considerably more effort on the part of the devs. I’m a longtime fan of the Hyperdimension series so that was a huge motivator in my purchasing. This game is for a niche audience so if you aren’t into anime girls it’s probably not for you.
As a side note, a lot of people are complaining about microtransactions. While the game definitely makes you want to purchase some strong cards and rub points just to progress faster, it’s absolutely not necessary. Some old-fashioned grinding and you’ll get there eventually.

I loved original Rayman on PlayStation. It had magnificent levels, absolutely awesome soundtrack and overally it gave to its player really good feeling despite having sometimes really challenging difficulty. In conclusion, it was a great success.
Reason, why I brought Rayman to here is how On A Roll 3D's beautiful retro-style gameplay reminds me of it a lot.
- It has tiny puzzles every here and there, where you have to think most usually from one vision to few seconds to how to accomplish it, whilst not being just runthrough over the maps.
- Levels are looking pretty with their effects (snowfall on mountains etc.) and the atmosphere while completing area stays entertaining from the start to the ending.
- Map designs have been made remembering both player-types: common casual players and speedrunners.
- Achievements are easily obtainable (pretty quick 100% for achievement hunters!).
Every level has its own soundtrack, which are decent and for every enemy type there is own sound effect, which are well chosen (or made).
Only downside which I've seen is that game has constant frame drops (60fps -> 51/55) but
It seems that this behaviour happens only, if your desktop frequency is set over 60hz and you're using windowed mode, since game is locked on 60fps.
Tl;Dr: If you liked good, old games like Sonic's and Rayman's, you most probably like this too. 3,99€/$ is a worthy price for such pleasure from this game.

After putting roughly 10 hours into this early access game I feel like it deserves a good review. I've been playing the game basically since it got greenlit on Steam and I've never regretted supporting these wonderful developers! The gameplay is fun, simple but also has a certain depth to it. It is strategic, but at the same time very open. The game allows you to play around with genetics and you get to decide what you're trying to achieve. The ultimate goal of the game is to survive though, which can be difficult at times, but never frustratingly so. As of every update, I feel like the game is becoming more balanced. The graphics in this game are simple, unique and cute. The creatures change in appearance as the player breeds them with each other and this is one of the things that are very fun to play around with! You never know quite what to expect, which is fun! You also get to explore and as you unveil tiles, you find resorces that will help you survive. This part can be fun when you find new things, but a lot of times you sadly don't find very much. The drawbacks this games has is that it can become repetitive and too easy if you play it for a long time. When the goal of surviving is reached there's not really anything else to strive for. I think this can and will be changed in future updates though, as the game is still in early access. Overall I'd like to recommend this game!

Any Star Trek fan will appreciate the depth and respect to the franchise in this game. Getting to take command of one's own vessel and lead an away team on a variety of missions is a uniquely rewarding experience that will keep you coming back for more.
Deep plot in all of the eight seasons to date mean that one never feels like it is a standard MMO, with a lack of grinding and 'collect this and kill that and come back' quest loops.
I have never gotten to end-game content in any other MMO as I always see through the shiny exterior to the simple 'we want your money' message underneath. Although this does have a 'freemium' quality with the C-Store for special ships, uniforms and the like, it is possible to play without spending a penny. The only purchases I made were for aesthetic purposes and I managed to get to Admiral level in hardly any time.
The major downside, whilst I refer to levelling, is that it only goes to 50 so far. I understand that there is a goal to increase this at some point, but 'some point' is hardly masively descriptive.
Overall, if you like the franchise in all iterations, even to a small degree, give it a go. Whether you live long and prosper, or decide that today is a good day to die, is entirely up to you...

As a Diehard fan of all the Star Trek Series (Yes, even Enterprise), it was not hard for this game to sway me. But i can surmise that even with little knowledge of the Star Trek Universe, the game can be compelling. The Graphics are of high quality for an MMO, though not class leading, and there are a few bugs. but these minor losses are justified when you look at the sheer scale of the game. The main storyline is interesting, compelling, and many mission can be very rewarding, offering you unique equipment. Though the campaign seems to focus on ground combat more than i would like, and ground combat is a bit tedious, the space combat system is superb. The ships are well balanced, and players are spoiled for choice when it comes to abilities. Case in point; My current ship is High damage, low defense, but i have several abilites to regenerate health and shields, allowing me to stay in the fight longer. another good point is that there are so many different types of weapons and consoles, that you can create your own playstyle, rather than have to stick to a role like in some MMOs. But one of the best points of Star Trek Online is that you dont need to spend money to enjoy it. I managed to acquire an excellent ship and gear without spendign a penny. of course,  i msut admit that i did buy one of the premium ship sets, and they are more powerful, but it is very hard to buy your way to victory in STO. One factor that i enjoyed was the PvE engagements. these are more popular than PvP, due to their rewards, and as such they wait times are much shorter. A few chinks in the armor appear though, after you reach the maximum level. it soons becoem very tedious, having to do wave after wave of PvE's to earn enough to unlock elite equipment, but it has been announced at the time of this publishing that late game play experience will be improved by a season update.
In short, I would recommend this game to someone who wants to play an MMO, but wants something slightly off the beaten path. it is fun, enjoyable, and able to be played for free.

I have to say, I went into this game with very low expectations. But it surprised me with the quality of the VO and overall tone of the game. Unlike most visual novels who give you a fairly unrealistic version of a girl, these one's cuss and talk about the kind of thing you'd expect someone to talk about. They actually sound natural instead of being some unreachable goddess that you have to become friends with before you seduce. Though the game borders on satire (unless I'm dumb and it's supposed to be) so you aren't expected to take the game seriously.
That brings me to the dating/sex scene segments. It's highly remniscent of Puzzle and Dragon, so take that for what you will. You can upgrade your stats before talking the scenes, so generally the only reason you fail would be due to not being prepared. However dates get more difficult regardless if you succeed or not, so it is a bit annoying that the only way to get money (which helps get more experience to level up your character) is to go through with dates. I recommend getting the unique items (which increase how much exp you get from dialogue permanently with a character) fairly early so you can get through to the good parts quicker.
Since the whole game is about unlocking the CG sets, there isn't too much replayability. Unless you really enjoy the puzzle segments, which even though I'm terrible at puzzle games are fairly enjoyable. At the very least, it doesn't feel like work like it does with some visual novels to unlock the scenes.
Overall, the game isn't too expensive, and if you enjoy the anime art style and are looking for a pretty funny game to pass the time I'd pick it up. Just a fair warning though, the Steam version is censored so you have to get a patch to uncensor it (though it's a really easy process).

I've put nearly thirty-five hours into the game. I've spent time on each and every character available. Despite that, I can't beat it, no matter how hard I try. It occurred to me at around 10~ hours in that this game, while hard, isn't
per se. To quote James Rolfe, "It's one of the hardest games I've ever played and for all the wrong reasons." So many reasons, in fact, I'm unsure of where to begin for a proper review. In which case, I'll simply state off everything that comes to mind right now and edit it later if anything else pops up. There's a TL;DR at the bottom.
1) Damage from...nothing?
In the time I've more or less sacrificed to this game, I've found many-but-rare instances where my character will seemingly take damage from naught. In most cases, I'm more than aware it was my own carelessness, but in a handful of these situations I've noticed that there really was nothing for me to take damage from. This is usually the case when there are many projectiles around the area. (I can only assume this is a visual bug.) That aside, some enemies will summon large, stationary balls of fire that will obviously harm you if you stand on them. The problem with that, though, is they summon slowly. FAR too slowly for you to notice. As in...you-take-damage-and-THEN-you-see-them slowly. This wouldn't be an issue if only their damage boxes would appear with them instead of before them.
2) Some enemies are faster than you.
"Why would this be an issue?" While that in and of itself isn't a big problem, it doesn't help that damage is both based on RNG and time-wasting grind (something I'll get to soon). Each character has a wide set of certain speeds, between attacking while trudging through webs/mud/water/friggin' LAVA to running the same direction as the camera orientation. Enemies do not. Enemies like the Goblins (or Orcs, whatever) and the Minotaurs move as fast as they want. Their movement pattern usually speeds up after taking damage. Sometimes they simply spawn infuriated long before seeing you. It's random, all random...intentional or otherwise, it's impossible to be cautious in this game because of that. If you just so happen to be in water and a Goblin has more health than you can chew down, you might as well just sit back and let it gnaw on your pixelated corpse. Melee enemies like that attack you by running into you. They don't have the speed penalties you do, therefore making your in-game life absolutely forfeit more times than not on later levels. Enemies like this should not be given a higher speed than the player if they don't follow the same rules as the player.
3) It's just a massive grind.
I've put 2,355 hours into Warframe, a game that was given the nicknames of Warfarm, Farmframe, and Farming Simulator...and let me just say Overture is the worst game I've played in terms of grind. There's no way to justify this. The gold in each level adds to the character's own level on that particular run. (While you can level up by also killing enemies, your main source of EXP is found in the collecting of gold.) Per character level, your health and mana pools increase with slight damage boosts on top of that. These increases are minimal unless you were to compare lvl 1 to lvl 5, or maybe even lvl 5 to lvl 10. However, despite the minute differences, there's something even more minimal than this to such an extent that it makes in-round leveling seem valid: the characters' levels outside of the rounds. See, that gold you've been collecting goes toward unlocking new characters OR boosting the damage (and just the damage) of characters already unlocked. After each level, your character's attack power is boosted by 5. "Five what?" you may ask. I don't know. It's never stated. Five points? Five in-round levels? Who the hell knows? Little to no information is provided. Whatever these +5 stages in character development are, they're more disappointing than anything I could compare to. Each level increased sends the next level's required gold multiplier through the roof, and there's hardly any difference to the damage dealt by your character. The amount required per rank far exceeds any plausible excuse that could be provided by the developer(s).
4) The loot is terrible and unbalanced.
Throughout the game, you'll find helmets, shields, rings, sword/knives, and ehm...gems that look like blobs of goop...in each stage. The weapons give a damage boost while the blobs and rings give you mana regeneration. Some of the items in these categories excluding the rings have additional enhancements on them that provide assistance. Summon skeletons on hit/kill, extra health or mana potions on hit/kill, EXP tomes on hit/kill, and things of the related sort. That, I like. I think it's a great part of the game that helped me attempt through it as far as I did. The problem is, it's all unbalanced. The loot doesn't get any little bit better each floor. If you were to get a sword that summons skellingtons on hit that deals 150 damage on the first floor but a knife of 20 damage and nothing else on floor five, you shouldn't be too confused. If you found a gem in the first floor that gives 15 mana regen and a large health potion on hit but end up getting a gem that gives 3 mana regen and not a damned thing else, don't be confused. It does that. The game just does that and there is no rhyme or reason why other than RNG. There's really no reason in continuing to the next floor unless you just want to kill more of the same kind of enemies that just have increased health pools and damage-dealing capabilities (with maybe one new enemy per floor, but that's barely worth the mention). What's worse is finding out most of the things you found in the room prior to the boss room far outweigh anything found in the "rewards" you have to buy after killing a boss. Yes, that's right. Four chests in a boss room that make you buy access to (with in-game gold, not a microtransation) a random item of random variety just to be disappointed you spent the gold in the first place. After a few times, you learn to not even bother and keep the outrageous amounts of gold you save by NOT opening the chests.
5) Boss battles
Alongside the aforementioned super-disappointing post-boss loot, the boss battles themselves are either equally disappointing or equally frustrating. Either too hard or complete pushovers. An example of the too-hard variety would be the Queen Spider. She jumps on top of you, something you can't avoid. She also has a tendency of doing this over and over and over again until you're dead...from the start of the fight to the end. Unavoidable damage despite anything and everything you do is an awful and terrible mechanic. But, I suppose that may make up for the sorry excuse of a Lava Golem whose projectiles are simple to dodge and can easily be out-meneuvered by a slower character. In addition to your randomized "prizes" at the end of each stage, you have the choice to upgrade your health or mana pools upon your victory. Both options are null and void, as there's hardly any increase in whichever pool you choose. It's a waste of a second of your time, a second you could have used to sneeze or take a breath of air. Either of those are a better use of time, but I digress. At least the boss drops 2-3 free items upon its death per boss room, I guess?
6) Lack of important and/or useful information.
There's barely any information provided in game. Any little bit given is on the pause screen, which doesn't help much at all. I don't know how much damage is increased per +5 rank on my character. I don't know how much my mana or health is increased per level or at post-boss battles. I don't know how much damage I do at all or how much that is increased/multiplied with a weapon. I simply don't know, and I shouldn't have to venture onto the forums to get a gist of anything at all.
TL;DR - Too much text for this review. Just don't buy this. Please.

The Good, the Bad, & just the plain Ugly.
Lets start off with the GOOD:
It carrys the spirit & essence of Star Trek, however; At the same time, it does go out its way to dilute Trek lore. The ships & character models are very well done, and the variety of ships are in great abundance, if you are willing to spend money that is. The game is simplistic enough so that the novice can master it, yet at the same time, it offers great rewards for those with big wallets, and lots of time in their hands. Space combat is one of the more enjoyable aspects of this game.
The BAD:
The game is plagued with bugs that interferes at times with gameplay and at the same time are just plain annoying. There are bugs that have been around since the game was released and the Devs do not take the time to address them. The ground game is very very shallow, requiring no skills whatsoever other than spamming your skill bar, & PVP is extremely unbalanced and/or non-existent. Despite the fact the game lacks true Z axis, the space combat is still its strong point. The tier classification for the ships is another draw back for the game, limiting your choices in regards to using ships for gameplay. This means you are stuck with certain types of ship models with a limited amount of customization. You're ship options does expand, but requires that you buy them from the CStore and/or exchange (This is in reference to the Lock Box Vessels).
The UGLY:
Lack of customer support, lack of End game content, constant heavy grinding, multiple in game currency, Lock Box spamming, and some mission breaking bugs. This also includes the devs total disrespect for Trek lore, disrespect for its gaming community, and the constant focus on Grind based gameplay. There are also time gated events, constant currency nerfing, the corralling of the player base, forcing them to play game content they do not desire (SEE: Delta Rising comments on the forums) - STFs or Strike Force Missions difficulty level has been vamped up to insanity, hence limiting the rewards players earn on a daily basis. Unnecessary changes to icons that need no changing, thus confusing many players. It goes to show you the strange decisions the Devs make that often times ruins the game or bugs the heck out of it.

A top down rogue-like shooter that feels and looks a bit like Realm of the Mad God. There are plenty of classes to choose from, but you do have to unlock those past the basic four. You acquire (and lose) gear and levels on a single playthrough, but you can buy "tiers" which add 5 atk per tier and you keep forever. Each character has a main attack and secondary magic attack that uses mana. Mana regenerates, health does not, but there are potions to refill both that drop amply. There's a movement mechanic that factors in your cursor position such that you move faster in the direction of your cursor. It's not an amazing feature, but it's nice. It seems there are 10 levels, but they do seem to get insanely hard. Because of those later levels, I'm more tempted to classify this as bullet hell than many other games I've played that have that label.

Vermintide is a refreshing take on the Zombie Obstacle Course. The zombies are rat-men and come in a variety of flavors from fragile horders, to well armored warriors. There are specialists as well, the giant bullet sponge, gunner, AoE-pool, pinner and draggers, many are very similar to incarnations seen in other ZOCs. As with many ZOCs  there is also equipment to be found around the course, that take the form of healing potions and kits, self-buffing potions (Damage or Speed) and Grenades
The warhammer background, brings a gothic backdrop and a variety of characters that while 2 are quite similar, each have their own particular strengths, Soldier/Dwarf can frontline shield wall while the Wizard brings AoE and DoTs for example. Each character has a range of semi-unique equipment that can be acquired giving some strategic choices when considering the mission or mode being played and what your teammates also provide.
Ontop of each character bringing unique tools to the team, there is a stratification of the equipment that can be earned through gameplay; lower rank gear bringing 1 modifier to top rank gear bringing 3. All of the non-standard items have some form of benefit that is provided. Most of which have some manner of triggering activity, hitting/ killing/ blocking/ assisting etc.These benefits run a gambit of potential abilities that can provide significant attack boosts: faster attacking, penetrating shots, multi shot etc. As well as Defensive and Support abilites, such as ally HP-shielding and personal Ammo replenishment.
This loot system is primarily controlled by a mass dice roll event performed after succesful missions, higher difficulties giving better chances at 'top end' gear. Its possible to stack your odds to a degree by collecting certain objects found hidden around the ZOC. These objects,Tomes and Grimoires take the slots of Potions, and Healing Items respectively, these increase the difficulty of runs significantly if all are gathered.
Unwanted Items can be used in a basic crafting system. As with each rank of gear there is a corresponding rank of Shard, gear is broken down into is matching shard rank. These shards are used to either enable the buffs of another desired weapon, attempt to increase the potency of the modifiers, change the modifiers on a weapon; or attempt to get an entirely new weapon, in a particular (Melee or Ranged) slot for a particular character.
The melee combat system is relatively simple, light 1/2/3/etc. combo with particular swing patterns which reward accurate swipes  and Heavy attacks that take longer to execute. Blocking provides personal protection from melee in all directions when in use and your guard eventually breaks after stamina has been depleted. An alternative use for stamina is to perform a knockback, an important tool for controlling hordes of weaker enemies and rescuing allies in danger. Between block knockbacks and the dodging mechanic everyone should have a fairly easy time quickly cutting through hordes of smaller enemies, giving one or two others time to focus on specialists.
Ranged Combat is controlled: nearly all forms of ranged weapons have an ammo count, and its prohibitively low, though with the low ammo count comes a sense of potency behind those shots. While the wizard and dwarven pistols run on a heat mechanic with effectively infinite ammo the deadly effects of overheat prevent its constant use. This implies that for low health enemies and during swarms its most effective to switch to melee and cleave away; but the ability to prevent specialists from engaging your teammates as quickly as possible is paramount in a ZOC and almost all ranged weapons can do this with ease.
My most negative thoughts of the game regard the post-victory dice roll, the particular number you happen to roll is the item that you get. Ergo, if there is a shotgun you want on 5 but roll 7, you get item 7 even though you had enough 'points' to exceed 5. This forces players to grind far more then most are willing, and 'perfecting' gear takes an extreme amount of tokens (runs) or luck.
While Vermintide does not provide a wholly unique experience, the meshing of RPG with a ZOC proves to be an amazing idea that gives players a reason to beat Ultra-Hard again and again.

A Left 4 Dead 2 clone, in the Warhammer world.
It's a fun game, except it is more stressful than L4D2 because there is no time to take a break, Skavens pop all the time and come from everywhere (which makes sense actually), but you don't hear the Specials (or common Skaven for that matter) nearly as well as in L4D2, which means you can easily get pinned down and die if you wander a bit too far from your companions.
Something else that makes me think of L4D2: the game updates that don't fix bugs...
- 4.5GB patch, and Skavens can still go through closed doors (hidden passage in Wizard Tower)
- 4.5GB patch, and you still can't shoot through what appears to be a *laaarge* empty space inside a fence (Horn of Magnus)
- 4.5GB patch, and you still experience visual bugs (10 meters long Packmaster's pike after it's dead)
- 4.5GB patch, and there are still poor hitboxes (e.g. pillars) which prevent you to shoot Specials even though you rightfully think you should be able to
- 4.5GB patch, and you can still see Tanks (Ogre Rat) blocked in some passages
- 4.5GB patch, and your game can still crash in the blacksmith area
- 4.5GB patch, and you still see the Repurgator visually drop guns each time he uses them (which makes no sense)
- 4.5GB patch, and you still see the Sorceress rigidly slide on the floor when overheating (no animation)
- 4.5GB patch, and you still can't block the Packmaster's pike (or I didn't find how, even though I am using a shield...)
- 4.5GB patch, and endgame stats are still ridiculously bugged (Specials killed, ranged kills, etc.)
- 4.5GB patch, and it's still difficult as hell to simply give a potion to a companion or pick up a potion (you have to aim almost "to the pixel" otherwise it won't work)
Well, you get my point. And I only played a couple of times, which means the developers should have seen these bugs like a hundred times. If it becomes like L4D2 and numerous obvious bugs never get fixed, it will quickly get upsetting.
Please fix the bugs!
Otherwise, it is a L4D2 clone in almost every possible aspect (except for the classes and stuff farming, obviously), which means if you liked L4D2, there is a good chance you'll like this one. Graphics are okay and the game should run on any decent computer.

This game is the first entry in a future "End Times" series where a select group of heroes of varying races fight a Skaven invasion of the city of Ubersreik. The Skaven in the Warhammer Fantasy world are a civilization of rat-men that live in the Under-Empire, a series of sunken cities connected to the hive-city Skavenblight. The skaven are the most populous race in the Warhammer world, but conversely their existence is a closely guarded secret by authorities of the Empire, so a full scale invasion to the extent of one depicted in Vermintide is indeed a sign of the End Times.
Vermintide essentially takes the gameplay of l4d2 and builds up on the melee combat. There are a lot of missions in the base game, and you get loot by rolling at the end of the game with your chances of getting higher tier gear increased based on objectives fulfilled in the mission and the difficulty of the mission chosen. I love unlocking stuff in games, but its pretty slow paced in vermintide as you're really only guaranteed a blue item when you're rolling on nightmare difficulty. I've also found the DLC to be somewhat expensive for how much you can expect to get out of it, but on the plus side people who own it can host the DLC missions for people who don't own them. With that said I enjoyed the game since it combines a solid IP with the welcome addition of a game based off a series that surprisingly hasn't had too many (if any at all) copycats.
TLDR: 7/10

Think rule of rose. The gameplay settings are incredibly varied (going from the forest to a run down city to a merry-go-round among other things) and just boosts the replayability value for me. Collectibles are there for a reason. Any problems people had with the PC release on the release date will find those problems are gone now; they were patched out in less than a month.

This game is not as bad as some people say it is. Seriously what is up with the hate this game is getting.
Pros
-Cool enemy designs ( Ruvik looks very awesome)
-Intense action
-Nice sound effects
-Some nice lighting and shadow effects
-Fluid shooting controls
-Interesting premise
Cons
-Bad choice of Ratio aspect ( I respect the artistic viewpoint but still...)
-For a game this demanding, the graphics are only "OK"
-Animations are pretty choppy, especially the running animation
-A couple of really bad and overdramatic moments
-Besides Ruvik, all the other characters are uninteresting
-Game doesn't seem to know if it wants to be a survivor horror game or an action game. Throwing a lot of enemies at you while giving you no bullets doesn't equal horror, just frustration.
Final Verdict
If you are expecting Silent Hill then look somewhere else, this game is more RE4. If you are looking for straight up action than also look somewhere else as this game has a couple of slow parts. This is a mix of action and stealth, which I think it does a decent job of. This is not the survivor horror revival game that I was hoping for but I still think it is a good game, not nearly as bad as so many people say.
Grade (8/10)
Decent game just don't expect the second coming of Jebus. Go into this game knowing that it "is" an action game with some moments of horror. If you are going in expecting something else then you will be disappointed.

Okay, I am writing this mainly because I want to address one pressing issue:
the hate on the microtransactions. The game is fun, its rather simple, its not a traditional tcg, you get cards out of packs which is nice, you build a deck which is nice, and then the gameplay itself is kind of like a castle defender game, except both sides are sending their troops forward. Its quite nice. From what I can see, there is no pay wall, cards are all avaliable and not even hard to collect. the packs are inexpensive, you can actually sell your duplicates which is a really nice feature, money isn't really that stingy, so yeah, it might take a bit of time to find your SS cards, but its not like it will take months. days maybe, but not months. The story isn't much to write up about, but we get uncensored anime card art that is fairly cute in design. ゲーム内容は皆さんが仰ってるように、確かに凄く面白いです。
なので自分は唯一凄く不満に思ったことだけを書きます。
まず一つ
このゲームのルールでは、よくあるカードゲームのように
１、先攻は最初のターンはカードをドローをしない
２、デッキからカードがドローができなかったら負け
というルールがあります
それなのに
３、このカードゲームにはデッキからターンドロー以外の方法でドローしたり、デッキにカードを戻す術が無い
１２３より導き出される答えは
「後攻は最後のターンまでに相手の拠点(ライフ)を０にできなかったら、どんなに拠点数で勝っていても強制負け」
つまり
先攻は拠点をある程度攻撃されても、最後まで防戦一方で勝てる。無理に攻めることばかりを考えなくてもいい
反面、後攻は相手の拠点を必ず落とさないといけない
という、システム的に先攻が有利というか、恐ろしく後攻が不利すぎる内容になっています
一応、拠点数を減らすなどのローカルルールである程度はこれを防げますが、デフォの拠点数３で拮抗している試合だとこの展開になることもままあります
次に、これが一番の不満点かつ問題点なんですが
カード絵柄の拡大表示機能がありません
カードの女の子を大きくエｒ目で見れるのは、1分の時間制限ありのスクラッチのときだけです
それも通常は体の一部分しか見れないほどのドアップになっているので、全体像を大きく見れる時間は十秒にも満たないです
ギャラリーモードはありますが、画面の左に小さく絵柄が表示されて、それよりも大きく右にカードの説明文が表示されています
腋のしわとか、こつえー氏の描くはいてない女の子のお尻の肉線とか、その他もろもろの素晴らしい部分がドアップのときはしっかりと描かれているのが見れるのに
ギャラリーでは絵自体が小さく表示されるため、それら重要な部分が全然見えないという悲しい事に
【よかった点】
・シンプルなルールで、ゲーム部分がしっかりしている点
・たまにかわいいキャラクターデザインのモンスターカードがある点
・「胸キュンスクラッチ」という馬鹿げたギミックが、面白い点
・短時間で、1プレイできる手軽さ
・追加料金を払わなくても、十分プレイできる点
【悪かった点】
・だらだらと長いストーリーモード
・一部、本当にプロのイラストレーターが描いたの？　と思わせるモンスターカードがある点
・モンスターカードの成長が固定である点（胸キュンスクラッチの結果で、カードがランダムに成長した方がよかったです）
クリア済み。
買うつもりはなかったですが、店舗で売り切れていたことによって逆に購買意欲が掻き立てられ、買ってしまいました。

今更買ってプレイしたわけですが.このゲームはターン毎に貯まるマナをコストにモンスター娘を召還するのですが、後半のCPUはマナ回復持ち＋高コスト召還のコピペデッキで個性も何もありません。単調でつまらない。

I shouldn't have to praise a game for being functional, but sometimes indie titles are a little spotty with control schemes and gameplay. If you're a fan of Sonic, Crash Bandicoot, or the original Gex, you will probably enjoy On a Roll 3D. Plus, you get to play as a cute ball.
'On A Roll 3D' tries to straddle the line between a fast paced platform and a thoughtful puzzler, but fails to deliver on either.

Windows 98 I've missed you... This game looks straight out the late 90's like PC shareware/demoware. It brings nostalgia to my very early encounters with windows 98 and it's plethora of low quality games and shovelware, and it plays like a game from around then. If this puts you off, this is definately not for you in the slightest. If you are not interested in playing something that doesn't feel new or even polished then this is also not for you. This is for people who understand that it's a small game with low quality cheesy textures and simple (but sometimes clunky feeling) controls. It will also help if you have played windows games from the 90's.
There are still small points in the game where it incorporates stuff from the 21st century, the shadows are pretty nice and when the camera rotates round as you move round a corner (pretty sure this happens like in the second half) it's something quite surreal and contradicting to the debatably eye-sore 90's style.
A few things to outline
- It took just over 2 hours to complete it start to finish. So expect play times around that, probably less if you're not as crap as me. I'd say between 1 1/2 hours to 2 is a reasonable guesstimate. I have not completed 100% achievements thus far and however the remainder of achievements I haven't completed is the time trial for the first level (which will probably take a few tries to crack) and the grindy achievements (get x score, collect x stars). The majority were collected through a straight playthrough. This could add another hour or so to play time. There is also 4 challenges on each levels (collect all stars, kill all enemies, don't die, don't get hit) which add to the replayability of the game but there's nothing really outside of just having a optional challenge that makes you want to do that. It does boost your score though.
- The controls are just the arrow keys however some of the controlling of the ball is a bit clunky and hard to grasp i.e. jumping isn't as sensitive as I'd want it to be and therefore precise jumping could be difficult sometimes. It does keep with the 90's windows platforming kind of games where controlling was far from perfect, so I guess it just adds more 90's. The levels aren't that difficult though so it's not too frustrating and the game isn't ruined by it either.
- Again don't expect major graphical content in it. Unless you have a 90's texture fetish.
Overall the game is pretty fun. It's nothing spectacular and it feels like 90's shovelware but I got some fun out of it. I personally wouldn't recommend it at full price though (I got it in a bundle, but a sale would suffice too), unless you understand the above points and like what you see. It'd be more suitable at half of it personally but with 100% achievements and everything completed you'd struggle to not find 3+ hours in it and £1/hour is usually a good ratio...
Anyway I was hoping on writing this review in hopes of putting in a 'I'm on a roll' pun, such as 'I'm getting through my massive library of games and have completed this is 2 hours, looks like I'm on a roll', however it's transformed into something semi-serious and I can't be bothered to delete it and it looks quite impressive and if you are still reading this, go outside.
Alternative drinking game (or biscuit eating game): Take a sip (bite) everytime 90's is mentioned.

Fundamentally a tun-based strategy game, Niche has an deep focus on the genetic development of your omnivorous species.
You explore a procedurally generated map while as the main aspect of gameplay, trying to gather food to survive each turn and make sure that you have your safety carved out for you. Mating is an integral part of insuring the continuation of your species as well, filling out the ranks of your little tribe by selectively (or carelessly) breeding dominant and recessive genes into or out of your tribe's bloodline.
Encounters with strangers complicate the development of your species. You can either attack them or offer them food to join the tribe, bringing in new genetic traits faster than natural mutations develop them. It's worthwhile to take a hard look at the stranger themself, as you don't want a mess of negative traits in your gene pool. It might be more beneficial to kill them and eat them, instead of accepting them into the tribe.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
This game is not finished, but it makes a strong case for funding. It's definitely worth a look, even if you plan on refunding the title. However, I'd urge you to put the money down for it to promote the development of the game. They've got a strong idea in its infancy, and their formula can only improve as time goes on. If twenty dollars seems steep for you, consider that it's a burgeoning development studio with very few resources, and that they're entirely self-published.
If you appreciate a radical idea, commit to the purchase. It's an intriguing game, and I appreciate the ingenuity of it.

Whenever I'd get stuck I'd just either wait out the script by looking down or shake the camera around until whatever scripted event was made to happen happened... I am not very brave. I actually had to look up a youtube video of various scenes that I had completly missed out by not looking at them at all on my playthrough.
Anyway... good game even if it feels a bit familiar and very linear.

I've never been effectively "gotten" by jump scares, but Layers of Fear blends them into the world so well, and messes with your head in so many ways, that it's just... amazing.  Get this game now. Play now. Poop your pants with fear now.

Lightly grease two baking trays. Pre-heat the oven to 220°C/425°F/Gas 7.
Measure the flour and baking powder into a processor. Add the butter and process until a crumble, then add the sugar. Or make by hand by rubbing  the butter into the flour using your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Stir in the sugar.
Beat the eggs together until blended and make up to a generous 300ml (1/2 pint) with the milk, then put about 2 tablespoons of the egg/milk aside in a cup for glazing the scones later. Gradually add the egg/milk mixture to the dry ingredients until you have a soft dough. It is far better that the scone mixture is on the wet side, sticking to your fingers, as the scones will rise better.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and flatten it out with your hand, or use a rolling pin, to a thickness of 1-2 cm (1/2 – ¾ inch). Use a 5 cm (2 inch) fluted cutter to stamp out the dough by pushing the cutter straight down into the dough (as opposed to twisting the cutter) then lift it straight out. This ensures that the scones will rise evenly and keep their shape. Gently push the remaining dough together, knead very lightly then re-roll and cut more scones out as before.
Arrange the scones on the prepared baking trays and brush the tops with the reserved beaten egg/milk mixture to glaze. Bake for about 10-15 minutes or until the scones are well risen and golden. Cool on a wire rack, covered with a clean tea towel to keep them moist. Serve as fresh as possible, cut in half and spread generously with strawberry jam and top with a good spoonful of thick cream.

Solid game hiding an interesting in depth deck building mechanic under its ecchi presentation.
Colors, skills, species, types, levels and duplicates are all the parameters you need to take into account when customizing your roster, and it works surprisingly well considering i've spent a good portion of my 5 hours so far reflecting on it.
For example, you can level cards sure, but it doesn't mean you always should. Some cards are best fielded at level 1 and then upgraded in battle through fusion with duplicates of higher levels. Some other cards should be straight used at max level. Some cards are best used in a pinch for their one time bonus while others will be the meat of your frontline.
And speaking of meat it doesn't hurt that it's full of eye candy.
Well optimized and runs without an itch, the story is simple but pleasantly not cringe worthy so far contrary to what often comes with the anime genre.
Artworks are a bit inconsistent but on the good quality side in general.
The soundtrack is surprisingly nice too, nothing to write home about but good.
Cash shop is 100% optional, i.e for whales with extra money they don't care about spending if ever they wish to unlock rare cards immediately as opposed to get them while playing naturally. And then again at 1 buck a booster, that's as tiny as whales can be. Don't be that player who whines just because.
A good suprise overall, had my eyes on this for a while waiting for PC port, and at this price it's absolutely worth it. Just don't do micro transactions if you don't want to, you don't need it, i for one won't use it, although i like my share of grind in games like these, so if you hate grinding maybe think about it twice.

Probably the only card game that I've seen that offers this type of gameplay, the only one that really comes close to this is Plants vs Zombies Heroes, but even that's a huge stretch, not to mention for completely different audiences of players.
Using a 3 lane system, you put down characters to swarm the other player, taking advantage of the game mechanics and card synergies that come with any card game.
Though the game does have a throwaway story, one-dimensional characters, odd typos and other random nonsense that show a lack of polish, the gameplay is more than enough to make up for that, and makes deck building quite fun as a result.
If you can also get past the fact that the game has gratuitious fanservice around one of the game mechanics, you can find a diamond in the rough and get quite a few hours of fun from this game.
To those who complain about the microtransactions in the game, its barely noticible.  There is exactly one button in the entire game that leads to the shop, and I didn't know its existence until I actively sought it out.  I've mostly played the game with the cards that the campaign provides, and have yet to even spend any of the earned ingame currency to pull cards.
Another detail I would like to address is that there is no multiplayer in this game.  I am personally fine with that as there is no shortage of digital multiplayer card games.  The current version of the game is quite relaxing to play as, taking time to decide moves without having to wait for the other side to take their turn.
Overall, if you can ignore all the minor flaws, you can find many hours of fun along with a decent execise in deck building.

We all know why we're here. A card game with ecchi cards, and this doesn't fail to deliver. It has a somewhat simple combat system, but with a few mechanics that can result in some interesting deckbuilding strategies, especially since you can have 3 of each type of monster at each evolution of it (so you can have a 3 goblins and 3 goblins evo 2 in your deck).
Speaking of evolution, it's probably the most bizarre part of the game. It'll be fun the first few times, but I recommend getting an auto clicker that you can toggle on and off like, Autohotkey, so you can save time since you'll be doing lots of evolving for... science reasons.
As a final note, I've noticed a lot of focus in the review section on the online shop. While I do understand it's a poor choice to add into games like this (I'm very anti-micro transaction and never intend to spend a dollar more on this game), it doesn't bother me anymore than any DLC would. Typically, they both fulfill the same purpose, and yes, there are plenty of single player games with single player focused DLC that does not expand content. That aside, the online shop isn't even upsold or highlighted in any way. You could play for hours like I did without even doing the normal gold summoning, so I've yet to feel any impact from not paying more than the asking price of the game. To shun the game simply because it has one button in it that you can choose to ignore seems to be more shallow than the premise of the game itself.
tl;dr
Fun ecchi card game for the price. I also suggest you don't focus so much on the shop online button that's easily ignored by not looking intently at it. Save your intent looks for the anime ladies.

Hotline Miami 2 is a worthy sequel. It's improves on almost everything that the original offers. And, yet again, it's as awesome as the previous game.
This game's story is vastly superior than the last game. Instead of playing Jacket (the main character of the first game), you play Jacket and many more people that are interesting, unique, and some have varied playstyles that require you to switch up how you play. The pacifist detective refuses to kill, and ops for blunt weapons to knock out instead of kill, and empties gun he picks up. The army soldier doesn't pick up guns. If you empty your ammo, you can use a knife he'll pull out until you find an ammo crate. There's also a few other dudes that play the same as Jacket, but they're still pretty cool because they have different personalities. Hell, the game even gets emotional. It's insane how the story for this franchise has evolved from the first game. The graphics, while 16-bit, are improved, having more detail than the first game. The camera is zoomed out, allowing you to see more of the map. The brutality and violence are still present, which is obvious as that's what everyone liked from the last game. The soundtrack, again, is fantastic, and has more songs than the first game, adding tons of variety. The final mission song for the gang, the army dude, detective, and cop are my personal favorites. The game is way longer than the first, which is always a good thing. There's also new features. There's Hard Mode, which is so ridiculously hard, it's unfair. I was only able to get to the second mission of the third chapter before giving up. There's even a map editor. Yes, a map editor, which is GENIUS. There's already some fantastic campaigns. Yes, people have made 15+ mission CAMPAIGNS using the map editor. I made my own level if you want to check it out under my profile.
Now, after fanboying over this game, let's get to the negatives, which is again, a small amount. You'll get killed numerous times off screen on the more open, large maps, which is frustrating and cheap. Melee weapons are less useful, and you'll be wanting a gun more often, which sucks, as my favorite thing to do is slice and dice everyone with a knife. The masks have gotten a huge nerf. Whereas we got around 15-20 masks in the first game, you get FOUR in this game. They brought back my main mask, Tony, but it's been massively nerfed. You can't pick up guns as Tony, whereas you could in the first game. Saying that, along with how guns are more sought after in this game, makes Tony useless, which is a shame.
Despite the negatives, Hotline Miami 2 is a fantastic indie game. It's great, and I can spend hours slaugtering Columbians and perfecting my combos. Dennaton Games delivers AGAIN!

This game would be better served by being a pay-once service, the way we used to pay for games!
It had so many cools elements but also a lot of missed opportunities to make the game great, instead we have a pretty standard grindy MMORPG.
The graphics (in space) are admittedly incredible and the ship models are true to the trek series, the very first romulan level had really good ground (planetary) graphics. However, later levels don't seem to reflect this, with ideas copied from other genres, like a map that looks like avatar and confusing maps that don't appear to have equivalents in the existing trek universe (as far as I could remember).
The concept behind the away teams are great, you get additional team members (bots) as you progress through the level and the bots can navigate really well, there's far less grind than games like WoW, but the missions seem to become grindy after u have to start collecting 3/4/5/6/7 of the same item. I spent hardly any time shooting opponents and left most of it to my bots, my job was just to run around resusitating them! It sadly, doesn't feel like you are required to interact to complete these missions.
I got to level 30 of 50 in 2 days (32 hours play), but after this the game starts to send waves of enemies (in space and on the ground missions) which take forever to destroy, at this point I gave up.
The most ludicrous part was being in a space shuttle battle but unable to move or fire at enemies, i couldn't see the enemy ships at all as they were too small, so all I could do was sit in cloaked mode directing my fighters, which incidentally respawn - which is good because you're vastly outnumbered on this particular mission. This mission had "walkers", I can't remember any star trek episode with walkers in, perhaps anime or star wars has them, but not trek. For that matter, how many star trek episodes had lots of fighters in!?
The space battles (PvE) would be epic aside from the fact, the turning circles of the ships are absurd. The romulan warbird you get at level 30 seems to be the worst! I can't remember romulan warbirds being so bad in trek. You're constantly stuck in a huge circle trying to hit the side of your enemy and eventually you have to press the speed boost buff every few minutes so that u can do head on damage. It becomes annoying when you damage the forward shields, but then you are stuck shooting the side shields for a long time again and so their forward shields go back up and you have to go in a circle, rinse and repeat!
The most awesome bit, was the borg "red alert" random missions in space. You really need to be level 50 or have a lot of level 50s to win these. The level 30 ship gets destroyed in a few seconds if you don't use the speed buff to move out of range after a strafing run. I frequently crashed into the borg cubes due to lack of turning circle. There are other persistent random space "dungeons" but people don't seem to enter most of them as there's no guarantee there are players in them. Which makes them rather pointless.
Not much else to say. This game had a lot of potential but it fails because it's to some extent unimaginative.

Okay, so where do I start? Where do we all start, for that matter?
Of course, for a story like this, we need to start at the beginning.
So we start off on a journey of pulling yourself back on your feet, as an artist who has fallen from grace in the circles he hanged out in. I'll spare you the story side, aside from the part where the reason why he fell from grace is because he went insane.
Still not offering anything new to the table so far, I'll get to the point. The great thing about this game is the execution of the premise. This game works on the same levels of Silent Hill, where layers of reality are peeled off into something otherworldy. Unlike Silent Hill, however, you don't have monsters to fight along the way to reach your goal. But a game of this genre is not in the monsters you fight; it's in the monsters of the mind, the inner demons. Or, in other words, the tragic pieces of the puzzle that make up the character's background, and that that as the player, you pick up along the way.
An artist sees the world in a different way than regular people, or so it is said. But just how differently can someone see the world, if you're insane? Reality's all a matter of perception, and in this game, it peels off like some poor-quality painting, a clear indication of how frail the protagonist's mind is.
Although still in development at the time I write this review, the game promises some considerable jumps right out of the chair. The daunting atmosphere can be felt from minute one, and the exploration will not allow you to miss one second of it; so all you faint of heart beware, for you will be put to the test, as the growing sense of unease settles in progressively.

HuniePop - A Dating Sim with full english VA?
For those who  are wondering what they are getting themselves into when purchasing such a game, I'd like to point out that the main gameplay element in HuniePop is it's Candy Crush style minigames where you align orbs (vertically or horizontally) in order to gain points. Unlike most date sims, you're not given dialogue during the actual dates themselves. Instead, you must reach a certan amount of points by completing the previously mentioned minigame in a certain amount of turns. While this detracts the game, the voice acting is suprisingly well done and it seems a fair amount of effort was put into the characters. Also, asides from the small conversations that you have when first meeting one of the eight female (love interest) characters, the chatting becomes rather monotonous once you've realized all you can do is ask these women about their personal information and background, and all they do is ask you seemingly random questions or quiz you on the information you've found out from them. Every now and then you get a text from your magical Hunie phone device, and these contain interesting or querky pics of the females (Great artwork!)
Pros:
Great art! You'll know what I mean when you see the texts messages ;)
Good voice acting! It's awesome to see a date sim with actual VA.
Unique characters! Each female has a different personality, with varying likes and dislikes which can take advantage of.
Cons:
You're constantly quizzed on information you've learned from talking to the ladies.
The dates (Pretty much the main part of a date sim) involve you winning a repetitive minigame.
Doesn't seem to be any other objective than just maxing out your relationships with the females by completing dates.
Important note: While the game is ecchi, it's definitely not eroge. If you're expecting H-action, don't go on steam.
TL;DR - Overall I'd give this game a 7/10. It's definitely worth checking out if you're into these kinds of games, but unless you reallly enjoy candy crush style minigames, it'll get boring quickly.

I mean, you can't take it seriously; all the girls are basically caricatures and the conversations never rise above ludicrous but the mechanics are entertaining, there's some laughs to be had and the puzzles ramp up to be challenging (mind you, I never play puzzle games so maybe the Candy Crush masters will find this easy). Your conversations are tempered by a constant need to buy food and gifts to keep her talking and the dates oddly give you the money you'll need to start all over again.  Eventually your night time dates can lead to bedtime frolicking represented by a "lightning round" style puzzle.
The game is unabashedly what is is and if you think you might be offended, you certainly will be so save your money.  If the trailer makes you laugh at either the dialogue or voice acting, you'll probably enjoy yourself for at least a while.  I don't know if the game will have a ton of staying power from a gaming standpoint (unless you want to collect a bunch of semi-naked pictures) but it's fun while it lasts.
Of special note is the musical score which is very catchy and well done.  It's rare that I notice game music enough to realize it and I found myself enjoying it multiple times throughout my playing.
