Not what i had expected. Clunky controls, unresponsive units. Game is quite tedious.
I can usually get past that, i don't mind slow and hard-to-learn strategy games. But it's just not responsive nor is it any fun, and frankly, i find the tactical value to be lackluster due to unavailible options for unit behaviour. (infantry only hit the dirt when under fire instead of ordering them to do so before they are under fire, for example) your units also act clunky and units are unresponsive, especially for tank and gun crews, which is my biggest issue. I am well aware that the game creates a somewhat realistic factor by having a delay in orders and units acting sort-of by themselves, but often at times it seems like my soldiers have a death-wish by simply deciding to hit the dirt right in the middle of a killzone, or tanks refusing to turn the right direction when under fire.
There are also a number of more 'hidden' factors in the game, such as morale, but i couldn't find it. Armor and penetration values for guns and ammo also only displayed the moment when i really started searching for them. While ammo penetration and armor resilience are displayed, they are only done so pre-game when assembling forces and in the encyclopedia. If you happen to stumble upon a tank in-game, you're just gonna have to guess or know these statistics beforehand - which is just silly.
The tutorial is practically nonexistant and explains nothing. While that's usually not too much of an issue for me (i dont mind googling, watching YT vids to get my information) it is still frustrating nonetheless.
I do applaud the creators for trying, the genre is kind of a niche and i really enjoy the setting and the armchair-general genre as a whole, but Theatre of War is just one big dissapointment. I recommend avoiding it.
I recommend picking up Men of War: Assault Squad instead. Not only is it more accessible, it's also got far more depth than Theatre of War, along with excellent sound effects, better graphics, immersion, and an active modding/multiplayer community. And most importantly: Unit behaviour and responsiveness works - unlike Theatre of War.

This is a straight port from the game designed for iOS. It is not a "remaster", nor does it claim to be. It is not a badly done port of that game, but anyone expecting a full-featured PC game is going to be unhappy with this. A lot of functionality from Deus Ex: Human Revolution isn't present in this game, and the graphics were obviously meant for a smaller screen.
I did not play enough to comment on the story, apart from to say that the beginning is formulaic, and non-compelling. What voice acting I heard was noticably more robotic and self-conscious than the acting in Human Revolution. Oddly enough this is what sealed it for me. I expected the game mechanics and graphics to be less impressive than those of Human Revolution, but I expected the story and voice acting to make up for it. I didn't give it much of a chance, only playing for about 30 minutes, but the game didn't really put it's best foot forward, even with my lowered expectations.

I recommend it with some conditions. It's not a very good game, but I still found enough fun to be worth my time. If you consider this a higher quality fan mod (which is about the level of quality to expect here, not that it is an actual fan mod), there is some fun to be had here. Obviously, expecting this to be comparable to Human Revolutions or even the original Deus Ex will only result in dissapointment.
VOICE ACTING
The voice acting is pretty bad, but a lot better than I've seen from some fan mods that have tried to do voice acting.  The dialogue options are extremely limited, with very few opportunities for it to make a difference.
STORY
It's ok and it keeps the pace going.
GAMEPLAY
A lot of areas are streamlined, probably primarily to do it being originally a mobile game. No jumping, which I disliked, but I can see why one might cut that here. It gives the designers a lot more control over where a player can go in the game without having to design additional ways to block player movement to account for jumping. This also focuses the type of gameplay they are offering, allowing multiple ways through environments.
STEALTH
I liked that full stealth options were available, as well as guns ablazing.
HACKING
Much easier than in Human Revolutions, but plenty of things to hack and a few good opportunities to turn robots and turrets against your enemies.
GOODS
I noticed a ton of weapons available for purchase... though I never bought any. The store might be too easy to access, but it gave a lot more options than typically can be found. Everything is probably too plentiful in the game.
LEVELING
Leveling up was really quick, which was good since the game was short.
ONE SAVE + BUGS
I hate single save options. Just make sure when you save, nothing screwy is happening, though I found only a couple bugs during my playthrough.
FINAL THOUGHTS
If anything, the game is too easy, but I still found it fun and I'm interested in seeing where things might go next, if they still planned on making another one. It's a nice diversion, as long as you don't expect much from it. Buy it on sale, if interested, and you should be good.

It's especially worth it if you find this game on a good steam sale.

Vermintide has a lot going for it.  It looks good, plays well, and the combat can be a lot of fun.  But playing with bots is absolutely frustrating, as their AI is criminially slapdash.  They will ignore the rats beating you up while they chase an enemy half a map away, they will continually swing and miss at a rat strangling you instead of switching to ranged.  They are incredibly, infuriatingly inept.  Playing solo is an exercise in frustration at times, and given that you have to randomly grind gear it takes a lot of time to equip them as anything more than a distraction.  I wish the bot AI was as good as the enemy AI, since the rats seem have most of the brains.  This is also the slowest ginding loot game I have ever played, which breeds its own set of issues.  All told, still worth it, I will still play, but it could be so much more.
Update: The AI on the bots hasn't received any improvement.  It is absolutely the worst I have seen in years.  I like the game, but if you are going to play mostly single player, pass on this one.  The bot AI is just that bad.

This game, like so many, has its ups and downs.  On the list of positives, there are things like the ship designs (which are really cool), the missions you get to go on (they all feel like actual things you would do if you were in a Star Trek episode), the fact that featured episodes are voice-acted (the most recent, involving the Sphere, has the actual voice of Worf from The Next Generation), the multiplayer element of the game (incl. PvE and PvP missions both on the ground and in space), and the events they run from time to time.  On the other hand, it gets really repetitive after a while...most of the things you do in missions are in text, not in actual minigames that you can play.
One way this MMO departs from others is that the combat is not "click-click-click you're dead", to put it that way...you actually have to dodge the grenades the Romulans across the room throw, or set up turrets and lure Klingons into a trap.  The game also has a difficulty controller; if you think your missions are too easy, you can change to a higher difficulty for better loot and more of a challenge (seriously, enemy disruptor blasts consume a lot more shield HP in Expert than they do in Normal!).
Its downfall is that it gets repetitive after a while.  Missions are usually "oh, go kill that small fleet of Reman ships" or "take an away team down to the planet and scan relics".  The crafting is also super boring; you need to collect (or purchase) a lot of items to put ship components together.
The game has a slight pay-to-play nature, not nearly as bad as I've seen but still very existent.  You'll need ZEN (the microtransaction currency) to purchase some of the best ships, though if you collect enough Dilithium (an in-game currency that everyone is available to collect in fair quantities) you can trade it in for ZEN.  But it's going to take a lot of Dilithium to buy that Osperey Cruiser or Advanced Obelisk Carrier (the best ships cost 2500 ZEN, which is ~350,000 Dilithium, and you can only collect a few thousand per day at most, even if you're subscribed).
Naturally there is an element of player-formed alliances; in this game they are called Fleets, and they can participate in otherwise closed battles against AI or other people, but I haven't gotten there yet.  You don't need to be any particular level to join a fleet, but lots of fleets will require that you reach the highest level in the game (currently lvl. 50, which translates to a Federation Vice Admiral).  The community doesn't seem too bad.  Also, leveling is a piece of cake.  All it usually takes is a single mission to gain a level.  Every 10 or so you get a newer, larger, better ship.
All in all, I say give the game a shot.  You may find that its repetitiveness gets the best of you.  Or you may be taken away by the scenery as you blow other starships to bits (oh yeah, the graphics are pretty cool).

This game deserves a second chance.
In short: do you want a mediocre Resident Evil 4 clone? Then on sale this is the game for you.
The Evil Within had a rocky start and its PC port was poor on launch, off putting plenty of people, including myself. After the patch, the game runs better, has less glitches, gets rid of the letterboxing and it can run at 60 FPS.
It is a genuinely fun game when it stops trying to be either something it isn't or a blatand carbon copy or Resident Evil 4. Whenever this title is being genuine, you'll experience some fun sequences. It ditches certain gameplay mechanics it tries stuffing down your throat at the beginning and is very poor at teaching the player about its rules, some of the tutorials and loading screen tips can be even misleading. Part of it is trial and error, but under the right conditions you may go on for too long without knowing something near-vital, the realisation of which might make you very irritated.
Story is dumb and the game takes itself too seriously. A smidgen of humor would have gone a long way, but the fun included is either not intentional or just flat jokes. The design is silly and some of it is reminiscent of what a 15 year old goth kid would think of being "scary". To its credit, the game has a lot of varied locales. If I'm shown a screenshot I'm certain I'll be able to pin-point which part of the game it is.

Oh boy, where do I begin with this game.
The Singleplayer is very fun. It's a 2 part RPG adventure - in the first main part your'e traveling around the world map with your band of warriors (which you recruit from villeges) in an almost free style maner - you can pillage villages, battle bandits and faction's armies, visit cities and buy from them, attack castles or cities and even participate in good ol medievel tournamnets. It's a unique RPG experience which I personally really like, however it can be frustrating if you have no idea what your'e doing. You start as a level 1 hero, and level up through killing enemies and completing objectives and quiests. Each time you level up you get to raise your stats (Agillity, Int, strength, charisma, all affect your adeventure in various ways), your skill points which also give many benefits and your weapon proficiencies.
You can co-operate with factions and eventually join them and become a lord with lands. Your relationship with each factions affects the others, and if you end up in war with one of them their armies will make sure to chase you around the world map and battle you.
The second aspect of the game is the battle mode - here you are in a 3rd or 1st person perspective, fighting your enemies along side your trusty warband in classic medievel combat. You command your troops to hold positions, follow you or charge. The goal is to slay all of the enemy units. Sounds easy, until you find out that you ARE NOT a super unit, and die just as fast as all the other ones. With good strategy and powerful warriors at your side you can win battles and gain glory and loot. The weapons and armour you loot or buy at cities, that you wear on yourself, is what you use in battle, and there is a wide range of weapons to use - pikes, crossbows, swords, cleavers, two and one handed axes, spears, lances, bows and many many more. You can also ride on horses along side your cavalry and slay the enemy with a hit and run strategy!
By winning battles, looting villages and caravans and selling stuff you get money (called denars) which you use to buy weapons, horses, armour and food (which is useful to boost your party morale) and pay for your parties wages. A good way to earn money is to take prisoner enemy warriors or lords and then ransom them. I once sold a KING of an faction for 15k!
Now we get to the most frustrating part of the game - Multiplayer and battle mechanics.
It's fun. REALLY fun. But annoying.
The multiplayer mod itself is very entertaining. You can participate in many game modes like DM, TDM, CTF, Battle (1 live a round, last man standing) and My favorite - Siegie, where you have to capture the defending team's flag as the attacker. There are many maps to play, and it's a fresh experience.  There can be up to 200 people in one server, which leads to massive and epic battles. You spawn each time with a set weapons and armour, which you can upgrade or replace with money you gain through killing and getting objectives. Each player has a minimum set of money they always have acces to when they respawn which they cannot lose (It's not uncommon to see fully naked peoeple running around with huge battle axes). This, however leads to the problems of capitalism - the rich, who have a lot of money buy the best gear and get only more money from kills and the poor are stuck with bad gear and stay poor because they barely get any kills (You LOSE MONEY WHEN YOU DIE!).
In addition, The game suffers from various bugs, glitches, lags and inbalances, which make the otherwise flawless combat a source of anger. 2 Handed weapons are wildly over powered compared to one handed weapons + shields becuase of their much faster swing times and higher damage (+ Many break shields very quickly). Bows and crossbows are insanely effective with low money matches, where everyone has less armour but almost useless when used against very armed people. The hit detection can be broken at time, mostly for the worse - I've had many times when my arrows went right through and my axes did no damage at all. Blocking with weapons (not shields), although hard to master and is very rewarding, simply doesn't work at times. The horses are insanly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and always either stop dead on when you budge into something, leaving you easy prey for infantry with 2 handed weapons, or go compeltly the other direction and end up slaming into an obstacle - again, having you killed by archers and 2 handed axes.
The game also has some hilarious glitches like the "Sky Faces".
Overall, I think it's a very good game and I highly recommend you try it out. You will rage, but the best way to have fun is get better! (Or use 2 handed weapons, which ever works).

X Sometimes specials won't activate when I press F, or will play the animation but won't actively do it. Heavy Knight's spin special commonly causes my camera to spin but not attack in a 360 radius, disorienting me and leaving me open to attack.

As a sequel I simply can't recommend this game. It seems to take several steps back, and in doing so hits it's head against an open cupboard.
Firstly, there's the issue of why Theatre of War 2 comes in 2 games, each with their own add-ons? The answer to which illudes me completely. The original game had way more content, more nations, and a wider time period. Poland and France have been removed, and Italy and the USA needlessly funnelled off into their own game (which is also suffers from a severe lack of content). The British only have equipment they had at Caen, and not even all of that is present (have you ever heard of the RAF, 1C?). Are we to believe the feed back for the first game was "there's too much stuff, I want less choice"? Obviously it wasn't, so this is another quandery with no real reasoning.
Secondly, there's a grand total of one new mechanic. It's not even pluralisable. Just the one thing that's been added. It's not a terrible one, just poorly executed. The new mechanic is points. You spend points on the task force which you take on missions, and you get points for destroying enemy units. This in and of itself works fine, although knowing what's worth what would be quite nice, as you've no way of knowing in the middle of a battle (or in the menus for that matter). The only real downside is that your support now costs points. So you need at least 3000 points before you can call in artillery. Given that the average tank kill gets you about 400~ points, you need to wipe out roughly an entire battalion of tanks before High Command decide the situation looks a little hairy, and grant you off-map arty support. I'm not sure why this change was made, as artillery and air support were finite resources anyway, so you could quite easily blow it all on a not-so-serious attack and only realise later there's still another 300 dudes to kill, and your 6 remaining shells probably won't do the trick.
These are just the starkest of the games faults. There's so many little things going wrong as well, from unforgivably bad sound design (Brits speaking in American voices and the generally empty feel of the soundtrackless battles (the music slider is actually greyed out but left in)), all the way to awkward, but sadly compulsary, infantry micro-management (I shouldn't have to manually give my MG ammo while I want to be flanking a Tiger with my SU-85). It's just so frustrating to have a beautifully rendered WW2 battlefield, and then feel consricted and fustrated by mechanics of the game.

I had low hopes for the game but after playing it I found the writing to be delightful! The conversations are quirky, though at times a little too cliche, but it doesn't keep the game from being anything other than fun. Just know this game ISN'T a visual novel so the dialogue is pretty lite.
The sound effects are great and the music is nice. Some people had issues with the art style but I personally like it and all the scenes are varied and the girls themsevles have a handful of hair and clothing sytles to unlock.
The core however is the puzzle matching game during dates. If you enjoy any kind of match-3 game type (Bejeweled, Candy Crush, etc.) then you'll have fun with this. The differences that make this game stand out from those however is the ability to move a gem anywhere in the row and colum it resides and counter-balanced by a move limit. Along with traits (leveling system from getting experience by talking to girls outside the puzzle segment) and gifts (which you obtain from giving gifts to girls outside of the puzzle segment) that when combined together can enhance your playing style. You might go for points, extra moves, changing gems, or a mix of all. It has enough flexibility to let you strengthen the way you want to play.
My only complaint is the game gets ridiculously difficult the further in you get. At the last few girls (including the unlockable) I had difficulty completing a level as I had long since maxed out my traits and ended up lowering the difficulty level to finish the stage. Not to mention the "bedroom" stage which involves filling a meter which constantly depletes, at later levels you have to match 4 or more to gain any footing.
Overall, I came in with low expectations but found them surpassed. It's a fun game and I highly recommend it if you like puzzle gems and match-3. Also, it rewards you for winning with bewbs, which is good because it gets hard as♥♥♥♥♥♥later on and you're gonna need that motivation.

Layers of Fear is a really interesting game with some fresh and great ideas.
First of all I should point out that I'm not a friend of horror games that adorn themselves with jumpscares but absolutely adore subtle scariness that doesn't shock but let oneself indulge in it.
In
you play an insane artist who tries to finish his masterpiece. Well, and his house... only so much be said: it has an inspirational effect...
First of all, the idea of an insane painter seeking inspiration is just charming and great, the dark design of the houses' magnificent rooms that in a way become alive is stunning and the graphical enactment bestows the player with shivers down the spine. Strange things happen in this mansion and you may feel it's insanity - like the mansion itself has a conscience - which is, however, deceased and ill of decay .
This game misses a lot of subtle scariness. Some paintings are changing but most of the time in a very spontanious or predictable way. What about some simple eyes following you around? Or a hand slowly reaching for your mind?
In addition this game uses a ton of sometimes really cheap jumpscares. There is no art in using the human instinct of being shocked if introduced to a very spontanious stimulus. Really, there is no art in that. Shocking fright has nothing to do with a scary atmosphere. Plus most of the time the shock effect is primarely triggered by audio (e.g. a loud 'whush' when some books randomly decide to suddenly fly into your face).
Some jumpscare effects (not going to spoiler here) are even causing the same animation over and over again and -
- make you wake up in a specific place with another repeating animation.
True madness is to indulge into darkness. This game doesn't even try to seduce you to do so but rather tries really hard (and with sometimes really cheap effects) to chase you away.
Don't get me wrong: this game has some ingenious effects and ideas and I'm absolutely
with the setting.
But in my opinion it doesn't get into the dark idea it created but only looks upon it.

This game is extremely fun and informative. Niche is a genetics manager game- where you must manage your tribe's food, amount of nesting material you have to be able to have children, and your population as well as their genes.
You must learn to balance out food for each tribe members. This can be a rough task at first, but as you pla the game more, you will realize how simple it is to get food, and how abundant the food in Niche really can be. Depending on your tribe's genetics, you may be able to quickly gain food by fishing, collecting berries, and collecting meat from crabs, rabbits, and other prey.
You must learn to gather nesting material or find a nest already placed on your island. Nests can be quite abundant as well, but it is nice having a nest you built yourself, because you can choose it's location. It can be placed next to a large amount of food. If you pick a pre-built nest it can be rough starting out depending on how close you are to your food sources. Building nests costs nesting material, and you get this from grass.
Like every ecosystem, there are predators. Depending on which habitat you choose to reside in, you will have different predators. These predators will easily kill you, unless you have the proper genetics to fend for yourself. There are many different genes you can use to protect yourself. All of these look different, and have different stats. The stronger genes you choose, the easier it will be to defend yourself.

Oh boy, where do I begin with this game.
The Singleplayer is very fun. It's a 2 part RPG adventure - in the first main part your'e traveling around the world map with your band of warriors (which you recruit from villeges) in an almost free style maner - you can pillage villages, battle bandits and faction's armies, visit cities and buy from them, attack castles or cities and even participate in good ol medievel tournamnets. It's a unique RPG experience which I personally really like, however it can be frustrating if you have no idea what your'e doing. You start as a level 1 hero, and level up through killing enemies and completing objectives and quiests. Each time you level up you get to raise your stats (Agillity, Int, strength, charisma, all affect your adeventure in various ways), your skill points which also give many benefits and your weapon proficiencies.
You can co-operate with factions and eventually join them and become a lord with lands. Your relationship with each factions affects the others, and if you end up in war with one of them their armies will make sure to chase you around the world map and battle you.
The second aspect of the game is the battle mode - here you are in a 3rd or 1st person perspective, fighting your enemies along side your trusty warband in classic medievel combat. You command your troops to hold positions, follow you or charge. The goal is to slay all of the enemy units. Sounds easy, until you find out that you ARE NOT a super unit, and die just as fast as all the other ones. With good strategy and powerful warriors at your side you can win battles and gain glory and loot. The weapons and armour you loot or buy at cities, that you wear on yourself, is what you use in battle, and there is a wide range of weapons to use - pikes, crossbows, swords, cleavers, two and one handed axes, spears, lances, bows and many many more. You can also ride on horses along side your cavalry and slay the enemy with a hit and run strategy!
By winning battles, looting villages and caravans and selling stuff you get money (called denars) which you use to buy weapons, horses, armour and food (which is useful to boost your party morale) and pay for your parties wages. A good way to earn money is to take prisoner enemy warriors or lords and then ransom them. I once sold a KING of an faction for 15k!
Now we get to the most frustrating part of the game - Multiplayer and battle mechanics.
It's fun. REALLY fun. But annoying.
The multiplayer mod itself is very entertaining. You can participate in many game modes like DM, TDM, CTF, Battle (1 live a round, last man standing) and My favorite - Siegie, where you have to capture the defending team's flag as the attacker. There are many maps to play, and it's a fresh experience.  There can be up to 200 people in one server, which leads to massive and epic battles. You spawn each time with a set weapons and armour, which you can upgrade or replace with money you gain through killing and getting objectives. Each player has a minimum set of money they always have acces to when they respawn which they cannot lose (It's not uncommon to see fully naked peoeple running around with huge battle axes). This, however leads to the problems of capitalism - the rich, who have a lot of money buy the best gear and get only more money from kills and the poor are stuck with bad gear and stay poor because they barely get any kills (You LOSE MONEY WHEN YOU DIE!).
In addition, The game suffers from various bugs, glitches, lags and inbalances, which make the otherwise flawless combat a source of anger. 2 Handed weapons are wildly over powered compared to one handed weapons + shields becuase of their much faster swing times and higher damage (+ Many break shields very quickly). Bows and crossbows are insanely effective with low money matches, where everyone has less armour but almost useless when used against very armed people. The hit detection can be broken at time, mostly for the worse - I've had many times when my arrows went right through and my axes did no damage at all. Blocking with weapons (not shields), although hard to master and is very rewarding, simply doesn't work at times. The horses are insanly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and always either stop dead on when you budge into something, leaving you easy prey for infantry with 2 handed weapons, or go compeltly the other direction and end up slaming into an obstacle - again, having you killed by archers and 2 handed axes.
The game also has some hilarious glitches like the "Sky Faces".
Overall, I think it's a very good game and I highly recommend you try it out. You will rage, but the best way to have fun is get better! (Or use 2 handed weapons, which ever works).

Cossacks : European Wars to me is one of the greatest RTS's ever made. There is a lot of complexity that can go on within the game, and really gives the player a sense of creating a city. I've put over 100+ hours into this game before purchasing it on steam (I lost my CD)!
They've done a great job to differentiate the different races within the game as not all units look the same.
The unit types are various, from priests, to serfs, to mercenaries, to drummers, to officers, to musketeers mounted on horses. Different units obviously offer different strategy. Priests and the like heal other units, archers to musketeers are available for range, ground units can be swordsmen to horsemen who ride extremely fast. If there is water present, the user can build shipyards and amass some major galleys or frigates. The ship battles are just as intense as the unit battles. One of the main features in this game that surpasses other RTS's is the unit organization. Units can be given a drummer and an officer and be given certain formations. Other units can be told simply to line up or square up accordingly. Until someone for themselves see how this system works, it becomes a game of "line up my armies behind one another". It's quite appealing and makes it extremely easy to line up and manage units. Building in the game is quite neat as more than one serf can work on a building at a time. Problem is though unlike some games, you cannot build more than one building at a time with the same serf. Meaning, you cannot line up to build a bunch of dwellings with one unit. You will have to either wait till he completes his work, or assign other serfs to build in different areas.
All buildings have a purpose and are diverse in their functions (such as marketplaces all the way to blacksmiths). What adds a unique touch to the game besides the buildings themselves, is the ability to build a wall all around your city, as well as gates and guard towers that shoot cannons at enemies. To harvest supplies, mines need to be built over certain resources while other resources such as wood or stone can be found above ground. Store houses need to be built by these areas for harvesting to be done properly. Food is also a commodity to look closely after and harvest as the more units you have, the hungrier they will all get! This is where Knights and Merchants sort of made sense as serfs would be needed to run out food to the armies. This game does that automatically. There can be a lot to manage and do in this game, and the computer does like to throw sneak attacks here and there. Building a giant city up is gratifying but beware when walls start getting attacked randomly from all sides.

Did you love Hotline Miami? Did you play it over and over again to get A+ scores on all the tight and neatly designed levels? Did it leave you wanting more?
Well, fret not! Hotline Miami 2 is here and it will take care of that. Nobody will leave this game wanting more.
You liked the strategic, high stakes gameplay in tightly designed levels? That's gone now, it's massive levels with most enemies far out of view gunning you down - over several floors, with no real save points in between. Need a break from Hotline Miami 2? Enjoy re-playing the massive three floors that you just painstakingly cleared over the last 40 minutes.
You enjoyed Hotline Miami's firmly tongue in cheek story that didn't interrupt the gameplay too much and left you more amused than bemused? That's gone now, it's a giant mess of a confusing and utterly pointless "story" that constantly gets in the way.
Hotline Miami 2 still, occasionally captures the magic of Hotline Miami - after all, it looks and plays almost exactly the same - but the terrible level design mostly makes it a chore and few people will be compelled to play this game to perfection.
If you haven't yet, buy and play Hotline Miami instead. If Hotline Miami left you wanting more, it's up to you - either re-play that one or buy this one, it will certainly cure you from all desire for more.

Super Noah's ark 3-d, has quite a history behind it. Way too much to go into, though it was made by wisdom tree, the same guy's known for the christen games on the NES ranging from "meh" to "Jesus christ why!?!" but luckily this is one of the better games they made.
This is pretty much a re-skin of wolfenstein 3-d but uses slingshots with food(instead of guns)
to put animals(instead of nazi's) to sleep(instead of "asleep with bullets"). This is because of the company being more based on christen games but it's a cute idea. And while this isn't as good as wolfenstein 3-d, it does make some improvements over it. It has a map (a godsend since  rooms look so similar) and more ammo types and weapon types(even if it's all slingshots)
There are plenty of stages and secrets. And enemy types become more varied the further you
go into the game. The graphics are nice(for a re-skin) as everything looks colorful and cartoonish. However the hit detection is weird. Enemies can kick you from far away and some hit's I took would come from enemies behind walls or at least I think so, sometimes I couldn't see them. Also like wolfenstein 3-d, I found it to get repetitive after a while, I'd recommend playing it in short bursts. My biggest issue is the weird difficulty spikes. Animals can kill you fast on all but the lowest difficulty. That difficulty kills you quick halfway through. It might be me, but it's seems harder to beat this than wolfenstein 3-d. Overall not amazing but a nice curiosity for gaming, or anyone wanting something that doesn't take itself too seriously. Just be aware that, while charming, it's not a masterpiece.

I had low hopes for the game but after playing it I found the writing to be delightful! The conversations are quirky, though at times a little too cliche, but it doesn't keep the game from being anything other than fun. Just know this game ISN'T a visual novel so the dialogue is pretty lite.
The sound effects are great and the music is nice. Some people had issues with the art style but I personally like it and all the scenes are varied and the girls themsevles have a handful of hair and clothing sytles to unlock.
The core however is the puzzle matching game during dates. If you enjoy any kind of match-3 game type (Bejeweled, Candy Crush, etc.) then you'll have fun with this. The differences that make this game stand out from those however is the ability to move a gem anywhere in the row and colum it resides and counter-balanced by a move limit. Along with traits (leveling system from getting experience by talking to girls outside the puzzle segment) and gifts (which you obtain from giving gifts to girls outside of the puzzle segment) that when combined together can enhance your playing style. You might go for points, extra moves, changing gems, or a mix of all. It has enough flexibility to let you strengthen the way you want to play.
My only complaint is the game gets ridiculously difficult the further in you get. At the last few girls (including the unlockable) I had difficulty completing a level as I had long since maxed out my traits and ended up lowering the difficulty level to finish the stage. Not to mention the "bedroom" stage which involves filling a meter which constantly depletes, at later levels you have to match 4 or more to gain any footing.
Overall, I came in with low expectations but found them surpassed. It's a fun game and I highly recommend it if you like puzzle gems and match-3. Also, it rewards you for winning with bewbs, which is good because it gets hard as♥♥♥♥♥♥later on and you're gonna need that motivation.

I'm going to be honest. I think this is the first review I've written for a game on Steam. I don't want to be the guy who slams an independent developer and expects unrealistic quality for $5, or what it was when I first picked this up, $3. And somehow the general steam ratings for Overture has changed from mostly negatve to very positive since the last time I looked at this game, and I can't tell why.
That being said, I really want to like this game more than I do. Deep down in it, somwhere, is a really fun game. A simple twin-stick shooter with elements of Gauntlet and roguelikes is a really cool idea, and mechanically it's implemented pretty well.
However, the game is a visual mess. It's not just the blown-up pixel graphics in it - it could have masterful, highly detailed sprites, and it would have been the same. The game is often incomprehensible. It is also really hard, and grindy. Not nessecarily a bad thing, though in this case it's rather maddening. I am constantly dying to enemies I don't realize are there until it's over. There's barely any cooldown on hits to your character, and there's so much commotion on the screen, it's sometimes very difficult to tell what's going on. The game qickly turns into a churning mass of large and tiny, sometimes hard to see projectiles, friendly and enemy characters, pickups and destructible objects all over a mess of dungeon debris from everything else you've been shooting that makes objects even less distinguishable. Both taking hits and some player attacks shake the screen and blur the action. When you are on low health, the screen turns a blurry red which camoflages everything even further. Try a cleric for the first time, and then try to figure out what is going on as your large attacks seem to behave not quite consistent enough to make immediate sense, and take up a majority of the center of the screen.
BUT, I do enjoy it somwhat, as it's the only game I know of that does what it does so mechanically well. As in, shoot with swords and friendly assists, gradius-style, a bullet-hell action RPG with vastly different playstyles between characters. Think of it as a more rogelike-y, singleplayer Realm of The Mad God. It can be very cathartinc when things are going well, and there are certain parts of it that do have some charm. Considering the price point and the lack of pretense, and you should be able to forgive a lot and appreciate the core gameplay.
It's just hard to forvige such bewilderingly confusing visuals.

Alright, so after 18 hours of playing this game, I'll give you guys my humble opinion about my experience so far.
If it's great graphics and high end quality you look for, get away from this game.
But if you're looking for a game with a (very) rich storyline and diversity (the game has loads of diversity thanks to both space and ground action). It isn't really MMO either, most of the stuff (storyline) does fine playing solo, although friends always can tag along.
Do not expect a FPS on the ground, it still is a sort of archer-like RPG experience, although it does have a good tactical depth in skills and equipment.
The space combat experience can compete with EVE's, keeping your shield, energy, and skills distributed, and facing the enemy from the right side through a whole battle always is a nice challenge.
Ship diversity is high for all the sci-fi fans out there, with nice customization for them aswell, they also come supplied to you for free until lvl 40, every 10 levels, so that is a pain in the wallet less. You don't really need to grind for "good" equipment until endgame I'd say.
Just bare in mind that this still is a F2P game with some server issues (they can be a ♥♥♥♥♥ when they're heavily loaded), and sure, all RPG's get repetitive eventually, but this one does a great job at keeping that barrier very far away indeed.

If you like experimenting with mechanical design, and making things go from just spare parts, then Scrap Mechanic is sure to hook you instantly. But, if you are mechanically challenged don’t worry. The Devs at Axolot Games have put together a fun assortment of “smart” parts that are pre-wired to have your designs rolling, spinning, sliding, or flying in one direction or another… or every direction at once. It also provides a user handbook in your hotbar, complete with video how-to links. The building mechanics are simple and allow you to build walls and parts to scale with ease. But, expect a learning curve and a lot of laughs as you find yourself hanging upside down from trees.
The art is incredibly well done. The landscape is covered with a realistic style of comic book trees, rocks, and farm equipment. Music is not only upbeat, but a radio is provided and can be attached to creations on the go. But, there is no water anywhere. This would be a feature that would be highly desired, as it would allow for design of boats. In the current early access state, the graphics run a bit slow. The lag is real… especially on low-end machines. This is a factor that needs more work, and from what the devs are saying in the forum and frequent dev blogs, it is a priority. They’ve doubled their team size this month, and while they are still adding new features constantly, they are also busy improving existing features in the program.  I’ve noticed the game runs faster on my pc already in just the couple of weeks I’ve been playing. Other early access games I’ve played started out with similar lag, but were soon running with ease for me.
The survival mode story has you playing the role of a robot maintenance mechanic in space. You crash land on your first assignment on an agricultural planet where you are supposed to keep the ag-bots in working order. But, you find the place deserted and a couple of old vehicles that you can commandeer as is, or salvage for scrap parts for your own creations. This should provide more options for those players like me who have a hard time getting started with their first build.
However, the current build has you playing in creative mode only. You can choose the terrain map, which has rolling hills and steep valleys. This seems designed much like the Disney Cars playset in Disney Infinity 1.0, (sorry, but Steam isn’t the only platform out there) very fun, lots of room to drive and do stunts, and a variety of land features. Or you can choose a flat world with nothing but dirt, for experimenting with designs or hosting mp competitions.
There seems to be no combat in the game at all at the moment. I haven’t found any indication of plans in this area either. The character takes no fall damage, and is not affected by hunger. Sunshine and noon are static for the time being. I assume the pending “survival mode” will include dynamic weather, and a day/night cycle, as well as other needs.  I also hope vehicular combat will be an option.
You are able to invite friends into your game with ease. This seems to be functioning well. I also discovered that you can go into the flat sandbox, set limits on the number of parts each player is allowed to use on their vehicle, and host a design competition with friends. This provides infinite options for hours of mp fun, as well as the ability to design your own world and even race tracks.
•	Creative, fun, and highly playable as is
•	Wide array of simple usable parts to build almost anything you can imagine
•	Flight, Mechanics, & Construction
•	Encourages trial & error
•	Suitable for all ages (even adult engineer types)
•	High replay value
•
---majorly improved, almost no lag at all now
•	No water, and limited map size in early access
•	No day/night cycle yet, creative mode only in current build
•	No combat yet
It is family friendly, creative, and fun all at the same time. It is definitely an upper tier game and worth the price, because it has tremendous replay-ability. I rate it an 8 out of 10 in the sandbox/ open world builder genre, but will probably change that rating after the final release

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

It is, with a heavy heart, I do NOT give the recommendation to play this game, despite it having Deus Ex in it's name.  The sloppy nature of the port of the mobile game hampers the playability and enjoyability of this game.  The graphics are unbecoming of a modern PC's cability (or that of one five years ago).  The controls are rigid and unresponsive, and the gunplay is spetacularly poor.  Bullets seem to not register damage with half of the hits, and enemies unwittingly walk to you as easy fodder during battles.  That said, those dedicated to stealth only gameplay will find a variety of options to play through the game without needing to fire a single bullet.  I did find the exploration of the game world satisfying, and hacking enthusiasts will find plenty of opportunities to hone their skills.   The minimal interaction and dialogue options with NPC's ensure a relatively linear story without meaningful choices, and the ending is an abrupt cliffhanger.  Overall, this game cannot be recommended in its current state, one which will likely be its final state.

Way back in the winter of 2009, I, as mere boy, was gifted a brand new Dell Inspiron 15. This was both the first computer I was ever able to call my own and the most capable machine I'd had access to at home in my life (really.) I was estatic, but being a poor wee child I had little to no means of obtaining modern games, and similarly slim chances of running them with any degree of respectable performance. However, thanks to the wonders of the internet, I was able to obtain a copy of Grand Theft Auto San Andreas and, soon after, its very own multiplayer mod.
Now, I sunk maybe 100 odd hours into that classic mod, and as of writing I've only spent three in this mod. But the waves of nostalgia pushed on me by this mod for that time are immense. People frantically hauling♥♥♥♥♥as fast as they possibly can back and forth along airstrips while people in carpet bombers and attack helicopters rain fire from above. Destinationless monster truck races. Demolition derby. Ultra persistent Japaneese children with rocket launchers and 1500 ping. The Cube.
On a less personal and, hopefully, less biased note, this mod in its current state is, at best, the equivelent of relentless slapstic comedy. There is zero substance or objective of gameplay from what I've seen so far. Most servers are mediocre performance wise and almost wholly unmoderated but overall not what I'd call terrible considering this mods aimless nature as of now.
Overall, if you can find a good populated server, this mod seems to be a great ~10 hours of free absurd directionless more-than-a-little-broken fun; if you manage to bring along a friend then probably a little longer. Development is ongoing and its community seems to be doing alright, so I am cautiously optimistic for its future as well.

I love exploring. I've spent thousands of hours spelunking through caves and devouring wastelands, and this game totally messes with your mind on a much deeper level than jumpscares or tangible enimies can ever achieve.
When one makes an effort to explore every nook and cranny that catches one's eye, the explorer feels a sense of sublime success after all doors are open and seen behind, yet a terrible longing for more. In Layers of Fear, escaping one area tends to trap you in the next in an ever-progressing descent into madness, self-loathing and definitely psychedelic horror. The house makes no sense and I love it! It's like a very long version of the house puzzle in The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, except the architecture never reveals its secrets.
You'll find yourself bumbling around a satisfyingly creepy labrynth of a tortured and mind with you controlling the body. A once-revered painter now trying to recover his past, insanity seeps in influencing his skill. His subjects: 19th century fatcats, cozy wooden chairs with colorful paint splatter, mutilated baby dolls. The usual oil painter paraphenalia. He has become a laughing stock among the art world and is shambling his way toward his next masterpiece through drunken anguish over a loved one's death. Hallucinations seem real and reality gives way to hallucinations, edges blur, shapes distort and colors do bleed indeed.
Every room is a piece of art, whether it be cluttered with eye candy or the environment is manipulated around you. Never does it become entirely tedious or boring. Even without an enemy besides yourself, the fear is never far away. After discovering notes to and from yourself, you piece together this puzzle that gradually shows the picture only by making you ask yourself more questions. Sure, you could run through every unlocked door and try to finish the game, but the gameplay incourages immersion by having you swing wide open doors, dishevel all the drawers,  flick on every lightbulb and pull down on torture-chains. There is no heath bar or sanity meter. No special abilities are there to aid you in your unending darkness. Only memories guide you though your mind's maze.
What has happened?
What have I done?
Where the hell is my cane?
I just hope all of this starts to make sense.

I bought this game just because it was made by the same people as SanctuaryRPG, heavy action games aren't normally something I favor but this one really impressed me.
Let's start with the good:
Really hard early on. There's people complaining about not making it past the first level out of 10. You actually can die there without being completely bad at the game.
Very gameplay dense. For a game with such simple mechanics as move and launch one of two different attacks it really does a lot with them and requires a lot of focus or you'll die.
Very gameplay focused. How many games regale you with their shiny water and copious offering of exposed breasts and then when you actually play them it's just a buggy, incomplete, boring trainwreck? You won't see that here, the focus is purely on the game itself - and the game itself is solid.
24 classes that can be unlocked fairly quickly, each of which feel and play very differently.
Steadily increasing intensity - the higher levels both have more enemies and more dangerous enemies, combat gets very chaotic very fast.
The developer is extremely active and maintains direct and regular contact with the userbase.
And now the bad:
Fairly weak graphical optimization. Even though these are SNES graphics they will still cause serious slowdown when there is extremely large amounts of activity on screen, and there almost always is later. The developer has tried fixing this, and it's usually fine but extreme activity will still cause performance problems.
Excessive graphical clutter from on kill/destroyed effects can obscure important parts of the screen.
Excessive graphical clutter from certain heroes' special abilities can obscure important parts of the screen.
Has the standard Roguelike problem at a very extreme level. You'll either die early or win in 99.9% of cases. The first time I reached floor 5 and didn't die near instantly because I got swarmed was the first time I won. Why? Because not only does the player have good tools at this point but also you start vastly outscaling the enemies, such that they do low or even single digit damage per hit while you hit for over 1,000 by endgame. You can't lose at that point no matter how bad you are even though those late game situations would otherwise be extremely dangerous.
Not a lot of enemy variety. Once you hit floor 4 or 5 you quit seeing new enemies and attacks until the end, which means once you know how you deal with the early game you know how the rest of the game works. Bosses start repeating as well, there should be 9 in a random order + the final boss at minimum, instead there are 6 + the final boss.
Overall I'd still recommend the game - it's one of the few on Steam worth full price but if you can get a sale certainly take it. I believe the developer will reduce the amount of graphical clutterr, add more content, and make the later game harder which fixes every problem on that list.

If your looking for a review on Hotline Miami 2, you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an amazing pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I wanted to like this game, but ultimately I can't. The main problems are the visual clutter and the uninspiring upgrade "system". It's not bad, but it's just not really worth playing over other games I own.

I'd advise against buying this one. Play Hero Siege, instead.
Both games sort of hinge on the same principle by going overkill with destructibles and number of exploding enemies. Honestly, while this game would have been something neat to see as freeware and a developer's experiment on making a game satisfying to play, it's simply not worth paying for, at all. This is, of course, my opinion - other people seem to be enjoying this, although this game is being given away for free.
They use particle effects, permanent bodies and bloodstaines, screenshake and overall a buttload of money and numbers on the screen to make the player feel overpowered. That aspect is quite nice, although it's very clearly an amateur take on it. With some refinement it could be really satisfying.
Despite having this one nice aspect, the whole game seems like simply filler, and it doesn't do anything new.
The games has probably dozens of classes, which sounds like a lot. However, they mostly play the same. There are only 2 attack: main and special. Special attacks drain mana. The main attacks between classes vary simply in range and power, but they're all essentially the same.
The game has one mechanic: you run faster is you're running in the same direction as the mouse pointer - i.e., you can't aim while running away.
It's an interesting mechanic, for sure!
But the game just swarms you with enemies, it's too zoomed in, attacks are way too big and obfuscating, as are the enemy corpses. Nothing interesting in the environments, you can't see what you're getting hit by, you often get stuck in random terrain that you can't see properly...
It was a fun game to play for 30 minutes. Again, if it was a freeware game like Cactus' or JW's, it would have been cool. The developers gets to create a name for himself while trying something new, and people get a couple of minutes of enjoyment. Once you have to pay for it... it's just not worth it, at all.
Very unpolished and bland, in general. Again, try Hero Siege - not perfect, but far better than this in every respect.

I like this game. It will certainly never become my favourite game (because THE DOG Island is my religion,) but in small doses it's fairly enjoyable. I see why people have poured over 100 hours into this, but there's a good reason why I didn't push 100 yet.
1. It gets extremely boring after a while. I don't know how Kiffy spent 366 hours into this. Sure, you can participate in a challenge or make up a story for your demons of Hell, but other than that I get bored fairly quick.
2. Lag. After like, 10 minutes of playing my computer will start to lag. And keep in mind I'm running on the lowest quality graphics for this game.
3. Speaking of graphics, they look really weird. It's kinda like Alpaca World where the alpacas are obviously in a different art style yet the backgrounds look like a cheaply made iPhone game. I don't know if it's because of how low quality I set my game to be, but come on. Bootleg Minecraft games are so 2014.
4. The community. In a second I will be complementing them, but let's be honest. There are three types of fans for Niche: the people that don't know when to stop posting art/screenshots, the people that don't know when to stop playing, or just regular fans. You can probably tell what most of the fans fit into (including me.)
Now let's see the pros.
1. The demons of Hell can sometimes look really cute or most of the time really did look like they came from Hell.
2. The community. They're actually really nice and
3. The premise is okay and the game turns out to be very educational.
4. The devs are really nice too.
5. Highly addictive. Looking at you Kiffy...
Overall, should you play this game? If you really want to, go for it! I'm not stopping you. If you tolerate being bored and like a friendly commnity, I reccomend this game!

Both ways provide interesting and unique gameplay, I didn't even see the genetics part of the game at first, and after I did the game was better as I tried to abolish bad genetics and keep the better ones alive. It gives the game a good aspect of strategy, and the scattered nests around each island gives the player a chance to have multiple different tribes of animals with different genes. From what I've seen updates are rather frequent and add new aspects and situations to the game, such as adding the water biome with swimming genes like webbed feet and gills. I'd say this game is worth at least 10 dollars, pick it up if you get the chance.

After looking for another co-op game to offer something new compared to the Left 4 Dead series I stumbled on this during a sale.  For FPS fans, the 3rd person view will take a bit of getting used to but most of us these days have played from both perspectives.  I found the NORMAL mode very challenging so played on CADET for a bit until I got used to the play mechanics, loadouts, and gameplay.  After getting used to it, its not so bad on the more difficult levels.  There are multipart campaigns with designated safe rooms like L4D, but at the end of each campaign/mission it launches you into the next rather than simply ending as I suspect the last campaign is the "ending/escape"
The zombies swarm you but in a very different way than L4D because they don't rush at you with a full on sprint but rather just emerge and move in large groups that tend to overwhelm just in sheer numbers.  The game relies on focused shooting with critical and headshots rather than brute force (like some other zombie games).  I do like the fact that enemies don't just randomly appear all around you.  That used to bug the heck out of me in R6 Vegas 2.  After you a clear a room it should remain clear and enemies shouldn't just spawn in instantaneously.
The ability to use more than just standard grenades and giving the ability to set trip mines and proximity mines is pretty sweet but be careful not to be too close when they go off.  And if you set them too early they do self-detonate after a fair amount of time.  Using grenades, and mines creatively is very effective against the boss characters as they will mow you down with their big guns of you try and take them head on.
This game was so worth the $3.75.  Fun as hell and looks great.  The co-op is fantastic.  You can't go wrong!!

Super 3-D Noah's Ark is most definitely the best port of an oldschool FPS on Steam. The game runs greatly and actually has settings to change keybinds, screen resolution, all other stuff to be expected in games nowadays.
As this game is on the Wolf3D engine, it's not surprising it plays a lot like Wolfenstein 3D. In fact it's almost exactly the same. The whole game is reskinned, the maps are different, other minor changes, but the game plays exactly like Wolfenstein. One difference is the inclusion of trivia questions placed throughout the maps, which is quite strange to include in an FPS. I actually found them to be quite enjoyable, and sparked my interest to get a deeper understanding of the Noah's Ark story.
If you're unfamiliar with the base gameplay of Wolfenstein 3D, it's basically navigating through maps, killing enemies, finding keys to open doors granting access to later parts of the level, until you eventually beat it. Instead of playing as B.J. Blazkowicz shooting Nazi guards to death to ultimately kill Hitler, you play as Noah himself, going around his ark feeding his naughty animals that won't go to sleep! Unlike the final boss being mecha-Hitler, the final boss of Super 3-D Noah's Ark is Burt the Bear. Evidently this is a Christian game, so a far more toned down, child-friendly experience can be expected. I personally feel as though this doesn't retract from the enjoyment this game has to offer.
I'd definitely recommend this over ths Steam port of Wolfenstein 3D, as it plays far, far better. Depite it being a changeup from brutally murdering Nazi guards to feeding farm animals so they go to sleep, it plays very similar to Wolfenstein 3D and is equally enjoyable. Having 6 episodes provides plenty of game content, each having unique and humerous bosses at the end.
If you're into this type of game, then go for it. If you're looking at this and Wolfenstein 3D at the same time, this game is the way to go. The game is a good price for what it is and offers a fair few hours of fun.

Oh boy, where do I begin with this game.
The Singleplayer is very fun. It's a 2 part RPG adventure - in the first main part your'e traveling around the world map with your band of warriors (which you recruit from villeges) in an almost free style maner - you can pillage villages, battle bandits and faction's armies, visit cities and buy from them, attack castles or cities and even participate in good ol medievel tournamnets. It's a unique RPG experience which I personally really like, however it can be frustrating if you have no idea what your'e doing. You start as a level 1 hero, and level up through killing enemies and completing objectives and quiests. Each time you level up you get to raise your stats (Agillity, Int, strength, charisma, all affect your adeventure in various ways), your skill points which also give many benefits and your weapon proficiencies.
You can co-operate with factions and eventually join them and become a lord with lands. Your relationship with each factions affects the others, and if you end up in war with one of them their armies will make sure to chase you around the world map and battle you.
The second aspect of the game is the battle mode - here you are in a 3rd or 1st person perspective, fighting your enemies along side your trusty warband in classic medievel combat. You command your troops to hold positions, follow you or charge. The goal is to slay all of the enemy units. Sounds easy, until you find out that you ARE NOT a super unit, and die just as fast as all the other ones. With good strategy and powerful warriors at your side you can win battles and gain glory and loot. The weapons and armour you loot or buy at cities, that you wear on yourself, is what you use in battle, and there is a wide range of weapons to use - pikes, crossbows, swords, cleavers, two and one handed axes, spears, lances, bows and many many more. You can also ride on horses along side your cavalry and slay the enemy with a hit and run strategy!
By winning battles, looting villages and caravans and selling stuff you get money (called denars) which you use to buy weapons, horses, armour and food (which is useful to boost your party morale) and pay for your parties wages. A good way to earn money is to take prisoner enemy warriors or lords and then ransom them. I once sold a KING of an faction for 15k!
Now we get to the most frustrating part of the game - Multiplayer and battle mechanics.
It's fun. REALLY fun. But annoying.
The multiplayer mod itself is very entertaining. You can participate in many game modes like DM, TDM, CTF, Battle (1 live a round, last man standing) and My favorite - Siegie, where you have to capture the defending team's flag as the attacker. There are many maps to play, and it's a fresh experience.  There can be up to 200 people in one server, which leads to massive and epic battles. You spawn each time with a set weapons and armour, which you can upgrade or replace with money you gain through killing and getting objectives. Each player has a minimum set of money they always have acces to when they respawn which they cannot lose (It's not uncommon to see fully naked peoeple running around with huge battle axes). This, however leads to the problems of capitalism - the rich, who have a lot of money buy the best gear and get only more money from kills and the poor are stuck with bad gear and stay poor because they barely get any kills (You LOSE MONEY WHEN YOU DIE!).
In addition, The game suffers from various bugs, glitches, lags and inbalances, which make the otherwise flawless combat a source of anger. 2 Handed weapons are wildly over powered compared to one handed weapons + shields becuase of their much faster swing times and higher damage (+ Many break shields very quickly). Bows and crossbows are insanely effective with low money matches, where everyone has less armour but almost useless when used against very armed people. The hit detection can be broken at time, mostly for the worse - I've had many times when my arrows went right through and my axes did no damage at all. Blocking with weapons (not shields), although hard to master and is very rewarding, simply doesn't work at times. The horses are insanly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and always either stop dead on when you budge into something, leaving you easy prey for infantry with 2 handed weapons, or go compeltly the other direction and end up slaming into an obstacle - again, having you killed by archers and 2 handed axes.
The game also has some hilarious glitches like the "Sky Faces".
Overall, I think it's a very good game and I highly recommend you try it out. You will rage, but the best way to have fun is get better! (Or use 2 handed weapons, which ever works).

As someone who loved the first game to the point of playing through the whole thing multiple times I have to say that I am sorely disappointed with Hotline Miami 2. The first game had compact levels, which enabled a fast paced playstyle and gameplay that felt punishing, but fair. The music was fantastic and hunting for those A+ ratings was interesting and fun. Therefore I find it hard to believe that the second game managed to throw almost all of that away. What we have here is a top-down camping simulator where the vast levels lead to nothing but frustration as you're repeatedly sniped with shotguns from off-screen. The distances are long enough that even moving the camera around while standing still is not enough to spot even a fraction of the enemies. The game practically forces you to clear a room and then lure enemies to run into you by shooting at a wall to create some noise. Adding to the effect are characters you have to use that cannot wield firearms and are therefore forced to melee their way through the seemingly endless onslaught of mobsters. It might be a l2p issue, but I found the game unfairly difficult especially towards the end.
The levels being simply too big is not the only issue I had with the level design. Some seemingly open doors and holes in chain-link fences are very picky as to where you try to pass through them. If you're one pixel too far to one side you'll more often than not end up running still. Sometimes there also seems to be some sort of invisible wall in doorways that enemies cannot see and you can't melee through. This lead to situations where there were a couple of guys standing next to an open door in the room next to me and I was forced to run into the middle of them if I wanted to take them out.
In addition to the shotty gameplay the story was very hard to follow. The clips in between levels jump from storyline to storyline and about two hours in I abandoned all hope of figuring out what was actually going on in the game.
All this lead to me not even finishing the game despite trying my best to soldier through an experience that left my nerves and patience in ruins. Turns out that dying for 20 minutes straight in a level where you're forced to step into a straight hallway unarmed, while 4 or so guards either play baseball with your skull or turn you into Swiss cheese from the back lines with their AK's was not my idea of fun. It just felt like the C- waiting for me at the end was not worth it.  I bought HM2 while it was heavily discounted, but at the moment I feel like I still should've strayed away from it so that Hotline Miami would've remained as one of my favourite games of all time.

Alright, bear with me now, because I'm about to ♥♥♥♥ing recommend Deus Ex: The Fall. Buckle up.
Now, first things first. This game is $9.99. Do not pay $9.99. If it's 75% or more off, I totally recommend purchasing, and I'm going to really struggle to articulate exactly how I feel about this game, but here we go.
This is a port of a mobile game. It was not developed for PC in mind. That is a shame, and I really do wish they would've considered that route instead, but this is the route Eidos took, so we just have to keep that in mind. It's graphics are shoddy, physics are missing, models look bland, levels are downscaled, and certain gameplay mechanics are missing entirely.
However... I had fun. I honestly did. The basic gameplay of stealthily manuevering throughout the shadows and picking off troops one by one is still there, and is still as fun as it was in Human Revolution. The level design is still well done, even if it is small, and features multiple paths to reach your objectives, just as Human Revolution did. The voice acting is very well done, with the exception of the tutorial lady, who should really be put on suicide watch. The story is incredibly well done, with the fantastic writing of Human Revolution manifesting itself in The Fall through dialogue, pocket secretaries, and emails. There are some sidequests that present some variety in options. There are interesting characters.
Of course, things have also been simplified, and probably not to its advantage. Multiple saves don't exist, which wasn't really a problem for me, but I can see that unnerving certain people. The inventory system allows infinite of anything, and items are actually purchased through a tab rather than an individual. It's convenient, but rather odd and unusual.
So to conclude, yes, I do actually recommend Deus Ex: The Fall. There is love in this game that is evident, and I hate to see their effort wasted under a plethora of hatred and backlash. If you loved Deus Ex and Deius Ex: Human Revolution just as much as I did, you'll enjoy this adventure as well. Hell, I did everything you could possibly do in the game and managed to clock in at 8 hours, which isn't too shabby.
Some of THE most cringe-worthy voice acting I have ever heard draped over a tired plotline. I think I would rather play Desert Bus.

I am old and jaded and find things like car payments and health insurance premiums scarier than most horror games nowadays. Despite this, Layers of Fear did a fantastic job of genuinely creeping me out. It has 1 or 2 jump scares you can see coming from a mile away but honestly the main attraction here is the fantastic attention to atmosphere, which is arguably the most important aspect of a truly scary horror game.
The game is very subdued and subtle at first but as the game progresses it becomes more and more unhinged, the environments and atmosphere transitioning from unnerving to outright disturbing. This game is very "passive" and you spend most of your time walking around looking at things  but it does a fantastic job of keeping you on your toes and wondering what's coming next.
If you've played Silent Hill games you're definitely going to notice the subtle homages here and there. I caught quite a few references to SH4 and at least one for SH2...
Overall I highly recommend it to anyone who wants a horror game that focuses less on monsters jumping out of closets and more on making you dread what's around the next corner,
Now for some criticism: The game feels a bit too predictable and linear in its current state. After playing it through once I really don't have much incentive to do it again because I already know everything that's going to happen and the order in which it happens. That's not a problem right now since it's just an early access game, but in the full version it would be great if it were more unpredictable or if it were possible to do things in a different order.

I really like this game so far. It reminds me of left4dead but with customizable weapons and different "heroes" you can play. Only complaint is the relatively low player count. But match making works very well when there are people trying to play and allow for people to join my on-going match at anytime.

While I would recommend this game, both the leveling and tiered item systems have significant limitations.  Specifically, levels gained after unlocking all the trinkets slots are in a word, useless.  Therefore, any subsequent level is outright e-peen. Yes, levels after this point do yield item drops, but these items pale in comparison to roll items acquired at the end of a map.  Furthermore, top level items (RED) generally are not as useful as lower tiered items.   While the gameplay is certainly enjoyable, the reward portion of the gamification model in Vermintide is unimpressive and incomplete.  With all this being said, I would tentatively recommend this game; however, don't expect it to provide 100, 250, 500+ hours for the average gamer.

Layers of Fear profusely messes with your mind and will keep you immersed until your emotions cannot take it anymore. Play it.

Niche belongs to a genre I rarely play, and if I play, then not for long.
I'm not generally a patient person, and I like to have a goal to work to get to.
I found this game randomly on youtube, and absolutely fell inlove with it. From the artstyle, to the gamestyle, to the way every move kind of mattered. I loved the idea of being able to breed my own animals and shape them in any way and form I wanted to - And with every update, the possibilities get bigger and better.
This isn't the game for you, if you need specific goals and achievements - At least not in its present form. However, it's very peaceful, it's engaging and with the ability to name your creatures, you can now bond further with them. Coming up with elaborate stories, personalities, etc. for each of them is a fun little pasttime. There's also always the chance of a mutation popping up at random. With some work though, you can completely costumize your creatures. I've become quite addicted to that.
With Early-Access games I never expect too much, because I know how much they can change. I've been so pleasantly surprised by this game however, that it's prompted me to write my first review.
Another big thumbs up goes to the developers. The developers of the game is active in the group as well, and takes suggestions and engages with the core-group of the game. Niche was an unexpectadly addictive game for me. I bought it on a whim a while back when seeing a few YouTube videos on it, and was drawn in by its interesting take on genetics, and the endless possibilities on offer in terms of creating creatures, and helping them survive despite difficulties in the environment.
It is a challenging game if you really want to strategise and create the 'perfect' creature genetically, but can also be relaxing if you focus less on the details and more on the aspect of survival, and exploring the islands on offer. You can really choose your playing style, and if you wish, you can create your own challenges since it's so open. This makes it perfect as, kind of, an accidental role-playing game, if you wish to get attached to your creatures, which you will.
You watch them grow, you watch them breed, you watch them protect, you watch them die, and the generations go on and on, at a fairly fast-paced speed; which I love.
All in all, I play this game for its awesome art style and relaxing nature, but also so I can use strategy to manipulate the genetics, and really get that feeling of satisfaction when I finally create the perfect creature and survive the more difficult islands.
It's so challenging at times, that the satisfaction is ever-more rewarding! Definitely a tricky game to conquer, but well worth the buy!
